as_thevanishing_inbox1_001_body:
AEGIS HEAD OFFICE
July 18th, 15:19
Office of Alba Tesreau

ALBA TESREAU: The information comes from a source I trust. I’ve combed the data for errors in their calculations. It seems frighteningly accurate.

ADEN TANNER: We’ve known about these rumours for years now. What’s changed?

TESREAU: This goes far beyond the occasional escape pod collected by Thargoid ships, Aden.

TANNER: Let me make sure I’m understanding the premise. Some analyst has compared the total population of Thargoid-invaded systems with the official refugee counts.

TESREAU: Correct.

TANNER: Then subtracted combat casualties, intercepted transports and people killed during port attacks. The official estimates, at least.

TESREAU: Along with other variables. Not all refugees pass through the rescue ships. Some of those don’t register as safe. Others fled as soon as the Maelstrom signals were first sighted.

TANNER: And a dozen other points, I’m sure. But ultimately the final totals don’t quite match up.

TESREAU: Even with a margin for error we’re looking at tens, maybe hundreds of millions of people unaccounted for. And the figure’s rising each week! If they’re not dead and they didn’t escape, then captivity must be the answer.

TANNER: I’ve never known the Thargoids to keep prisoners. Doesn’t quite seem their style.

TESREAU: They’d have to construct a method to house organisms of a different biochemical makeup. That would only be worthwhile if the captives were deemed important.

TANNER: We did the same for studying live specimens.

TESREAU: I’m going to assume you mean the historical ‘we’, admiral. Aegis doesn’t capture Thargoids for research purposes. Just one of the many distinctions between us and INRA.

TANNER: ‘We’ as in the human race, yes. My point is that surely the aliens have had plenty of opportunity to study us by now. If what you’re saying is true, and the Thargoids are abducting millions of people… well, there’s a grander plan here than research. One that we need to figure out.

TESREAU: I suppose it’s too much to hope that the Thargoids will treat our people more considerately than INRA treated theirs?

TANNER: Honestly? It’d be a wasted prayer to ask that much.
as_thevanishing_inbox2_001_body:
AEGIS HEAD OFFICE
July 18th, 15:24
Office of Alba Tesreau

ALBA TESREAU: We’ll have to manage how this information is shared. Of course, we’ll need to reassure people that we’re doing everything we can to locate the missing…

ADEN TANNER: Just to play devil’s advocate for a second - Are mass abductions something we need to go public with?

TESREAU: Yes, I think so. With numbers this high it would be cowardly to pretend we don't know what’s going on.

TANNER: Hm. I’m not sure all of Aegis's financers will agree.

TESREAU: We’ve been given the authority to make firm decisions for ourselves. Besides, I’d rather be in trouble for telling the truth than lying.

TANNER: Couldn’t agree more. I’ll back you up if needed. But I suggest being economical with that truth. Think about it: Aegis announces millions have been captured alive for unknown reasons. It’ll scare the crap out of the trillions listening.

TESREAU: ‘Unknown reasons’… We have to find out why the Thargoids are taking so many people. I’m not looking forward to the answers.

TANNER: Your rivals are going to spin any press statement, too. Torben Rademaker will be on every newsfeed telling people that Azimuth would never have allowed this to happen. Without going into details, obviously.

TESREAU: Oh, screw Torben. He can play politics all he likes. Scoring points in the face of a major humanitarian tragedy is just his style. But then he did learn from the best . <sighs> This is horrible.

-N£TW@RK BRE&CH DETEC+ED-

SEO JIN-AE: They’re harvesting us.

TESREAU: Seo? For goodness sake, this is a private conversation! Why are you on comms?

TANNER: Sounds like it isn’t just the Thargoids she listens to.

TESREAU: Shut down your comms link until I can find someone to secure it—

SEO: I said they’re harvesting us. As a resource. You wanted to know why the Thargoids are abducting people. I can help figure out the answer.

TESREAU: If we’re going to talk, you may as well come to my office. We’ll discuss this in person.

SEO: No. I want to be alone. There’s a lot of noise  today.

TANNER: Okay. What type of resource are we to them? Food? Fuel?

TESREAU: We have no evidence the Thargoids view us as edible. Any more than we do them.

SEO: Not food. Not fuel. It’s more accurate to say the Thargoid race has a purpose for us. One which is giving me some real shitty dreams.
as_thevanishing_inbox3_001_body:
AEGIS HEAD OFFICE
July 18th, 15:28
Office of Alba Tesreau

SEO JIN-AE: The noise changed a few weeks ago. But it wasn’t until you mentioned millions of people vanishing that the new melody made sense.

ADEN TANNER: What do you mean by melody?

ALBA TESREAU: Seo’s connection to the Thargoid telepathic network doesn’t include an understanding of their language. Aegis is working with her to establish a method of interpreting what she sees and hears.

SEO: Describing parts of the Thargoid noise like music helps. I can pinpoint certain notes and melodies… even different instruments. Sometimes images appear. The sound is still awful, and triggers emotions which are harder to process. But focusing reduces the chaos of it all.

TANNER: And you say this noise is different to when the invasion started?

SEO: Yes. The original buzz grew louder as the Maelstrom signals approached the bubble. It announced the invasion, drawing their fleets. When the Maelstroms arrived, I understood that the Thargoids would claim as many star systems and destroy as many ports as possible. Territory was the only goal.
Now there is a different melody underneath it. An image keeps repeating, what looks like tunnels and caves… Rows and rows of what I thought were eggs.

TESREAU: Seo mentioned these ‘eggs’ to me before, and it’s logical to assume that the Thargoids have a method of replenishing their war casualties.

SEO: But there was never any sense of compassion or protection. Maybe Thargoids are just bad parents. But now I think it’s because the eggs aren’t eggs. They’re pods. Containers for humans. If I focus on that concept, the noise is less abrasive. That’s usually a sign that I’m understanding something in the alien broadcast.

TANNER: This is a lot to take in. Do you think these pods are on the Titans?

SEO: Yes. And the people inside are important to the next phase of Thargoid invasion. I’m sure of it.

TANNER: Okay. I don’t understand how that brain of yours works, kid. But the information you’ve given us up to now has been solid. Alba, you said earlier that Aegis is autonomous now, correct?

TESREAU: Within reason. Why?

TANNER: Because I’m not interested in waiting months for approval from the superpowers. Let’s go with Seo’s music. Can you have your people develop a way to recover pods from a Titan, if we can figure out where they’re being stored?

TESREAU: I’ll see what I can do. But even if we design something suitable, it isn’t going to be an easy mission. A ship would have to fly dangerously close to a Titan.

TANNER: Our pilots have done incredible things so far. I learned long ago never to underestimate them. With the right tools they’ll figure out a way to get any job done. And if Seo’s right, and these things contain human captives… well, we’ve got a lot of work to do.
as_timetomoveon_001_body:
Expedition Log: 09/10/3274

We've made it. For a while there I thought we might be in real trouble. Came out of our jump into what I can only describe as a meteor storm. The ship took a lot of damage and it was touch and go there for a minute. But here we are, Checkpoint 14.

The habitats have been set up and our auto-rover has discovered some mineral deposits that might help with repairs. Symons thinks he can reprogramme the rover to harvest these. It'll take a long time, but it's the best option we have.

Richards is working on the agri-habs. AG Hab 1 is up and running and Hab 2 is up and ready for planting. Hopefully we should have fresh vegetables in a matter of weeks. I can't tell you how sick we all are of the food cartridges at this point.

So this is it, life out in the deep dark of space.
as_timetomoveon_002_body:
Expedition Log: 11/05/3275

Okay, I have a good news, bad news situation here. So let's see... bad news first I think.

Bad news: It's going to take longer than we hoped to make repairs and get moving again. We're not going anywhere any time soon. It looks like this place is home for the foreseeable future. With the agri-habs fully up and running we can, in reality, live out the rest of our natural lives here if necessary.

Good news: We're going to have a wedding out here. It looks like a little ship board romance has turned into something. Woods and Symons have decided to tie the knot.

I know the official guidelines say that this kind of thing is not allowed, that it somehow clouds judgement. But it's not like we're going to be coming back. I mean we're not just exploring out here. That's what the payload is for. Seeding new life.

Besides, maybe we'll set a record for the first marriage deep in space. We might even start a trend.
as_timetomoveon_003_body:
Expedition Log: 25/12/3275

We knew this journey wouldn't be easy. As I said in the press conference before we left, "As pioneers we tread the difficult path so that those who follow in our footsteps can benefit from our knowledge and reach deeper into the galaxy".

And I hold to that. We knew this wasn't going to be easy. We knew there would be hardship and sacrifices along the way. That is what being a pioneer and an explorer is. We endure these hardships so that we can discover new ground and pave the way for others.

In the years to come, I'm sure explorers will be able to jump larger distances and see things we can only dream of. I'm sure they will make discoveries that we can't possibly imagine and travel to the furthest reaches of our galaxy. But these early expeditions into the black will be remembered as a significant step in humanity's journey out into the stars.

Oh yeah, I almost forgot... Happy Holidays.
as_timetomoveon_004_body:
Expedition Log: 24/08/3277

Today we break camp to move to our next checkpoint.

After so many months growing food, repairing the ships and refuelling for the next jump, this camp feels like home. We've spent a lot longer here than our previous sites, due to all the damage we sustained crashing through that meteor shower on the last jump.

These habitats were designed to be disposable. Temporary camps to allow us to recharge for the next jump. It's good to know that these habitat modules can last this long. We've decided to leave the settlement largely intact. We can spare the materials and who knows, maybe one day a future explorer will find it and be able to use it as a kicking off point on their own expedition.

I'll be sorry to leave it all behind, but that's the deal. Time to move on.

as_voxgal_alliance_didio_inbox1_001_body:
The journalist Jade Sanderlyn of Vox Galactica was recently invited to conduct rare public interviews with admirals of the three superpowers. This excerpt is from a conversation with Admiral Rachel Ziegler of the Alliance.

Jade Sanderlyn: This is Jade Sanderlyn reporting for Vox Galactica. I am here with Admiral Rachel Ziegler of the Alliance. I'm pleased to have this opportunity to speak with you, Admiral.

Rachel Ziegler: You're welcome.

JS: We're on board the Salote Charm, which is currently stationed in the Didio system. Two days ago, a large Thargoid force arrived here and began attacking human ships and ports. There are reports that Salvation has asked your fleet, and those of the other superpowers, to hold the Thargoid force at bay until the anti-xeno superweapon--

RZ: Let me clarify your question before you finish it. My priority is the safety of the billions who call Didio home. We are not here to keep the Thargoid forces occupied. We are here to defeat them.

JS: Understood, Admiral. Salvation has asked for time to prepare his superweapon, though?

RZ: Yes, he has. But the Alliance does not operate with the assumption that Salvation will deliver on his promise.

JS: Do you support Salvation's methods? Critics have suggested he endangers lives by using a powerful weapon that has not been independently assessed by experts.

RZ: Whether I support or do not support Salvation is immaterial. The fact is that, on two previous occasions, the superweapon has eliminated Thargoid fleets from entire systems. Rejecting such a powerful device would be unwise. Still, I think the question of risk is wholly appropriate. Military and political figures alike must not become complacent or over-reliant on Salvation's technology. Particularly when we know so little about it.

JS: Is that ambiguity a concern for the Alliance?

RZ: It should be a concern for everybody. So far, Salvation has acted in our best interests. But a weapon that powerful would be considerably dangerous if recalibrated to damage human technology. Imagine what the NMLA could have done with such a device.

JS: Terrible things, no doubt. But your fleet in Didio could be seen as a tacit endorsement of Salvation by Allied leadership, regardless of your personal views.

RZ: As I said, Salvation's results are highly impressive.

JS: Let's hope they remain so. We'll take a short break. Join us after these messages.
as_voxgal_alliance_didio_inbox2_001_body:
Continuing the Vox Galactica interview with Admiral Rachel Ziegler, who commands the ongoing defence of the Didio system from Thargoid incursion.

Jade Sanderlyn: Welcome back. I'm here with Admiral Ziegler of the Alliance. I want to touch on the recent dissolution of the Aegis initiative. Has that decision had any impact on the Thargoid war, in your view?

Rachel Ziegler: From a logistical standpoint? Not really, no. Aegis vessels have been repurposed by skilled pilots. I know of several prominent colleagues who are displeased, however.

JS: Can you elaborate on why?

RZ: Aegis Research provided several notable contributions to the war effort. For example, meta-alloy studies gave us safe methods of storing Thargoid artefacts. Decontamination limpets increased ship survivability during Thargoid combat. Aegis also played a key role in the safe development and distribution of Guardian hybrid weapons technology. It remains to be seen who will lead such efforts now.

JS: Critics have argued Aegis was poorly managed and achieved less than expected, given the resources available to it.

RZ: Critics are going to focus on the negatives. That's why they're called critics. I'll bet you a Kobe Beef supper these people have never encountered a Thargoid vessel in person.

JS: Are you referring to the political aspect of Aegis's disbandment? You've previously spoken out against decisions made by the Alliance Assembly.

RZ: Only the very poor decisions.

JS: Does the end of Aegis fall under that category?

RZ: No, I don't believe so. The decision to end Aegis is understandable given the evidence presented in the Baumann Report. Even if I do not personally agree with it. My perspective has always been one of security. The ADF is a quickly mobilised fleet, but we lack the resources of the Federal and Imperial navies. Aegis improved the Alliance's ability to defend itself from a prolonged Thargoid invasion.

JS: Sirius Corporation has offered to fulfil that role for the Alliance.

RZ: Yes, well Sirius went about it very poorly.

JS: Li Yong-Rui has since recognised the lack of approval from the Assembly and appears keen to make amends. Does that sway your opinion at all?

RZ: I have no doubt that Sirius Corp would improve the strength of the ADF long term. But let us not pretend that Mr Yong-Rui's interest in the Alliance is altruistic. We'll see what he wants in return soon enough, I expect.

JS: Admiral Ziegler, it has been a pleasure talking to you. Good luck in the coming conflict.

RZ: Thank you.

JS: From the Salote Charm in Didio, this is Jade Sanderlyn for Vox Galactica. Stay safe out there.
as_voxgal_empire_novas_inbox1_001_body:
The journalist Jade Sanderlyn of Vox Galactica was recently invited to conduct rare public interviews with admirals of the three superpowers. This excerpt is from a conversation with Admiral Henry Paul Atherton of the Empire.

Jade Sanderlyn: This is Jade Sanderlyn reporting for Vox Galactica. I am sitting with Admiral Henry Paul Atherton of the Imperial Navy. Thank you for agreeing to this interview, Admiral.

Henry Paul Atherton: Oh, please. Call me Henry.

JS: I'd be delighted to. This is a very impressive ship, Henry.

HPA: Some might say Majestic. [laughs] Yes, the Succession is a wonderful vessel. 

JS: How long have you commanded her?

HPA: Several years now. It has been an honour to have my name listed on the Succession's exemplary service record.

JS: You were promoted to admiral only three years ago. Does that change the personal dynamic with your crew at all?

HPA: Well, they salute a little faster, I suppose. Happily I enjoy a strong relationship with my officers, so they took the change fully in stride.

JS: Let's talk about Novas. I understand that the Imperial Navy has deployed a fleet here at Salvation's request.

HPA: That's correct.

JS: Emperor Arissa recently resumed her duties following… an extended absence from the throne. Having now surely been briefed on Salvation's work, does the Emperor endorse Salvation?

HPA: If the Emperor had objections, her navy would not be in Novas.

JS: What are your objectives in the system?

HPA: Well, in case it has gone unnoticed, there is a major Thargoid invasion occurring here. It is our duty to protect civilian populations and prevent the loss of strategic assets.

JS: I'm pleased that you mentioned civilian lives first. Does Salvation share this approach?

HPA: Almost certainly. Why else would he invest so much effort into his marvellous superweapon if not to protect people?

JS: Some have claimed that Salvation prioritises victory over safety.

HPA: Jade, dear: they are the same thing. The cost of war is human lives, and the Thargoids extract a heavy toll. Every invaded system. Every burning starport. Every ambushed convoy. Every ship lost to hyperspace. We have repeatedly driven the Thargoids back from our space, but the wretched things keep returning. That cost grows each day. Salvation's superweapon has proven effective at wiping Thargoids from entire systems at a stroke. If Salvation calls that victory while you and I call it saving lives, then I'm comfortable with the difference in perspective.

JS: Thank you for elaborating. Let's take a break. We'll be back after these messages.
as_voxgal_empire_novas_inbox2_001_body:
Continuing the Vox Galactica interview with Admiral Henry Paul Atherton, who commands the ongoing defence of the Novas system from Thargoid incursion.

Jade Sanderlyn: Welcome back. I'm here with Admiral Atherton of the Imperial Navy. Henry, I wanted to get your thoughts on Aegis. Has the disbandment of that organisation had any effect on the anti-Thargoid efforts?

Henry Paul Atherton: Yes, I would say that's a fair assessment.

JS: In what way?

HPA: Aegis Defence pilots were skilled at engaging Thargoid ships. That experience was valuable to the younger pilots defending Imperial territory.

JS: Are you disappointed that Aegis is gone?

HPA: Hm. I think so, yes. Despite Aegis's faults – and it certainly had those – the initiative achieved much over the years. Also, Alba Tesreau is a delightful individual. Have you had the pleasure?

JS: No, I have not spoken with Professor Tesreau. I hope to soon, though.

HPA: She has worked as hard as anybody to improve our understanding of the Thargoids. That dedication was reflected in Aegis's work. Poorly managed it may have been, but it was certainly not poorly led.

JS: Did you follow the news of the Alexandria wreckage discovery in recent months?

HPA: Yes, I did.

JS: Do you have any comments to share?

HPA: The loss of the Alexandria is tragic, of course. A ghastly turn of events.

JS: Has there been any attempt to identify the perpetrators?

HPA: Not to my knowledge. But then I am not an intelligence officer.

JS: The Alexandria's logs suggest Aegis's efforts were undermined by other parties, though.

HPA: Perhaps, but that event was not the sole reason for Aegis's disbandment. What's done is done. Our focus rests firmly on what is yet to do.

JS: Which brings us back to Salvation.

HPA: Indeed it does. The Imperial Fleet will provide Salvation with the time required to deploy his superweapon by engaging the Thargoid forces in this system. The people of Novas will see first-hand how effective Salvation's methods can be. I believe that this war has an end in sight.

JS: I truly hope so. Thank you for your time, Admiral. From the INV Succession in Novas, this is Jade Sanderlyn. Stay safe out there.
as_voxgal_federation_sosong_inbox1_001_b:
The journalist Jade Sanderlyn of Vox Galactica was recently invited to conduct rare public interviews with admirals of the three superpowers. This excerpt is from a conversation with Admiral Maxton Price of the Federation.

Jade Sanderlyn: My name is Jade Sanderlyn, reporting for Vox Galactica. I'm here with Admiral Maxton Price, onboard the FNS Amphion in the Sosong system. I was very impressed with the tour of the ship prior to our interview, Admiral.

Maxton Price: I can't say I'm surprised, Miss Sanderlyn. Is this your first time on a Farragut-class battle cruiser?

JS: Yes. It's one the reasons I was so excited that my interview request had been granted. The Amphion is just as impressive as I'd hoped.

MP: That's gracious of you to say. Of course, the Farragut-class vessels value performance over aesthetics. It's a lesson our Imperial friends would do well to learn one day.

JS: I take it, then, that you consider yourself a utilitarian?

MP: In military matters, what other philosophy is there? A sleek ship will turn heads and attract investors, but when something dangerous enters your space, most soldiers would choose a powerful response over a pretty one.

JS: Which brings us to the current conflict in this system. The Federal fleet has been asked to contain the Thargoid threat while Salvation prepares his anti-xeno superweapon.

MP: And I have no doubt that we will succeed. Federal military power is as strong as it's ever been. Funding provided by the Hudson administration over the past seven years has allowed us to expand and modernise our fleet. It's a pleasant time to be an admiral.

JS: I presume that you are in favour of Salvation's work.

MP: Wholeheartedly. His results speak volumes to a man like me. The anti-xeno superweapon has incredible range, a devastating impact on Thargoid craft, and is harmless to our own ships. What's not to like? 

JS: Aside from independent studies by the engineer Ram Tah, we have very limited information about the weapon. We also know nothing about its long-term effects on human physiology. Do you think there is any risk to the public?

MP: Let me ask you a question, Miss Sanderlyn. Do you think this hypothetical health risk poses a greater danger to the general public than a Thargoid fleet crawling through a populated system?

JS: No, but surely the lack of transparency--

MP: No, it does not. I've seen what the Thargoids are capable of. It's impressive, it's scary and it results in considerable loss of life if not dealt with quickly. Salvation has proven he can achieve significant victories for an entire system. Timid hand-wringing over the future is fine with me, once we've secured a future in which to do so.

JS: Let's take a break for a word from our sponsors. We'll be right back.
as_voxgal_federation_sosong_inbox2_001_b:
Continuing the Vox Galactica interview with Admiral Maxton Price, who commands the ongoing defence of the Sosong system from Thargoid incursion.

Jade Sanderlyn: Thanks for staying with us. I'm here with Admiral Price of the Federal Navy. We were just talking about Salvation's contributions to the Thargoid war. Do you believe he is a true replacement for Aegis?

Maxton Price: Absolutely. Aegis hasn't been a factor in this conflict for some time. I've viewed them as an auxiliary force, at best. A hindrance at worst.

JS: Could you elaborate on that?

MP: Where would you like to begin? Perhaps with the lack of concrete results for several years. Or the over-reliance on independent pilots to fight their battles for them. Maybe the loss of the Alexandria and the valuable Guardian artefacts it carried.

JS: The Alexandria was sabotaged by outsiders, as proven in audio--

MP: Whatever the method, the outcome was the same. Poor decisions and bad leadership led to the Alexandria's loss. Look at the chief military liaison for Aegis, Aden Tanner. The man tried to forcibly invade Salvation's allies over some wild conspiracy theory about illegal research. That's the kind of leadership we're talking about.

JS: Aden Tanner was formerly an admiral of the Federal Navy.

MP: Never liked the guy. Bought into his own hype a little too much. Now he's in custody while a judge decides how long he'll spend in jail. The Federal Navy is better for it.

JS: I appreciate your honesty, Admiral. Before we wrap up, I was wondering if you'd asked for command of the fleet here in Sosong.

MP: I did, yes.

JS: May I ask why?

MP: I felt the defence of Sosong was a high-priority task and wanted to oversee matters personally.

JS: This isn't the first time you've taken part in a Thargoid-related operation.

MP: No, it isn't. At this stage of the war, any officer who lacks experience with Thargoid vessels is doing a disservice to the people they lead.

JS: In 3302, you ordered Farragut-class battle cruisers to the Merope system soon after the discovery of Thargoid barnacle sites. It was claimed that independent vessels exploring the area were fired upon.

MP: Claimed incorrectly, but yes.

JS: It was reported that the JAG would open an inquiry those claims, but no further details were ever released. Can you share the outcome of that investigation?

MP: If the findings were worth a damn, you'd have heard about it. And if a crime had been committed, maybe I'd be sitting alongside Aden Tanner in a jail cell. But instead here I am, doing what I do best. Protecting us from the Thargoids. Does that answer your question?

JS: It sure does. Thank you for your time, Admiral Price. This has been an enlightening conversation.

MP: I'm sure it has, Miss Sanderlyn. I'll have someone escort you to your shuttle now.

JS: That's kind of you. From the FNS Amphion in Sosong, this is Jade Sanderlyn for Vox Galactica. Stay safe out there.

as_wishcarefully_001_body:
Personal Log:

They called this Project Traveller.

Sending hundreds of ships out into deep space to locate habitable planets, resource sites, mineral deposits.

We were the honoured few to make it through the training programme. We were the ones made of the 'right stuff', as they put it.

I thought it would be interesting, exciting even. Exploring new systems, getting deeper into space than anyone before us.

But the reality is very different.
as_wishcarefully_002_body:
Personal Log:

We're furthering the human race, one system at a time. Jump in, scan the system. Tag points of interest and send the data back to control.

It's just so monotonous. Doing the same thing every day.

I guess my expectations were just too high. I've been hearing about possible alien life and strange anomalies out in deep space. But all I see is another rock or ball of gas floating in the black.
as_wishcarefully_003_body:
Personal Log:

Ever heard the phrase "be careful what you wish for"? I sure had, and paid it no mind. Just something people say.

I wished for excitement and boy did I get it.

Seems all our jumping put too much strain on the ship's systems. Our last jump threw us way off and into a collision course with this rock I now call home.

The others were killed in the crash. I have no idea how I survived.
as_wishcarefully_004_body:
Personal Log:

I've salvaged what I can, but it's not much. I've build the emergency shelter and jury rigged equipment to make this place habitable.

My supplies will last a while, I'm not kidding myself there's not enough to last forever, but what can I do?

Maybe one day I'll have to face up to the fact that I'll die out here, but that's not today.

ax_combatgeneric_harvest07: Nobody told me how crazy these bug ships can move around!
ax_combatgeneric_harvest08: Aim for the hearts when you see 'em, people.
ax_combatgeneric_harvest09: We've gotta get these bastards out of our system. Fight for your families, your friends!
ax_combatgeneric_harvest10: No surrender! This is our home, and I refuse to give it up to these monsters.
ax_combatgeneric_harvest11: Hold your aim steady and your flight path clean. Let's give these bugs a show.
ax_combatgeneric_harvest12: This is our space! Not theirs! They'll never take it away from us
ax_combatgeneric_harvest13: Whatever happens, don't be left with regrets. Give the aliens everything you've got.
ax_combatgeneric_harvest14: This is for Salvation, you insect scum!
ax_combatgeneric_harvest16: We ain't getting paid by the hour here, people. Take them out as quickly as you can.
ax_combatgeneric_harvest17: Watch my flanks, I'm going in.
ax_combatgeneric_harvest18: Watch your radar in case more of them jump in. We need a victory quickly.
ax_combatgeneric_harvest19: Expose the hearts then focus on them. You know the drill, people. Rinse and repeat.
ax_combatgeneric_harvest20: Hey Commander, how you doing over there? Planning on finishing these things off anytime soon?
ax_combatlosing01: The bugs are taking control. We need to fight harder.
ax_combatlosing02: If we don't turn things around soon we're gonna have problems.
ax_combatlosing03: We can't let the Thargoids keep the momentum. Lives depend on it!
ax_combatlosing04: I don't have a good feeling about this - the insects are winning!
ax_combatlosing05: Not sure how much more of this we can take. Fire everything you have.
ax_combatlosing06: We have to take the fight to the bugs now or we're done for.
ax_combatlosing07: I'm freaking out, these monsters are unstoppable!
ax_combatlosing08: This isn't looking good. The Thargoids have us beat if we don't do something.
ax_combatlosing09: Sign up to fight aliens, they said. It'll be fun, they said…
ax_combatlosing10: The Thargoids have us where they want us. We need to mix it up!
ax_combatlosing_harvest01: I got shot up. Bleeding out...
ax_combatlosing_harvest02: How many Thargoids are left? I can't focus - I think I'm losing it...
ax_combatlosing_harvest03: This is bleak, man. This is so bad. The Thargoids are too powerful.
ax_combatlosing_harvest04: They're too fast, too strong! We're gonna lose!
ax_combatlosing_harvest05: The Thargoids want to take over our home. We can't let that happen.
ax_combatlosing_harvest06: This is too much. I need to get out of here before it's too late!
ax_combatlosing_harvest07: Does anyone has a repair limpet with them?
ax_combatlosing_harvest08: I don't know how much more damage my ship can take.
ax_combatlosing_harvest09: If my ship is destroyed, don't let them take my body. You hear me?
ax_combatlosing_harvest10: I'm in serious trouble here. Tell my kids I love 'em.
ax_combatunderattack01: We're getting our asses kicked here. Time to double our efforts.
ax_combatunderattack02: Maybe today is a good day to die... Because that's what'll happen if we don't flip this fight around!
ax_combatunderattack03: The Thargoids are pushing the advantage and we can't let that happen. Focus, people.
ax_combatunderattack04: They're all over us! If we don't fight harder we're bug food.
ax_combatunderattack05: It's time to fight with everything you have. Our homes are lost if we don't take control here!
ax_combatunderattack06: I can't shake 'em! The damn bugs know what I'm gonna do next, I swear it!
ax_combatunderattack07: How are we supposed to beat these things! They're relentless...
ax_combatunderattack08: We've got to hold out for the people still in this system. Buy them time to get out.
ax_combatunderattack09: There are still refugees being ferried to safety. Don't give up hope - hold the line.
ax_combatunderattack10: We can't afford to lose this fight. Too many people in this system are depending on us.
ax_combatunderattack_harvest02: I'm taking fire, trying to move clear.
ax_combatunderattack_harvest03: Need a little help here. This Thargoid's really taken a liking to me.
ax_combatunderattack_harvest04: The bugs have me in their sights. Will try to evade.
ax_combatunderattack_harvest05: I'm flying defensive! This is getting heated.
ax_combatunderattack_harvest06: Now we're talking! C'mon, bugs. Show me what you got.
ax_combatunderattack_harvest07: Oh, you wanna play, huh? Bring it on, I can take it!
ax_combatunderattack_harvest08: These Thargoids aren't messing around. I'm under attack.
ax_combatunderattack_harvest09: Oh crap, they're on me. Taking fire, need some backup! Send everyone!
ax_combatunderattack_harvest10: I'm under attack. If I can't shake them off I'll bloody well take them with me.
ax_combatwinning01: Keep going, we're pushing the insects back!
ax_combatwinning02: These Thargoids bit off more than they can chew.
ax_combatwinning03: Don't stop now - we've got the upper hand!
ax_combatwinning04: We have the bugs reeling, stay on 'em!
ax_combatwinning05: Ain't so tough now, are ya? This is human space!
ax_combatwinning06: This is our chance. We're hitting them hard, keep at it!
ax_combatwinning07: Whatever you do, don't stop fighting! They're in trouble!
ax_combatwinning08: The Thargoids weren't prepared for what we're giving them, haha!
ax_combatwinning09: We've got the advantage, don't let it slip away.
ax_combatwinning10: We'll have some stories to tell when this is over - the Thargoids are in trouble!
ax_humanretreat01: Heads up! We are leaving - disengage from the enemy!
ax_humanretreat02: We're getting the hell out of here before the Thargoids claim more victims.
ax_humanretreat03: It's time to retreat We can't beat the Thargoids this time.
ax_humanretreat04: Fire up your FSD's, everyone. We're pulling out the area.
ax_humanretreat05: We can't handle the bugs this time. If your ship can jump, get somewhere safe.
ax_humanretreat06: We have to get out of here or the Thargoids will finish us! Pull back!
ax_humanretreat07: Thargoids have taken the area. Time to leave.
ax_humanretreat08: If we stick around much longer we're dead. Get out of here!
ax_humanretreat09: Damn bugs are in control of this zone. We're pulling out, get moving!
ax_humanretreat10: I'm not sticking around any longer. If you' ve got any sense you'll leave too!
ax_map_help_text_1: The Thargoid War Information mode provides an overview of the ongoing conflict between humans and Thargoids. This panel lists all confirmed Titan locations and the number of star systems each one currently influences. The total number of systems with a level of Thargoid presence are also listed.
ax_map_help_text_2: With multiple star systems facing Thargoid aggression, a fleet of Rescue Megaships have been deployed in specific locations. These act as the focal point for civilian evacuation missions, and accept occupied escape pods and black boxes rescued from deep space. Rescue Megaships also offer a range of anti-xeno modules for Commanders to outfit their vessels with.
ax_map_help_text_3: In Map Mode, the State tab now offers system filters for all levels of Thargoid invasion. Meanwhile, the Display Options panel lists toggles for locations with damaged or repairing ports, Rescue Megaships or Thargoid Titans.
ax_map_help_text_4: The Thargoid War panel shows the current status of the conflict in a selected system. Here you'll find the system's current war status and the time remaining until the next state change. Activities available to Commanders which help humanity's efforts are listed, along with the potential next system state determined by the week's results.
ax_npc_neartitan_highdamage_01: You see that? The Titan's in trouble now!
ax_npc_neartitan_highdamage_02: I can't believe we've made the mothership panic. At last!
ax_npc_neartitan_highdamage_03: How much more can this giant Thargoid take?
ax_npc_neartitan_highdamage_04: We're right behind you, Commanders. Let's finish the job.
ax_npc_neartitan_highdamage_05: The Titan can't handle much more of this. Let 'em have it.
ax_npc_neartitan_highdamage_06: If we can sustain this attack the Titan is finished…
ax_npc_neartitan_highdamage_07: We're fought so hard, don't ease off now.
ax_npc_neartitan_highdamage_08: You've really got this Titan on the ropes, Commander!
ax_npc_neartitan_highdamage_09: Give 'em hell, Commander! Fight for all the lives these insects cut short!
ax_npc_neartitan_highdamage_10: And we piled upon the Titan's green hull…
ax_npc_neartitan_lowdamage_01: The Titan's showing signs of damage, keep it up!
ax_npc_neartitan_lowdamage_02: We're making good headway, keep up the pressure.
ax_npc_neartitan_lowdamage_03: Promising start, Commanders! Maintain course, don't let the Titan recover.
ax_npc_neartitan_lowdamage_04: The Titan's actually hurt. This is our chance to press the advantage!
ax_npc_neartitan_lowdamage_05: Lock and load, people. These Commanders are doing fine work, so watch their backs.
ax_npc_neartitan_lowdamage_06: The Titan's hurt! We're actually hurting it!
ax_npc_neartitan_lowdamage_07: Confirmed damage. Our Titan's starting to feel the burn.
ax_npc_neartitan_lowdamage_08: That core is the weak spot. Keep hammering at it.
ax_npc_neartitan_lowdamage_09: Keep going, Commanders. We'll try and keep the Thargoids outta your way.
ax_npc_neartitan_lowdamage_10: The Titan's looking angry, so keep your cool.
ax_patrol_harvest01: Scanning for signs of Thargoids. Nothing yet...
ax_patrol_harvest02: The bugs aren't going to let us pass through this system unattended. It's just a matter of time.
ax_patrol_harvest03: Nothing on scanners. Damn it, where are they?
ax_patrol_harvest04: If no murder flowers show up soon, we should move on. They must be occupied somewhere else in the system...
ax_patrol_harvest05: We've been chasing signals for over an hour. When are we gonna shoot some insects?
ax_patrol_harvest06: Don't get lazy. We know the Thargoids could appear at any minute.
ax_patrol_harvest07: Sensor sweeps haven't completed yet. Just hold position in case we get jumped.
ax_patrol_harvest08: Nothing on the radar yet. A bit too quiet, isn't it?
ax_patrol_harvest09: Got a Commander in the area. Welcome to the party, pal.
ax_patrol_harvest10: Looks like we have some backup in pushing the Thargoids out of our home. Right, Commander?
ax_patrol_peace01: Nothing on the scanners. Keep an eye out for non-human activity.
ax_patrol_peace02: Catching a few signals on the FSS. Stay alert.
ax_patrol_peace03: Nothing for a while. Hope it stays that way.
ax_patrol_peace04: All peaceful at the moment. Don’t get too comfortable, though. Thargoids won’t give us much warning.
ax_patrol_peace05: Ever feel like it’s too quiet? I mean, we know they’re in the system...
ax_patrol_peace06: Wake me up when the bugs arrive, yeah? I signed up for combat.
ax_patrol_peace07: No Thargoid activity in the area. Will start another sweep.
ax_patrol_peace08: Interceptors are going to show up any minute now. I can feel it.
ax_patrol_peace09: Not much worth mentioning on this patrol. Got a Commander in the area, though.
ax_patrol_peace10: If a Thargoid arrives now we’ll have some backup. Right, Commander?
ax_thargoidarrival_timer01: Energy surge detected. Here they come!
ax_thargoidarrival_timer02: Looks like they’re bringing the fight to us. Thargoids inbound!
ax_thargoidarrival_timer03: Bugs are warping into the area. Move to engage.
ax_thargoidarrival_timer04: Seems the xenos took notice of us. Deploying hardpoints.
ax_thargoidarrival_timer05: Thargoids spotted. This is gonna get ugly!
ax_thargoidarrival_timer06: We’ve got Thargoids converging on our position.
ax_thargoidarrival_timer07: Thargoids dropping into view. Time to earn our pay – get onto them!
ax_thargoidarrival_timer08: Well, that didn’t take so long. Warm up those weapons – we got Thargoids on us!
ax_thargoidarrival_timer09: Thargoids are coming for us. Let’s make ‘em regret trying.
ax_thargoidarrival_timer10: Oh crap, here we go! Thargoids are coming straight for us!
ax_thargoidarrival_trigger01: Well, that got their attention. Thargoids inbound!
ax_thargoidarrival_trigger02: Whatever you did, you’ve annoyed the Thargs. Heads up, here they come!
ax_thargoidarrival_trigger03: Now you’ve done it. Picking up a Thargoid energy surge!
ax_thargoidarrival_trigger04: Thargoid ships are approaching – whatever you did, they didn’t like it.
ax_thargoidarrival_trigger05: Got some Thargoid activity on my radar. Can’t be a coincidence, something drew them in. Look out!
ax_thargoidpresent_engaged01: Glad you could make it, Commander – give us a hand with these bugs?
ax_thargoidpresent_engaged02: We’ve got a situation here, need all the help we can get!
ax_thargoidpresent_engaged03: Gotta push these xenos back, with everything we’ve got!
ax_thargoidpresent_engaged04: Congrats, Commander – you're the backup. Thargoids are giving us a rough time.
ax_thargoidpresent_engaged05: We might be in trouble without some help, Commander. Sure hope you're equipped for xeno hunting.
ax_thargoidretreat01: The bugs are pulling out! We showed 'em who rules this system!
ax_thargoidretreat02: Look at them go! Get back to your holes, you stupid insects!
ax_thargoidretreat03: Thargoids are retreating. Repeat: Thargoids are retreating!
ax_thargoidretreat04: I think the Thargoids are withdrawing. We've won this one!
ax_thargoidretreat05: We did it! The Thargoids are running, haha! Chew on that, xenos!
ax_thargoidretreat06: Thargoids are leaving the area. Victory is ours! Well done!
ax_thargoidretreat07: The xenos are fleeing! They'll think twice before coming back here… right?
ax_thargoidretreat08: The bugs are bravely running away! Don't forget what happens when you mess with the best.
ax_thargoidretreat09: Looks like the Thargoids are retreating. Good work, everyone.
ax_thargoidretreat10: What's the matter? Too much firepower for you? Get lost, Thargs.
ax_titan_combatgeneric01: Pick your targets. Don't fly off on your own!
ax_titan_combatgeneric02: Trust your eyes and ears, people. Scopes aren't much use in here.
ax_titan_combatgeneric03: If you get a lock on a Thargoid, blast it. No second chances.
ax_titan_combatgeneric04: Don't stray too close to the turrets. Those things will burn your down quick.
ax_titan_combatgeneric05: The Thargoids don't know how many of their ships I've put down so far… right?
ax_titan_combatgeneric06: Stay clear of turret fire. If the Titan starts charging its Torus weapon, get out of here.
ax_titan_combatgeneric07: If anything alien appears in front of you, blast it.
ax_titan_combatgeneric08: This is revenge for all the people you took from us!
ax_titan_combatgeneric09: We're getting closer to victory. Keep fighting!
ax_titan_combatgeneric10: Keep fighting the Thargoids with everything you have. This is for humanity!
ax_titan_combatunderattack01: This is too much! I'm never gonna make it out of here!
ax_titan_combatunderattack02: I'm taking fire! Can anybody help me out?
ax_titan_combatunderattack03: Taking damage. It's not looking good.
ax_titan_combatunderattack04: Oh damn it, one of the bugs has a lock on me!
ax_titan_combatunderattack05: A Thargoid has taken an interest in me. Under fire.
ax_titan_coreexposed01: Got eyes on the heat core. Who's on it?
ax_titan_coreexposed02: Keep the Thargoids occupied while the Titan's vulnerable!
ax_titan_coreexposed03: Take out the heat core to kill this monster. Keep to the plan.
ax_titan_coreexposed05: The sabotaged heat vents are giving us our chance. Protect any Commanders in the area.
ax_titan_coreexposed06: This is our chance. We're hitting them hard, keep at it!
ax_titan_coreexposed07: Let the heat core have everything you have, all hardpoints!
ax_titan_coreexposed08: Don't give the Titan a chance to recover. Destroy that heat core.
ax_titan_coreexposed09: Empty your weapons into that heat core, Commanders!
ax_titan_coreexposed10: Damage that core enough and we can put this Titan down for good.
ax_titan_patrol_peace01: Look at the size of that thing.
ax_titan_patrol_peace02: We're supposed to survive that? Are you kidding me?
ax_titan_patrol_peace03: They better be paying us overtime to take the Thargoid fleet down.
ax_titan_patrol_peace05: These xenos don't know what's coming. Let's give 'em hell.
ax_titan_patrol_peace06: Get ready, everyone. This isn't going to be an easy fight.
ax_titan_patrol_peace07: Y'all ready to take these insects down?
ax_titan_patrol_peace08: Xenos made a mistake sending this thing into our space.
ax_titan_patrol_peace09: People will talk about this event for years to come. Make sure we don't fail them.
ax_titan_patrol_peace10: You've all been briefed on the mission. Stick together, stay focused, come home.
ax_titan_titanventing01: Gotta sabotage the heat vents if we're gonna survive this encounter.
ax_titan_titanventing02: Target the heat vents with nanite torpedoes!
ax_titan_titanventing03: The plan is to make the Titans run hot. Close up those heat vents.
ax_titan_titanventing04: The torpedoes Palin and Ram Tah cooked up should shut the vents down.
ax_titan_titanventing05: If we disrupt the heat vents the Titan will expose its core.

bakedgreebles_info:
These tough, limpet like creatures were originally thought to be inedible. However, pioneering colonists discovered that a combination of high pressure and chemical treatment in an ammonia-based solution could render these iron rich creatures into a digestible and delicious food source. They are now considered a delicacy around their galaxy.

This rare good is legal in all markets.

baltahsinevacuumkrill_info:
Vacuum Krill are astonishing creatures. One of the few species to live in the hard vacuum of space, they are native to the ice rings around Baltah'sine 4b. Their eggs grow in vast numbers in tiny water pockets within the rocks - kept liquid by secretions from the mother when the eggs are first laid. When mature, they eventually burrow their way out, propelling themselves between rocks with tiny excretions of fluid, in search of a mate.

This rare good is legal in all markets.
baltahsinevacuumkrill_info_short: Vacuum Krill are astonishing creatures. They are native to the ice rings around Baltah'sine 4b.

bastnasite_info:
Produced by: Surface Mining only
Consumed by: High Tech, Industrial and Refinery

Chemical formula (La, Ce, Y)CO3F. Bastnasite is a scarce mineral and never in great concentrations. It typically takes the form of a honey-yellow or reddish brown crystals. Bastnasite ore is commonly used to produce rare-earth metals and for use in advanced electronics.
bastnasite_info_short: Produced by: Surface Mining only Consumed by: High Tech, Industrial and Refinery Bastnasite ore is commonly used to produce rare-earth metals and for use in advanced electronics.

Traditional cure-all and cocktail ingredient. The venom of the snake entombed in the bottle adds to the intoxicating effect of the drink.

This rare good is legal in all markets except for Prison Colony markets and Federal and Allied Theocracy markets.

Please note that if a market’s controlling faction changes, some formerly legal rare goods may become illegal. Should this occur the rare good will be unavailable for sale or purchase at that market for the duration of the prohibiting faction’s tenure.

Due to the particular chemical conditions of the water on Belalans, the rays have a particularly soft skin.

borasetanipathogenetics_info:
These tiny crawling creatures have been called 'a lab in a bag'. They exude tailored biological agents that adapt and mutate to overcome the defences of their enemies. When deployed in large numbers they resemble a viscous yellow goo that slowly crawls over the victim, devouring them completely. When there are no further nutrients to absorb, the insects will become dormant, and can be recovered by specially trained teams to be used again.

This rare good is legal in all Dictatorship markets; Independent and Allied Communist markets; and Federal and Imperial Confederacy markets. It is prohibited in all other markets.

Please note that if a market’s controlling faction changes, some formerly legal rare goods may become illegal. Should this occur the rare good will be unavailable for sale or purchase at that market for the duration of the prohibiting faction’s tenure.

brand_coredynamics_description:
'Unmatched interstellar supremacy.'

Core Dynamics is one of the galaxy's premier manufacturers of starships, with a particular focus on combat vessels. Its product line ranges from the compact Eagle to the gargantuan Farragut-class Battlecruiser. The company maintains a long-standing supply agreement with the Federation, and is responsible for the Federal Assault Ship, Corvette, Dropship and Gunship.
brand_faulcondelacy_description:
'Bridging the stars for half a millennium.'

One of the most enduring and successful corporations in history, Faulcon deLacy is responsible for three of the most recognisable ships ever released: the Sidewinder, Cobra and Viper. The company also pioneered the now-standard modular system of ship design that allows pilots to upgrade and replace components with ease. Today, Faulcon deLacy is regularly lauded by critics and customers alike for its dedication to quality.
brand_gutamaya_description:
'Effortless elegance.'

As a company founded by the Empire, Gutamaya’s remit today still matches the original vision: to produce a line of ships that combine functional excellence with a distinct visual style. As such, the Gutamaya range is considered to embody Imperial opulence and are instantly recognisable for their sleek contours and distinctive silhouettes. The company enjoys a rewarding supply agreement with the Imperial navy, which includes its nimble take on the Eagle and the widely admired Cutter.
brand_kinematicarmaments_description:
'Conquer All.'

Defence industry veteran Kinematic Armaments is the galaxy’s largest producer of ballistic weaponry. Founded in 3240, the company maximises output while minimising production costs, using a business model seen as monopolistic by some critics. Yet their firearms remain wildly popular and are often used by security forces across colonised space.
brand_lakon_description:
'Hard-working ships for hard-working people.'

Lakon Spaceways specialises in sturdy vessels for cargo haulage and deep-space exploration. It has a longer pedigree than most other ship manufacturers, with its first dedicated transport vessel built on Earth in the 26th Century. The company is currently partnered with the Alliance to produce military vessels capable of countering the Thargoid threat; this has so far resulted in the Type-10 Defender and the Crusader designs, among others.
brand_manticore_description:
'Finish the Fight.'

Established in 2990, Manticore was for many years associated solely with ship-based technology, making a name for itself as a manufacturer of cannons, missiles and limpets. In recent years the company widened its remit to encompass personal defence. Manticore’s successful range of plasma-based weaponry has cemented its reputation for quality designs and smart leadership.
brand_remlok_description:
'Above All, Survive.'

Remlok is the galaxy’s largest manufacturer of space suits. Led by CEO Sebastien Croix, it is noted for its employee-centric ethos, which offers workers generous benefits and competitive wages. Perhaps unsurprisingly given the company’s commitment to fair treatment, it is vocally opposed to slavery. Such overt principles inspire much discussion but never overshadow Remlok’s dedication to excellence.
brand_saudkruger_description:
'The finest, for the best.'

Saud Kruger is best known for luxurious passenger liners such as the Beluga, Dolphin and Orca. Exquisite Goldskin leather has been used in the interiors of Saud Kruger ships for years, and is part of the company's distinctive aesthetic. The company also competes in the field of interstellar mapping and deep-space exploration, and likes to emphasise the danger and glamour of exploring. Its vessels are suited to completing such journeys with paying passengers.
brand_supratech_description:
'Innovation in Everything'

Despite its comparative youth, Supratech is one of the galaxy’s preeminent technology companies, its rapid ascent having earned it both the admiration and envy of its competitors. A series of personal computing devices cemented it as a serious contender on the tech scene. This was soon followed by the Artemis suit which has proven a big hit with explorers.
brand_takada_description:
'Harmonious by Design'

Initially started as a haulage corporation, Takada's dominance of the industry left their shipments vulnerable to pirate attacks. Rather than relying on mainstream weapons for defence, Ronan Takada tasked the company's engineers with developing concepts for personal laser weapons. These prototypes debuted to mass defence industry acclaim, resulting in the Takada corporation's decision to transition out of haulage to personal defence production.
brand_zorgonpeterson_description:
'Where finesse follows function.'

A subsidiary of Faulcon deLacy since 3126, Zorgon Peterson established its reputation with freighter and exploration vehicles that are popular among pilot freelancers. In recent years, there has been a noted evolution of the company’s hardy and practical designs, hallmarks present in the Hauler and Adder ships. The revitalised Fer-de-Lance saw a sleeker vessel with additional maneuverability, while the Mamba’s stunning aesthetic has been well received by critics.

chameleoncloth_info:
Woven from living plants, the fabric created retains the native Flora's sympathetic camouflage. When worn, the user will blend in with whatever their current environment is. This rare good is legal in all markets.

chat_help:
Communication System v3.3.
Available Channels and Commands:

/l, /local - Local space.
/sy, /system - Current star system.
/w, /wing - Wing.
/mc, /multicrew - Multi-crew.
/vc /voice - Text message to voice chat.
/s, /squadron - Squadron.
/sl - Squadron Leaders (if accessible).
/r, /reply - Replies to recent Direct messages.
/d [name], /direct, /to - Send a message to [name].
/t, /target - Direct message your current target.

/clear - Clear the current tab's messages.
/help - Displays this information.

Channels may be displayed in the main panel, tabbed, or hidden. Change these at any time in the Comms settings tab.

chateaudeaegaeon_info:
Wines from Aegaeon are some of the most valued and prized possessions in the galaxy. In great demand in wealthy systems, these wines are purchased for large sums, but rarely actually drunk.

This rare good is legal in all markets except for Prison Colony markets and Federal Theocracy markets.

Please note that if a market’s controlling faction changes, some formerly legal rare goods may become illegal. Should this occur the rare good will be unavailable for sale or purchase at that market for the duration of the prohibiting faction’s tenure.

cobramkiii_info:
A true multipurpose ship, the Cobra Mk III can fit comfortably into a range of roles. In combat it can hit hard and – if necessary – make a swift exit, while its spacious cargo hold allows it to carry more than other ships of similar price and size. The Cobra is also a solid choice for explorers, boasting an ample fuel tank and six internal compartments.

The Cobra Mk III has been designed for small-size landing pads.

A development of the versatile Cobra Mk III, the Cobra Mk IV has been designed primarily with combat in mind. Its hardpoint placement, damage output and armour make it a formidable combat ship, able to hold its own even against larger vessels. These features come at a cost, however, making the Mk IV slower and less agile than the Mk III.

The Cobra Mk IV has been designed for small-size landing pads.

A multi-purpose vessel, the Mk V offers impressive exploration, trade and combat role performance for its size and price point. codex_ent_a_types_desc: A type stars are hot white or bluish-white main sequence stars. They usually range in mass from 1.4 to 2.1 solar masses and have a surface temperature reaching 10,000 K.
codex_ent_a_typesupergiant_desc: A blue-white supergiant star that is approaching the end of its life. Hydrogen burning has stopped in its core and the star has begun expanding towards being a red supergiant.
codex_ent_aebe_types_desc: Herbig Ae/Be stars are young stars typically less than 10 million years old, with characteristics of either class A or B main sequence stars. They are usually between 2 and 8 solar masses. The mass of the proto-star determines its spectral class when it joins the main sequence.
codex_ent_aleoids_01_desc: This aleoida species has upright clumps of long serrated leaves, which can open up to expose a reproductive organ containing tiny round seeds.
codex_ent_aleoids_02_desc: This interleaved crown of mottled leaves can grow to head height, with explosive seed pods emerging on long protruding stalks.
codex_ent_aleoids_03_desc: An aleoida species with long spiky leaves that can reach over two metres high, surrounding a single reproductive organ on a long central stalk.
codex_ent_aleoids_04_desc: These aleoida have a circle of upturned leaves marked with patterns, surrounding a bright fleshy pod with darker markings which matures in their centre.
codex_ent_aleoids_05_desc: These aleoida's wide flat leaves on a heavy bark base can reach huge sizes, and sprout a dome-shaped reproductive organ at their peak.
codex_ent_aleoids_genus_desc:
Extremely hardy photosynthetic organisms that thrive in arid environments. Thick, waxy leaf structures protect them from extreme surroundings. When gaseous exchange becomes unfavourable, the leaves can completely shut off the organism from the atmosphere, causing a state of hibernation. The pointed leaves create precipitation slopes, which draw liquids to the heart of the organism. Here they are absorbed through a series of specialised cells, and stored in the root structure until needed.

Clonal Colony Range: 150m
codex_ent_ammonia_worlds_desc: A terrestrial ammonia planet with an active ammonia-based chemistry and carbon-ammonia-based life.
codex_ent_ancient_casket_desc: An artefact created several million years ago by the Guardians, an extinct nonhuman civilisation.
