No sooner was the bomb in place then Voss detonated it, annihilating her rivals in a single stroke.

Voss had realised that her competitors, for all their brutality, were bound by a simple code of honour. To them, the use of extreme tactics such as suicide bombers was unthinkable. And that gave her a clear advantage.

In the decades that followed, the Consortium’s expansion continued unopposed, the fear of extreme retaliation keeping rival criminal organisations in line. Indeed, potential competitors quickly realised it was smarter to side with the Coalition than against it, which allowed the organisation to assimilate dozens of smaller criminal enterprises.

It is not known if Catelyn Voss still controls the Consortium, or even if she is still alive. Some rumours assert that she spent much of her personal fortune on progenitor cells, allowing her to artificially extend her life and maintain control of her criminal empire. Others insist that she has retired, and is now living a life of quiet anonymity in a remote corner of space. Still others opine that Voss is long dead, and that control of the Consortium passed to one of her lieutenants many years ago. The truth may never be known.

Efforts on the part of law enforcement to topple the Consortium have been largely unsuccessful. The organisation is now so large that Omnipol can do little more than chip away at the margins. Ironically, many of the organisation’s most senior figures are believed to have segued into legitimate business, leading intelligence agencies to theorise that those at the top of the Consortium may, to all outward appearance, be law-abiding citizens. Only the capture of the Consortium’s leader – whoever that may be – could threaten its dominion.
codex_knowledgebase_theconsortium_precis: An overview of the Consortium, a notable crime syndicate.

codex_pilotshandbook_bountyhunter_advequ: FRAME SHIFT DRIVE INTERDICTOR Optional Internal
Attempts to pull target ships out of supercruise, rendering them vulnerable to scanning and combat. The effective interdiction range is determined by the module's class and rating.
FRAME SHIFT WAKE SCANNER Utility Slot
Analyses the frame shift wake generated by ships which have recently entered hyperspace, revealing their destination system.
codex_pilotshandbook_bountyhunter_advfli: Flight assist is an onboard computer that restricts flight parameters, simulating how a ship behaves when flown in an atmosphere. This makes the ship easier to operate for pilots unfamiliar with the physics of flight in zero gravity.

The default setting is flight assist on. However, some pilots opt to deactivate flight assist during combat, in order to increase a ship's turn rate. Flight assist can be toggled on and off using $BINDING_input_either:#value=TOGGLEFLIGHTASSIST; or via the control options.
When flight assist is deactivated, the speed and rotation of a vessel are dependent on the pilot manually employing thrust and counter-thrust to maintain control.
Although flying becomes less intuitive, deactivation of flight assist grants pilots the ability to perform advanced manoeuvres that can achieve superiority during combat.
codex_pilotshandbook_bountyhunter_basicc: To use a weapon or module, it must be assigned to a fire group. Fire groups allow fast movement between customised hardpoint configurations. For example, one fire group may be set to deploy weapons, while another fire group operates scanners. You can select the next fire group using $BINDING_input_either:#value=CYCLEFIREGROUPNEXT;.

Hardpoints can be assigned to either primary or secondary fire. This allows each fire group to have two triggers.

For example, a fire group may be configured so that a ship's beam weapons are fired with the primary trigger, while missiles are launched with the secondary trigger.

Some combat-related modules set in utility mounts, such as scanners and chaff launchers, can also be assigned to primary or secondary fire.
All ships have a number of hardpoints, which are mounting positions on the hull for weapons and modules. Hardpoints come in four sizes:

• Class 1 – Small
• Class 2 – Medium
• Class 3 – Large
• Class 4 – Huge

Alongside hardpoints, all ships contain a number of utility mounts. These can be used to install additional devices, such as scanners and chaff launchers.
Weapons can be one of three different types:

• Fixed: The weapon fires straight forward with minimal target tracking. Fixed weapons generally do the most damage and are unaffected by chaff. • Gimbal: The weapon has limited movement and is able to track targets within a limited arc, increasing accuracy. Gimballed weapons offer standard damage output but can be countered with chaff. • Turret: The weapon has full rotational movement and tracks targets autonomously, with predetermined settings available in the Functions menu. Turreted weapons have the lowest damage output and can be countered with chaff.

When a hardpoint is deployed, it emerges from a compartment within the ship's hull in preparation for use. When a hardpoint is retracted, it is withdrawn back into the compartment.
Deployed weapons and modules provide a targeting reticule in the centre of the weapon brackets. This can be used to track targets and determine when to fire.
Weapons can be bound to automatically deploy when a trigger is used, rather than manually deploying the hardpoint(s) first.
It is good practice to retract hardpoints when in the vicinity of a starport, to prevent accidental fire zone infractions. All hardpoints must be retracted prior to entering supercruise.

Targeting $BINDING_input_either:#value=SELECTTARGET; allows the ship computer to track the position and status of an object. This is done by manually targeting once within range $BINDING_input_either:#value=SELECTTARGET;.

When an object is within your targeting reticule, you can lock into it manually. Alternatively, you can select a target from the Contacts tab on the External interface panel. This adds a marker to the target on your scanner display and provides some basic information about the target. Only a single object can be targeted at a time.
codex_pilotshandbook_bountyhunter_basice: Provides a ship with the firepower needed to destroy opposing ships.
Forms a protective energy shield around the vessel, which continually regenerates while powered.
Scans a ship for any outstanding bounties posted by any jurisdiction in the galaxy.
Scans an individual for any outstanding warrants.
codex_pilotshandbook_bountyhunter_interd: Interdiction is the act of locking onto another ship's supercruise vector and forcing them to disengage the frame shift drive. This is a useful technique bounty hunters can use to ambush wanted ships, or pull targets out of supercruise for closer inspection with a Kill Warrant Scanner.

The Frame Shift Interdictor is required to perform this action. The module must be assigned to a fire group and triggered when behind and in range of a target. When interdiction begins the HUD gains two new elements, an escape vector and alignment progress bars.

To win the interdiction you must keep the escape vector aligned with the centre of the HUD, the longer the escape vector stays in this position the more the blue progress bar grows. If the red bar hits maximum the target ship will escape. If the blue progress bar hits maximum your ship and the target ship will be dragged out of supercruise. The target ship will have to wait for their frame shift drive to reboot before they can escape back into supercruise.

Bounty hunters do risk fines for interdicting clean ships, however. Even if the hunter knows that a target has outstanding bounties, interdicting a ship not flagged as wanted in the current system is considered a hostile act by system authorities.

When this occurs filling the blue bar will allow you to escape being interdicted. Should the red bar fill first you will be pulled out of supercruise instead. You can submit to the interdiction by reducing your throttle to zero. Doing this will drastically decrease the amount of time you must wait for your FSD to reboot.
codex_pilotshandbook_bountyhunter_intfac:
Bounty vouchers can be redeemed via Interstellar Factors, regardless of where the bounty was issued - the monetary reward will however receive a deduction of roughly 25%. 

Stations at which Interstellar Factors are present can be found as follows:
• Open the Galaxy Map from the External interface panel • Select the Map Mode tab • Choose the Services overlay from the provided options • Here you can filter for Interstellar Factors
Interstellar Factors are most commonly found in low security systems. They are known to appear in medium security and anarchy systems also.
codex_pilotshandbook_bountyhunter_introd: Bounty hunters track down and destroy wanted individuals in exchange for bounty vouchers, which can be redeemed for credits. Using specific scanners and tools, bounty hunters can identify outstanding warrants and pursue outlaws attempting to avoid justice.

Commanders can hand in bounty vouchers to the Administrative Contact, found in the Starport Services menu or via terminals, at any starport or surface facility where the faction issuing the bounty is present. Alternatively, vouchers for any faction can be handed in to any Interstellar Factor for a percentage fee. Those looking for bounty hunting work should pay attention to the following mission types: • Onslaught, where a faction requires a number of enemy ships are destroyed. • Raid, where a criminal faction's members are engaged at surface locations. • Assassination, which offers a specific target which must be taken out within a set time frame and may require some tracking to locate.
codex_pilotshandbook_bountyhunter_precis: How to bring criminals to justice in a dangerous galaxy.
codex_pilotshandbook_bountyhunter_proces: Bounty hunters operate across inhabited space, and occasionally outside of it. Wherever pirates, smugglers and other outlaws are found, bounty hunters are likely to find targets to engage. Often it is worthwhile following similar paths as the pirates themselves: busy trade routes, navigation beacons and resource extraction sites can offer lucrative hunting grounds. Criminal factions may occupy settlements, while scavengers will often seek out crash sites or prowl for easy targets on a planet's surface.

Finding criminals Any pilot can use the default scanner to identify whether a ship is wanted in the current system. Bounties outside of the local jurisdiction are not shown by the basic scanner however, and must instead be identified with a Kill Warrant Scanner. This is particularly useful when in Anarchy systems, where bounties are not issued locally but the inhabitants will likely be wanted in other jurisdictions.

It can be valuable to perform a kill warrant scan on a ship for which a local bounty is revealed in a basic scan. This may increase the bounty value of a ship wanted in the current system, or flag up additional bounties posted in other jurisdictions.

Attacking a ship which has committed no crimes in the current system is illegal everywhere except in anarchic systems, regardless of the presence of other bounties. Bounty hunters who bring down outlaws may incur a bounty themselves as a result. Paying these bounties off at an Interstellar Factor is the safest, easiest way of removing these bounties.

For surface-based bounty hunting, scanning an individual with the profile analyser will reveal any outstanding warrants. Identifying a wanted target gives the bounty hunter the legal authority to take them down. But be careful - a wanted target will respond aggressively if they catch you scanning them. See the Profile Analyser page of the Suit Equipment guide for more information.
Unidentified Signal Sources Pirate activity is often associated with the following signal types:

• Distress Call
• Weapons Fire
• Pirate Activity Detected (in systems in the Lockdown state)
• Combat Aftermath Detected
• Convoy Dispersal Pattern Detected

Signal sources come with a threat level reading. The higher this level, the greater the risk estimated at the signal.

Planetary Signal Sources Scavengers may be active at multiple surface signals, seeking to take advantage of wreckage or stranded vehicles. These signal types also carry a threat level. Scavenger activity is often associated with the following types:

• Crash/Impact Site
• Distress Beacon
• Irregular Markers
• Combat Aftermath Detected
• Minor Wreckage
codex_pilotshandbook_bountyhunter_redeem: Upon destruction of a wanted target, the total value of any and all outstanding bounties will be assigned to the Commander responsible in the form of a bounty voucher. These vouchers grant credit rewards when redeemed at any administrative office where the issuing faction is present.
Small Bounties Small bounties are placed by jurisdiction, and are not galaxy wide. As such only the faction which issued the bounty will honour the credits offered for them. So, as an example:

• A bounty hunter destroys an outlaw with two outstanding bounties; one with Faction A, another with Faction B.
• Faction A owns a station in the current system. The bounty voucher issued by this faction can be redeemed at that station.
• Faction B is present in a neighbouring system only, however. The bounty hunter will need to travel to this system to hand in the second bounty voucher.

Interstellar Bounties If a criminal builds up to 10,000 cr worth of bounties with minor factions aligned to a specific superpower, it will be upgraded to an interstellar bounty. This greatly increases the territory in which the bounty can be legally claimed. For example:

• A pirate has an interstellar bounty with the Federation. This allows a bounty hunter to intercept, attack and destroy that pirate anywhere in Federal territory.
• The bounty voucher acquired can then be handed in to any station where the controlling faction is aligned with the Federation.
codex_pilotshandbook_bountyhunter_surfac: Combatants engage on a planet’s surface using hand-held weaponry, protected by the shielding and armour of their suits.

Removed from the many ship functions available to combat pilots, surface combatants must instead rely on their mobility and accuracy. Personal weapons are not gimballed, targets are not autonomously tracked and there are no fire groups to set.  Instead, the use of cover, suit radar awareness and health management become key skills in surviving a firefight.

Equipment A variety of weapons, suits and consumable extras are available. Combat-focused Commanders should consider the Manticore Dominator suit for its extra weapon options and survivability. See the Suit Equipment guide for more information.

Surface Recon Vehicles, or SRVs, are also useful vehicles for surface combat. They offer additional protection and manoeuvrability along with a mounted turret, but can be vulnerable to explosive damage and higher grades of weapons.
codex_pilotshandbook_bountyhunter_weapon: There are four hardpoint types: Thermal, Kinetic, Thermal-Kinetic and Explosive. These types have various strengths and weaknesses, with some more suited to certain situations than others.

Thermal Weapons Thermal weapons require no ammunition, but they do use a capacitor charge provided by the ship's power plant. If this charge is spent, it must be recharged to allow the weapon to continue firing. These weapons are the most effective means of stripping away shields but are less successful against hulls. A common tactic is to deploy thermal weapons to remove a target's shield prior to using kinetic weapons against its hull. Examples of thermal weapons include beam lasers, pulse lasers and burst lasers. A mining laser is also capable of delivering damage to a ship but is not designed for combat.

Kinetic Weapons Kinetic weapons require ammunition to function, but consume less energy and produce less heat than thermal weapons. They are the most efficient means of damaging a target ship's hull but are less effective against shields. Examples of kinetic weapons include multi-cannons and fragment cannons. Ammunition can be replenished at stations or synthesised.

Thermal-Kinetic Weapons Thermal-kinetic weapons are capable of dealing very high damage to both a target's shield and hull. They require both ammunition and energy and produce a lot of heat. Examples of thermal-kinetic weapons include railguns and plasma accelerators. Ammunition can be replenished at stations or synthesised.

Explosive Weapons Explosive weapons require ammunition and produce a large amount of heat when fired. However, they consume little energy and are capable of dealing high damage to a target's hull. Examples of explosive weapons include missile racks, torpedo pylons and mine launchers. Missiles come in two types:

• Dumbfire, which shoot directly forward immediately after firing and impact with full damage. • Seeker, which will lock onto a target and follow their trajectory, but require several seconds to establish a lock and impact with slightly less damage.
codex_pilotshandbook_crime_bounties_desc: Bounties can then relate to three further criteria:

Interstellar bounties Issued when fines and bounties for factions aligned within a superpower pass 10,000 cr or more. They are valid in any jurisdiction governed by that superpower or any of their associated minor factions.

Power bounties Issued for Powerplay related crimes. They do not affect starport services access and are only valid in Powerplay-specific scenarios. For example, if your Power bounty is with Denton Patreus, then you will only be flagged as wanted in systems owned by that Power.

Pilots' Federation bounties Issued for crimes against other Commanders. This bounty is valid in all jurisdictions that are not classified as lawless or anarchies. Due to repeated incidents of licensed Commanders engaging in open combat, the Pilots' Federation has also introduced a ship rebuy penalty for members that destroy each other. This penalty is calculated based on the cost of the ship used to perpetrate the crime.

Should a Commander commit the crime of murder against a fellow Commander, their ship insurance rebuy cost will always be at least the cost of the ship used to commit the crime - assuming the rebuy occurs in a starport controlled by the faction that issued the bounty. 

If an insurance rebuy is less expensive than the ship used to commit the crime, the Commander will be faced with an additional ship rebuy penalty. The amount of this penalty will be the difference between your current ship's rebuy and the rebuy of the ship used to commit the crime. If multiple ships were used to destroy other Commanders, then the most expensive one will be used in this calculation.
codex_pilotshandbook_crime_detention_des:
These huge megaships were created to process pilots caught while trying to evade the law. If a Commander is found to have outstanding fines or bounties following a scan then they will be transferred to a detention centre if defeated in combat.

Here, detainees will be forced to pay off all outstanding fines and bounties in that jurisdiction. If the pilot cannot afford to do so then they must select the default Sidewinder loadout before being allowed to leave.

Hand Yourself In A wanted criminal can hand themselves in to the Administrative Contact via starport services or a concourse terminal, providing they have an outstanding bounty and a Notoriety rating of zero. This option will pay off the bounty and result in deportation to the nearest detention centre. Power bounties are issued instead of normal bounties for Powerplay activities. The Kill Warrant Scanner detects all standard bounties and can grant a license to kill if the faction that issued the bounty is aligned to the same superpower as the faction controlling the jurisdiction.
codex_pilotshandbook_crime_finesbounties: The punishment for committing crimes fall into one of two criteria:

Minor violations in the law result in fines, which are credit penalties placed against you.

Outstanding fines restrict access to the services of any starport, outpost or planetary port owned by the issuing faction.

Bounties are issued for major violations of the law. While consisting of a credit penalty similar to fines, they carry a significant added consequence: an active bounty makes you a legal target within the jurisdiction of the issuing faction.

Bounties apply to jurisdictions. A target may have an outstanding bounty, but if that bounty is not valid for the jurisdiction they reside in then attacking them is considered a hostile act. Ships wanted in the current jurisdiction will be identified as wanted.
Multi-crew Committing a crime in another pilot's ship via multi-crew will apply a fine or bounty to your most valuable ship.
Duration Fines never mature into bounties, while bounties never become dormant or expire.
codex_pilotshandbook_crime_hotships_desc: When a crime is committed in a ship, that ship is considered 'hot'. Hot ships have some additional rules relating to their management:

• If modules are removed from a hot ship into storage, they must be cleaned individually - at 5% of their rebuy cost - before being transferred to a clean ship.

• Hot modules in storage will not be cleaned along with a ship when paying off incurred legal fees, potentially creating costs greater than a low-value fine/bounty.

• Hot ships can be cleaned at Interstellar Factors if your Notoriety is at zero.

• Hot ships can be sold for a significantly reduced profit if necessary.

• Paying off any outstanding bounties at an Interstellar Factor will clean all hot ships.

Impounding If you are placed in a detention centre all hot ships will be impounded at the same location. Impounded ships cannot be accessed or transferred until a release fee is paid. A hot ship that is destroyed immediately before incarceration is not impounded but must have its rebuy fee paid. If you do not have enough credits to release any impounded ships then a free Sidewinder will be provided by the detention centre.
codex_pilotshandbook_crime_introduction_: With humanity spread through so many systems, it was essential to create a way of enforcing the law of each respective government efficiently. Criminal acts are reported by ships, stations and settlements automatically, with fines and bounties registered by the local authorities. These must be paid off in due time, particularly bounties; a pilot with a price on their head will not go unnoticed for long.
codex_pilotshandbook_crime_notoriety_des:
When an individual commits the act of murder, their Notoriety increases. Each additional murder after the first increase the value of the bounty against them.

The notoriety rating increases by one unit with each kill, up to a maximum of ten. Like fines and bounties, Notoriety is applied to the perpetrator, not the ship. The higher the notoriety, the greater the bounty associated with them.

If a highly notorious Commander defeats a clean Commander, the victim's rebuy cost is decreased.

Notoriety decreases one unit every two hours of play when obeying the law. Notoriety does decay while docked, but the rating will not update in the Statistics panel until the Commander undocks and initiates an FSD jump. 

Notoriety must be at 0 before an Interstellar Factor will accept payments to wipe outstanding bounties.

Advance Tactical Response (ATR) A notorious Commander who continues to commit ship-based crimes in a jurisdiction will attract the attention of an Advanced Tactical Response team. The ATR consists of heavily armed security ships, designed to counter dangerous criminals of high notoriety. Their orders are simple: to intercept and destroy an assigned target within their jurisdiction.
codex_pilotshandbook_crime_offenses_desc: Below is a list of criminal offences, their triggers and the type of punishment they incur. Fines and bounties are assigned to the perpetrator. These penalties persist when changing ships or disembarking.

Murder Bounty, Notoriety Gain • Destroying a clean, occupied ship through weapons fire or collision. • Killing an individual using personal weapons. Assault Bounty • Damaging a clean ship with weapons fire (when targeted). • Damaging an individual using personal weapons. • Attaching a limpet to a ship's cargo hatch or external fixing without authorisation. Theft/Piracy Bounty • Illegally obtaining cargo/data from a cargo bay/data link. • Visually detected taking settlement property by the owning faction. Carrying Illegal goods Fine • Having stolen or prohibited items in the cargo hold or suit inventory when scanned.

Weapons Violation – No Fire Zone Fine • Discharging weapons in a no fire zone. Weapons Violation – Docking Area Bounty • Discharging weapons in a docking area. Loitering Bounty • Positioning a ship over a non-assigned landing pad, or blocking a starport's access corridor. Illegal dumping Fine • Jettisoning cargo within a set boundary, such as in the vicinity of a starport.

Trespassing Bounty • Being detected in a trespass zone. • Entering a starport without docking permission. Reckless weapons discharge Fine • Discharging weapons against a ship you have not targeted. • Discharging personal weapons in an operational settlement. Detection of a weapon Fine • Observed holding a personal weapon in an operational settlement. Breaking and Entering Bounty • Visually detected overcharging a charge port or cutting access panels in an operational settlement. Failure to Submit to Scan Fine • Fleeing from a faction guard or Omnipol scan attempt.
codex_pilotshandbook_crime_omnipol_descr: While Advanced Tactical Response units are dispatched to hunt down notorious pilots in deep space, ground operations belong to Omnipol. This highly respected law enforcement organisation specialises in maintaining order at and around settlements. Omnipol agents are expertly trained, well equipped and lethal in combat.

Omnipol reacts to escalating combat and may arrive to reinforce faction guards. High-security systems are more likely to call in Omnipol agents when needed.

Criminals with large bounties in their current jurisdiction may attract the attention of Omnipol agents, as they carry out searches for known criminals with outstanding warrants.
codex_pilotshandbook_crime_precis: A guide to the laws of the galaxy.
codex_pilotshandbook_engineers_equipment: <font size='16' color='#f8f8f8'>AN ENGINEERS EQUIPMENT MODIFICATION SCREEN</font>

Speaking to the engineer will display the engineer’s profile and the modifications they offer, along with any requested donations. You will be asked whether you wish to modify suits or weapon. Donations can also be made here.

Selecting an equipment choice will bring up the Engineer Modifications screen. Here you can select the item you want to work on. Equipment has up to four mod slots, which are listed on the right side of the screen.  An empty mod slot is required to accommodate a modification.

With the suit or weapon selected, the available modifications are presented. A description of the modification’s effects is listed on the right side of the screen, while the modification cost is shown on the left. The list of required resources is shown next to your inventory count.
Confirming application will add the modification to your item. Modifications cannot be removed once installed, so be sure that you’ve made the right choice.
codex_pilotshandbook_engineers_experimen: As well as improving a module’s performance, engineers can also add an experimental effect for an additional one-time material cost.
Experimental effects fall into one of two categories:

There is a wide range of experimental effects, but only one of these can be present on a module at a time. Some experimental effects are available for a variety of modules, while others are exclusive to a specific module.
Replacing an existing modification with a different one will remove any experimental effect currently applied to the module
Not all experimental effects are offered by all engineers. Experimental effects can only be applied at an engineer’s workshop.

Experimental effects for hardpoints will generally add enhanced damage, utility or defences. Examples include increased hardpoint integrity, reduced power draw, additional thermal damage or armour weakening effects.

Experimental effects for modules will usually impact performance, efficiency or durability. Examples include additional shield strength, reduced mass, damage resistances and faster function recharge speeds.
codex_pilotshandbook_engineers_howtofind: The names and specialities of some engineers are public knowledge. Though the exact location of their workshops is unknown to new pilots, they are known to make contact once certain accomplishments have been made. Other engineers will make contact as your reputation with this initial group grows.

Information about your known engineers in the Engineers section of the Home screen on your ship’s internal interface panel. This information can also be accessed via the Engineer option in your suit’s Insight hub.
Upon arrival at an engineer’s home system, you will need to complete a discovery scan to reveal the engineer’s workshop on the system map.
codex_pilotshandbook_engineers_introduct: Engineers are expert inventors and mechanics who display remarkable skill in modifying technology. The most successful of these set up workshops to exchange their talents for goods and materials.

Some engineers remain aligned with a superpower while others are truly independent. Their backgrounds, personalities and motives vary wildly. But the result of working with an engineer is the same: a considerable increase in the performance of one’s ship or on-foot equipment.
codex_pilotshandbook_engineers_materialt: Material traders can be found in the contact list of certain starports. These traders offer exchanges of materials at a fixed conversion rate. Each trader deals in one material type:
ENCODED MATERIAL TRADERS Encoded Material Traders are found in Military and High Tech economy systems.
MANUFACTURED MATERIAL TRADERS Manufactured Material Traders are found in Extraction and Industrial economy systems.
RAW MATERIAL TRADERS Raw Material Traders are found in Extraction and Refinery economy systems.

As well as rarity, items of interest to a material trader are also grouped by category. This is a sub-group of a material type. For example, Firmware is a category of encoded material which includes modified consumer firmware, cracked industrial firmware and modified embedded firmware.

The conversion cost of exchanging materials in the same category is dependent on the relative rarity grade. If you are offering a Grade 1 material and want a Grade 2 material in exchange, this cost is fairly minimal. Trading to obtain a Grade 5 material will require a far higher investment, however.
A separate conversion cost exists for trading materials of a different category. Exchanging materials of the same grade but different categories also incurs a conversion cost.

Many Commanders find themselves acquiring a large number of common materials as they progress through their careers. When you need higher-grade materials for a specific engineering blueprint, material traders are a useful method of acquiring them quickly.
codex_pilotshandbook_engineers_modificat: Each engineering blueprint has a material cost, which is displayed beneath the Cost header. Each blueprint uses different materials. The material cost is deducted from your inventory each time a blueprint is modified. The number of available applications you can afford is calculated for you. See the Ship Engineering Materials page for more information.
Once an engineer’s services have been unlocked, you will have access to the Engineers Workshop interface while docked at the workshop.

As well as a summary of the engineer’s profile and your current reputation level, you will be able to browse the engineer’s blueprints. You can filter these by the blueprints available for your installed modules, or by all blueprints offered by the engineer.

If you have more than one module of the same type, you will be prompted to select which one you wish to work on. If you’re simply browsing, you will be asked to choose which grade of blueprint to view if the engineer offers more than one.
Experimental effects can be applied to some modules for an extra cost. See the Experimental effects page for more information.

Selecting the Generate Modification option will prepare the blueprint for application. A final prompt will advise you of any negative effects the modification will have. If the blueprint will replace an existing one the prompt will alert you to this also.

Confirming will tell the engineer to proceed with the work. This applies a percentage of the module’s maximum possible improvement is gained. Several modifications are required to achieve maximum improvement for the selected grade.
When a module has been improved to its maximum value you will have the option to apply a higher grade of blueprint. This allows you to improve a module even further, gaining even greater benefits.
Note: In the bottom-left of the modification screen is a Help button. This will explain what each panel of the screen contains, helping you navigate the modification process.

Blueprints are selected from a list on the left-hand side of the modification screen. Selecting one will present the different effects. Effects in blue are positive and outline the general performance and efficiency improvements you can expect.

Some modifications result in a negative effect in some aspect of a module’s performance; these are marked in red. Negative effects are typically trade-offs to accommodate the modification, such as increased power draw or added mass.
codex_pilotshandbook_engineers_precis: A guide discussing interactions with engineers.
codex_pilotshandbook_engineers_shipengin: Materials are resources used in several manufacturing processes. There are three types of material:
ENCODED MATERIALS A type of data provided by scanning certain objects or signals.
Materials can be earned as part of a mission reward package. They are also gathered from a variety of sources, including shipwrecks, scan results, surface resources and more.

When browsing an engineer’s blueprints, highlighting a specific material in the cost list will reveal where the material can be found. This includes which signal sources to visit, desirable system states to search in and which ship types tend to carry the material.

Some resources will require special equipment to find, such as a mining laser for prospecting asteroids or an SRV for harvesting surface resources. Be sure that you are properly equipped to collect material before heading out.
MANUFACTURED MATERIALS Materials used in construction which are usually acquired as salvage.
Each material has a rarity grade and category.
Rarity is listed from Grade 1 to Grade 5. Grade 1 materials are commonly found throughout the galaxy, while Grade 5 materials are acquired from a few sources only and can be hazardous to collect.
RAW MATERIALS Chemical elements present throughout the galaxy obtained by prospecting.

Each engineering blueprint has a material cost. This cost is displayed when viewing the blueprint information. Every time you apply a blueprint’s effects to your ship, the material cost is deducted from your inventory.
codex_pilotshandbook_engineers_suitengin: ASSETS Smaller physical components stored in the suit backpack. Assets are categorised into tech, chemicals and circuitry. Usually found in containers or looted. Assets can be traded with a Bartender. Much like material traders, the bartenders of the galaxy allow for the exchange of assets for a conversion fee. See the Bartender page of the Concourse guide for more information.
DATA Files and documentation stored on a suit’s data bank. Data is copied from data ports or offered as a mission reward.
The resources required to engineer suits and weapons are a mixture of goods, assets and data.

These resources are commonly gathered from settlements, various points of interest on a planet’s surface, or salvageable wreckage. Some resources are easier to find than others based on their value and rarity.
GOODS Manufactured or treated items carried in the suit backpack. Goods can be found in locked containers or offered as a mission reward.
codex_pilotshandbook_engineers_suitunloc: Suit engineers provide modifications to suits and personal weaponry. In contrast to ship engineering, each suit engineer offers a fixed number of blueprints that can be applied to any suit or weapon.
DYNAMIC - Modifications that focus on agility and movement.
FORCE - Modifications that focus on damage output and protection.

All suit engineers have an invitation requirement. You will receive an invitation to an engineer’s workshop once this requirement has been satisfied. Requirements vary between the engineers and include reputation levels, progress criteria or mission completions. These requirements are displayed on the Known Engineers screen.
Suit engineers specialise in one of three areas:
STRATEGIC - Modifications that focus on range and utility.
Once an invitation is received there are no additional unlock requirements for suit engineers Commanders can visit the engineer’s workshop and access their services immediately.

Most engineers will request a quantity of goods; these can be donated in person. When the donation quota has been met, the engineer will refer you to another engineer. This referral is important, as an engineer will not provide access to their workshop until you have been referred to them.

Referrals direct Commanders to an engineer of a different speciality. For example, an engineer specialising in Force modifications will refer you to an engineer offering Strategic or Dynamic modifications.
The final engineer in a reference chain does not have a donation request.
codex_pilotshandbook_engineers_unlock_de: Ship engineers provide modifications to ship modules and hardpoints. Each engineer has a selection of blueprints relating to different modules, and these blueprints progress in quality from Grade 1 to Grade 5.
The full unlock process for an engineer is as follows:
codex_pilotshandbook_engineers_unlock_in: All ship engineers have an invitation requirement. You will receive an invitation to an engineer’s workshop once this requirement has been satisfied. Requirements vary between the engineers and include rank unlocks, progress criteria or reputation levels. These requirements are displayed on the Known Engineers screen.
codex_pilotshandbook_engineers_unlock_pi: Each unlocked engineer allows you to pin one of their blueprints to your ship’s computer, which can then be recalled at a remote workshop. A pinned blueprint enables you to apply that modification to a ship module without the need to return to the engineer’s workshop. Remote workshops are offered in any landing pad hangar that has access to an outfitting service.
codex_pilotshandbook_engineers_unlock_re: With the unlock task complete, a ship engineer will offer access to their modification services while docked at their workshop. Using these services will increase your reputation with that engineer, unlocking higher grades of blueprint. Reputation can also be increased by using certain services while docked, such as the commodity market or administrative contact.
codex_pilotshandbook_engineers_unlock_un: Once an invitation has been received, you will also learn of the engineer’s location. While you can now land at the engineer’s workshop, the engineer’s services must be unlocked. With one exception, this is done by donating something the engineer wants. The outstanding unlock request is displayed in the Known Engineers screen.
codex_pilotshandbook_exploration_dss_des: The Detailed Surface Scanner is used to map astronomical objects. Ships must be in supercruise for the DSS to function. Engaging the DSS brings up a unique interface to operate the scanner.

When a planet has been fully mapped, your ship computer will generate a digital overlay that highlights the presence of organic life on the surface. Using the provided filter it is possible to set the overlay to show a specific genus only.

The DSS is capable of launching probes at stellar bodies and planetary rings within range. The marker on the DSS reticule denotes when a probe will hit the horizon of the body. The reticule can be moved around, allowing the accurate placement of probes. If the reticule is aiming at a location where launched probes would miss a target, this will be displayed.

When a probe hits the surface of a stellar body, it maps a region of the surface. Using multiple probes the entire surface of a body can be mapped. A mapped area is highlighted following each successful probe scan.

The gravity of a body affects probes, and with clever aiming can be used to send probes to map the far side of a body. The scanner's interface will help you to aim probes in this way. Once more than 90% of a body's surface has been highlighted, your ship computer will consider the body fully mapped.
As landable planets are mapped, points of interest on the surface will be highlighted. These can then be selected and navigated to.
When mapped, rings around a body provide the location of mineral hotspots within the ring. This is of particular interest to miners seeking the most profitable area to gather resources.

Every stellar body has a mapping efficiency target. Fully mapping a surface using an equal or fewer number of probes will provide a bonus to the associated exploration data. Probes that miss a body entirely do not count towards this efficiency target.
Supercruise assist can place a ship into orbit around a targeted astronomical body.
codex_pilotshandbook_exploration_fss_des: A Full Spectrum System Scan is used to study a system in details. Ships must be in supercruise $BINDING_input_either:#value=HyperSuperCombination; and throttled down to zero $BINDING_input_either:#value=SETSPEEDZERO; for the FSS to function. Engaging the FSS brings up a unique interface to operate the scanner.
If the Discovery Scanner has not already been used, then an energy pulse can be emitted in this mode to populate the filtered signal analysis (FSA) and provide the system's orbital plane.
The filtered spectrum analysis displays all the signals detected by the Discovery Scanner. This can be interpreted in the following ways:

• Low-intensity signals, on the left side of the spectrum, are generated by smaller sources. These tend to include transient signal sources, such as emissions and distress calls. • Concentrated signal source, generated by conflict zones, stations and megaships, or beacons. • Medium intensity signals, around the centre of the spectrum. This ranges from asteroid belts and non-atmospheric bodies on the left to atmospheric planets on the right. • High-intensity signals, on the right side of the spectrum, are generated by large sources. These represent any water or gas based giants present in the system.
The larger and higher the peak of these signals, the greater the likelihood that multiple signals of that type are present.
While moving the scanner around, blue pulsing signal fields should be visible. This indicates that a signal is present in that location. Signals are most commonly found along the orbital plane.

Tuning a position on the FSA $BINDING_input_either:#value=ExplorationFSSRadioTuningX_Raw; focuses the scanner for that signal type, isolating fixed points within the signal fields. When aligned with a calibrated signal, the scanner can zoom in $BINDING_input_either:#value=ExplorationFSSZoomIn; to confirm the signal and acquire exploration data.

Some signals will represent a cluster of additional signals, which can be investigated with a partial zoom. It will then be necessary to align your scanner within this new layer of signals. If the scanner is aligned with a signal but the target circle is dotted rather than solid then the scanner is not tuned correctly.

As signals are confirmed, they are marked on the FSA in place of the unverified signal waveform. Astronomical bodies scanned in this way for the first time will be tagged with the First Discovered By tag upon successful hand-in of the related exploration data.
codex_pilotshandbook_exploration_integra: All ships come with the following equipment installed:
Allows a ship to approach and land on any planetary body that lacks an atmosphere.
Emits a signal pulse which calculates how many astronomical objects inhabit the current system.
Maps systems by identifying signal fields. These fields represent various astronomical objects, conflict zones, signal source types and more.
Interacts with a variety of technical devices, granting access to emission data and audio logs. Highlights modules on scanned megaships and installations.
Analyses organic and inorganic entities found throughout the galaxy, uploading records to the Codex.
codex_pilotshandbook_exploration_introdu: One of humanity's oldest traditions, exploration offers the opportunity to become a pioneer charting star systems, some for the first time in human history. Scanning a variety of stars, planets and points of interest gathers data which is then sold for credits and to earn reputation. Explorers may also stake their claims with First Discovery and First Footfall tags, map planets with probes, and take in beautiful vistas found throughout the galaxy.
Commanders can sell exploration data at the Universal Cartographics station service. Data cannot be sold within 20 light years of where it was collected.
Any system in the galaxy can be scanned. The value of the acquired data varies based on the number and type of astronomical bodies within the system.

To engage a ship's scanning utilities, Analysis Mode must be activated $BINDING_input_either:#value=PlayerHUDModeToggle;. Then a superficial scan of the system can be made with the Discovery Scanner's energy pulse. This will provide instant feedback on how many astronomical bodies are in the current system.
codex_pilotshandbook_exploration_maint_e: Converts hydrogen collected from a star's corona into usable fuel.
Repairs other modules installed on your ship. Useful as insurance against unexpected damage in deep space.
Ejects heatsinks, rapidly reducing a ship's heat levels. Provides some protection from close encounters with stars.
codex_pilotshandbook_exploration_optequi: Launches sensor probes to scan a planet's surface. See the Detailed Surface Scanner chapter for more details on operation.
Holds one or more Surface Recon Vehicles (SRV), used to travel on the surface of eligible planets and moons.
ADVANCED PLANETARY APPROACH SUITE Optional Internal
Allows a ship to approach and land on any planetary body with a tenuous atmosphere.
Comes equipped with the genetic sampler tool, used to scan and index organic material.
codex_pilotshandbook_exploration_precis: A guide to exploring the vastness of the galaxy.
codex_pilotshandbook_exploration_ranks_d: The following ranks are granted to Commanders by the Pilots' Federation for their dedication to mapping the stars. Ranks are acquired based on the amount of profit made from selling exploration data.

• Aimless
• Mostly Aimless
• Scout
• Surveyor
• Trailblazer
• Pathfinder
• Ranger
• Pioneer
• Elite
• Elite II
• Elite III
• Elite IV
• Elite V
codex_pilotshandbook_exploration_selling: Exploration data is sold at the Universal Cartographics station service found at starports, outposts and planetary docks. Data cannot be sold within 20 light years of where it was collected.
The value of each system's data is calculated by a number of factors:

• The quality of the data. Data is generated with the Discovery Scanner's energy pulse, but the value of that data is lower than using the Full Spectrum System Scanner to scan individual bodies. This, in turn, provides less valuable data than when mapping each body in a system using the Detailed Surface Scanner. • Efficiency bonus. Planetary bodies mapped with an equal or fewer number of probes required to meet the efficiency bonus will provide a higher number of credits for that body. • Type of astronomical objects scanned. Earth-like, water and ammonia worlds are the most valuable planet types, while black holes and neutron stars are the most valuable star classes. • Terraforming candidates. Water, high metal content and rocky worlds in a system's habitable zone are considered terraforming candidates. These bodies offer a value multiplier to their respective data. • First discovered bonus. Astronomical objects scanned or mapped for the first time will grant various bonuses.

There are six discovery bonuses available: • First Discovery. An object scanned with the Full Spectrum System Scanner for the first time. This also tags the object with a 'First Discovered By' tag displaying the explorer's name. • First Mapped. A planetary body fully mapped with the Detailed Surface Scanner for the first time. This also tags the body with a 'First Mapped By' tag displaying the explorer's name. • Being the first to fully scan a system, earning First Discovery bonuses for every astronomical object in a system, will grant an additional credit bonus. • Being the first to fully map a system, earning First Mapped bonuses for every planetary body in a system, will grant an additional credit bonus. • First Footfall. A planet that the explorer was the first to disembark and set foot upon. • First Logged. Organic data handed in to a Vista Genomics representative that catalogues a species on a planet for the first time.
codex_pilotshandbook_exploration_surface: Explorers are also able to explore the surface of planetary bodies with thin atmospheres. Being the first human in history to step on the surface of a new world will be granted the First Footfall tag upon selling the associated exploration data.

Organic life can be found on most worlds and catalogued with the genetic sampler. The Supratech Artemis suit comes equipped with this tool. The collected organic data is then sold at a Vista Genomics outlet, typically found on a starport concourse.

The Codex will register first-time organic discoveries in a region of space. If another explorer has already recorded an organic genus in that region, your data will confirm it. The first explorer to sell organic data from a planet will have their name registered in the First Logged entry for that planet.
See the Suit Equipment guide for more information about the genetic sampler, and the Concourse guide for information about Vista Genomics.
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_cmbar:
The Bartender runs the carrier’s bar, welcoming patrons and keeping an eye on the crew during their free time. They also buy and sell goods, assets and data – collectively known as resources - which are typically used for upgrading and engineering suits and personal equipment.

The resources traded at each carrier's bar are determined by the carrier owner.
Resource Capacity A full breakdown of the carrier’s resource capacity. It displays how much capacity space is currently allocated, reserved or free. This capacity is shared by all resource types.
Total Resource Stock Value The credit value of all resources currently stored on the carrier.
Active Resource Requests The total number of resource types the bartender will purchase.
Resource Types Sold The total number of resource types the bartender will sell.
Bartender Sales Trend This graph provides eight weeks of trade history at the carrier bar, showing activity trends. The highest and lowest single-week values are highlighted.
Manage Bar Trading A full list of tradable resources. The carrier owner can select individual resources for purchase or sale, along with the desired price and quantity limits.

RESOURCE INVENTORY TRANSFERS Only items in the fleet carrier inventory can be traded at the bar. Resources can be transferred between the fleet carrier inventory and the carrier owner’s active ship in two ways: - Using the Fleet Carrier Inventory Transfer tab in the Backpack menu - Using the Transfer tab of a docked ship’s Internal interface panel
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_cmbla: The trade of stolen goods is possible with a Fence present on a fleet carrier. Owners who permit such activity should note that a fleet carrier's security rating impacts the difficulty of importing and exporting stolen goods. Additional system authority ships will patrol carriers with higher security ratings.
Total Stolen Goods Value The total value of all stolen goods currently stored on the fleet carrier.
Number of Commodity Types The total number of stolen commodities available for trade.
Capacity Allocation The amount of the carrier's current capacity allocated to illegal goods.
All-time Fence Profit The total number of credits earned by the Fence during the carrier's service.
Secure Trading Sales Trend This graph provides eight weeks of carrier trade in stolen goods, showing activity trends. The lowest and highest single-week values are highlighted.
Manage Secure Warehouse A full list of commodities traded from the secure warehouse. The carrier owner can set individual goods for purchase or sale, along with the associated price and stock limits.
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_cmbud: The Budget tab provides information related to the financial management of a fleet carrier.

Carrier Balance A full breakdown of the budget's allocation. This includes the number of credits set aside for commodity trades, the amount reserved for weekly upkeep payments, and the remaining available credits.
Weekly Upkeep A rundown of the next upkeep payment. It details where the carrier's budget will be allocated following actions taken in the current week.

Service Tariff The carrier owner can set a tariff on services used by visiting pilots. Services such as refuelling and rearming charge a fee that covers their operational costs. The tariff level increases the price of that service, with the extra credits assigned to the carrier's budget. Note that the tariff system is not applicable to some services. The Universal Cartographics, Vista Genomics and Redemption Office services take a cut of each transaction instead. Credits are allocated as follows: - 75% to the visitor. - 12.5% to the carrier bank. - 12.5% convenience fee to the service provider.

Fleet Carrier Banking Facilitates the transfer of credits between the owner's credit account and the carrier's budget. This budget will be used for all fleet carrier expenses. It is important that an adequate number of credits are available each week to avoid incurring an operational debt. The Fleet Carrier Banking sub-menu will also forecast the remaining budget following the next weekly upkeep payment.

Failure to maintain weekly upkeep payments may lead to a fleet carrier's decommission. Carrier owners are expected to cover all operational costs; leaving a carrier's crew stranded with no wages on an unmaintained vessel is considered grounds for forcibly removing that carrier from service. Should a carrier's balance reach a value that is unable to complete a weekly upkeep payment then the Banking menu will warn of insufficient funds. See the Fleet Carrier Decommission section for further information.
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_cmliv: The final two tabs on the management screen relate to a fleet carrier's appearance and operational settings.

Browse and apply any available cosmetic options for fleet carriers. Several aspects of a carrier's appearance can be customised to the owner's preference. A carrier's Livery is not remotely accessible.
Docking Access Set docking access permissions between several groups.
Notorious Commander Access Determines whether pilots who are currently considered notorious are allowed to dock on the carrier.

Set Current Activity Select the fleet carrier's activity icon for the Station Services screen and the Navigation panel. Activity icons help inform other pilots of the types of services they can expect at a carrier.
Illegal Equipment Trading This sets permission for the carrier’s Pioneer Supplies vendor to sell illegal items, such as the E-Breach.
Decommission Carrier Submit a request to decommission the fleet carrier. See the Fleet Carrier Decommission section for further information.
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_cmmar: The Commodities Trader oversees all trade that takes place on a fleet carrier. This is an important role as the fleet carrier acts as a self-contained independent market. Prices are set by the carrier owner and only stocked goods are available for purchase.
Total Inventory Value The total value of all commodities currently stored on the fleet carrier.
Number of Commodity Types The total number of commodities available for trade.
Capacity Allocation The amount of the carrier's capacity which is currently used by commodities.
All-time Trade Profit The total number of credits earned by the Commodity Trader during the carrier's service.
Market Sales Trend This graph provides eight weeks of carrier trade, showing trends in activity. The lowest and highest single-week values are highlighted.

Market Management A full list of tradable commodities. The carrier owner can set individual goods for purchase or sale, along with the associated price and stock limits. Note that Rare and Powerplay goods cannot be traded on a fleet carrier.
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_cmnav: The Navigation tab provides information about a fleet carrier's current and pending locations.
Current Location The fleet carrier's current star system. Includes the system's primary economy type.
Scheduled Destination The carrier's plotted route. Includes the target system's primary economy type.
Estimated Departure The time remaining until a pending jump is initiated.
Landing Pad Lockdown The time remaining until the fleet carrier's landing pad access is disabled.
Tritium Reserves The carrier's current and projected tritium stock.
Jump Capability The carrier's current and projected jump capability, based on tritium reserves and carrier capacity usage.
Open Galaxy Map Opens the Galaxy Map, from where a fleet carrier jump can be scheduled. See the Movement and Fuel section for further information.
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_cmout: Fleet carriers with an active outfitting facility will offer pilots the chance to upgrade, exchange and store modules. The modules available for trade are determined by the stock selected by the carrier owner.
The carrier owner will always have access to outfitting services for the storage and management of their personal modules, regardless of whether the public facility has been installed.

A variety of stock can be purchased for a fleet carrier's outfitting facility. They are dictated by type and tier. Stock can only be purchased, restocked or sold in a system offering the Fleet Carrier Administration service.
Type The category of outfitting stock indicates the common function of the modules contained within. This varies between mining tools, laser weaponry, limpets etc.

Tier The tier of stock dictates the quality and cost of the modules contained within. As a general rule, a higher tier will provide modules of a greater class and grade, which is reflected in the increased purchase value.
Refill Stock When available, this will replenish the stock levels of the selected category. Adequate capacity must be available to successfully refill stock.

Sell Stock When available, this will refund all remaining items of the selected stock category. This will increase the available capacity, and return a percentage of the stock's credit value to the carrier's budget.
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_cmser:
A fleet carrier is capable of offering a wide variety of services, which the owner can tailor according to preference and budget. Carriers must be situated in a system with a Carrier Construction Dock to install or remove services.

Visitors should note that carriers are regarded as independent markets. As such the use of these services have no impact on local faction standings.
SERVICE INSTALLATION

Installing a service provides all necessary workshop equipment required in the fleet carrier. This fills the required capacity and deducts the installation cost from the carrier's budget. In addition, a Head of Service is hired to lead that service's personnel. This individual can be replaced at any time at zero additional cost.

Active services incur a weekly running cost to cover operational expenses and staff wages. Deactivating an installed service will lower this cost, but will switch off that service until reactivated.
SERVICE REMOVAL
Removing a service will recoup 100% of its initial cost, as the installed equipment is packed up and shipped off with its personnel. This frees up carrier capacity for use elsewhere.
<font size='40'>INSTALLING SERVICES</font>
CORE SERVICES
Armoury Offers the resupply of weapons to docked ships.
Redemption Office Grants the exchange of vouchers and combat bonds for credits.
Outfitting Enables pilots of docked ships to trade, install and store modules.
Shipyard Allows pilots to trade and store ships. Can also be accessed from the carrier's concourse.
Secure Warehouse Facilitates the trade of stolen goods.
Universal Cartographics Accepts exploration data in exchange for credits and discovery tags.
CONCOURSE SERVICES
These services are optional and must be selected for installation by the carrier owner. They can only be accessed from the carrier's concourse.
Concourse Bar Installs a bar in the concourse, allowing the purchase and sale of resources.
Vista Genomics Installs a Vista Genomics booth on the concourse, allowing organic data transactions.
The following services are included as standard on all carriers, and will continue to function regardless of a carrier's status.
Pioneer Supplies Installs a Pioneer Supplies booth on the concourse, where suits and personal equipment can be purchased.
Bridge Crew All carriers require a crew, and this service represents the personnel on board.
Commodity Trading Allows the trade of select goods as specified by the carrier owner.
Tritium Depot Allows the donation of tritium towards the carrier's fuel stores.
OPTIONAL SERVICES
These services are optional and must be selected for installation by the carrier owner.
Repair Crews Provides repair work on docked ships.
Refuel Station Supplies fuel for docked ships.
<font size='40'>LIST OF SERVICES</font>
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_cmshi: A fleet carrier's shipyard allows docked pilots to purchase, sell or exchange ships. The variety of ships available is determined by the type of stock categories purchased by the carrier owner. Ship stock can only be purchased, restocked or sold in a system offering the Fleet Carrier Administration service.
The carrier owner will always have access to shipyard services for the storage and management of their personal fleet, regardless of whether the public facility has been installed.

A number of options exist for the fleet carrier's shipyard stock. Ships suited to various activities such as mining or exploration are available. The selected contents are then added to the shipyard, filling the carrier's capacity.
Refill Stock When available, this replenishes the levels of the selected ship stock. Adequate capacity must be available to successfully refill stock.

Sell Stock When available, this refunds the remaining stock of the selected ship category. This will increase the available capacity, and return a percentage of the stock's credit value to the carrier's budget.
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_cmsum: The Summary tab provides a quick status report for the carrier which is available to both the owner and guests.
Carrier Capacity A full breakdown of the fleet carrier's capacity, displaying how much space is allocated to various categories and how much free space remains.
Available Services A list of all the installed and active services on the carrier.

Carrier Security Rating Fleet carriers are assigned a security rating by each of the superpowers, which is determined by several factors. Independent systems also aggregate a security rating for individual carriers. See the Security and Reputation section for further information.
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_conco:
Visitors to the fleet carrier can disembark to stretch their legs and take a stroll around the concourse. The carrier owner and their teammates may also enjoy exclusive access to the command deck.

The following services can be found on the concourse, providing the carrier owner has installed them:
Pioneer Supplies Offers suits, personal weapons and consumables for purchase only. Unlike starport vendors, items cannot be sold to equipment traders on a carrier.
Bartender Trades resources as determined by the carrier owner. Unlike starport bartenders, resources cannot be exchanged but can be bought and sold.
Vista Genomics Accepts organic data collected using the genetic sampler in exchange for credits.
Shipyard Contains a number of terminals through which guests can manage their fleet and purchase ships stocked by the carrier.
See the Concourse guide for more detailed information on using these services.
Escape pods are installed on every carrier concourse. These can be used to return an individual to the last safe location they docked at prior to arrival at the fleet carrier.
Any ship docked on the carrier will be left behind and must be transferred or collected by the owner. Individuals using an escape pod will also lose any unregistered organic data.
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_decom:
A fleet carrier can be decommissioned for two reasons:

- Following a direct request from the owner.
- Due to the excessive neglect of finances.

Once a fleet carrier is pending decommission, all optional services are disabled and any outstanding purchase orders are cancelled. Pilots arriving at the carrier will be informed of the expected timeframe involved, allowing them to depart before the end of this period.

Fleet carriers in this state will still be able to sell existing services if in a carrier administration system, dismiss crew, sell/transport cargo and plot jumps. New service installations, crew hires, purchase orders and fuel donations will be blocked.

The Pending Decommission state will last for a minimum of seven days. After this period, a Pathfinder Solutions crew will arrive to implement the decommissioning process. This effectively removes the fleet carrier from the owner's control.

Following decommission, any credits remaining in the fleet carrier budget will be returned to the owner, minus any running costs incurred since the decommission request was submitted. A final inbox message breaking down the total of credits reclaimed will be sent to the owner.

Pilots with ships or modules stored on the newly decommissioned carrier will be informed of the situation via inbox message. These assets can be recovered by following the instructions provided in this message.
A carrier owner may decide that they no longer require their fleet carrier. They can request a formal decommission using the Fleet Carrier Management interface.

Owners will be shown the total number of credits that will be reclaimed, alongside the proposed decommission date and the number of assets currently stored. Once confirmed, the fleet carrier will be classed as Pending Decommission.

Upon decommissioning a fleet carrier, pilots will receive a remunerative sum contingent on the following:

- The purchase cost of all installed facilities aboard the carrier
- The galactic average price for all non-stolen commodities stored on board and the minimum sale price for all stolen commodities.
If a fleet carrier voluntarily decommissioned, a fee of 125,000,000 cr is deducted from the refund, along with any outstanding debt.

Carrier owners are expected to cover all operational costs; leaving a carrier's crew stranded with no wages on an unmaintained vessel is considered grounds for forcibly removing that carrier from service.

The Banking menu of the Budget tab will inform owners if a carrier has insufficient funds to cover operational costs. The total outstanding debt amount must be paid as soon as possible to avoid the loss of a carrier.
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_intro: Fleet carriers are massive ships fitted with multiple hangar bays, functioning as a mobile base of operations. Services offered by a fleet carrier can be fully customised by the carrier's owner; this includes the traded commodity types, available outfitting modules and the contents of a shipyard.

Manufactured by the Brewer Corporation, these remarkable craft offer significant advantages in all professions. Unlike single-pilot vessels, carriers require a dedicated budget to cover weekly expenses. A unique interface allows owners to easily manage their fleet carrier, covering all aspects of operation from a single screen.
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_manag: The Fleet Carrier Management screen utilises the CarrierAdminOS software to provide a custom interface. Here, fleet carrier owners can access all administrative tools needed for the smooth operation of their vessel.

This screen shows the following information, clockwise from top-right:

- The fleet carrier class, name and designation.
- The carrier's balance, weekly upkeep and capacity.
- The carrier's integrity and fuel.
- The next scheduled destination and countdown to jump initiation, if applicable.
- The carrier's current location.

Individual functions can be selected from the icons listed along the left of the screen. Owners will have access to far more icons than guests. Some of the options presented in these tabs are dependent on the installation of a service. See the Installing Services section for further information.

The Carrier Management screen can be accessed remotely by an owner via the Home tab of the Internal interface panel on the right of the cockpit chair.
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_movef: Fleet carriers utilise a capital ship-scale Frame Shift Drive to jump between star systems. This drive requires a unique type of fuel: tritium.
Fleet carrier jumps can be cancelled up to 10 minutes before the scheduled jump slot. After this point, owners must wait until the jump has completed before scheduling any further movement.

Due to the vast number of navigational calculations involved in a carrier jump, it is possible for a jump to fail. In this situation, the carrier will remain at its current location. An inbox message from a carrier's Deck Officer will be sent to the owner to inform them of a scheduled jump's outcome.
Tritium is a radioactive isotope of hydrogen. This substance can be reliably mined from planetary ice rings. Alternatively, tritium can be purchased as a commodity from certain economies.

The amount of tritium required for a particular jump is dependent on the following:

- Carrier Mass
- Carrier Capacity Usage
- Scheduled Jump Distance

Docked pilots may donate via the Tritium Depot or sell units of tritium to a Commodity Trader.

Frame shift jumps are scheduled in advance and require a period of preparation. All fleet carriers have a maximum jump range of 500 light years. Note that fleet carriers are not authorised to enter permit-restricted systems.

When viewing a star system in the Galaxy Map, a carrier's owner can set the carrier's destination. Following this, using the System Map to select a body within the system will set an orbital location. The icon below will appear once a carrier's new destination has been scheduled:

A frame shift jump can only be scheduled if the destination is within the fleet carrier's jump range. The standard jump time is 15 minutes, with short variations depending on system traffic and navigation telemetry checks.
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_preci: A guide covering the ownership and operation of a fleet carrier.
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_purch: Fleet carriers are available for purchase in any system with a <font color='#f8f8f8'>Carrier Construction Dock</font>. In the Galaxy Map, these systems can be located using the Fleet Carrier Vendor filter.
While docked at the designated starport within these systems, a Fleet Carrier Vendor will be listed in the Contacts section of the Starport Services interface.
Selecting this contact will present the option to purchase a fleet carrier.

Following a successful purchase, new fleet carrier owners will receive an inbox message providing the carrier's location. This location will also be indicated in the System Map with the following icon:
codex_pilotshandbook_fleetcarriers_secur: Fleet carriers are subject to the laws of a system's governing faction. Since carriers offer commodity trading services, they are routinely patrolled by system authority vessels who screen visitors for illegal goods.

Fleet carriers monitor transgressions that relate to its operation or safety. These include trespassing, blocking landing pads or jettisoning cargo canisters in the carrier's vicinity. In addition, fleet carriers are authorised to defend themselves with lethal force.

System authority ships around a carrier enforce the laws of the governing faction. They respond to violations of these laws in the same manner as around a starport. Crimes such as murder, assault and transporting illegal goods fall under this criteria.

The legality of commodities is determined by the laws of a system's governing faction. For example, an Imperial Feudal system allows the trade of tobacco whereas a Federal Corporate system prohibits this commodity. As a fleet carrier moves from system to system, certain commodities may fluctuate from legal to prohibited. Carrier owners are advised to consider this when selecting a destination.

Every fleet carrier has a security rating, which is determined by several factors:

- The superpower aligned with the system's governing faction.
- Criminal actions against security forces in the vicinity of the carrier.
- Ships discovered carrying illegal goods originating from the carrier.
A higher security rating results in more system authority ships being assigned to that fleet carrier. This is generally an effort to reduce negative activity resulting from a carrier's presence.
codex_pilotshandbook_maps_basicnav_descr: The basic controls for moving the camera around the galaxy and planetary maps are:

Scroll horizontal: Forward $BINDING_input_either:#value=CamTranslateForward|CamTranslateYAxis;, Back $BINDING_input_either:#value=CamTranslateBackward|CamTranslateYAxis;, Left $BINDING_input_either:#value=CamTranslateLeft|CamTranslateXAxis;, Right $BINDING_input_either:#value=CamTranslateRight|CamTranslateXAxis; Scroll vertical: Up $BINDING_input_either:#value=CamTranslateUp|CamTranslateZAxis;, Down $BINDING_input_either:#value=CamTranslateDown|CamTranslateZAxis; Zoom: In $BINDING_input_either:#value=CamZoomIn|CamZoomAxis;, Out $BINDING_input_either:#value=CamZoomOut|CamZoomAxis; Pitch: Up $BINDING_input_either:#value=CamPitchUp|CamPitchAxis;, Down $BINDING_input_either:#value=CamPitchDown|CamPitchAxis; Yaw: Left $BINDING_input_either:#value=CamYawLeft|CamYawAxis;, Right $BINDING_input_either:#value=CamYawRight|CamYawAxis; Select: $BINDING_input_either:#value=UI_SELECT;

Orrery View in the system map follows the same controls as above.
Map View in the system map is a two-dimensional display navigated with the horizontal and zoom controls shown above.

Select a Target To select an object on a map, move your map cursor or pointer to it and press $BINDING_input_either:#value=UI_SELECT;. To set it as your target, select it twice or use the Set Target tab. To clear a target, simply select another area of the map or use the Clear Target tab.

Plot Route To plot a route, you must first set a destination. To do so, hold the select input over the intended destination or use the Set Destination tab. To clear a destination, use the Clear Destination tab.
Target Focus The Target Focus tab moves the map camera’s focus to your currently selected target.

Copy Target Name The Copy Target Name tab copies the name of your current map target. This can then be pasted into other areas, such as the Comms panel or map search function (Default command: CTRL + V).
codex_pilotshandbook_maps_bookmarks_desc:
The Bookmarks tab shows all active bookmarks. Bookmarks are useful for fixing waypoints along a journey, marking a favourite system or an area of interest, or pinpointing a system for Squadron members to navigate to. Selecting a bookmark will set it as your target.

This tab displays a sub-list with the following options:

Systems - Displays all bookmarked star systems. Bodies - Displays all bookmarked astronomical bodies. Stations - Displays all bookmarked starports and outposts. Settlements - Displays all bookmarked planetary settlements. Squadron Bookmarks - Bookmarks for each of the above categories which have been shared by members of your Squadron.
The Manage Bookmarks tab opens a unique screen for bookmark management. All of the above categories and entries are presented with additional options:

Focus Location - Sets your map cursor to the selected bookmark. Set Destination - Sets the selected bookmark as your destination, plotting a route to it. Share With Squadron - Shares the selected bookmark with all members of your current Squadron, populating the appropriate Squadron Bookmark panel. Rename Bookmark - Allows the entry of a custom name for the selected bookmark. Remove Bookmark - Removes the selected bookmark from your records.
codex_pilotshandbook_maps_description_de: The Description tab lists information about your currently selected target in the system map.

The information is contextual based on the type of object selected. An astronomical body, or a location on the surface of that body, will populate details such as its mass, radius, surface temperature and gravitational constant. These last two details are of particular importance to those intended to land upon a planet surface; high gravity will make landing more difficult, while extreme temperatures can be hazardous over an extended period.
A starport, on the other hand, will populate details such as its economy type and owning faction.
codex_pilotshandbook_maps_displayoptions: The Display Options tab allows you to switch aspects of the map display and various map markers on or off.

DISPLAY Sets the visibility of several map name categories and visual navigational aids. All display toggles are unique to the galaxy map except for Show Controls, which is available when viewing the system map also.

MARKERS Markers are icons shown above star systems in the galaxy map view or individual objects within the system map. These are used to highlight certain information at a glance. Each marker can be toggled off as preferred.

Dry dock markers - Highlights locations where fleet carriers can be purchased or managed. Fleet Carrier markers - Marks the presence of a fleet carrier. Repairing starports - Shows all starports currently under repair. Damaged starports - Shows all starports reporting significant damage sustained. Starter zone markers - Denotes areas within the Pilots’ Federation District, used to train new pilots. Squadron bookmarks - Shows all bookmarks shared by your Squadron. Bookmarks - Shows all your current bookmarks. Show ship markers - Marks where a ship you own is currently docked. Show Engineers - Indicates the location of a known Engineer workshop. Show community goals - Indicates where community goals are currently active. Show mission markers - Shows locations related to active missions. Show team markers - Shows the location of all active teammates.
