colonia_beacon_01_body:
Colonia started, as with many historical discoveries, with an accident.  

In May 3302, Jaques Station set off from Gliese 1269 with the intention of travelling to Beagle Point – 65 thousand light years away. A tide of excitement among observers was quickly swept away following a hyperdrive malfunction, blamed on Thargoid sensor interference. Jaques Station misjumped, vanished, and was soon presumed destroyed. 

During the weeks that followed, fragmented messages sent from Jaques Station alerted pilots of its survival. The starport was discovered surprisingly quickly by the explorer Commander Cly. 

It took a vast effort by independent pilots to rescue and repair the station deep in the black. This led to the establishment of a permanent human presence in the region and Colonia’s first colony.
colonia_beacon_02_body:
The region’s peaceful beginning was shattered October 3303 when The Nameless, a criminal organisation based in the Carcosa system, started attacking ships without provocation. 

The Council called for independent pilots to help end the violence. At the same time, The Nameless appealed for anarchists to join their ranks and overthrow the Colonia Council. 

In the end, justice prevailed. Thanks to the efforts the Council and pilots who supported their counter-attacking campaign, The Nameless were defeated. Peace was once again restored to the Colonia region.
colonia_beacon_03_body:
Following weeks of conflict between humanity and Thargoids in the Pleiades Nebula, many inhabitants of the core systems fled to Colonia seeking refuge from the growing tensions. 

Thousands of newly arriving citizens prompted the Colonia Council to establish new outposts throughout the region. A campaign to welcome the influx of migrants was launched in December 3303 to enormous success.  

To increase safety to the region in case of Thargoid attack, a new security installation, Colonia Bastion, was built and placed in orbit around Colonia 4 in March 3304.
colonia_beacon_04_body:
With the region’s population growing at an unexpected rate due to Second Thargoid War refugees, scientists in Colonia recognised an impending deficit of resources and set about resolving the issue. 

In mid-3304, led by Professor Alexei de la Vega and Professor Diana VanCleef, Colonia Council agreed to proposals to build state-of-the-art installations in Tir and Randgnid. These monitor local population data, allocate interstellar resources, and sustain hydroponic crops to manage and feed the growing number of colonists.
colonia_beacon_05_body:
By August 3304 it was recognised by the Colonia Council that, as the local population had expanded, so too must the services offered to independent pilots in the region.  

Councillor Giselle Kingspear announced the arrival of four Engineers: Etienne Dorn, Marsha Hicks, Mel Brandon and Petra Olmanova. These highly valued experts founded workshops across the Colonia region to provide ship and hardpoint modifications. 

Since then, that number has doubled and locals now have access to four suit and personal weaponry Engineers: Baltanos, Eleanor Bresa, Rosa Dayette and Yi Shen.
colonia_beacon_06_body:
The Colonia Bridge was a massive infrastructure project that took place between October 3307 and March 3008 to build a fleet of megaships positioned between the core systems and Colonia. 

It took the combined efforts of the Colonia Council, Brewer Corporation, and thousands of independent pilots to successfully complete the project across four phases. Six starports and 56 megaships were permanently established at 400-500ly intervals between the Alcor and Colonia star systems. 

The Colonia Bridge's ports will support travel and trade between humanity’s main territory and its distant enclave for centuries to come.

comm_help_into: Engineers are among the most sought-after technicians in the galaxy. Their ability to craft ship or equipment modifications is unrivalled. Commanders can trade materials with an engineer in exchange for their skills.
comm_help_invitations_help: By satisfying an engineer's invitation requirements you can access their workshop. Ship engineers have an additional donation request before offering their services. Once unlocked you can access the engineer's blueprints.
comm_help_modifications_help: Modifications allow you to customise ship modules and personal equipment, increasing performance and versatility. The best modification blueprints guarantee superb results and unique effects.
comm_help_workshop_access_help:
Suit engineers provide their full range of blueprints from the first meeting.

Ship engineers retain their best work for favoured customers. Access ranges from Grade 1 to Grade 5 and governs the quality of modifications available to you. You can gain access levels with an engineer by upgrading your ship's modules with them and using the local services at their workshop.

cs_jameson_logs_001_body:
Hey there, kiddo. Now I know I said I'd be coming home soon, but they've asked me to do something - something important - and I couldn't say no.

I wanted to be there, believe me but sometimes you have to make sacrifices, well this is one of those times. I don't know if that makes much sense to you, but maybe it will do when you're older.

Anyway, I thought I'd send you this log. I know it's not the same as being there in person, but it's the best I could do. I'm sorry.

I'm not really supposed to talk about my mission, but if I'm going to miss your birthday the least I can do is give you a good story. Consider yourself sworn to secrecy, soldier, okay?

I'm sitting in the cockpit, waiting for the all clear. They want to tinker with her for a while first, but they don't seem to have done any harm. All systems online. Everything's... everything's looking good.

I'd be lying if I said I wasn't feeling just a little jittery. You know I've fought bugs before, sure, but never more than one at a time. Flying up to one of their hive ships? Well, that's a whole different story.

Hell, I don't even know what I'm carrying. Classified, they said. All I know is it's designed to target the bugs' hyperdrives so they won't be able to leave the system.

Of course if it doesn't work, I'm just kicking the hornet's nest. That's why I've set the nav system to jump out as soon as I've deployed the payload. Can't be too careful.

Wish me luck.
cs_jameson_logs_002_body:
That was almost too easy. Threaded my way past their perimeter, masked my heat signature so I could get close to the superstructure.

I tell you... I'd never seen a hive ship up close before. I doubt many people have. It was amazing, kiddo. Beautiful, really. Makes you realise just how smart they are, how advanced.

I admit it: I hesitated for a moment before I hit the button. I had to remind myself that it wasn't them I was attacking, just their technology. That's if this mycoid virus of theirs even works.

Man, I watched the payload rocket into the belly of their ship and stuck around just long enough to make sure it hit home. Then I punched the throttle. Woah!

I'm coming home, kiddo. I'm coming home.
cs_jameson_logs_003_body:
It was supposed to target their hyperdrives. That's what they told me. Just the hyperdrives. So we'd be safe again. So we could live without fear. Well, it did a hell of a lot more than that.

There were sensors on the payload so I could monitor the reaction and make sure it activated properly. I'm staring at the data now.

The weapon is... lethal.

They knew what it could do. They knew what it could do and they used it anyway. How many have we killed? Thousands? Millions? God forgive us.
cs_jameson_logs_004_body:
Got myself a bit of a situation here, kiddo.

My guess is that they installed a program in my ship and set it to trigger after I'd deployed the payload. All my systems are dead. The controls are out. Can't even access the escape pod. And the ship is on a collision course. And there is nothing I can do about it.

“We need to inspect your ship, Commander.” How did I fall for a ruse like that? Oh god. I'm at least partly to blame. I've gotten old, careless. I should have quit years ago.

I guess I should have known they wouldn't want me coming back. The bugs are dangerous - no doubt about it - but er, well this is mass murder we're talking about. You can understand why they'd want to keep it secret.

I know some men wouldn't want to admit they'd killed thousands of sentient beings. I guess... I guess the guys back at base think they're doing me a favour by burying me out here in the black. Personally, I'd rather people knew what happened. Even if I didn't come out of it looking too good.

I don't have much time. There's a big old planet in my viewport and it's getting bigger by the second.

People will talk about what I did, after I'm gone. The missions I flew, the things I accomplished. But there's something I want you to remember. No matter what they say, whatever garlands they hang on my name, whatever they write on my tombstone.

You... you were my greatest achievement. I love you, son.

cs_valkyrie_crash_001_body:
Voice transcript log: Captain Niamh Seutonia
Timestamp: 22/03/3307 15:38

After analysing traffic reports from the nine attacked stations, I think I've correlated a pattern. I traced the flight plans of all recent ships and there are nine cargo vessels – one at each starport – that passed through the Mudhrid system on the same date a week before. That can't be coincidence!

I'm taking the Valkyrie and a small team to see what we can find.

Timestamp: 23/03/3307 12:56

We're at Payne-Scott City. Local IISS are already monitoring one of the smaller factions here: the Order of Mudhrid. Its leader, the Landgrave Delacroix, has expressed support for replacing the Duvals with new rulers.

My theory is that the NMLA were using Mudhrid as a staging post for the bombings. There are Imperial, Federal and independent factions in this system. So maybe they had agents within them, arranging cargo transports into each superpower's space.

Timestamp: 23/03/3307 23:33

We've raided a cell of NMLA activists being hidden by the Order of Mudhrid. Captured data confirms that the Landgrave is gathering Neo-Marlinists to his megaship, the Steel Majesty.

But that's not the real prize. Theta Group itself are here! Have we got a chance to take out the NMLA's bomb-makers?

Timestamp: 24/03/3307 07:01

We're back on the Valkyrie. We managed to identify Theta Group's ship before it jumped into hyperspace, and are currently in hot pursuit.

It looks like they're heading toward the Marlinist Colonies. I've made contact with Captain Castile, who's en route to intercept them.

Still... I'm starting to wonder about the veracity of this info. Are Theta Group really on that ship, or is it bait? I'm duplicating all our data and logs into the flight computer core as a precaution. But I hope this will be an early victory for us.

cz_human_accept_001: Good to have you on the team, Commander.
cz_human_fail_001: I'm ordering a tactical retreat. We're outnumbered and outgunned. It's over.

deltaphoenicispalms_info:
A truly organic pest eradication tool, these sterile plants can only be grown from cuttings. Their pollen is lethal to most insectoid life forms. Historically it used their bodies as a host to germinate. Note this may cause hallucinations if workers are over-exposed.

This rare good is legal in all markets.

dentonpatreus_overview_control_ethos: As controller of one of the largest private fleets in the Empire, Senator Patreus is able to muster numerous armed squadrons, capable of overpowering most stellar naval forces.
dentonpatreus_overview_description: Hailing from Eotienses, Denton Patreus is a highly influential Imperial senator who holds the position of Admiral of the Fleet. He is popular with the Empire's citizenry thanks to his record of low taxation funded through aggressive economic and military conquests.
dentonpatreus_overview_expansion_ethos: Senator Patreus protects those under his care by providing vessels and personnel to bolster local security forces. Private contractors working for Patreus have an excellent track record for enforcing his will.
dentonpatreus_overview_preparation_ethos: In order to make systems more susceptible to his commanding persona, Senator Patreus offers an extensive line of credit to all parties interested in ordering bulk shipments of Imperial armaments.
dentonpatreus_overview_quotation1: Honour and honesty are vital attributes in a modern society.
dentonpatreus_overview_quotation2: It is with a singular purpose that the Empire will maintain the glory it has become accustomed to.
dentonpatreus_overview_quotation3: Any interference from outside of the Empire is an affront to our proud people. Such meddling must be crushed.
dentonpatreus_overview_quotation4: The Imperial Navy provides the ultimate societal safety net - something the Federal government should learn from.
dentonpatreus_overview_quotation5: We should use the Empire's traditional values to inform progress toward a technologically prosperous future.

deuringastruffles_info:
More of a lichen than the fungus that they resemble. They have a similar musty flavour to ancient Earth truffles, but the process of metabolising Deuringas's metal-rich rocks leaves trace amounts of metals on its surface - which is why Deuringas truffles must be shaved in preparation for eating.

This rare good is legal in all markets.
deuringastruffles_info_short: More of a lichen than a fungus. They have a similar musty flavour to ancient Earth truffles.
deuterium_info:
Produced by: Surface Mining only
Consumed by: Military and Industrial

Chemical formula 2H). Nearly all deuterium found across the galaxy was created in the Big Bang 13.8 billion years ago. Early 21st century attempts at creating fusion energy focused on using a combination of deuterium and tritium with mixed success.

diamond_info:
Produced by: Surface Mining only
Consumed by: Tourism, Terraforming, and Industrial

Chemical formula C. Diamond is a solid form of pure carbon with its atoms arranged in a crystalline structure. Still popular among socialites and the wealthy throughout occupied space, despite their common occurence across the galaxy.
diamond_info_short: Produced by: Surface Mining only Consumed by: Tourism, Terraforming, and Industrial Diamond is a solid form of pure carbon with its atoms arranged in a crystalline structure.
diamondback_armour_grade1_info: Hull reinforcement that provides standard protection against all types of attack.
diamondback_armour_grade2_info: Hull reinforcement using an advanced structure and higher quality compounds, offering improved protection against all types of attack.
diamondback_armour_grade3_info: Hull reinforcement using an advanced structure and military-grade compounds, offering superior protection against all types of attack.
diamondback_armour_mirrored_info: Hull reinforcement using a specially formulated structure, offering superior protection against thermal damage caused by energy weapons. It is vulnerable to projectile weapons and other kinetic attacks.
diamondback_armour_reactive_info: Hull reinforcement using a dynamically reactive, impact-resistant material offering superior protection against projectile weapons and other kinetic attacks. It is vulnerable to thermal damage caused by energy weapons.
diamondback_cockpit_info: Transparent protective canopy on a ship's cockpit that shields pilots from the many dangers of space travel.
diamondback_info:
Developed by Lakon Spaceways, the Diamondback Scout is a dual-purpose combat and exploration ship. Its 30 light-year jump range makes it popular with aspiring explorers, while its exceptional manoeuvrability makes it excellent at evading incoming fire. And with two medium and two small hardpoints, the Scout can also pack a punch.

The Diamondback Scout has been designed for small-size landing pads.
diamondbackxl_armour_grade1_info: Hull reinforcement that provides standard protection against all types of attack.
diamondbackxl_armour_grade2_info: Hull reinforcement using an advanced structure and higher quality compounds, offering improved protection against all types of attack.
diamondbackxl_armour_grade3_info: Hull reinforcement using an advanced structure and military-grade compounds, offering superior protection against all types of attack.
diamondbackxl_armour_mirrored_info: Hull reinforcement using a specially formulated structure, offering superior protection against thermal damage caused by energy weapons. It is vulnerable to projectile weapons and other kinetic attacks.
diamondbackxl_armour_reactive_info: Hull reinforcement using a dynamically reactive, impact-resistant material offering superior protection against projectile weapons and other kinetic attacks. It is vulnerable to thermal damage caused by energy weapons.
diamondbackxl_cockpit_info: Transparent protective canopy on a ship's cockpit that shields pilots from the many dangers of space travel.
diamondbackxl_info:
The Diamondback Explorer is a dual-role ship designed with both exploration and combat in mind. Sibling to the smaller Diamondback Scout, the Explorer's superior firepower and hardpoint array make it more flexible than its sister ship, while its long jump range and exceptional heat efficiency make it an excellent choice for explorers.

The Diamondback Explorer has been designed for small-size landing pads.

dredger_art_001_body: Artificer Log #748 Rictus XIII: The Long Dark stretches, and we move into it. Nothing but the low hum of the machine. Following the scent of salvage. The light-years flash by and my sensor readings tick them down, but I've long since stopped counting. Doesn't matter how far; we always get there in the end.
dredger_art_002_body: Artificer Log #756 Rictus XIII: Three days into the run. This is a good haul. A lot of useless scrap but there's been a battle here so we always find wheat amongst the chaff. FSD drives still salvageable, control units, uplinks, system drives. All the ingredients we need. The scoop buzzes on and I can feel my servos start to twitch with anticipation.
dredger_art_003_body: Artificer Log #771 Rictus XIII: The workshop is alive. Solder and seal. The spark of a welder. The heat of the forge. It's like we're resurrecting this material. Never ceases to fill me with a sense of belonging. I am a small part of this machine, but an integral part. Junkers they call us, but we are so much more. Craftsmen and mechanics and artisans all.
dredger_art_004_body: Artificer Log #776 Rictus XIII: Docking sequence was initiated successfully. It's only been eighteen months since we last locked onto a starport. No one debarked this time. What's the point? The gravity only weighs us down, makes us slow. It was a good haul this time; they seemed to like what we'd made. Even gave us some custom specs, asked if we could make something bespoke. I'll take a look later, no big deal. For now it's back off into the Long Dark... following the scent of salvage.
dredger_bvc_001_body: +++System Hack+++ Junker Log345/1: News fresh in. Been a massive battle in Maia. Thousands of ships in the mix. Death toll cataclysmic. Can't begin to express how stoked the crew is. Of course we plotted a course and polished the scoop! Engines to full!!
dredger_bvc_002_body: +++System Hack+++ Junker Log359/7: Nearly at Maia. Received comms from another dredge crew: Ferran scum been spotted in the area! Don't they know this swag is for Blue Viper Club? We won't be taking no greck from them! Don't care what it says in the Code.
dredger_bvc_003_body: +++System Hack+++ Junker Log364/0: Ferran guttersnipes already in the area but they haven't had a chance to dredge yet. Boosted engines to max, scoopers on full power. Humming all the way to that junk like tomorrow don't exist. BRING ON THE SCRAP!
dredger_bvc_004_body: +++System Hack+++ Junker Log369/5: They thought they could beat us, but they were too slow. As soon as we started scooping they backed right off. Cannibals shmannibals! Their bite don't live up to their rep. Blue Viper Club all the way!!
dredger_pha_001_body: Mayday Alert - Channel Encryption 34D-X: This is an all systems mayday. I'm Commander Hal Coultard and I'm trapped. I was taking palladium from Lave to Reorte when I ran straight into a dredger. Scoop just sucked me right in. I'd heard these guys were pretty oblivious to passing traffic but this is ridiculous. My ship is fried but I managed to eject. Now I'm trapped in the guts of this thing. Maybe I'll try and communicate with the crew. Then I could get them to drop me at the nearest station. It'll be a surprise when I send them the bill for a new ship next week!
dredger_pha_002_body: Mayday Alert - Channel Encryption 34D-X: Alert! I am in serious trouble here. I was moving through one of their tunnels - this place is like a maze of tubular corridors - and I saw one. It was fierce! And I mean looking-a-tiger-in-the-eye fierce. I almost messed my flight suit. I can't believe these things are human - all long limbs and cybernetics. They're like giant spiders. Maybe I won't communicate with them after all. Maybe I should just wait until they dock somewhere and sneak off. No one even needs to know I was here.
dredger_pha_003_body: Mayday Alert - Channel Encryption 34D-X: Mayday. Things have gone from bad to worse. I just hacked into their on-ship surveillance system and I've seen... things!! Rituals. Feeding frenzies. It's horrible. I need help. Someone. Anyone...
dredger_pha_004_body: Mayday Alert - Channel Encryption 34D-X: They've found me. They put out some kind of hail over the intercom - told me to come out of hiding. To be perfectly honest they sounded kind of nice. Even offered to have me for dinner. Maybe the ritual stuff was just a religious thing and they're not psychopathic killers after all. I'm sure it was all just a misunderstanding. They couldn't possibly be cannibals or anything. Could they. Could they?
dredger_scr_001_body: Pontifex Macharius [Scrivener Log VII-3]: Once more we ride the Long Dark, purging the black of its unholy detritus. We travel on a sea of flotsam, cleansing as we cruise through the filth, eradicating the taint of the Wasteful. Though a thankless task, it is one to which we are entirely suited - for we are the pure, the holy, the sanctified and blessed.
dredger_scr_002_body: Pontifex Macharius [Scrivener Log VII-5]: The magno-scoop sings its blessed hymn, as hydraulic teeth grind and blast furnaces immolate the detritus into naught but embers. We sail amid a vast belt of debris. A colossal slick of sewage among the vast ocean of emptiness, and we are here to purify it. The dredger sings its hallowed cant, joyous in its blessed labour between the stars.
dredger_scr_003_body:
Pontifex Macharius [Scrivener Log VII-8]: Oh day of days! Oh joy of joys! We have found lost travellers amongst the broken ships and floating wreckage. Survivors in the sea of salvage. Of course they were welcomed aboard, as are all the Wasteful who would seek the righteous path.

They balk at our visage, for we are alien to them. Vast spiders in the dark, and they the flies caught in our web. They fear we might smite them, not realising that we only wish to liberate their tainted souls. Some are reluctant, fretful, but I am sure with some gentle enticement they will throw off the shackles of their former lives, abandon the way of the Wasteful and embrace the tenets of the Scriveners like starving pilgrims to a feast.
dredger_scr_004_body: Pontifex Macharius [Scrivener Log VII-9]: All but one hearkened to the call of the Scriveners and they eagerly pledged their commitment - whether out of fear or devotion it matters not. The former Wasteful are now safely among the fold. Only one refused, no matter how I tried to envelop him within our virtuous wings. And so as the filth of the Long Dark must be cleansed, so the heretic was purged. It was a magnificent ceremony, the fires of the furnace blazed with his immolation, and as our prayers rose to a crescendo they drowned out his last cries with an immaculate hymn of beatitude.
dredger_til_001_body: Raphael of the Tillers - Log 234-4: We have plotted an interception vector after picking up a distress signal. There is a fleet - a civilian flotilla - under attack by an unknown enemy. We don't have any hardpoint capability aboard our dredger but we can't just leave these people. Surely there is something we can do...
dredger_til_002_body:
Raphael of the Tillers - Log 254-6: By the time we arrived it was all over. All that was left was devastation. I wept as we activated the scoop. It looked like thousands had died, but we still had our job to do.

One good thing did come of it. Among the devastation we found a cryo-pod. It didn't contain any human life, but some kind of fauna. Even with our extensive knowledge of xenoculture none of us could identify it. I am authorising further investigation.
dredger_til_003_body: Raphael of the Tillers - Log 262-3: After testing the alien fauna at some length we have discovered it contains some kind of sentience. This manifests most strongly when the sample, which to all intents and purposes looks like a terran shrub, is introduced to other mundane fauna. It seems to communicate, imbuing other samples with what can only be described as “life”. Further tests will be made.
dredger_til_004_body: Raphael of the Tillers - Log 295-5: After several weeks I gave permission for the alien shrub, which some have taken to calling “Adam”, to be planted with the other fauna aboard our dredger. The results were dramatic. Within days our cryo-gardens had grown beyond their limits. We opened the containment hatches, and within a few more days the dredger was filled with lush greenery. It converts so much of our carbon dioxide to oxygen that we have had to regulate life support to compensate. The dredger seems to have developed its own self-sustaining eco system. Something beautiful has flourished from the tragedy we encountered.

eagle_info:
Developed by Core Dynamics, the Eagle is a compact combat ship with peerless manoeuvrability. For many independent pilots it represents a natural progression from the Sidewinder, boasting superior cargo capacity and combat ability in addition to a better hardpoint array. These features are offset by a comparatively short jump range, however.

The Eagle has been designed for small-size landing pads.

edmundmahon_overview_control_ethos: By establishing diplomatic links and crafting bespoke legislation which enables swift membership, Prime Minister Mahon seeks to increase the number of systems loyal to the Alliance.
edmundmahon_overview_description: Edmund Mahon is the Prime Minister of the Alliance of Independent Systems. As the leader of the Alliance Assembly, he represents the union - based on political and economic interests - as a collective entity. Mahon is the only Prime Minister in Allied history to be elected to serve a second term.
edmundmahon_overview_expansion_ethos: Prime Minister Mahon galvanises his presence in systems by establishing greater governmental links and trade protectionism, designed to limit the potential for competing interests to gain influence.
edmundmahon_overview_preparation_ethos: Prime Minster Mahon aims to provide a broad range of trade agreements and other benefits to prospective members. While these terms typically favoured independent systems, recent amendments to some clauses have proven appealing to systems considering a change of allegiance.
edmundmahon_overview_quotation1: Each year we remember those brave souls who sacrificed themselves to ensure the Alliance was born free from Federal or Imperial control.
edmundmahon_overview_quotation2: The Alliance stands as a unifying force for independent systems with a common ethos of the individual's rights.
edmundmahon_overview_quotation3: Any independent system has the right to retain their independence. Allegiance can be offered but must never be imposed.
edmundmahon_overview_quotation4: The Federation condemns the Empire for its outdated traditions, while ignoring the financial slavery seen throughout its own society.
edmundmahon_overview_quotation5: We hear the Empire disparaging the Federation for not providing a financial safety net to its people - all while Imperial citizens face indentured servitude over matters of debt.

One of the most compact vessels on the market, the Imperial Courier is a lightweight combat ship from Gutamaya. With agility to rival the Viper Mk III, the Courier is adept at evading incoming fire, while its three medium hardpoints have made it popular with those who want a balance of power and style.

The Imperial Courier has been designed for small-size landing pads.

empire_eagle_info:
Based on Core Dynamics' Eagle, Gutamaya's Imperial Eagle places greater emphasis on speed and combat than its predecessor. The ship's armour and shields have been enhanced, and one of the small hardpoints of the original has been replaced with a medium hardpoint. Naturally, these features have made the ship heavier and less manoeuvrable than its predecessor, but the Imperial Eagle remains a solid choice for those seeking a high-speed attack ship.

empire_trader_armour_grade3_info: Hull reinforcement using an advanced structure and military-grade compounds, offering superior protection against all types of attack.
empire_trader_armour_mirrored_info: Hull reinforcement using a specially formulated structure, offering superior protection against thermal damage caused by energy weapons. It is vulnerable to projectile weapons and other kinetic attacks.
empire_trader_armour_reactive_info: Hull reinforcement using a dynamically reactive, impact-resistant material offering superior protection against projectile weapons and other kinetic attacks. It is vulnerable to thermal damage caused by energy weapons.
empire_trader_cockpit_info: Transparent protective canopy on a ship's cockpit that shields pilots from the many dangers of space travel.
empire_trader_info:
The very definition of a multipurpose ship, the Imperial Clipper is a versatile vessel well suited to a range of roles. A generous quantity of internal compartments has made it popular with miners, while a sizeable cargo hold and robust defences have endeared the vessel to traders. Impressive straight-line speed rounds out the ship's profile, and makes it one of the most distinguished members of the Gutamaya family.

The Imperial Clipper has been designed for large-size landing pads.
employeedirectory_info: A complete list of staff members with their relevant personal details.
employeedirectory_longinfo: A complete list of staff members with their relevant personal details.
employeeexpenses_info: Records of business expense claims and charges made to company credit accounts.
employeeexpenses_longinfo: Records of business expense claims and charges made to company credit accounts.
employeegeneticdata_info: Unique genetic data records for a settlement's past and current personnel.
employeegeneticdata_longinfo: Unique genetic data records for a settlement's past and current personnel.
employmenthistory_info: A detailed list of an individual’s prior employment, roles and professional experience.
employmenthistory_longinfo: A detailed list of an individual’s prior employment, roles and professional experience.
enableaimassistonfoot_description: Enable automatic aim guidance when using personal weapons.
enablecameralockon_description: When this option is enabled the camera will turn and lock to the UI panel.
enablemenugroups_description:
Allow some buttons to open a menu of multiple sub-control bindings when held.

Disabling this option could cause conflicts between the existing bindings which will need to be manually resolved.
encodedscandata_info:
Captured from settlement data point networks.

Scan data usually forms a large data set, with only a small quantity of pertinent information. For the most part these are easily analysed, but some sensor data has unusual properties and while this is often caused by a malfunction can yield some interesting results.
encodedscandata_info_short: Captured from settlement data point networks.
encripteddatastorage_info: It is sometimes safer to transport sensitive data physically and also quicker if immense quantities need transferring. They usually have little intrinsic value except to the organisation attempting to secure these items.
encripteddatastorage_info_short: They usually have little intrinsic value except to the organisation attempting to secure these items.
encryptedcorrespondence_info: Heavily encrypted data that is of little interest, although some hackers use it for training or practise, or simply enjoy the challenge of breaking the encryption. There is a limited black market for these items.
encryptedcorrespondence_info_short: Heavily encrypted data that is of little interest, although some hackers use it for training or practise, or simply enjoy the challenge of breaking the encryption.
encryptedfiles_info:
Captured from settlement data point networks. Known to be salvaged from signal sources.

Data files are often encrypted, on occasion a novel method of encyption can be encountered which is useful elsewhere.
encryptedfiles_info_short: Captured from settlement data point networks. Known to be salvaged from signal sources.
encryptedmemorychip_info: An integrated circuit designed to securely store software data.
encryptionarchives_info:
Discovered in private data beacons salvaged from deep space.

The nature of encrypted data makes it difficult to predict its contents, however certain forms of data have recognisable structures even when encrypted. This can then be used to break into the data and as such is highly prized in some quarters.
encryptionarchives_info_short: Discovered in private data beacons salvaged from deep space.
encryptioncodes_info:
Captured from settlement data point networks. Known to be salvaged from signal sources.

Encryption codes are typically very sensitive data because of their use in decrypting confidential information. In the right circumstances these can be captured remotely and as such are highly sought after by certain people.
encryptioncodes_info_short: Captured from settlement data point networks. Known to be salvaged from signal sources.
energycell_info: A single-use item that restores energy to suit batteries.
energydrinks_info: Refreshments designed to provide gratuitous amounts of energy. Ingredients are often arguably toxic, illegal or simply undisclosed.
energydrinks_info_short: Refreshments designed to provide gratuitous amounts of energy. Ingredients are often arguably toxic, illegal or simply undisclosed.
eng_baltanos_annotation_001: Each of our senses can be augmented to levels far beyond our natural abilities. It is no different from modifying your equipment.
eng_baltanos_annotation_002: The union of man and machine is a process that began thousands of years ago. Where will it ultimately lead?
eng_baltanos_annotation_003: Many generations of innovation have led to this meeting, Commander. Our trade is an offering to their memory.
eng_baltanos_annotation_004: Whether you pursue knowledge, profit or war, know that the Gods smile upon each technological marvel used in the chase.
eng_baltanos_annotation_005: I consider it a privilege every time I optimise the weapons and tools of another. Efficiency of action is one of humanity's ever-present goals.
eng_baltanos_annotation_firstaccess: You are most welcome in my place of worship, accordant. My name is Baltanos, honoured servant of the Hybrid Gods. I am eager to see what technology you have brought to me. Only through enhancement can we truly see our purpose.
eng_baltanos_callout_002: It is time to commune with the Hybrid Gods.
eng_baltanos_callout_003: Your return is most welcome, accordant.
eng_baltanos_callout_004: Through our tools we find truth. Let us seek it.
eng_baltanos_callout_005: My workshop is ready, Commander. As am I.
eng_baltanos_callout_firstaccess: Blessings of the Merged upon you. By Their design we meet in health and with focused spirits.
eng_baltanos_choose_equipment_001: Which artefact is to be sanctified?
eng_baltanos_choose_equipment_002: Which item do you wish to improve?
eng_baltanos_choose_slot: You must choose a slot, of course.
eng_baltanos_nextengineer: Thank you for your contribution. I shall pass on my recommendation to Yi Shen on your behalf. His work is truly divine, though a darkness clouds his soul. Should you meet him, be kind.
eng_baltanos_option_suit_improvedjumpass: A true sign of our mastery over nature.
eng_baltanos_option_suit_increasedo2capa: What better way to show one's faith?
eng_baltanos_option_suit_increasedsprint: One of the gods' many boons.
eng_baltanos_referraltask: My insight to the true path will be well-received by the influential here in Colonia. Bring me data which helps identify that audience and I will aid you in meeting a prominent engineer.
eng_baltanos_resourcedonate: Your donation is recognised and appreciated.
eng_baltanos_signoff_002: May the gods keep you curious.
eng_baltanos_signoff_003: Apply your gifts to the proper cause.
eng_billturner_annotation_001: What can I do for you this time? Let's go through my blueprints.
eng_billturner_annotation_002: Y'know what I think when someone stops by with work for me? I think: "Bill, it's going to be a good day."
eng_billturner_annotation_003: I'm glad I managed to secure a facility in Alioth. A lot happened in this system, even before the Alliance was founded. Anyway, what do you need from me?
eng_billturner_annotation_004: That's a nice ship you've got there. I've got enough blueprints here that'll make we can make it a little better, though.
eng_billturner_annotation_005: Are you still working with the Alliance, Commander? I'm probably biased, but I think they're the right choice for a pilot like you. Not a lot of 'questionable history' to worry about - disregarding a few power-hungry Councillors.
eng_billturner_annotation_firstaccess: Good to meet you at last, Commander. I'm Bill Turner, and I offer improvements to a wide range of scanners and ship utilities. I'm pretty good with tweaking plasma accelerators as well, if you have one installed.
eng_billturner_callout_003: Great to see you again, Commander.
eng_billturner_callout_004: Back again, huh? Must be a fan of my work.
eng_billturner_callout_firstaccess: Any friend of the Alliance is a friend of mine. Thanks for the supplies.
eng_billturner_signoff_001: Have a damn good time, Commander.
eng_billturner_signoff_002: Any time you need more work just stop by.
eng_billturner_signoff_004: I hope you find my blueprints useful.
eng_brootarquin_annotation_001: Assuming you have energy weapons installed on your vessel, I'd be glad to see them.
eng_brootarquin_annotation_002: Expecting trouble, are we? Then you've come to the right place. Let's explore how we can improve your hardpoints.
eng_brootarquin_annotation_003: I named this base Broo's Legacy for fairly obvious reasons. I hope that the advancements made in this workshop will continue long after I am gone. There is plenty to do in the meantime, however. Shall we?
eng_brootarquin_annotation_004: Some clients expect my highest grade blueprints right away. A reasonable request, I suppose. But I prefer to establish a productive relationship first. Trust means a lot these days.
eng_brootarquin_annotation_005: One can never have enough tea, I find. The pause in a schedule to prepare it, the aroma as it brews, the flavour. All very enjoyable. And now, fully refreshed, I offer you my services.
eng_brootarquin_annotation_firstaccess: Name's Broo Tarquin. I work on energy weapons of all types: beams, bursts or pulses, I'll have them firing to you preferred specifications. I can take bounty vouchers of your hands, as well. There is no reason why justice and wealth cannot walk hand in hand.
eng_brootarquin_callout_001: Welcome back. Readying your ship for battle?
eng_brootarquin_callout_003: How may I assist you today, Commander?
eng_brootarquin_callout_004: I will take your return as an endorsement of my work.
eng_brootarquin_callout_005: Well, if it isn't one of my regulars.
eng_brootarquin_callout_firstaccess: A member of the Pilots' Federation getting their hands dirty? Now that's what I like to see.
eng_brootarquin_signoff_002: Keep me in mind for future upgrades.
eng_brootarquin_signoff_003: Come back any time you wish.
eng_brootarquin_signoff_004: I'll be here if you need me.
eng_chloesedesi_annotation_001: This area of space is usually calm, at least compared to when I first came here. Thargoids were not happy that we colonised the place! But then when are they ever happy?
eng_chloesedesi_annotation_002: I miss working with ol' Ishmael. I'm proud of my own base, but that guy's just a nice person to be around, y'know? I learnt a lot from him.
eng_chloesedesi_annotation_003: New colonists make the move to this region of space every week. I hop over to the starports when I can, just to stay connected, you know. There's a good community spirit in our little enclave.
eng_chloesedesi_annotation_004: There was an Asp hovering in front of the base yesterday. You'd be surprised how often that happens. Anyway, let's start work!
eng_chloesedesi_annotation_005: Have you met Ram Tah? Palin says he's brilliant but I've always found him...I don't know. Intense? Still, can't argue with his achievements. Would love to work with him one day. Speaking of work, we should do some!
eng_chloesedesi_annotation_firstaccess: Nice to meet you! I'm Chloe; Chloe Sedesi. Former student of Professor Ishmael Palin and recent migrant to the Witch Head Nebula. I can smarten up your thrusters or frame shift drive, if that's what you need. I'll pay for survey data, too, if you grabbed any on your journey here. C'mon, I wanna look at your ship.
eng_chloesedesi_callout_001: You came back to my humble home! Well, incredibly expensive research installation.
eng_chloesedesi_callout_002: Back again, huh? I'm flattered, Commander.
eng_chloesedesi_callout_003: Oh hey, cookie. What do you have in mind this time?
eng_chloesedesi_callout_004: Hey! I'm already thinking about how to tweak your ship. Up for it?
eng_chloesedesi_callout_005: We totally have to work out a secret handshake if you're gonna be a regular.
eng_chloesedesi_callout_firstaccess: I had a feeling we'd be working together at some point, Commander. Good to know my instincts are still calibrated.
eng_chloesedesi_signoff_004: Stay safe out there in the black!
eng_colonelbrisdekker_annotation_001: A lot of history in this system, Commander. Hard to imagine that we all shared the same world not so long ago.
eng_colonelbrisdekker_annotation_002: What do you need, Commander? Just select the blueprint that interests you and let me do the rest.
eng_colonelbrisdekker_annotation_003: If you have materials with you then I'll implement any design you want. No such thing as a free lunch here.
eng_colonelbrisdekker_annotation_004: If a pilot has a bounty on their head then it makes no difference what they've done. In my view, they're fair game. A good interdictor will help you subject them to the justice they deserve.
eng_colonelbrisdekker_annotation_005: I'm always willing to make time for my repeat clients. Let's get started.
eng_colonelbrisdekker_annotation_firstac: At ease, Commander. Colonel Dekker, at your service. I have a few FSD blueprints for operation and interdiction. They're based on ad-hoc adjustments picked up from my time in the Federal Navy, but refined in this facility. I'm ready when you are.
eng_colonelbrisdekker_callout_002: Figured you'd be back before long.
eng_colonelbrisdekker_callout_003: Good to see you at the Yard again.
eng_colonelbrisdekker_callout_004: Still keeping Federal space secure, Commander?
eng_colonelbrisdekker_callout_firstacces: Seems you know how to use those weapons after all. I'm impressed.
eng_didivatermann_annotation_001: Since you're here, I ought to mention that I have a market interface installed at the base. You can sell goods while docked, and I'd appreciate the trade. Now, do you need some mods?
eng_didivatermann_annotation_002: Weapons tech is improving with every generation, so shield tech needs to keep up. There isn't much point flying a glass cannon without it.
eng_didivatermann_annotation_003: Some of my peers from years gone by have retired once they had the wealth. But, between you and me, retirement sounds awfully boring. Let's evaluate your shield loadout.
eng_didivatermann_annotation_004: A good frame shift drive will carry you far across the galaxy. But a good shield can help you make it home again.
eng_didivatermann_annotation_005: Is that a new vessel? Maybe just a different paint job? Never mind - once I have perused the internals I'll know for sure.
eng_didivatermann_annotation_firstaccess: Good to make your acquaintance. I'm Didi Vatermann. I'm very pleased with the Lavian Brandy you brought me, but there's work to be done before I can sample it. My focus is shield tech, and my designs will hold the galaxy's dangers at bay for a little longer. May I examine your ship?
eng_didivatermann_callout_001: Hello, Commander. Interested in some upgrades?
eng_didivatermann_callout_002: Welcome back. What can I do for you?
eng_didivatermann_callout_003: Your custom is always appreciated, Commander.
eng_didivatermann_callout_004: Lovely to see you again. We must share a drink one of these days.
eng_didivatermann_callout_005: Our paths cross once more, Commander.
eng_didivatermann_callout_firstaccess: Fellow traders are always welcome, Commander. I'm glad to have you here.
eng_didivatermann_signoff_005: Time for a beverage, I think.
eng_dominogreen_annotation_001: Alright, let's get to work. I can fix your gear up something fierce.
eng_dominogreen_annotation_002: I can't remember what I did for you last time, but I'm sure it was great. Let's do more of that!
eng_dominogreen_annotation_003: My blueprints are great for someone who likes to work from distance. By that I mean a long-range fighter. Not, like, remotely. That's kinda boring.
eng_dominogreen_annotation_004: I can fix up anything you need, Commander. Well, anything I have a design for, anyway. Don't ask me for bionic ears or a third arm or whatever.
eng_dominogreen_annotation_005: So what will it be? Suit mods? Weapons mods? Brain mods? Actually, I can't do brain mods. Last time I got yelled at by some guy with a moustache.
eng_dominogreen_annotation_firstaccess: What do you want? Haha, just kidding. You clearly want equipment upgrades so you can go save the galaxy or something. Whatever, I'm game. Name's Domino Green, and you're standing in my office.
eng_dominogreen_callout_001: Back again, huh? Did you get all the baddies yet? Your medal's probably in the nearest Drop'n'Go.
eng_dominogreen_callout_002: Just can't stay away? I don't blame you, I am pretty great. Wow, that sounded arrogant, didn't it?
eng_dominogreen_callout_003: Didn't I just see you here? Or was that someone else? Ah, it doesn't matter.
eng_dominogreen_callout_004: Welcome back! So nice to see you, Commander...uhm...y'know, you. Yeah. Yay!
eng_dominogreen_callout_005: Hi. You're here for mods, right? Because if you're looking for coffee you've come to the wrong place.
eng_dominogreen_callout_firstaccess: Ugh. This office is too bright. Don't you think?
eng_dominogreen_choose_slot: Just pick out a slot for me to work on.
eng_dominogreen_nextengineer: Oh yeah, I asked you for this stuff. Thanks! Okay, so there's this guy called Kit Fowler. He thinks the galaxy's about to explode or something and broadcasts these crazy paranoid rants from his apocalypse bunker. But Kit's engineering work is ace, so I'll send you his details.
eng_dominogreen_option_suit_backpackcapa: I like stuff. Do you like stuff? Carry more of it!
eng_dominogreen_option_suit_improvedrada: If you like pings, this will ping your pings to be pingier.
eng_dominogreen_option_suit_reducedtoolb: Gotta be economical with your batteries, Commander.
eng_dominogreen_option_weapon_range: Sometimes the best way to introduce yourself is from far, far away.
eng_dominogreen_option_weapon_stability: If you're all jittery this will help steady your hands.
eng_dominogreen_purchase_suit_backpackca: You're all set. Time to go shopping!
eng_dominogreen_purchase_suit_reducedtoo: Less time at the recharge station it is.
eng_dominogreen_purchase_weapon_stabilit: They'll be calling you 'Captain Composure' now.
eng_dominogreen_referraltask: Actually, if we're gonna do business and all...I have a bit of a business relationship with Push. It keeps me focused when my brain's all 'waaahhh'. Y'know? Anyway, bring me some and I'll make it worth your while.
eng_dominogreen_resourcedonate: Oh...This'll keep me focused for a while.
eng_dominogreen_signoff_002: Have fun! Or don't. You do you.
eng_dominogreen_signoff_004: Good, thanks for coming. See ya.
eng_eleanorbresa_annotation_001: I've spent half my life applying other people's blueprints. Now I'm offering my own designs at last. I'm confident they'll meet your specs, Commander.
eng_eleanorbresa_annotation_002: My designs will help you in most combat situations. Eight out of ten clients will testify to that! The other two probably won't be available.
eng_eleanorbresa_annotation_003: Never stay in one place too long. Learned that from Mama Bresa: 'Soon as those feet start itching you'd better start walking,' she'd say. Guess I walked pretty far to end up here!
eng_eleanorbresa_annotation_004: Can't remember the last time I got a full eight hours sleep. It's a good thing I'm enjoying this little enterprise! Sure is a lot of work. Speaking of which, what do you need?
eng_eleanorbresa_annotation_005: There are a lot of engineers in this region. Most of us come to Colonia for a fresh start, I think. Twenty-two thousand light years cleans your slate as well as anything.
eng_eleanorbresa_annotation_firstaccess: Eleanor Bresa at your service, Commander. Have you been in Colonia for long? I'm kind of new myself, but I've already secured plenty of clients. I learned how to generate buzz from the best, heh. So what can I do for you?
eng_eleanorbresa_callout_001: Think big, Commander. Let's make it happen.
eng_eleanorbresa_callout_002: I've got the highest quality combat mods in Colonia.
eng_eleanorbresa_callout_003: What's the weather like? Let me guess - outrageously cold.
eng_eleanorbresa_callout_004: Oh, hi! I was just, uh, having a moment.
eng_eleanorbresa_callout_005: If you keep coming back I'll have to find you a basket to sleep in.
eng_eleanorbresa_callout_firstaccess: Welcome to the best engineering service in the galaxy!
eng_eleanorbresa_choose_equipment_002: What would you like to modify?
eng_eleanorbresa_nextengineer: These look great! I'll go through them in a while. First I'll message Yi Shen for you, as agreed. The guy's a wizard with mods but less great with people. I'll tell him that you're a customer worth having. Hopefully it'll help.
eng_eleanorbresa_option_suit_increasedam: This will help in longer firefights.
eng_eleanorbresa_option_suit_increasedme: They'll regret invading your personal space.
eng_eleanorbresa_option_weapon_backpackr: Let the tech do the work.
eng_eleanorbresa_option_weapon_reloadspe: Less downtime makes all the difference.
eng_eleanorbresa_purchase_suit_improveda: Maybe I should put a logo on this one.
eng_eleanorbresa_purchase_suit_increased: Great decision. Let's get that ready.
Don't get in too much trouble.
eng_eleanorbresa_purchase_weapon_clipsiz: I'll be done before you know it.
eng_eleanorbresa_referraltask: Mama Bresa always said engineering is about taking someone else's idea and making it better. Bring me some digital designs to help the inspiration flow. I'll help you make contact with one of Colonia's finest techs as thanks.
eng_eleanorbresa_resourcedonate: That's just the design style I wanted. Thanks!
eng_eleanorbresa_signoff_001: Don't be shy about recommending me, Commander.
eng_eleanorbresa_signoff_002: Drop in any time. Safe travels.
eng_eleanorbresa_signoff_003: Always happy to work with the Pilots' Federation.
eng_eleanorbresa_signoff_004: Goodbye! Be sure to tell your friends and family about me.
eng_eleanorbresa_signoff_005: I hope your next journey is your best one yet.
eng_elviramartuuk_annotation_001: Every so often someone asks me about my life before this workshop. They tend not to ask a second time. You wouldn't make the same error, would you?
eng_elviramartuuk_annotation_002: I try not to waste a client's time if I can avoid it. It's unprofessional. But some of my regulars pull the most amusing faces if their orders take longer than expected.
eng_elviramartuuk_annotation_003: Soontill relics fascinate me. The engravings are beautiful, but so far impossible to decipher. We know almost nothing about the culture that created them, too. How many other civilizations existed in our galaxy?
eng_elviramartuuk_annotation_004: You can have any of my designs that you can afford. Materials don't come cheap.
eng_elviramartuuk_annotation_005: I don't travel much myself at the moment, but I'm still interested in survey data. You can sell it here at the base. I'd be grateful.
eng_elviramartuuk_annotation_firstaccess: Elvira Martuuk, at your service. Since you've already got some light years on your record, you should be interested in the drive designs I have. I know a few tricks for shields and thrusters, too. Are you interested?
eng_elviramartuuk_callout_001: What do you have in mind, Commander?
eng_elviramartuuk_callout_002: Hello again. Have your travels been enjoyable?
eng_elviramartuuk_callout_003: I'm always glad to see you, Commander.
eng_elviramartuuk_callout_004: I'm pleased you're here. The workshop can get lonely at times.
eng_elviramartuuk_callout_005: Just couldn't stay away, hm? Good. I'm ready for a new assignment.
eng_elviramartuuk_callout_firstaccess: You're willing to embrace the grandeur of our galaxy. I like that trait in those I deal with.
eng_elviramartuuk_signoff_005: I'll be here if you want me.
eng_etiennedorn_annotation_001: In the past, I have been accused of ulterior motives regarding the recovered escape pods I acquire. Baseless, of course. I have only good intentions for the poor souls within.
eng_etiennedorn_annotation_002: People are too loud. They always talk about themselves, their problems, their insignificant wants. Quite frankly, the occasional client is as much as I am willing to endure.
eng_etiennedorn_annotation_003: I am the master of this facility, Commander. Every aspect of its operation has my explicit oversight. Unsurprisingly, it all runs as smooth as mercury.
eng_etiennedorn_annotation_004: What may I assist you with this time? Just select one of the many blueprints while I assess the materials you have to trade.
eng_etiennedorn_annotation_005: I may consider using your likeness for one of my next mechanical creations. What do you think?
eng_etiennedorn_annotation_firstaccess: My name is Etienne Dorn. No doubt you have heard of my brilliance in a variety of engineering disciplines. Scanners, weaponry, ship power, even life support - I am quite masterful in many fields. Not to mention my advances in the field of robotics. I suppose it is arrogant to highlight my talents so openly, but I only speak the truth. Let me show you.
eng_etiennedorn_callout_001: Should I take your return as tacit approval?
eng_etiennedorn_callout_002: I trust my talents are to your liking?
eng_etiennedorn_callout_003: How can I assist you this time, I wonder?
eng_etiennedorn_callout_004: I ordered my robots to leave us alone. Some find them...distasteful.
eng_etiennedorn_callout_firstaccess: Those pods are acceptable. Let's get down to business.
eng_etiennedorn_signoff_002: Return if you feel the need.
eng_felicityfarseer_annotation_001: Jump range is all well and good, but don't neglect your other equipment when exploring. I once had to fix a leaking life support component with duct tape and a stick of gum.
eng_felicityfarseer_annotation_002: You've got some light years behind you now, Commander. Should I be jealous yet?
eng_felicityfarseer_annotation_003: I must say that it warms my heart having so many visitors seek out my knowledge. It means all those years I spent in the depths of our galaxy meant something.
eng_felicityfarseer_annotation_004: I'm rather curious to see what modules you have brought me this time. Let us not delay any longer than necessary!
eng_felicityfarseer_annotation_005: Have you seen anything unusual during your voyages among the stars? I remember one time when I found the... hm, I probably shouldn't mention that. Shall we examine your modules?
eng_felicityfarseer_annotation_firstacce: Just call me Felicity, dear. I'm not one for standing on ceremony. I dabble in various ship functions, with plenty of designs to browse. But I am quite fond of my frame shift drive modifications. Plenty of explorers have passed through here before departing on a grand adventure. Perhaps you will be one of them.
eng_felicityfarseer_callout_001: Welcome, Commander. How goes your journey through the void?
eng_felicityfarseer_callout_002: It's good to see you again, Commander. I know a kindred spirit when I see one.
eng_felicityfarseer_callout_003: Your voyages must be fascinating, just as mine were.
eng_felicityfarseer_callout_004: Wherever you intend to travel next, I should be able to help.
eng_felicityfarseer_callout_005: How many new horizons have you seen since last we met?
eng_felicityfarseer_callout_firstaccess: I recognise the look in your eyes, Commander. The void has weaved its spell on you.
eng_heratani_annotation_001: Would you like me to look at your power systems? My designs are quite useful.
eng_heratani_annotation_002: Your contributions to my work are highly appreciated. I certainly hope they continue.
eng_heratani_annotation_003: I appreciate any Pilots' Federation member who chooses to work with the Empire.
eng_heratani_annotation_004: Let me take a look at your ship. I haven't had an engaging assignment in a while.
eng_heratani_annotation_005: I'm relieved that you're here for more work. It demonstrates that good service is possible without the need for artificial camaraderie.
eng_heratani_annotation_firstaccess: Welcome to my facility, Commander. I am Hera Tani. Most of my clients seek improvement to their ship's power, but I dabble in sensor and surface scanner modifications too. Thank for you the cigars, of course. I wouldn't wish to seem ungrateful.
eng_heratani_callout_002: What brings you to The Jet's Hole?
eng_heratani_callout_003: Your repeated visits are noted, Commander.
eng_heratani_callout_005: Welcome. I trust the journey was pleasant?
eng_heratani_callout_firstaccess: Another citizen of the Empire? I'd be honoured to offer my services.
eng_heroferrari_annotation_001: My work tends to help people move. Shots that don't hit you can't hurt. Would you like to see the designs for yourself?
eng_heroferrari_annotation_002: I was just about to continue a painting I've been working on, but I suspect you've brought me something more interesting.
eng_heroferrari_annotation_003: You'll excuse me if I skip the small talk. I have some tea brewing in my private quarters that I don't want to spoil.
eng_heroferrari_annotation_004: As long as you have the necessary goods, I can make you what you need.
eng_heroferrari_annotation_005: I could tell you some fascinating stories about my career prior to the workshop. I'm not going to, but I could.
eng_heroferrari_annotation_firstaccess: Don't believe we've met before, and I've got a good memory. I'm Hero. If you're spending materials, my work will help you in most field situations. A gun-for-hire should appreciate that, and you look like you've worked a few contracts.
eng_heroferrari_back_005: Take a look at my other mods.
eng_heroferrari_callout_001: Well at least I didn't scare you away last time.
eng_heroferrari_callout_002: Welcome back. Need a little more spring in your step?
eng_heroferrari_callout_003: Isn't this a nice surprise. Repeat business is always welcome.
eng_heroferrari_callout_004: Just tell me what you need, Commander. The less questions the better.
eng_heroferrari_callout_005: Good to see you again. Let's get to work.
eng_heroferrari_choose_equipment_001: Where do you want the work?
eng_heroferrari_choose_slot: Which slot should I fix up?
eng_heroferrari_nextengineer: Thanks for the data; this will be very useful. In return, I'll point you towards one of the smartest men I know: Wellington Beck. For top quality mods he's definitely a name worth remembering.
eng_heroferrari_option_suit_improvedjump: Some well-placed enhancements will increase your agility.
eng_heroferrari_option_suit_increasedo2c: This mod is popular for extended field operations.
eng_heroferrari_option_suit_increasedspr: This mod will help you go faster for longer.
eng_heroferrari_option_weapon_handling: A good weapon should be smooth to use.
eng_heroferrari_option_weapon_suppressio: Hitting your target before they hit you is ideal.
eng_heroferrari_referraltask: In fact, maybe you can help me out. New automated weapons are sketched out every day. There's always a new calculation or alloy variant being tested. Bring me defence data to help inspire my ideas.
eng_heroferrari_resourcedonate: Good. This will help me with my designs.
eng_judenavarro_annotation_001: What did you have in mind, Commander? You've seen my mod designs. With a few materials we can fix them in place.
eng_judenavarro_annotation_002: I don't get many social calls these days. What are you after?
eng_judenavarro_annotation_003: Just tell me what you're after this time. With luck, it'll carry you through the next fight you find yourself in.
eng_judenavarro_annotation_004: Are we working on the suit or the firearm? Maybe both, if you have the resources. I'll take whatever you can spare.
eng_judenavarro_annotation_005: Found any worthy causes recently? I guess so, if you still need my help. I don't get many pacifists passing through here, if you catch my meaning.
eng_judenavarro_annotation_firstaccess: Good to meet you, Commander. I'm Jude, and I'm happy to take a look at any suits or weapons that you want to improve. Make sure you use your gear responsibly, though. The galaxy already has enough people exploiting military tech to step over the less fortunate.
eng_judenavarro_callout_001: Let me guess: You want a little extra to take into combat.
eng_judenavarro_callout_002: Welcome back. You got some work for me?
eng_judenavarro_callout_003: I'm glad you're still fighting, Commander.
eng_judenavarro_callout_004: Time to go to work. What do you need?
eng_judenavarro_callout_005: Well, look who it is. Glad to see you back at the base.
eng_judenavarro_callout_firstaccess: Now here's someone who would appreciate some quality mods.
eng_judenavarro_choose_slot: Which slot do you want a mod for?
eng_judenavarro_nextengineer: If you're looking for additional work, I recommend a colleague of mine. Terra Velasquez. She can be a little feisty, but her work is excellent. I'll send you the details.
eng_judenavarro_option_suit_improvedarmo: If you're expecting weapons pointing your way, this might help.
eng_judenavarro_option_suit_increasedamm: A little extra goes a long way.
eng_judenavarro_option_suit_increasedmel: Let's add some venom to your swing.
eng_judenavarro_option_weapon_clipsize: This offers a little extra time in the fight.
eng_judenavarro_option_weapon_reloadspee: Cutting downtime between exchanges can make all the difference.
eng_judenavarro_purchase_suit_improvedar: All finished. A little help rarely hurts.
eng_judenavarro_purchase_suit_increaseda: All done. You'll have an edge in combat now.
eng_judenavarro_purchase_suit_increasedm: I can make that work. Smart choice.
eng_judenavarro_purchase_weapon_clipsize: Your enemies won't know what hit them.
eng_judenavarro_purchase_weapon_reloadsp: Make sure your targets deserve the wrath you'll be bringing.
eng_judenavarro_referraltask: I try to keep a stock of genetic repair meds at the base. Don't concern yourself with the reasons. Bring me some and I'll point you towards a talented friend of mine.
eng_judenavarro_signoff_003: Keep up the good fight, Commander.
eng_judenavarro_signoff_005: I'll be here if you need me.
eng_juriishmaak_annotation_001: Preparation is everything in combat. High quality sensors will help in this regard.
eng_juriishmaak_annotation_002: I heard about your recent exploits. Very nice. And before you ask: yes, I like to stay informed about all my regular clients.
eng_juriishmaak_annotation_003: Shall we get some modifications in place? Of course we should. Why else would you be here?
eng_juriishmaak_annotation_004: If you know your opponent's loadout before a battle you know what to expect, how to counter, and what you need to do to win.
eng_juriishmaak_annotation_005: Once you've selected a design I'll get to work immediately. Only the best service for the Pilots' Federation.
eng_juriishmaak_annotation_firstaccess: Welcome to Pater's Memorial, Commander. You may call me Mr Ishmaak. I have designs to improve ship sensors, a variety of scanners and most launcher weapons. You can also hand in bounty vouchers or combat bonds here. I've spent a lot of my life fighting, and I know how much the credits help to prepare.
eng_juriishmaak_callout_005: My tools are ready to start work immediately.
eng_juriishmaak_callout_firstaccess: Nice ship. It could be better, though. You've come to the right place.
eng_kitfowler_annotation_001: You're here for modifications, aren't you? It would be very suspicious if you weren't.
eng_kitfowler_annotation_002: Let's not procrastinate. What do you need?
eng_kitfowler_annotation_003: Since you're here, can I be of service? I offer excellent designs, top quality craftsmanship...and the truth.
eng_kitfowler_annotation_004: Did you have a modification in mind? We shouldn't delay, in case they think we're collaborating.
eng_kitfowler_annotation_005: Let's get down to work. I'm sure you're a busy individual, with many contracts to pursue.
eng_kitfowler_annotation_firstaccess: Welcome to my base, Commander. I'm running a full background check and biometric data scan on you, the results of which will be stored locally. If you have any issue with this, you can leave. Of course, there is nothing you need to hide from me...right?
eng_kitfowler_callout_002: I'm trusting that your ship is clean.
eng_kitfowler_callout_003: Ah, Commander. You...weren't ordered here, were you?
eng_kitfowler_callout_004: A fan of my radio show! Yes, yes, come in!
eng_kitfowler_callout_005: Your ship's being analysed for tracking devices.
eng_kitfowler_callout_firstaccess: I'm not telling you where I get my infor-...Wait, you're somebody else. A customer. Forget I said anything.
eng_kitfowler_choose_equipment_001: Do you want suit or weapon enhancements?
eng_kitfowler_choose_equipment_002: Well? A suit or a gun?
eng_kitfowler_choose_slot: Which slot did you have in mind?
eng_kitfowler_nextengineer: Your contribution to my personal safety is noted, Commander. Listen: there are very few people in this galaxy that I trust. Yarden Bond is one of them, and her talent for engineering arguably rivals my own. I'll forward her information to you, and suggest that you make contact soon.
eng_kitfowler_option_suit_increasedammor: If you plan on extended firefights, this will be of use.
eng_kitfowler_option_suit_increasedshiel: Sometimes they really are out to get you. This will help.
eng_kitfowler_option_weapon_backpackrelo: This modification will assist your damage output.
eng_kitfowler_option_weapon_clipsize: This will offer extra utility in combat.
eng_kitfowler_purchase_suit_increasedamm: You'll certainly be more effective in combat now.
eng_kitfowler_purchase_suit_increasedmel: Consider your field options suitably expanded.
eng_kitfowler_purchase_suit_increasedshi: Equipment utility should never be overlooked.
eng_kitfowler_purchase_weapon_backpackre: Done. That'll get the chips out of their brains, so to speak.
eng_kitfowler_purchase_weapon_clipsize: There. Survivability is an admirable trait.
eng_kitfowler_referraltask: Before we begin, I have a request. There are always new ways to spy on each other, Commander. I can never have enough eyes and ears.  Bring me surveillance equipment and I'll consider introducing you to an associate of mine.
eng_kitfowler_resourcedonate: Your donation will be anonymous, of course.
eng_kitfowler_signoff_001: Leave the base quickly, won't you.
eng_kitfowler_signoff_004: Until next time...if they let you live.
eng_leicheung_annotation_001: People always argue whether strong shields or a tough hull is better for their ship. I say, why would you want to find out?
eng_leicheung_annotation_002: I'm comfortable here in the Rest. Explorers tell me about their expeditions and all the amazing finds out in the galaxy, but it's never much interested me. I have my kin, my family, everything I need here. Why leave?
eng_leicheung_annotation_003: I just got lucky with a talent for engineering. That's the reason people come here. You think I'm smart having people bring me gold for it? You should meet my nanna. She'd have them bringing void opals.
eng_leicheung_annotation_004: I like your ship. I think I can do things with her that'll have you smiling. Let's take a look at the modules.
eng_leicheung_annotation_005: Someone here before you accused me of being too friendly. Imagine that! 'You should be less friendly. Be sterner.' Haha, I thought that was silly thing to say. Oh well. We should start work.
eng_leicheung_annotation_firstaccess: I appreciate the gold. It's funny how pilots are willing to bring me units of it just for workshop access. I'm Lei, and I can improve your shielding, sensors and surface probes. There is also a market facility you can trade on, which would please my kin.
eng_leicheung_callout_001: I'm pleased that a fully-fledged Commander is interested in my wares.
eng_leicheung_callout_002: Are you here for mods or trade? Either way, it would be my pleasure.
eng_leicheung_callout_003: Welcome. I'm glad to see you at the Rest again.
eng_leicheung_callout_004: May the galaxy bring you good fortune, Commander.
eng_leicheung_callout_005: You grace us with your visit, Commander.
eng_leicheung_callout_firstaccess: I'm guessing you've heard what I can do with shield tech. Let's begin.
eng_leicheung_signoff_004: Please visit next time you're in the area
eng_lizryder_annotation_001: I'm selective with picking my friends these days. If I come across as rude...well, that's because I am. But don't take it personal.
eng_lizryder_annotation_002: Are we launching or surviving the booms today? Maybe both, if you're really lucky.
eng_lizryder_annotation_003: A friend of mine used to say that all problems can be resolved with a big enough explosion. Makes sense. I mean, all problems were created by one, too.
eng_lizryder_annotation_004: The sooner we get your mods in place, the sooner you can be on your way.
eng_lizryder_annotation_005: I guess the Pilots' Federation types like yourself bring me interesting work. Good thing, too. Wouldn't want all the arrogance to be for nothing, would we?
eng_lizryder_annotation_firstaccess: I imagine you're a useful person to know. I'm Liz Ryder. If you want something more than a standard launcher can give, I can get it done. I know a few entry-level tweaks to protect your hull, as well. Tell you what, let's just look at my designs. Saves me talking too long.
eng_lizryder_callout_001: Did you have a nice trip? Eh, I'm not really interested.
eng_lizryder_callout_002: You're not here for small-talk, so let's get started.
eng_lizryder_callout_003: You're back. Need some more work?
eng_lizryder_callout_004: Welcome back. Shall I get my tools ready?
eng_lizryder_callout_firstaccess: You're a pilot with good connections. Welcome to my workshop.
eng_lorijameson_annotation_001: Done much exploring recently? I considered joining one of those exploration fleets we've seen the last few years, but my work here kept me too busy. Maybe next time.
eng_lorijameson_annotation_002: What did you have in mind this time? Just point out the module and let me work my magic.
eng_lorijameson_annotation_003: It's been kinda quiet around here recently. Only kidding! Shinrarta Dezhra never stops. There's so much going on! I guess you Commanders know how to keep busy.
eng_lorijameson_annotation_004: It's weird having a memorial in your family's name, especially since it's such a popular starport. That's part of why I clarify the connection when I introduce myself. I can see people's brains churning if I don't.
eng_lorijameson_annotation_005: I need a vacation, I think. Been cooped up in this base for too long. Don't get me wrong, I love the work. I just think I need a change of scenery. Never mind all that, though; what have you brought me?
eng_lorijameson_annotation_firstaccess: I'm Lori Jameson, and before you ask: yeah, I'm related to THOSE Jamesons. I've established a bunch of designs at this base. They're good for ship functionality: scanners, scoops, refineries, life support mods, that kinda thing. Wanna take a look?
eng_lorijameson_callout_001: Yeah, I remember you. How's it going?
eng_lorijameson_callout_002: Nice ship you have there. She's a real beauty.
eng_lorijameson_callout_003: Hi, Commander. Been having fun without me?
eng_lorijameson_callout_004: I saw your callsign on the scanner as you docked. All good?
eng_lorijameson_callout_005: Commander! I'm real happy to see you again.
eng_lorijameson_callout_firstaccess: So you know which side of the crosshairs to sit on. I like it. We can deal.
eng_marcoqwent_annotation_001: Sirius Corp keeps me busy enough as it is. How much of my time do you need?
eng_marcoqwent_annotation_002: Sirius Corp gets a bad rep in some systems, where they're branded as an evil megacorp trying to monopolise the galaxy. I've never seen evidence to support the claims myself. Sure, it wants profits and influence. Who doesn't?
eng_marcoqwent_annotation_003: My professional situation is tailored to my preference. I share my research with Sirius Corp from time to time, and it pays for this facility. Which means I can work freelance, with pilots like yourself, whenever I choose.
eng_marcoqwent_annotation_004: A ship's power system is the most vital piece of equipment. Doesn't matter about your jump range, how many hardpoints you've loaded or the strength of your shields. Without power you're just sitting in a metal box, floating through the void.
eng_marcoqwent_annotation_005: Thanks for stopping by. I've got some free time to work on your ship. In case you weren't aware, you can trade commodities here as well. You are in the Sirius system.
eng_marcoqwent_annotation_firstaccess: I'm Marco. Elvira told me about you, and she's usually a good judge of character. I work with power systems, so I can give you more options in that area depending on your flying style. May I take a look at your ship?
eng_marcoqwent_callout_001: I can have that ship purring by the time we're done.
eng_marcoqwent_callout_002: Do those power modules of yours need a tune-up?
eng_marcoqwent_callout_003: Back again, Commander. More upgrades, I suppose?
eng_marcoqwent_callout_004: You're becoming quite the regular, Commander.
eng_marcoqwent_callout_005: A familiar face is always welcome here.
eng_marcoqwent_callout_firstaccess: You earned a Sirius permit and found the terminals I requested. Impressive, Commander.
eng_marcoqwent_signoff_004: See you when I see you.
eng_marshahicks_annotation_001: Shall we have a look at that vessel of yours?
eng_marshahicks_annotation_002: What do you need this time, Commander?
eng_marshahicks_annotation_003: There is no need to learn more about each other, Commander. How can I help you?
eng_marshahicks_annotation_004: My designs are fairly flexible. Do you know what you want?
eng_marshahicks_annotation_005: You should already know if you prefer kinetic or energy weapons. If it's the former, I can improve them.
eng_marshahicks_annotation_firstaccess: I'm Marsha. I'll be frank with you: I much prefer working to chatting with strangers, so you'll excuse me for getting to your requests. With that said, my designs are for cannons, limpet controllers and a few ship functions.
eng_marshahicks_callout_005: Good to see you're still alive.
eng_marshahicks_callout_firstaccess: Thanks for the ore. What do you need?
eng_melbrandon_annotation_001: I've never stopped in my pursuit of knowledge. There are far more questions than answers, of course. But every new discovery furthers my understanding of the technology that drives us forward.
eng_melbrandon_annotation_002: Each of us has a thread within the tapestry of human existence. I do hope you're making the most of yours. Let's work on your ship.
eng_melbrandon_annotation_003: Before we start: a lot of my clients have mentioned pirate activity along nearby trade routes. Do investigate for yourself, if you feel so inclined.
eng_melbrandon_annotation_004: Some engineers of note have specialised in modifying a single aspect of ship performance. I consider that approach quite limiting, but to each their own.
eng_melbrandon_annotation_005: What did you have in mind, Commander? Have a look through my various designs, and let me know when you've found one matching your requirements.
eng_melbrandon_annotation_firstaccess: I'm Mel Brandon. Here at The Brig, I've established a library of blueprints to improve a ship's agility, shielding and damage output. I can also modify frame shift drives to meet your needs. If you wanted I could show you some card tricks too, but I'm pretty sure that isn't why you've come.
eng_melbrandon_callout_001: That ship of yours has character. Or maybe it's the pilot in charge of it?
eng_melbrandon_callout_002: You're just the client I had in mind. I enjoy working with a pilot of substance.
eng_melbrandon_callout_003: A pilot of your skill is always welcome, Commander.
eng_melbrandon_callout_004: Good to see you, as always. I hope the Council has kept you busy.
eng_melbrandon_callout_005: You must be pleased with my skills to visit once again.
eng_melbrandon_callout_firstaccess: I'll never turn away those that stand up against the trouble-makers of the galaxy.
eng_melbrandon_signoff_004: Be a positive force out there.
eng_odengeiger_annotation_001: I have earned and lost several fortunes during my colourful life. I do not regret a moment of it. Make sure your own time is embraced wisely.
eng_odengeiger_annotation_002: My intuition tells me that you have a plan for the designs I provide. A lifetime of experience makes such ambition easy to read.
eng_odengeiger_annotation_003: My engineering work these past few decades has proven as rewarding as any other venture. And I have participated in many, let me tell you.
eng_odengeiger_annotation_004: Both my suit and weapon modifications are of superior quality. A member of the Pilots' Federation would surely settle for nothing short of excellence.
eng_odengeiger_annotation_005: My modifications are of particular interest to those who favour strategy and patience over a hail of weapons fire. Does that fit your profile, I wonder?
eng_odengeiger_annotation_firstaccess: Seeing your equipment reminds me of my own adventures, many years ago. Perhaps one day we can exchange anecdotes. But for now, I'm certain you would like to browse my designs. Shall we?
eng_odengeiger_callout_001: Hello again, Commander. Returned for some upgrades, have we?
eng_odengeiger_callout_002: Good to see you, my friend. How may I be of assistance?
eng_odengeiger_callout_003: Our paths cross once again, Commander.
