mission_onfoot_assassination_001_mission: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.
mission_onfoot_assassination_001_narrati:
I run a team that makes and delivers speciality items. It’s just a small operation, but we get by. Or at least we did until a smuggler started cutting in on our business.

Most people hear about smuggling and think it’s no big deal. People get what they want with a little discount. Nobody gets hurt, so what’s the problem? Except that’s not how it works. Businesses like mine suffer, workers lose their jobs as our customer base moves elsewhere and soon you have whole settlements run by criminals. So, please, do us all a favour and take care of this conniving little...

My apologies. What I meant to say is: please eliminate our ‘competitor’.
mission_onfoot_assassination_002_mission: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.
mission_onfoot_assassination_002_narrati:
Don’t you hate it when someone comes along and ruins a perfectly good situation? All I want to do is help people forget their troubles. I find the best merch, hire some reliable individuals to get it where it needs to be, and everyone’s happy. Until some lowlife decides to muscle in on my territory and mess it all up.

As far as I’m concerned, there’s only one way to deal with assholes like that. That’s where you come in. Let’s get the operation back to how it ought to be.
mission_onfoot_assassination_003_mission: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.
mission_onfoot_assassination_003_narrati:
I’m a great boss. Ask anyone and they’ll tell you. I give my workers a respectable income. I take care of them when they’re in trouble. It’s as though they were part of the family. But when someone in your family starts stealing out of your pocket, you’ve got a problem. The kind that needs to be dealt with as soon as possible.

There's a runner who decided that smuggling good merchandise wasn’t enough for them. Started cutting it with crap and pocketing the extra profit. That kind of betrayal just hurts like hell, I don’t mind admitting.

So I’m forced to send a message that'll remind the rest of my people what happens when you turn on me. Don’t be afraid to make it messy.
mission_onfoot_assassination_004_mission: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.
mission_onfoot_assassination_004_narrati:
Think you can take down a smuggler and maybe save some lives? I’m serious. Our settlements are usually safe, quiet places. But things have been getting out of hand lately, and there's a gunrunner pouring fuel on the fire. If we don’t put a stop to the black market trades, we could have a full-blown riot on our hands.

We’re still trying to find out which group is behind the flood of weapons, but for now a single elimination will slow things. Take out the gunrunner and we'll have a better chance of getting things under control.
mission_onfoot_assassination_005_mission: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.
mission_onfoot_assassination_005_narrati:
Some days it seems to me like every system's economy revolves around conflict. And, truthfully, I'd kinda made my peace with it. But just lately a new gunrunner trying to make their name has been making some bold moves. It's almost like they're taking a perverse joy in stoking the fires by selling to both sides in any dispute. Not sure who's keeping track of the casualty count, but I bet this person has more blood on their hands than most.

This constant escalation has to stop. And the simplest way to do that is by killing that damn smuggler.
mission_onfoot_assassination_006_mission: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.
mission_onfoot_assassination_006_narrati:
How would you like to help us fight a bunch of terrorists? Don’t worry, I’m not asking you to go up against the whole lot of them. We’ve got the system authorities tracking down some of their cells. In the meantime, we need someone to deal with the leader of a smuggling operation that’s supplying the terrorists with weapons.

This creep’s been hell to find, but now that we have their location we can take them out and deal a serious blow to their leadership. It won’t be easy, but it could make a real difference. You in?
mission_onfoot_assassination_007_mission: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.
mission_onfoot_assassination_007_narrati:
There’s a pirate who’s been making our lives a misery for months. Usually it's the kind of trouble you learn to live with - fighting back risks more than just meeting their demands. But now they've killed one of my closest friends and that’s more than I can take.

Maybe revenge doesn’t bring people back from the dead, but it sure helps them rest easier. I’m not going to let these bastards keep attacking our ships, taking our cargo, killing our people. I want that monster in the ground. And if you have to tear through the scum that works with them, well, even better.
mission_onfoot_assassination_008_mission: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.
mission_onfoot_assassination_008_narrati:
In my line of work, routine is everything. So when a band of pirates moves into the neighbourhood, I tend to get nervous. Having a bunch of criminals roaming around doesn’t just hurt my business. It gets people killed.

The real problem is the mob's leader. A real nasty piece of work, but they’re smart and have a loyal following. Take them out and the rest will scatter like the maggots they are. Then things can get back to the way they’ve always been, and I can breathe easy again.
mission_onfoot_assassination_009_mission: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.
mission_onfoot_assassination_009_narrati:
Let me tell you a story. A courier runs into engine trouble on a routine journey and is forced to crash-land on a nearby planet. The ship’s a wreck so he sets up a beacon and waits for help. Only it’s not a rescue team that picks up the signal, it’s scavengers. And these parasites don’t just take the cargo. They butcher the pilot for sport.

Well, that courier was a friend of mine, and I’m going to make sure they get some payback. I've tracked down one of the killers and it's cost me a lot of credits to find them. Now I'm spending more to finish the job. I want them dead now.
mission_onfoot_assassination_010_mission: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.
mission_onfoot_assassination_010_narrati:
Have you ever seen a settlement being evacuated? It can get crazy if you don’t have a proper plan in place. And it can get even worse if you're short of people and a bunch of those you do have are still wet behind the ears. That's how important tasks like properly securing the power regulator get overlooked. Idiots.

Of course, by the time we got back, the regulator was gone, stolen by scavengers. It’s just pure luck that we managed to track it down on the black market. There’s already a bounty out for the ringleader but we want to make this very clear - Steal from us and you don't get to live.
mission_onfoot_assassination_011_mission: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.
mission_onfoot_assassination_011_narrati:
There are smart criminals and there are dumb criminals. And trust me: there are a lot more dumb ones. I mean, you’d have to be to try and steal from my people. Just so happens the one I’m after is also one of the unluckiest thieves who ever lived. We might have let the whole thing go with some scare tactics if they’d taken a few junk items.

Turns out, the thief accidentally lifted something valuable. So valuable they’ve spent months trying to find a buyer while hiding at the same time. When they finally found a client, turns out it was one of my fences. Like I said. Dumb.

Anyway, at this point it's going to make me look bad if they aren't dealt with. I need someone to make sure it’s the last mistake this screw-up ever makes.
mission_onfoot_assassination_012_mission: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.
mission_onfoot_assassination_012_narrati:
I’m out here looking for revenge. A man very dear to me, who took me under his wing and taught me everything I know about piloting, has been murdered. I won’t stop until the person who killed him pays for it. My crew are out gathering evidence for the authorities but that’s not the kind of justice I need right now.

I know who did it. I don't know if they were acting alone or not but that hardly matters. The others will figure that out and we'll handle anyone we need to. Right now all I want is this snake face-down in the dirt.
mission_onfoot_assassination_013_mission: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.
mission_onfoot_assassination_013_narrati:
A contact I've been developing tipped me off about someone buying minerals way over the market price. My contact even said that they'd arrange an introduction for me as they had business in the area. Well, it seems they were playing me because as soon as we arrived at the settlement my contact disappeared. Along with my ship. I had a lot of credits tied up in that cargo and the fact I was so blatantly ripped off just don't sit right with me.

But sometimes life throws you a bone. I've found out where the thieving jackal is holed up. I'll pay you to make sure that they won't be making fools of anyone else.

Most people hear about smuggling and think it’s no big deal. People get what they want with a little discount. Nobody gets hurt, so what’s the problem? Except that’s not how it works. Businesses like mine suffer, workers lose their jobs as our customer base moves elsewhere and soon you have whole settlements run by criminals. So do us all a favour and take care of this conniving little...

My apologies. What I meant to say is: please eliminate our ‘competitor’.
mission_onfoot_assassination_covert_002_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

Don’t you hate it when someone comes along and ruins a perfectly good situation? All I want to do is help people forget their troubles. I find the best merch, hire some reliable individuals to get it where it needs to be, and everyone’s happy. Until some lowlife decides to muscle in on my territory and mess it all up.

As far as I’m concerned, there’s only one way to deal with assholes like that. That’s where you come in. Let’s get the operation back to how it ought to be.
mission_onfoot_assassination_covert_003_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

I’m a great boss. Ask anyone and they’ll tell you. I give my workers a respectable income. I take care of them when they’re in trouble. It’s as though they were part of the family. But when someone in your family starts stealing out of your pocket, you’ve got a problem. The kind that needs to be dealt with as soon as possible.

There's a runner who decided that smuggling good merchandise wasn’t enough for them. Started cutting it with crap and pocketing the extra profit. That kind of betrayal just hurts like hell, I don’t mind admitting.

So I’m forced to send a message that'll remind the rest of my people what happens when you turn on me. Don’t be afraid to make it messy.
mission_onfoot_assassination_covert_004_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

Think you can take down a smuggler and maybe save some lives? I’m serious. Our settlements are usually safe, quiet places. But things have been getting out of hand lately, and there's a gunrunner pouring fuel on the fire. If we don’t put a stop to the black market trades, we could have a full-blown riot on our hands.

We’re still trying to find out which group is behind the flood of weapons, but for now a single elimination will slow things. Take out the gunrunner and we'll have a better chance of getting things under control.
mission_onfoot_assassination_covert_005_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

Some days it seems to me like every system's economy revolves around conflict. And, truthfully, I'd kinda made my peace with it. But just lately a new gunrunner trying to make their name has been making some bold moves. It's almost like they're taking a perverse joy in stoking the fires by selling to both sides in any dispute. Not sure who's keeping track of the casualty count, but I bet this person has more blood on their hands than most.

This constant escalation has to stop. And the simplest way to do that is by killing that damn smuggler.
mission_onfoot_assassination_covert_006_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

How would you like to help us fight a bunch of terrorists? Don’t worry, I’m not asking you to go up against the whole lot of them. We’ve got the system authorities tracking down some of their cells. In the meantime, we need someone to deal with the leader of a smuggling operation that’s supplying the terrorists with weapons.

This creep’s been hell to find, but now that we have their location we can take them out and deal a serious blow to their leadership. It won’t be easy, but it could make a real difference. You in?
mission_onfoot_assassination_covert_007_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

There’s a pirate who’s been making our lives a misery for months. Usually it's the kind of trouble you learn to live with - fighting back risks more than just meeting their demands. But now they've killed one of my closest friends and that’s more than I can take.

Maybe revenge doesn’t bring people back from the dead, but it sure helps them rest easier. I’m not going to let these bastards keep attacking our ships, taking our cargo, killing our people. I want that monster in the ground. And if you have to tear through the scum that works with them, well, even better.
mission_onfoot_assassination_covert_008_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

In my line of work, routine is everything. So when a band of pirates moves into the neighbourhood, I tend to get nervous. Having a bunch of criminals roaming around doesn’t just hurt my business. It gets people killed.

The real problem is the mob's leader. A real nasty piece of work, but they’re smart and have a loyal following. Take them out and the rest will scatter like the maggots they are. Then things can get back to the way they’ve always been, and I can breathe easy again.
mission_onfoot_assassination_covert_009_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

Let me tell you a story. A courier runs into engine trouble on a routine journey and is forced to crash-land on a nearby planet. The ship’s a wreck so he sets up a beacon and waits for help. Only it’s not a rescue team that picks up the signal, it’s scavengers. And these parasites don’t just take the cargo. They butcher the pilot for sport.

Well, that courier was a friend of mine, and I’m going to make sure they get some payback. I've tracked down one of the killers and it's cost me a lot of credits to find them. Now I'm spending more to finish the job. I want them dead now.
mission_onfoot_assassination_covert_010_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

Have you ever seen a settlement being evacuated? It can get crazy if you don’t have a proper plan in place. And it can get even worse if you're short of people and a bunch of those you do have are still wet behind the ears. That's how important tasks like properly securing the power regulator get overlooked. Idiots.

Of course, by the time we got back, the regulator was gone, stolen by scavengers. It’s just pure luck that we managed to track it down on the black market. There’s already a bounty out for the ringleader but we want to make this very clear - Steal from us and you don't get to live.
mission_onfoot_assassination_covert_011_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

There are smart criminals and there are dumb criminals. And trust me: there are a lot more dumb ones. I mean, you’d have to be to try and steal from my people. Just so happens the one I’m after is also one of the unluckiest thieves who ever lived. We might have let the whole thing go with some scare tactics if they’d taken a few junk items.

Turns out, the thief accidentally lifted something valuable. So valuable they’ve spent months trying to find a buyer while hiding at the same time. When they finally found a client, turns out it was one of my fences. Like I said. Dumb.

Anyway, at this point it's going to make me look bad if they aren't dealt with. I need someone to make sure it’s the last mistake this screw-up ever makes.
mission_onfoot_assassination_covert_012_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

I’m out here looking for revenge. A man very dear to me, who took me under his wing and taught me everything I know about piloting, has been murdered. I won’t stop until the person who killed him pays for it. My crew are out gathering evidence for the authorities but that’s not the kind of justice I need right now.

I know who did it. I don't know if they were acting alone or not but that hardly matters. The others will figure that out and we'll handle anyone we need to. Right now all I want is this snake face-down in the dirt.
mission_onfoot_assassination_covert_013_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

A contact I've been developing tipped me off about someone buying minerals way over the market price. My contact even said that they'd arrange an introduction for me as they had business in the area. Well, it seems they were playing me because as soon as we arrived at the settlement my contact disappeared. Along with my ship. I had a lot of credits tied up in that cargo and the fact I was so blatantly ripped off just don't sit right with me.

But sometimes life throws you a bone. I've found out where the thieving jackal is holed up. I'll pay you to make sure that they won't be making fools of anyone else.

mission_onfoot_assassination_covert_miss: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.
mission_onfoot_assassination_covert_narr:
A few months ago, one of our operatives disappeared. Not a big deal, you might think. After all, the galaxy’s a big place. These things happen. But this particular individual had been involved in the planning of an important operation, and was privy to some highly sensitive information.

Now we’ve learned that the individual in question has defected to a rival organisation. Naturally we have taken steps to ensure they cannot use their knowledge against us, but it remains a serious matter. Not only has this individual compromised our organisation, they have betrayed our trust.

My personal feeling is that an assassination contract is excessive given the nature of the offence. But my superiors have made it clear that they want this individual eliminated. And you, I assume, have no reservations about accepting such an assignment.

mission_onfoot_assassination_ncd_mission: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.
mission_onfoot_assassination_ncd_narrati:
A few months ago, one of our operatives disappeared. Not a big deal, you might think. After all, the galaxy’s a big place. These things happen. But this particular individual had been involved in the planning of an important operation, and was privy to some highly sensitive information.

Now we’ve learned that the individual in question has defected to a rival organisation. Naturally we have taken steps to ensure they cannot use their knowledge against us, but it remains a serious matter. Not only has this individual compromised our organisation, they have betrayed our trust.

My personal feeling is that an assassination contract is excessive given the nature of the offence. But my superiors have made it clear that they want this individual eliminated. And you, I assume, have no reservations about accepting such an assignment.

mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_001_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

One of my associates is in trouble. And whenever someone in our crew has a problem, we handle it. No matter the cost.

We sent a member of our team on a somewhat delicate mission. Not strictly legal, but sometimes you have to navigate the letter of the law in the course of business. Usually these low-profile operations come off without a hitch, but this time there was a witness. A guard at the facility was able to successfully identify my associate after the fact and is now due to testify against them at trial.

The case hinges on this guard's testimony, so I need you to make sure they never get to give it.
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_002_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

If there’s one thing I can’t abide, it’s a snitch. Anybody with a shred of honour should be willing to throw themselves out an airlock before spilling secrets and betraying their crew. But you know how it is; some people need a little help keeping their mouth shut. That’s where you come in.

This particular idiot managed to get themselves caught and we’re pretty sure they’ve tried to buy their way out with information. Names of informants, cache locations...who knows what they’ve offered? It’s the only explanation for why they’re not currently rotting in a prison ship. You need to end them before they get a chance to talk. Won’t be easy though. The authorities are pretending they’re some material witness in need of protection, but trust me. It’s just another rat that needs to be put down.
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_003_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

I recently took over our company's records department. Obviously I needed to familiarise myself with the data, so I started checking through it. Whoever had the job before me must have sucked at it, because there were big gaps. Particularly with personnel accidents, some of which resulted in fatalities.

Digging further, there was a common thread between each of the sites when accidents increased for a period. Every time, they’d been assigned the same employee, one with a position that allowed them to move often. I’m pretty sure this person had been moving from place to place with the intention of getting people hurt, or worse. One of those who didn’t survive was a friend of mine. I always knew there something strange about their death.

That employee's no longer with our company; given they're now working for a long-term rival, maybe they were recalled by their handler. But I've found them. The courts would drag this out for years, Commander. They need to face real justice.
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_004_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

It takes a lot to be at the top of a corporate ladder. My client has access to the latest research, the highest precision machinery, and most of the time, the best people. But what happens when a prime candidate says no to your offer of employment? Well, it comes down to two choices. Let them work for the competition, or ensure they never work again.

I'm going with option two. How do you feel about delivering the target's redundancy notice?
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_005_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

My company has lost out on every juicy contract bid made this month. And who do you think’s responsible for signing up new clients? That’s right, me. I normally do fine, but there’s an insufferable new go-getter out there nailing every single business opportunity for our main rival. Stealing credits right out of my hands! If I don’t find a way to fix this, I'll be cleaning taxi shuttles come the year's end.

I don’t know how they do it. They must be bribing everyone they can or making crazy promises. Whatever it is, I don’t care. They need to be stopped, you hear me? Permanently.
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_006_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

Fancy taking a trip to a nice planetary vista? You can take a few images, chill out, and maybe kill someone.

There’s a courier who’s been nothing but grief for my clients and has to go. It’s not that this courier is bad at their job - quite the opposite. They never miss a delivery and seem to know every time-saving trick in the business. Problem is, they work for a rival to my clients, who are sick of seeing them perform so well.

I’ve managed to find out where the target is taking a well-deserved vacation, and I have a feeling they’re about to have an unfortunate accident. Don’t you agree?
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_007_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

Want to know something funny about business? My client has thousands of employees contributing to its success, and almost all of them are replaceable. It’s the ones you can’t replace that matter, see? One of them goes and you’re in trouble.

Luckily, the same goes for our rivals. There are only a certain number of people with the right knowledge and experience available, so imagine what would happen if a recently headhunted executive were to meet with an unforeseen end. It would disrupt the quarterly forecasts somewhat, hm?
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_008_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

How are you supposed to run a business if a competitor can come along and make everything you’ve worked for obsolete? Don’t get me wrong, progress is a wonderful thing. New technologies, improved quality of life, so on and so forth. But sometimes you just want things to stay the same for a damn minute.

One scientist seems to have gone out of their way to target my team. They've taken one of our most successful products and rushed it out to the local pharmaceuticals with all kinds of cost-cutting hacks in place. Calls it a 'financially preferable alternative'. If he secures a distributor we'll be facing a drastic loss in sales! So I need to stop this jerk from turning everything upside down. What do you say?
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_009_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

If there’s one rule that always proves true it’s this: everybody’s got a price. It's one of those solid, reliable facts that gives people like me comfort. So when you come across someone who refuses several generous offers, it gets me thinking. I just like my world to make sense.

I was willing to pay an industrial worker a lot of money for some critical trade secrets. I’m talking enough money to retire on any planet they wanted. When they turned me down, the obvious question was 'who made them a better offer?'

Whatever the answer, I’d like you to make sure this person doesn't live to say yes. Some secrets are worth killing for.
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_010_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

The business I represent has something of a PR problem on its hands because of one idiot mouthing off to the press about certain ethical arguments. All lies as far as we’re concerned, of course. Trouble is, this attention-seeker is well connected and a few journalists are starting to look closer.

We could try to silence the whistleblower through traditional means, but any legal action would be a public and messy affair and just end up drawing more eyes. Discrediting them would take too long and has a limited guarantee of success. In the end, it's much simpler to hire an outsider to eliminate the problem. Just another tragic act of violence claiming an innocent life. You would be suitably compensated for your time, of course.
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_011_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

Faction guards are all the same. Give them a uniform and a weapon and they think they can do whatever they want. There's one in particular who gets the bright idea of messing with my crew’s shipments. This piece of work is holding up our deliveries for days, marking them for inspection while letting other canisters slide. Now they've started asking for credits to speed things up. That's where I draw the line.

We would have got the law involved, but extortion’s hard to prove and the guard's been smart enough to avoid outright illegal behaviour. They just impounded a highly sensitive shipment I've made promises about to some serious hitters. Put a few holes in the guard for me and maybe their replacement will be more understanding.
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_012_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

A good friend of mine died recently. Not only were they a friend, but they were a member of my crew - a really solid worker, everyone loved them. It doesn't matter how stressful the situation we were in, they were always calm and dependable. I don't think I ever even heard them raise their voice.

So, when the police told me my friend has been killed after starting a fight in a bar and being stabbed in self-defence I didn't buy it. I've been in this business long enough to smell corruption. The good thing is, corruption works both ways. Enough credits in the right account and you can find the truth. Such as the name of the person who killed your friend.

I'm sure my friend would tell me to turn the other cheek, but they're not here anymore. I want the killer dead.
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_013_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

One of my people has been arrested. Not the strangest event in the world, but it wasn’t supposed to happen. We had an arrangement with the guard who picked them up. You know how it is; they let our guy off with a warning and we make it worth their while. Well, either they misunderstood the deal or thought they could ignore it. Either way, they're dead wrong.We can’t let this person go without making an example of them. If we don't then some of the other mindless authority drones will get the idea that we're to be treated like common criminals. It’ll be your job to remind them just how scared of us they should be.
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_014_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

The company I represent deals in information. You don't need to know the company nor the type of information. You just need to know that some of it is worth more than a Type-9 full of platinum. That's why we take security so seriously. That's why we don't have breaches. Except, of course, when we do.

Were the galaxy at large to know that, it would be crippling to our reputation. And that is why - on occasion - we have cause to hire outside contractors like yourself. People who can't be tied to us.

I have the details of someone who recently left our employ with information they weren't cleared to see. The company would rather they didn't have the chance to sell that information. I trust we're clear?
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_015_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

You ever hear the old phrase 'it never rains but it pours'? Well, that's the situation we're in at the moment. Not only do we have a faction conflict to worry about, but we've just discovered that someone in an otherwise neutral organisation is sympathetic to our enemy's cause. The worm's been supplying them with weapons and who knows what else.

That sympathiser, though? They've got no idea we're onto them. We're pretty sure they the only person holding that whole deal together. If we kill them ourselves, someone already working for the enemy may step in. But if someone who isn't tied to us takes them out, well, maybe the problem goes away.
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_016_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

You've probably seen the news about the conflict in this system. Makes plenty of work for mercs such as yourself, I guess?

Some people we thought were our friends have been helping out our enemy with tactical information. It's a purely financial arrangement, so perhaps if it’s made clear that further involvement is going to cost these sell-outs dearly, I’m pretty sure they'll back off.

Only problem is, the person we need to take out will see our people coming from a mile off. They’re expecting us to act. But an independent gun like you? I don't imagine the target will suspect a thing until it’s far, far too late.
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_017_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

One of my squad’s ships just botched a covert op so badly that it could ruin our whole operation. The pilot was sent to destroy an enemy target with a VIP on board. They managed to disable the ship but not before taking critical damage themselves. The last thing they sent us was the other ship's projected touch down location.

We were trying to do this without attracting attention to ourselves so we can't risk a clean-up operation that further exposes our involvement. That's why I need you to head to the landing site and finish the job, whereupon you’ll be paid accordingly.
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_018_: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

I represent a company which deals in the production and supply of certain goods valued in times of war. Our last quarter's profit was concerning, though, so we recently engaged in an operation to re-invigorate the market. Assassinating one of our faction's political rivals in the hope would have done the trick, I think. Unfortunately, it did not go to plan and the target ship merely crashed instead of exploding.

As such we can't be certain of the target's successful elimination, or that our involvement isn’t already known. With our original contractor unwilling to finish the job, I need to hire someone who to brings matters to a satisfactory conclusion. I'm hoping that someone is you, and that you are a fast worker.

I don’t know how they do it. They must be bribing everyone they can or making crazy promises. Whatever it is, I don’t care. They need to be stopped, you hear me? Permanently.
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

Fancy taking a trip to a nice planetary vista? You can take a few images, chill out, and maybe kill someone.

There’s a courier who’s been nothing but grief for my clients and has to go. It’s not that this courier is bad at their job - quite the opposite. They never miss a delivery and seem to know every time-saving trick in the business. Problem is, they work for a rival to my clients, who are sick of seeing them perform so well.

I’ve managed to find out where the target is taking a well-deserved vacation, and I have a feeling they’re about to have an unfortunate accident. Don’t you agree?
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

Want to know something funny about business? My client has thousands of employees contributing to its success, and almost all of them are replaceable. It’s the ones you can’t replace that matter, see? One of them goes and you’re in trouble.

Luckily, the same goes for our rivals. There are only a certain number of people with the right knowledge and experience available, so imagine what would happen if a recently headhunted executive were to meet with an unforeseen end. It would disrupt the quarterly forecasts somewhat, hm?
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

How are you supposed to run a business if a competitor can come along and make everything you’ve worked for obsolete? Don’t get me wrong, progress is a wonderful thing. New technologies, improved quality of life, so on and so forth. But sometimes you just want things to stay the same for a damn minute.

One scientist seems to have gone out of their way to target my team. They've taken one of our most successful products and rushed it out to the local pharmaceuticals with all kinds of cost-cutting hacks in place. Calls it a 'financially preferable alternative'. If he secures a distributor we'll be facing a drastic loss in sales! So I need to stop this jerk from turning everything upside down. What do you say?
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

If there’s one rule that always proves true it’s this: everybody’s got a price. It's one of those solid, reliable facts that gives people like me comfort. So when you come across someone who refuses several generous offers, it gets me thinking. I just like my world to make sense.

I was willing to pay an industrial worker a lot of money for some critical trade secrets. I’m talking enough money to retire on any planet they wanted. When they turned me down, the obvious question was 'who made them a better offer?'

Whatever the answer, I’d like you to make sure this person doesn't live to say yes. Some secrets are worth killing for.
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

The business I represent has something of a PR problem on its hands because of one idiot mouthing off to the press about certain ethical arguments. All lies as far as we’re concerned, of course. Trouble is, this attention-seeker is well connected and a few journalists are starting to look closer.

We could try to silence the whistleblower through traditional means, but any legal action would be a public and messy affair and just end up drawing more eyes. Discrediting them would take too long and has a limited guarantee of success. In the end, it's much simpler to hire an outsider to eliminate the problem. Just another tragic act of violence claiming an innocent life. You would be suitably compensated for your time, of course.
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

Faction guards are all the same. Give them a uniform and a weapon and they think they can do whatever they want. There's one in particular who gets the bright idea of messing with my crew’s shipments. This piece of work is holding up our deliveries for days, marking them for inspection while letting other canisters slide. Now they've started asking for credits to speed things up. That's where I draw the line.

We would have got the law involved, but extortion’s hard to prove and the guard's been smart enough to avoid outright illegal behaviour. They just impounded a highly sensitive shipment I've made promises about to some serious hitters. Put a few holes in the guard for me and maybe their replacement will be more understanding.
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

A good friend of mine died recently. Not only were they a friend, but they were a member of my crew - a really solid worker, everyone loved them. It doesn't matter how stressful the situation we were in, they were always calm and dependable. I don't think I ever even heard them raise their voice.

So, when the police told me my friend has been killed after starting a fight in a bar and being stabbed in self-defence I didn't buy it. I've been in this business long enough to smell corruption. The good thing is, corruption works both ways. Enough credits in the right account and you can find the truth. Such as the name of the person who killed your friend.

I'm sure my friend would tell me to turn the other cheek, but they're not here anymore. I want the killer dead.
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

One of my people has been arrested. Not the strangest event in the world, but it wasn’t supposed to happen. We had an arrangement with the guard who picked them up. You know how it is; they let our guy off with a warning and we make it worth their while. Well, either they misunderstood the deal or thought they could ignore it. Either way, they're dead wrong.We can’t let this person go without making an example of them. If we don't then some of the other mindless authority drones will get the idea that we're to be treated like common criminals. It’ll be your job to remind them just how scared of us they should be.
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

The company I represent deals in information. You don't need to know the company nor the type of information. You just need to know that some of it is worth more than a Type-9 full of platinum. That's why we take security so seriously. That's why we don't have breaches. Except, of course, when we do.

Were the galaxy at large to know that, it would be crippling to our reputation. And that is why - on occasion - we have cause to hire outside contractors like yourself. People who can't be tied to us.

I have the details of someone who recently left our employ with information they weren't cleared to see. The company would rather they didn't have the chance to sell that information. I trust we're clear?
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

You ever hear the old phrase 'it never rains but it pours'? Well, that's the situation we're in at the moment. Not only do we have a faction conflict to worry about, but we've just discovered that someone in an otherwise neutral organisation is sympathetic to our enemy's cause. The worm's been supplying them with weapons and who knows what else.

That sympathiser, though? They've got no idea we're onto them. We're pretty sure they the only person holding that whole deal together. If we kill them ourselves, someone already working for the enemy may step in. But if someone who isn't tied to us takes them out, well, maybe the problem goes away.
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

You've probably seen the news about the conflict in this system. Makes plenty of work for mercs such as yourself, I guess?

Some people we thought were our friends have been helping out our enemy with tactical information. It's a purely financial arrangement, so perhaps if it’s made clear that further involvement is going to cost these sell-outs dearly, I’m pretty sure they'll back off.

Only problem is, the person we need to take out will see our people coming from a mile off. They’re expecting us to act. But an independent gun like you? I don't imagine the target will suspect a thing until it’s far, far too late.
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

One of my squad’s ships just botched a covert op so badly that it could ruin our whole operation. The pilot was sent to destroy an enemy target with a VIP on board. They managed to disable the ship but not before taking critical damage themselves. The last thing they sent us was the other ship's projected touch down location.

We were trying to do this without attracting attention to ourselves so we can't risk a clean-up operation that further exposes our involvement. That's why I need you to head to the landing site and finish the job, whereupon you’ll be paid accordingly.
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

I represent a company which deals in the production and supply of certain goods valued in times of war. Our last quarter's profit was concerning, though, so we recently engaged in an operation to re-invigorate the market. Assassinating one of our faction's political rivals in the hope would have done the trick, I think. Unfortunately, it did not go to plan and the target ship merely crashed instead of exploding.

As such we can't be certain of the target's successful elimination, or that our involvement isn’t already known. With our original contractor unwilling to finish the job, I need to hire someone who to brings matters to a satisfactory conclusion. I'm hoping that someone is you, and that you are a fast worker.
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

There’s someone out there right now who’s walking and breathing way past their due. They just don’t know that time’s up yet. Perhaps you can be the one who delivers the message. How else would you deal with a former associate who decides they’d rather join your rivals before paying back what they owe you?

Maybe they thought I’d just forget the debt and leave the whole thing alone. That I’d be happy with my peers thinking you can swindle me and get away with it. Or maybe they thought their new friends would protect them. Whatever it is, they’re not counting on the likes of you coming along. And that will be the last mistake they'll ever make.
mission_onfoot_assassinationillegal_mb_m: On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

One of my associates is in trouble. And whenever someone in our crew has a problem, we handle it. No matter the cost.

We sent a member of our team on a somewhat delicate mission. Not strictly legal, but sometimes you have to navigate the letter of the law in the course of business. Usually these low-profile operations come off without a hitch, but this time there was a witness. A guard at the facility was able to successfully identify my associate after the fact and is now due to testify against them at trial.

The case hinges on this guard's testimony, so I need you to make sure they never get to give it.
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

If there’s one thing I can’t abide, it’s a snitch. Anybody with a shred of honour should be willing to throw themselves out an airlock before spilling secrets and betraying their crew. But you know how it is; some people need a little help keeping their mouth shut. That’s where you come in.

This particular idiot managed to get themselves caught and we’re pretty sure they’ve tried to buy their way out with information. Names of informants, cache locations...who knows what they’ve offered? It’s the only explanation for why they’re not currently rotting in a prison ship. You need to end them before they get a chance to talk. Won’t be easy though. The authorities are pretending they’re some material witness in need of protection, but trust me. It’s just another rat that needs to be put down.
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

I recently took over our company's records department. Obviously I needed to familiarise myself with the data, so I started checking through it. Whoever had the job before me must have sucked at it, because there were big gaps. Particularly with personnel accidents, some of which resulted in fatalities.

Digging further, there was a common thread between each of the sites when accidents increased for a period. Every time, they’d been assigned the same employee, one with a position that allowed them to move often. I’m pretty sure this person had been moving from place to place with the intention of getting people hurt, or worse. One of those who didn’t survive was a friend of mine. I always knew there something strange about their death.

That employee's no longer with our company; given they're now working for a long-term rival, maybe they were recalled by their handler. But I've found them. The courts would drag this out for years, Commander. They need to face real justice.
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

It takes a lot to be at the top of a corporate ladder. My client has access to the latest research, the highest precision machinery, and most of the time, the best people. But what happens when a prime candidate says no to your offer of employment? Well, it comes down to two choices. Let them work for the competition, or ensure they never work again.

I'm going with option two. How do you feel about delivering the target's redundancy notice?
On behalf of our organisation, I'd like to thank you for handling this so expediently.

mission_onfoot_collect_001_missioncomple: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_collect_001_name_title: Collection: Fetch the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_collect_001_narrative:
I hope you prove more reliable than the last courier I hired. They were supposed to collect a piece of equipment for my team’s latest project, but they’re long overdue and I can't make contact with them.

It might not seem like much to you, but it’s crucial that I get the listed equipment as soon as possible. Of course, there are other ways of getting it delivered, but I’d rather use a specialist to speed up the process. I’m trusting you to do what the last runner couldn't and bring me what I need.
mission_onfoot_collect_002_missioncomple: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_collect_002_name_title: Collection: Fetch the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_collect_002_narrative:
I work with a research team on the verge of a medical breakthrough. One that could truly revolutionise our field of study. Unfortunately, there are powerful people out there who would rather not find a solution to the problem we're trying to solve. As a result, we’ve had to operate in total secrecy until now.

As you can imagine, this has made our work rather difficult, particularly when it comes to obtaining the chemicals we need for our analyses. I’ve managed to arrange for the collection of an important sample, though; I’m hoping you can bring it to me safely. Please don't let me down.
mission_onfoot_collect_003_missioncomple: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_collect_003_name_title: Collection: Fetch the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_collect_003_narrative:
The group I work with is in the process of creating a real technological advance. Of course, it will be years before we can produce anything ready for the market, but every step brings us closer. To keep up to date with our competition we’re eager to study the latest experimental schematics, no matter where they are.

I’ve tracked down one schematic of interest and I’m hoping you will agree to collect it for me. This is a real opportunity to help with the continued progression of human technology. And who could turn that down?
mission_onfoot_collect_004_missioncomple: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_collect_004_name_title: Collection: Fetch the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_collect_004_narrative:
Ever wanted to make your life simpler? I got talking with a group of really zen people, who helped me understand the benefits of making a fresh start. Get rid of your belongings and embrace life as it comes!

The only problem is that during the clear-out I accidentally gave away the one thing I wanted to keep. It’s a personal recording of a very dear friend. They’re dead now, so it's all I have to remember them by.

Luckily, an old colleague noticed it among all the junk they took off me and realised what it was. They’ve set it aside, so I just need someone to pick it up. Interested? You'd be helping me bring a good memory to the next chapter of my journey.
mission_onfoot_collect_005_missioncomple: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_collect_005_name_title: Collection: Fetch the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_collect_005_narrative:
How much do you know about bacteria?

There’s nothing more fascinating in the whole universe. Tiny organisms of infinite variety and beauty that open up endless possibilities for research. Oh, excuse me - I’m getting carried away again. The reason I’m here is that there’s a newly engineered bacterial strain that I simply must get my hands on.

The scientists who created it have genetically modified the bacteria in a way that makes it very useful for my company’s bio-matter experiments. As soon as you bring it to me I can make arrangements to start replicating it at my team's production facility. Exciting times!
mission_onfoot_collect_006_missioncomple: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_collect_006_name_title: Collection: Fetch the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_collect_006_narrative:
Can you believe this place? There’s just nothing to do around here. I'd kill to go to a party, maybe get wasted, wind up in the wrong person's quarters. Trust me: there's no chance of that ever happening here.

But there is a ray of hope - a friend of mine has got hold of some experimental sims that they reckon will blow my mind. They were supposed to come by and drop them off, but I must have slipped their mind. Can you believe that?  Luckily I've got a bit of surplus in my budget that needs spending anyway so I figure I can kill two birds with one stone. Please, bring me those sims before I lose my mind.
mission_onfoot_collect_007_missioncomple: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_collect_007_name_title: Collection: Fetch the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_collect_007_narrative:
I'm sure you're regularly transporting clandestine packages for shadowy cabals and the like, but I've got something a little different in mind. I need you to collect a genetic sample for me. Don't worry, it's nothing sinister - at least, not yet. It's from alien flora on a low-atmosphere world.

That may not sound terribly exciting to you, but trust me: in my little circle of exobiologists, we're positively buzzing with anticipation. It has some fascinating genetic markers that could fill in significant gaps in a project we've spent years working on.

This is why I'm willing to pay to have it transported by a reputable courier. The last thing I want is it getting lost amongst the usual logistical clutter or pirated from some cheapskate's cargo hold. Are you in, Commander?
mission_onfoot_collect_008_missioncomple: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_collect_008_name_title: Collection: Fetch the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_collect_008_narrative:
You’re looking at somebody on their way up! I’ve been stuck in middle management forever, but this is the year I make it to the next level. I’ve finally confirmed a weapon design that can be manufactured on our existing assembly line at a faster rate than our current product. The higher-ups are bound to take notice!

I can’t sit around waiting for the usual courier services to bring the schematic to me, though. They always turn up late, assuming they don’t dump your shipment into a star first. That’s why I’m looking for a professional. The peace of mind is more than worth the money.
mission_onfoot_collect_009_missioncomple: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_collect_009_name_title: Collection: Fetch the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_collect_009_narrative:
I've been contacted by a friend at a settlement and they're in pretty dire straits. Ever since they set up operations there, the workers have been coming down with an illness. My friend has gone all-in on the location and invested everything. Obviously, they can't sell up - I mean, who'd buy the place if the workers are going to get sick?

The good news is they've identified the problem. It's some micro-organism native to the soil in the area - and they think they can wipe it out. But until they do, they need a particular chemical to keep the stuff controlled. If you can get that agent to me, I can get it to them. Because believe me, right now, you don't want to go near my friend's settlement if you don't have to.
mission_onfoot_collect_010_missioncomple: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_collect_010_name_title: Collection: Fetch the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_collect_010_narrative:
I'll keep this short because it's a simple pick-up job. I'd prefer to use one of my people but, what with us being in the middle of a stellar turf war, I can't exactly spare someone for a single-item run.

Look, all the details of the consignment are attached. Just get to our supplier, get the package, and get back.

And do it fast. Okay?
mission_onfoot_collect_011_missioncomple: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_collect_011_name_title: Collection: Fetch the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_collect_011_narrative:
This war has us in a real bind, and it's exposed some shortcomings in my company's supply network. The upshot is that we've had to contract an outside faction for some of our supplies. Here's hoping that doesn't bite us in the ass in some way down the road, huh?

Anyway, the production we need has been paid for. There's a sample of the work that needs collecting. I had someone in mind but their ship made a bad landing yesterday and won't be operational for a while.

So, their loss is your gain, isn't it?
mission_onfoot_collect_012_missioncomple: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_collect_012_name_title: Collection: Fetch the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_collect_012_narrative:
I'm going to need you to finish a job for us. My team has an urgently important package in the possession of a pilot ferrying it from one of our agents. The pilot’s ship suffered a complete critical system failure en route. Suspicious, I know.

We're lucky, though - if it had been any other pilot, their ship would have burned up around the nearest planet, but not this one - they somehow landed the damn thing. Not that it's ever going to take off again.

Listen, we need that package before our enemies can change all their plans and render it useless. The clock's ticking.
mission_onfoot_collect_013_missioncomple: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_collect_013_name_title: Collection: Fetch the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_collect_013_narrative:
I need you to pick up an important package. It was being couriered to my company but the pilot had some kind of mechanical failure - even their comms was spotty so I don't know all the details - but suffice to say, they're going nowhere for the time being.

I'd far prefer to send one of our people but with the conflict going on we’d be painting a target on that ship’s back. You'll find everything else you need to know in the attached details. Don't screw this up, okay?

mission_onfoot_collect_narrative:
I’ve been given the green light to procure a valuable item for my department. It can be a hassle trying to convince the financial team to relinquish credits, but sometimes quality is necessary for results.

The only thing is that a few packages have been going missing among my company’s couriers recently. An investigation is ongoing and no doubt we’ll find out whether theft is the cause, but for now I’d rather hire an outsider to collect the item for me. People talk highly of the Pilots’ Federation, so a Commander will do just fine.

Head to the pickup, get the package and bring it here for a reward. What could be simpler?
mission_onfoot_collect_travelpanel_descr:
Travel to $#DestinationSettlementName:style:name=keyword; in the $#DestinationSystemName:style:name=keyword; system.
Collect the $#CommodityName:style:name=keyword; from the settlement.
mission_onfoot_defence_macguffin_001_mis: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_defence_macguffin_001_nar:
A research and development site we run has just produced a one-of-a-kind prototype which has been sold to a large manufacturer. Unfortunately, another manufacturer has caught wind of this and wants to destroy it, which would be financially disastrous for us.

That team has poured everything they've got into this project, and we'd hate to see it fail because of some industry dispute. For that reason we're appealing to mercenaries to help them mount an effective defence against the threat they face. Get there as soon as you can. And be sure to take your weapons.
mission_onfoot_defence_macguffin_002_mis: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_defence_macguffin_002_nar:
My company operates a mining operation which needs your help. Not with mining, though - you'll need your gun instead. One of our long-term gambles just paid off and the crew recently hauled some extremely valuable minerals out of the ground. We have a brand new buyer lined up and they're ready to go, but a source at one of our rivals tells us there's a plan to stop the transaction. They've already dispatched a hit squad to our settlement.

That settlement will have trouble defending itself without backup. It needs the help of people like you. Will you stand with them?
mission_onfoot_defence_macguffin_003_mis: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_defence_macguffin_003_nar:
A settlement of ours just made a pretty fantastic find - an exceptionally complete fossil, or at least that's what it appears to be. The settlement has partners with some specialists to determine its true value, but the early indications are very positive.

But here's the rub: another xenoarchaeological company has found out about it and they're notorious for stifling competition. Up to and including destroying fossils they fear will enhance the reputation of their rivals. We think an attack is imminent. But, if you leave now, you'll have time to get to our settlement and help our people. Are you in?
mission_onfoot_defence_macguffin_004_mis: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_defence_macguffin_004_nar:
I've just received some very disturbing news. One of our chemical production settlements has learned that an attack is imminent. I'm not convinced the local security force is prepared to handle a targeted incursion, so we're willing to pay you to help them.

The reason they aren't capable themselves is that the chemicals they produce are fairly common, so security was always a secondary concern. But the company we're contracted to only uses a small number of suppliers. It also has some powerful rivals, the sort who will stop at nothing to damage the competition. Please, don't waste any time getting to our settlement.
mission_onfoot_defence_macguffin_005_mis: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_defence_macguffin_005_nar:
My company has a situation at one of our settlements. One of the senior personnel there has been taken extremely ill and had to be placed in an escape pod to ensure they reach a medical facility alive. A rival faction is seemingly taking this opportunity to try and neutralise them, and we need anyone with a gun to help prevent that.

The individual you'll be defending is key to our efforts in the region. If we lose them, it won't just be a personal tragedy for the people at the settlement - it could set our operation back by months.
mission_onfoot_defence_macguffin_006_mis: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_defence_macguffin_006_nar:
I need help with the defence of one of my client's settlements. More specifically, with its head of security. Normally they'd be exactly the person to deal with these issues but they were badly injured in a fight with a raider gang. They're currently in a medically induced coma awaiting evacuation.

That evacuation will require ship cover, which I'm trying to organise. In the meantime we believe the gang will try to finish what they started. We're asking anyone in the area to help with the settlement's defence, and a Commander fits the bill just fine. To earn a few credits you know what to do.
mission_onfoot_defence_macguffin_007_mis: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_defence_macguffin_007_nar:
The people at one of our sites have experienced a stroke of luck. They managed to apprehend a mercenary who's been involved with several raids in the area. From what I hear the mercenary is being very co-operative. That's not something their gang is going to appreciate.

We want to safely extract them from our site so they’ll be smuggled in an escape pod. However, it appears the poor sap had a tracking chip installed, so we're concerned that their gang are on the way to either liberate them or kill them. Probably the latter; less work.

I’m looking for people to assist the settlement in making sure the captive survives. Can you help?

The settlement is requesting that any and all pilots who are willing to help their defence efforts get to them ASAP. If you succeed, you'll be handsomely rewarded.

No doubt the mercenaries were hired by one of our rivals. They'll do anything to prevent the pioneering work we're conducting. Work which could benefit many, many people one day. The settlement is requesting that any and all pilots who are willing to help their defence efforts get to them ASAP. If you succeed, you'll be handsomely rewarded.

mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_001_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_001_narr:
I'm sure I don't need to tell you how easy it is to lose touch with old friends. There's a whole galaxy to get lost in. I had a friend that I thought I'd never hear from again, but last month I got a message from them out of the blue. It was just one of those moments, y'know?.
Sorry, I'm rambling. The point is it's their birthday soon and I want to send them a gift. Back in the day we used to recommend novels to each other, so I've put together a bunch of the ones I've read since we lost contact. Think you can get it over to them?
mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_002_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_002_narr:
Thanks for stopping. One of our settlements needs a $#CommodityName; sending over. Except this isn't the first request - it's the third in a month. So either the last two were misplaced or something they're working on has gone awry. They didn't sound panicked in the requisition message, so hopefully it’s the former, but they're also keeping tight-lipped about why they need it.
I guess the long and short of it is: this'll probably be a simple delivery run, but just in case, keep your eyes peeled when you’re there.
mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_003_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_003_narr:
I've got a chemical sample I need shipping over to a potential customer. Their last supplier went out of business - apparently some clueless tech got clumsy and now there's a crater where their work station used to be - and we're the nearest company who supply what they need.
Even though you'll only be transporting a small sample of gas, it is explosive. If you hear hissing...You know what? You're a professional. I'm sure it'll be fine.
mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_004_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_004_narr: My employers have been suckered into a terrible deal with another settlement, and I just know it's going to backfire spectacularly. We're letting them in on a custom filtration process we spent a fortune developing and they may as well be handing us some magic beans in return. But can anyone talk management out of it? What do you think? Do me a favour and take this data off my hands. I don't want to be part of this jackassery any longer than I have to. The way I see it, the sooner this whole thing blows up, the sooner us factory-floor workers can start pointing fingers to get some of our 'superiors' fired.
mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_005_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_005_narr:
I bet you hate red tape, huh? As a Commander you probably have rules and regulations you have to follow. As an enterprising retailer of personal goods, I have similar issues. There’s a lot at stake if I choose to ignore them.
Are the items I sell completely legit? Depends who’s asking. But anyone looking at them would be hard placed to tell. They're every bit as good as the originals produced by the manufacturer. It's just that they're made elsewhere by independent craftspeople.
I need you to make this delivery for me because customs are monitoring my ship. I sure hope you accept, because if I get caught with counterfeit merch again then it’s gonna be the last time.
mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_006_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_006_narr:
You're gonna think I'm crazy asking a Commander to do this job, but I've arranged a delivery for a fossil collector willing to pay a premium for a cast. Yes, a cast fossil; not even a real one. Some people have way too many credits, I guess.
Anyone with an ounce of sense would just find one at a crappy market stall, but this customer really wants authenticity and my sample is supposedly from some species their collection lacks. People who’re into these things can tell the difference, I suppose.
I’m telling you, the team back at the office are going to get a laugh out of this one.
mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_007_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_007_narr:
Looking for work? I need you to get some custom spyware we've developed over to a settlement and I'd appreciate it happening without delay. Someone has been poking around the settlement’s network - which is precisely what happens when you continually forget to upgrade your encryption software. Fools.
Thing is, before we close the many loopholes in their security, I'd like to do a little detective work so I can figure out who's been snooping around. There hasn't been any damage yet, so for all I know it could be some bored worker with too much time on their hands rather than corporate espionage. But either way, I'll sleep easier once I know which it is.
A contact will be waiting to collect the data package. You'll be paid upon your return.
mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_008_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_008_narr:
Don't you just love it when you have a customer exactly where you want them? It makes selling mundane items so much more interesting when you can smell how desperate their need is. If you ask me, when you allow for leeway in your experiments you deserve to be taken advantage of. It's how the corporate world operates.
But enough about my personal entertainment. I have a package waiting to be delivered. Providing you’re willing, I’ll let you get going with the consignment. Considering how much I've charged them for it, I can give you a decent fee for your trouble.

mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_missionc: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_delivery_contact_narrativ:
This should be nice and easy. We just got an order from another settlement for a mining rig optimisation schematic. Our team came up with a few tweaks which have seen our yields bumped a few percentage points. Sounds small, but believe me - that's not to be sniffed at when you're pulling tons of resources out of the ground each day.
The schematic is proprietary work, though, so it's not something we just want to transmit over comms and risk interception. People want an edge? They can pay for it. Anyway, if you'd oblige me, get it over to them, will you?
