mission_onfoot_hack_download_001_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_001_name_ti: Digital Espionage: Download $#CommodityName; from a data port
mission_onfoot_hack_download_001_narrati:
A facility owned by a partner of mine was attacked recently. The raid did extensive damage to expensive equipment and some good men were lost, so we’ve been working hard to discover who was responsible.

I’ve been able to establish where the attack was orchestrated from, but little else of worth. That’s why I need someone who can infiltrate the location’s security network and download some of their records. The data should be able to tell us who ordered the strike, and we can ensure that person faces the consequences of their actions.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_002_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_002_name_ti: Digital Espionage: Download $#CommodityName; from a data port
mission_onfoot_hack_download_002_narrati:
A family member has been arrested for something she didn’t do. I know it for a fact, I just haven’t been able to prove it. I’ve tried hiring the best legal team I can afford and pleading with the people accusing her, but nothing’s worked. I thought I was completely out of options.

That’s when a friend suggested I hire someone who can find hard evidence. Surveillance footage from the location they’re saying the time took place. If you can get hold of it, I’m sure we’ll be able to prove my kin was nowhere near that place. Do you think you can help me keep her out of prison?
mission_onfoot_hack_download_003_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_003_name_ti: Digital Espionage: Download $#CommodityName; from a data port
mission_onfoot_hack_download_003_narrati:
There is no greater crime than disloyalty. And when the betrayal comes from your own crew, you have to act before it tears the whole team apart.

I need to find out which of my people has turned on us. Records show one of our shuttles regularly visiting a facility owned by our rivals. Whoever the traitor is, they did a piss-poor job of covering their tracks. All you have to do is download the relevant surveillance data so I can identify them.

Then I can decide how to deal with them.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_004_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_004_name_ti: Digital Espionage: Download $#CommodityName; from a data port
mission_onfoot_hack_download_004_narrati:
Things are pretty tough for my business at the moment. A few of the larger corps have identified topographical surveying as an easy way to make money from settlement developers and they've moved into an already crowded market. It's putting the squeeze on us smaller operators. The corps have the money to hire droves of surveyors with the best equipment and we simply can't compete with budgets like that.

But I can afford to hire someone to steal a copy of all the data one corp has accumulated. If you bring that data to me it should even the odds for a while.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_005_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_005_name_ti: Digital Espionage: Download $#CommodityName; from a data port
mission_onfoot_hack_download_005_narrati:
I don’t know if you keep up with local politics, but there’s a rising star making headlines. A combination of good looks and lofty promises is enough to turn anyone into a successful politician. But if you look carefully at their actual policies you'll see they're going to destroy businesses like mine. The taxes they’re talking about are downright criminal, and I refuse to let it happen.

The best way to bring down a politician never really changes. Scandal. I’m sure this one has a few questionable financial backers which could be shared with suitable newscasts. I know where one of their coordinators has been working recently; I want you to get in and grab some campaign details. Let's see if we can't shake some secrets loose.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_006_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_006_name_ti: Digital Espionage: Download $#CommodityName; from a data port
mission_onfoot_hack_download_006_narrati:
I’ve been coordinating informants for my company for years, but I’ve never had a problem like this one before. One of my operatives was spotted somewhere they should never have been, and I can’t help but wonder if they’ve switched sides. This is one of my top sources, so I need to find out for sure if they’ve gone rogue.

I’m hoping the sighting was a mistake or a clever misdirection by another corp. I’ve started similar rumours myself in the past. I need to examine records from the settlement this individual was reportedly at before I'll know. Grab it for me and I'll pay you for the trouble.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_007_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_007_name_ti: Digital Espionage: Download $#CommodityName; from a data port
mission_onfoot_hack_download_007_narrati:
I’ve been enjoying watching the rough ride of a certain political advisor in the press lately. Their party belongs to an organisation that is at odds with the people I work for. Only the bad publicity doesn't seem to be sticking, and it won't be long before this wretch squirms their way out of it. Unless the skeletons keep marching out of the closet, of course.

There have always been rumours about this person’s private life, particularly in regards to illegal substances. It just so happens I know where to find evidence of them. Get it to me and I’ll find some way of leaking it. You'll disappear with credits, never to be spoken of again.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_008_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_008_name_ti: Digital Espionage: Download $#CommodityName; from a data port
mission_onfoot_hack_download_008_narrati:
I’m in touch with a group of activists doing important work that could save lives. I can’t go into detail because, well, it’s a politically sensitive subject. What I can tell you is that my associates believe in the project. That’s why I’ve promised to make their next excursion to obtain necessary components as safe as possible.

I need someone to hack into the target settlement’s network and pull information related to security measures. Once we’re confident the activists can sneak in without being tracked, they can proceed. Everyone will be satisfied, and you will be paid.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_009_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_009_name_ti: Digital Espionage: Download $#CommodityName; from a data port
mission_onfoot_hack_download_009_narrati:
My associates and I are growing concerned about a company operating in this system. Especially the political lobbying they’ve been involved with. We've heard rumours that this company has been throwing a lot of credits in some questionable directions and I want to find out if it's true. If it is, it’s important to know what their broader objective is.

I need you to infiltrate one of the company’s facilities and obtain the listed data. Using that we can track the movements of their executives, check who they might be meeting with, and maybe - if necessary - arrange a meeting with them ourselves.

Does that sound like the sort of thing you are willing to handle?
mission_onfoot_hack_download_010_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_010_name_ti: Digital Espionage: Download $#CommodityName; from a data port
mission_onfoot_hack_download_010_narrati:
One of my company’s more reliable partners has finally decided to support the war effort in this system. Only, for some baffling reason, they’ve chosen to supply the wrong side. Why they would do such a thing is beyond me, but the owners must have their reasons.

While my boss works on a strongly worded comms message, I’d like you to head to one of the settlements involved and access its network. If we can find out what the corp is getting in return for its support, it may help our efforts to make the owners change their mind. Though given the poor decision making on display that may be optimistic on my part. Interested?
mission_onfoot_hack_download_011_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_download_011_name_ti: Digital Espionage: Download $#CommodityName; from a data port
mission_onfoot_hack_download_011_narrati:
Across this system, a war is taking place between two factions, one of which I represent. History will record a single victor and a single loser. Now that humanity operates on a galactic scale, most are uninterested in further granularity.

The reality of the situation is that both factions are supported by a myriad of smaller companies, contractors and mercenaries such as yourself. This network of assistance allows the broader conflict to continue. With enough supply chains cut, a faction will find itself struggling to maintain an offensive.

This is where you come in. I have identified a suitable target known to be supplying our enemy. I will pay you well to bring me the listed data from its secure network so that a suitable counter-measure can be prepared.

mission_onfoot_hack_download_narrative:
You’d think trying to stop the next health crisis would be something everyone would care about, right? Then why does no one seem to want to do anything about it? The next pandemic could be one made in a lab; a bioweapon that gets loose and wipes out whole planets. And it’s being created right now, as we speak! The only thing that can save us is the work being done on possible counter-measures by one small, underfunded group of researchers, and I’m doing everything I can to help them.

Right now, it's vital that we access to any data the developer of one of these abominations has amassed so far. Please, we need someone who can hack into my contract target's systems and bring the information back before it’s too late.

mission_onfoot_hack_upload_001_missionco: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_001_narrative:
Maybe you’ve heard the buzz surrounding a local company hitting the stock market soon. It’s going to bump a lot of credits into a lot of personal accounts. But that will only happen if the company’s financial performance is accurate. A client of mine has reason to believe some quarterly reports have been tampered with.

All you have to do is gain access to their database so we can see verify the public reports against their internal numbers. If my client’s suspicions are correct, it may be far more profitable to short the new stock when it goes live. But that’s none of your concern, friend.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_002_missionco: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_002_narrative:
My people have been locking horns with members of another faction for months. We’ve had some skirmishes here and there, competed for a few contracts. The usual. Now this faction is saying they want to bury the hatchet, and are “looking forward to a new era of cooperation” with us.  They’re even saying they’ll stop manufacturing competing products.

Clearly, this offer is bullshit. I don’t believe a word of it. Given the faction’s track record, it’s all a ploy to keep us quiet before making a big play in the system. I’d like to show my bosses proof of this theory.

If we could listen in on their comms, we’ll be able to monitor their movements and determine what their real intentions are. I need someone to get us hooked in. Are you interested?
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_003_missionco: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_003_narrative:
Want to help me catch one of the worst criminals in the system? The agency I work with has been chasing them for months, but we’ve never been able to prove anything. Smuggling, piracy, terrorist connections... They’re smart enough to make sure we can’t make anything stick, but I’ve finally figured out how we’re going to nail them.

I’ve been piecing together financial investments of known proxy companies, and one settlement keeps popping up as a recipient. It’s the perfect place to launder dirty credits and, with your help, I'm going to prove it our target is doing just that. Undeclared income is small fry compared to their real crimes, but it’s better than nothing.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_004_missionco: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_004_narrative:
My company is in a race to develop a key piece of technology that could be worth a lot of credits in contracts. Our researchers are as qualified and well-funded as any team out there, but development takes time. Now we’re hearing that another corporation working on the same tech is already close to a working prototype. I’m sceptical, but people can’t help themselves from gossiping.

The whole thing is destroying morale in our labs and, even though it’s still just a rumour. My boss told me to drop it and focus on the work, but I just have to know the truth. Upload this software and I’ll be able to review this competitor’s project notes myself.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_005_missionco: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_005_narrative:
My crew just pulled off a real coup. One that’s going to set us up for years to come. Can’t give you all the details, but we’ve obtained a shipment of expensive gene meds. I’m sure some soulless corp puppet will lose his job as result but that ain’t our problem.

Anyway, people will be looking for the meds and I need to be completely sure nobody’s gonna look our way. One of our software engineers has written a nasty virus that will chew up log on any system exposed to it. A sneaky upload to the right facility and we’ll be in the clear. You in?
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_006_missionco: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_006_narrative:
I’ve been thinking a lot about revenge. For example, what’s the best way to get back at someone who’s been spreading rumours about you? Violence seems excessive. Killing is way out of line.  No, what I want is for this liar to feel the same humiliation I had to go through. It was their fault everyone was talking behind my back; their fault I was forced to quit my damned job.

I think I've settled on the perfect method. You’re going to upload some ‘evidence’ back at my old job’s outpost that implies the liar has been leaking confidential data. That'll be just the thing.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_007_missionco: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_007_narrative:
One of my associates has just come back from what I’d call a very successful mission feeding us information about a rival corp. Eventually, a few people started getting suspicious and my friend had to get out of there. It appeared to be a clean departure until we realised a backdoor comms port was still active that, if discovered, could incriminate my team.

I've gotten hold of some software that'll root out and erase the problem. Under the circumstances, I think an outsider should take care of it.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_008_missionco: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_008_narrative:
I'm in charge of our organisation's competitor analysis division. These days it's important to make sure nobody's outperforming you or making any threatening moves. And so far, so good. There is one possible fly in the ointment, though. A particular operation which - if it pulled its socks up - could spell real trouble.

Luckily for us, this competitor is being utterly mismanaged. We'd like to keep it that way. Get this installed on their systems and, with any luck, the employees will never stop chasing their tail. I'm sure you'll agree it's the best possible outcome for everyone concerned.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_009_missionco: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_009_narrative:
The company I work for has a single byword: security. After some unfortunate breaches in the past, we’ve made a point of keeping our systems watertight. I take personal pride in our continued success.

Of course, we like to keep up to date with the latest network protection software, and it was while trialling one of the options that I came to a sudden realisation: most of our competition still harbour massive security weaknesses.

You see, the software manufacturer we're trialling listed several other companies who were considering a partnership with them, which means they must currently be using outdated software with known vulnerabilities. I need you to install a program that will let us sail right through them. Purely for research, of course.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_010_missionco: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_010_narrative:
I need someone who hasn't got ties to the conflict my clients are currently in to carry out a mission. Nothing too dangerous; I need some software uploaded to the right network. The good news is that the target facility doesn't belong to a hostile force, so the personnel shouldn't be on especially high alert.

My clients intend to borrow portions of the target’s satellite array to keep an eye on developments in the system. If everything goes to plan, the owners won't even know anybody was hijacking their network. After all, the last thing we want to do is to start another war right now.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_011_missionco: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_011_narrative:
My team’s statisticians have been examining what they know about our faction’s enemy and known supply routes. They’ve come up with an interesting hypothesis: given the manifests of traders between two specific ports, the enemy is likely being supplied by a particular third party. Of course, since this is based on statistical modelling, we don't have any solid proof. That's why I need an independent contractor like yourself to confirm it for us.

I have a file with some dormant spyware as an attachment, as well as a target location. Get the file onto the local network and I'll do the rest. Honestly, I hope the guys are wrong because if we aren't then this war just got a whole lot harder.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_covert_001_mi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.

mission_onfoot_hack_upload_covert_missio: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_hack_upload_covert_narrat:
You wouldn’t believe the amount of corruption that goes on in the galaxy - or how little of it is ever exposed. One of my clients is adamant that a rival corp continues to expand despite obvious structural incompetence. Somehow they keep getting richer and absorbing personnel from other companies. It just doesn’t add up.

Looking at the numbers, I’m starting to think this corp might be dealing in fraudulent stock to inflate their earnings. That’s a hard claim to prove, though. I need someone to get into one of their settlement networks and insert a tracking program so I can inspect their transaction history. That should fill in the remaining pieces of the puzzle.

mission_onfoot_heist_001_missioncomplete: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_001_name_title: Theft: Obtain the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_001_narrative:
A very wealthy client of mine has set their sights on a rare fossil as the centrepiece of a growing collection. Unfortunately, the fossil's current owner just won’t sell, no matter how much money I dangle in front of them. Apparently it has 'sentimental value'. A gift from a lost love or some crap.

My client is already in talks with other brokers to see if any of them has better luck. I think a more forceful method of acquisition is in order, however. Bring me that specimen before anyone else can get hold of it and I’ll share the commission with you.
mission_onfoot_heist_002_missioncomplete: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_002_name_title: Theft: Obtain the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_002_narrative:
There’s a rare fossil out there, just sitting around doing nothing but looking pretty. I know what you’re thinking, isn’t that what fossils usually do? Most of them, sure, but this particular specimen could be put to better use in a lab. The research team I represent have been trying to get hold of it for a while now.

A recent funding injection has given the team some new options. We still don't have the funds to meet the owner's asking price, but I think we have enough here to hire someone of your talents to obtain the fossil for us. Just make sure you bring it to me in one piece.
mission_onfoot_heist_003_missioncomplete: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_003_name_title: Theft: Obtain the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_003_narrative:
A government official starting to make a name in this system received a package full of dangerous chemicals last week. Fortunately, the sensors in his office detected the threat before the package was opened, but we still need to find out who sent it.

I’ve traced the chemicals to a scientist who has some form when it comes to political activism. But if we try to get access to the samples through official channels, it risks tipping off this lunatic and giving them a chance to delete potential evidence. I’m betting you could sidestep that problem and get me what I need, though. Right?
mission_onfoot_heist_004_missioncomplete: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_004_name_title: Theft: Obtain the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_004_narrative:
A group of scientists have decided to play God, messing with things they don’t understand. Such arrogance! They’re trying to engineer a rapidly evolving virus that targets cancerous cells within the human body. Can you imagine what will happen when they let that thing loose and it evolves past its original purpose? Well, I'm not going to let that happen.

My people and I have made it our life's work to keep science in check, and we’ll use any means we have to. I’m sure you can appreciate that the rampant development of man-made diseases isn’t worth the risk. Get us access to that research so we can learn how to effectively terminate the project before it's too late.
mission_onfoot_heist_005_missioncomplete: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_005_name_title: Theft: Obtain the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_005_narrative:
My crew has a lot of enemies, but that’s okay. It just means we’re doing our job right. Someone takes a shot at us, we return fire. But then there are threats you don’t see coming. Like intel saying a new chemical agent is being developed by some zealot anarchists and we're likely to be one of the targets if they manage to weaponise it. The worst part is that market antidotes are usually ineffective against basement lab-grown strains like this. I haven't told my crew all the details, but it worries me a lot.

We're trying to stop the scumbags before they can finish, but in the meantime, we'll need to work on a counter-agent. If you can bring me a sample of this chemical agent to start running tests on, you could save a lot of lives.
mission_onfoot_heist_006_missioncomplete: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_006_name_title: Theft: Obtain the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_006_narrative:
One of my best friends was killed in a crash recently. The authorities claim pilot error, but my friend was one of the best pilots I’ve ever known. I started digging into the accident and found out there have been lots of similar crashes involving a particular module installed on that ship. I refuse to believe that the part manufacturer doesn't know about it, either.

I found some of the production facilities used to construct the module. They must have copies of the schematics. If you can get a copy to me, I've got a few mechanics ready to study them for a fatal flaw. If I'm right, there’s going to be hell to pay.
mission_onfoot_heist_007_missioncomplete: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_007_name_title: Theft: Obtain the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_007_narrative:
My people have been working on some really interesting ship modifications for months now. We’re a small operation, but we’ve got better ideas and smarter engineers than any of the giant corporations in this system. You can imagine how pissed off we were when we heard one of them was working on a project almost identical to our current one.

We think either someone leaked our designs or they were able to steal them from us. Well, we can play that game too. I want to see their designs and, if we’re right, sue their asses for corporate theft. Don't look at me like that - they stole from us first, so we're just taking back our property!
mission_onfoot_heist_008_missioncomplete: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_008_name_title: Theft: Obtain the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_008_narrative:
We’ve got a mole in our company. Someone I work with every day is leaking our internal memos to one of our biggest rivals. I haven’t been able to find out exactly who it is, but I do know who they’re reporting to. I don't want to waste time with internal investigations and disciplinary committees. I want to follow a more direct route.

The only lead I have is that the mole sends updates by Insight comms. If you can find their recordings I'll get someone to open it up and uncover the traitor. I need this dealt with quickly, so I'll pay you accordingly.
mission_onfoot_heist_009_missioncomplete: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_009_name_title: Theft: Obtain the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_009_narrative:
Someone very close to me has gone missing and no one seems to know anything about it or even care that they’ve disappeared. It's been driving me crazy with worry! I’ve spent every hour I have trying to find something to go on. I even hired a private investigator, but all they could tell me who last met with the missing person.

The contact I was given has refused to acknowledge any meeting took place and eventually blocked me from their comms. Find them and get me all their documents, there must be something in there!

mission_onfoot_heist_covert_narrative:
There’s a group of researchers who’ve figured out a way of improving the survivability of crops in low-quality soil, but they won’t let anyone in on their findings. Don’t you hate it when people won’t share? This could save lives...and perhaps help the conglomerate I work with expand even further.

Believe me, it’s hard to colonise a new planet. It's even harder to make that colony self-sustaining. If you can find a way to bring me this crop research, it’ll make our next venture a lot easier.

mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_001_name_title: Nonviolent Theft: Take the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_001_narrative:
A very wealthy client of mine has set their sights on a rare fossil as the centrepiece of a growing collection. Unfortunately, the fossil's current owner just won’t sell, no matter how much money I dangle in front of them. Apparently it has 'sentimental value'. A gift from a lost love or some crap.

My client is already in talks with other brokers to see if any of them has better luck. I think a more forceful method of acquisition is in order, however. Bring me that specimen before anyone else can get hold of it and I’ll share the commission with you.
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_002_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_002_name_title: Nonviolent Theft: Take the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_002_narrative:
There’s a rare fossil out there, just sitting around doing nothing but looking pretty. I know what you’re thinking, isn’t that what fossils usually do? Most of them, sure, but this particular specimen could be put to better use in a lab. The research team I represent have been trying to get hold of it for a while now.

A recent funding injection has given the team some new options. We still don't have the funds to meet the owner's asking price, but I think we have enough here to hire someone of your talents to obtain the fossil for us. Just make sure you bring it to me in one piece.
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_003_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_003_name_title: Nonviolent Theft: Take the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_003_narrative:
A government official starting to make a name in this system received a package full of dangerous chemicals last week. Fortunately, the sensors in his office detected the threat before the package was opened, but we still need to find out who sent it.

I’ve traced the chemicals to a scientist who has some form when it comes to political activism. But if we try to get access to the samples through official channels, it risks tipping off this lunatic and giving them a chance to delete potential evidence. I’m betting you could sidestep that problem and get me what I need, though. Right?
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_004_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_004_name_title: Nonviolent Theft: Take the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_004_narrative:
A group of scientists have decided to play God, messing with things they don’t understand. Such arrogance! They’re trying to engineer a rapidly evolving virus that targets cancerous cells within the human body. Can you imagine what will happen when they let that thing loose and it evolves past its original purpose? Well, I'm not going to let that happen.

My people and I have made it our life's work to keep science in check, and we’ll use any means we have to. I’m sure you can appreciate that the rampant development of man-made diseases isn’t worth the risk. Get us access to that research so we can learn how to effectively terminate the project before it's too late.
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_005_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_005_name_title: Nonviolent Theft: Take the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_005_narrative:
My crew has a lot of enemies, but that’s okay. It just means we’re doing our job right. Someone takes a shot at us, we return fire. But then there are threats you don’t see coming. Like intel saying a new chemical agent is being developed by some zealot anarchists and we're likely to be one of the targets if they manage to weaponise it. The worst part is that market antidotes are usually ineffective against basement lab-grown strains like this. I haven't told my crew all the details, but it worries me a lot.

We're trying to stop the scumbags before they can finish, but in the meantime, we'll need to work on a counter-agent. If you can bring me a sample of this chemical agent to start running tests on, you could save a lot of lives.
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_006_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_006_name_title: Nonviolent Theft: Take the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_006_narrative:
One of my best friends was killed in a crash recently. The authorities claim pilot error, but my friend was one of the best pilots I’ve ever known. I started digging into the accident and found out there have been lots of similar crashes involving a particular module installed on that ship. I refuse to believe that the part manufacturer doesn't know about it, either.

I found some of the production facilities used to construct the module. They must have copies of the schematics. If you can get a copy to me, I've got a few mechanics ready to study them for a fatal flaw. If I'm right, there’s going to be hell to pay.
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_007_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_007_name_title: Nonviolent Theft: Take the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_007_narrative:
My people have been working on some really interesting ship modifications for months now. We’re a small operation, but we’ve got better ideas and smarter engineers than any of the giant corporations in this system. You can imagine how pissed off we were when we heard one of them was working on a project almost identical to our current one.

We think either someone leaked our designs or they were able to steal them from us. Well, we can play that game too. I want to see their designs and, if we’re right, sue their asses for corporate theft. Don't look at me like that - they stole from us first, so we're just taking back our property!
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_008_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_008_name_title: Nonviolent Theft: Take the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_008_narrative:
We’ve got a mole in our company. Someone I work with every day is leaking our internal memos to one of our biggest rivals. I haven’t been able to find out exactly who it is, but I do know who they’re reporting to. I don't want to waste time with internal investigations and disciplinary committees. I want to follow a more direct route.

The only lead I have is that the mole sends updates by Insight comms. If you can find their recordings I'll get someone to open it up and uncover the traitor. I need this dealt with quickly, so I'll pay you accordingly.
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_009_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_009_name_title: Nonviolent Theft: Take the $#CommodityName; from a settlement
mission_onfoot_heist_ncd_009_narrative:
Someone very close to me has gone missing and no one seems to know anything about it or even care that they’ve disappeared. It's been driving me crazy with worry! I’ve spent every hour I have trying to find something to go on. I even hired a private investigator, but all they could tell me who last met with the missing person.

The contact I was given has refused to acknowledge any meeting took place and eventually blocked me from their comms. Find them and get me all their documents, there must be something in there!

mission_onfoot_heist_poi_001_name: Seize the $#CommodityName; from a hidden cache
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_001_name_title: Seize the $#CommodityName; from a hidden cache
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_001_narrative:
I'm here on behalf of the local law enforcement agency. From time to time, pressing matters will prevent them from being able to dedicate adequate resources to certain aspects of an investigation. In these instances, it's not uncommon to hire independent contractors like yourself.

The job in question is to verify statements made by a defendant facing a lengthy prison term. The information offered in exchange for a reduced sentence is quite interesting, though. To whit: the location of several stashes of weapon-related paraphernalia. We're just looking to verify a single stash; once we have concrete evidence that our information is telling the truth, we'll take it from there.
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_002_missioncomp: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_002_name: Seize the $#CommodityName; from a hidden cache
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_002_name_title: Seize the $#CommodityName; from a hidden cache
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_002_narrative:
I just lost a good friend, and truth be told, I'm at a loss to explain exactly how she died. She'd been looking into a local gang's activities and I think she'd been out to try and find one of their stashes. When she came back, though - she stepped out of her SRV and just dropped dead. Our doc said she'd been exposed to some kind of chemical agent. Problem is, she's always been a thorn in the side of local law enforcement so they just chalked it up to misadventure and closed the case.

I'm not letting her die for no reason. I pulled the logs from her SRV so I know where she was looking - I just need someone to find the evidence there and get it back to me.
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_003_missioncomp: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_003_name: Seize the $#CommodityName; from a hidden cache
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_003_name_title: Seize the $#CommodityName; from a hidden cache
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_003_narrative:
I was on an inter-system transport last month which was raided by pirates. Fortunately, they were the kind that don't blow up our escape pods, but the ship they took had almost everything I owned on it - including an Insight recording which means a lot to me. Honestly, they could keep everything else they took from me if it meant I got that recording back.

I had a private investigator track down the location of the cache, but they were unwilling to risk recovering the recording themselves. They recommended I look for someone who looked like they could handle themselves - someone like you.
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_004_missioncomp: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_004_name: Seize the $#CommodityName; from a hidden cache
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_004_name_title: Seize the $#CommodityName; from a hidden cache
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_004_narrative:
I like to think that the organisation I work for helps people. Yes, the drugs we sell aren't legal. But a lot of our customers rely on our products just to get through the day. Our chems are clean and only as addictive as they need to be. Someone, though, has been producing something far more dangerous and sneaking it into our supply chain somewhere. We've got a fairly good idea which gang is doing it but we don't want to start a war with the wrong people if we can avoid it.

I'm going to give you the location of one of their stashes. Go get us a sample from there so we can compare it with the stuff which is killing our customers. We'll handle everything else ourselves.
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_005_missioncomp: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_005_name: Seize the $#CommodityName; from a hidden cache
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_005_name_title: Seize the $#CommodityName; from a hidden cache
mission_onfoot_heist_poi_005_narrative:
The operation I'm with has been looking to move on from common or garden narcotics into something where the profit margins are a lot higher. We've spent a whole bunch on research and development and we think we've got something that could be of real interest to the right buyers. The wrinkle is that one of our rivals got wind of it and has stolen a sample of our new product.

As it happens, one of our crew used to run with their gang a long time ago and has a good idea where they'll have stashed our stuff. They'll probably try moving it soon so the clock's ticking. We don't want to see our product show up on the black market unless it's us selling it there, understood?

mission_onfoot_heist_poi_narrative:
The situation is this: I've got a lot of friends in a community which has been plagued by theft, violence and drug use of late. It's only a matter of time before someone gets killed. They're pretty sure they know the gang which is dealing the drugs, but local law enforcement has them down as petty thieves at worst and won't investigate them. There's always bigger fish to fry.

Look, all my friends need is for someone to search one of the gang's stashes and find evidence that they've graduated from theft to drug running. They've identified the location of a likely stash, but none of them has the combat training to risk raiding it. They need someone like you.

mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_001: Okay, fine. Circumstances change and jobs get cancelled sometimes. Just don't expect to be high on my list of future hires…
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_002: Just what I wanted; a logistical nightmare. Apparently I have to find someone else to do a job I've already contracted out.
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_003: Most people take a very dim view of people who let them down in this manner. A very dim view indeed.
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_004: I genuinely thought I'd found someone who could handle the mission. Fine - no hard feelings, Commander.
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_005: Kind of you to stick me with the paperwork on this one. No, really. You just go about your day and have a lovely time, alright?
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_006: Understood. I'll get someone else to handle the contract, then. Just don't make abandonment a habit if you want a good rep with us.
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_007: That's all I need today. A Commander who can't see things through to the finish. What a waste of time.
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_008: You do know that quitting this job isn't exactly going to endear you to my associates, don't you?
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_009: I just knew from the moment I posted it that this task wouldn't go smoothly. Makes sense that a quitter would take the contract.
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_010: This is going to be a red mark against your name, Commander. I don't like quitters, and neither does my boss.
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_011: Well, that'll teach me for hiring some freelancer instead of a professional.  Are you sure you're a licensed Commander?
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_012: I had enough on my schedule already without chasing after a broken contract. Next time you want work make sure you're going to complete it, okay?
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_013: Why did you even take the assignment if you had no intention of finishing it? Go waste someone else's time next time you need credits.
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_014: If you keep behaving like this then one day it's going to bite you in the ass. Eventually, you're gonna cross the wrong person.
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_015: I hope you understand the consequences of quitting that contract. Innocent people are at risk because you didn't keep your word.
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_016: You couldn't possibly appreciate the trouble you've dropped me in by bailing on the contract. Maybe I can salvage this in time… maybe not.
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_017: How could you do this?! I was relying on you to complete the job and it's too late to use someone else! This is so bad...
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_018: If there's ever an opportunity to aggravate you in the future then I'd appreciate it if you gave me a heads up. Because now I'm in serious crap because you decided to quit.
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_019: I took you at your word and this is how you repay me? You can't even begin to know the amount of damage you've just caused. I guess you don't believe in karma.
mission_onfoot_inbox_abandon_020: By quitting that contract, chances are you've condemned multiple people to death. I hope this information keeps you up at night.
mission_onfoot_inbox_assassination_fligh:
Commander,

You should know that $#PilotName1; is aware that they're a target. If they believe they're in immediate danger, whether from you or anyone else, they're likely to try and flee.
Make sure you take them out before that can happen.
mission_onfoot_inbox_assassination_targe:
Commander,

I've received word that your target has been taken out by a third party. While unexpected, the mission objective as been achieved and I will uphold the terms of our contract. Return to me to collect your reward.
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_001: I don't know how you managed to fail such a simple task. Did you accidentally flush the package out of an airlock?
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_002: You're not the only contractor I've had screw a job up this week, but this is the one that annoys me the most. Thanks for nothing.
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_003: I practically handed you success on a golden platter and you still failed. Maybe we should demand an aptitude test from the people taking our contracts.
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_004: A word of advice: if you're not sure you're capable of handling a job, don't apply for it in the future.
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_005: I am tired of dealing with amateurs. Next time I'll just throw the contract straight in the trash and save myself some time.
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_006: I understand these things happen. Space isn't very forgiving and I'd be lying if I said I hadn't screwed up myself before. Better luck next time.
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_007: Listen, we all have bad days sometimes. It just sucks that your bad day means mine will be even worse.
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_008: You've let me down, Commander. I had a lot riding on you completing this mission successfully.
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_009: A Ceti rabbit could have completed that task. What the hell were you doing?!
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_010: Oh, great. Now I have to tell my boss that I hired an idiot. This is going to be a fun message to write…
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_011: You failed? I had such high hopes for you, Commander. This is a firm kick in the nethers, you know?
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_012: I didn't think anyone could botch such an easy job so badly. In some ways I'm impressed. Although not in any good ones.
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_013: That blunder of yours has turned my headache into a migraine. For both of our sakes, I hope something can be salvaged from this mess.
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_014: I don't care how you botched the mission, I just care about the world of trouble your failure has stranded me in.
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_015: This little mistake of yours is going to have some messy repercussions for a lot of people. I hope you can live with that.
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_016: Did you not understand how important this job was when you took it? Because your failure to complete it is going to have some serious consequences.
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_017: How did you screw the contract up? I can't even begin to explain the damage you've done. Thanks for nothing.
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_018: After that performance, I wouldn't bother coming back to me for a job any time soon. Chances are I won't be around much longer.
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_019: This was a straightforward hit but somehow you let the target escape. Next time I'll send someone who knows how to use a gun.
mission_onfoot_inbox_failure_020: All you had to do was access their network but somehow this was beyond you! I just hope the target doesn't relocate and wipe their databanks. How irritating.
mission_onfoot_inbox_hitman_001:
I've received word that you completed the contract, Commander. I'm impressed.

Unfortunately, it looks like your work has attracted some attention; as I have received word that a hitman has been sent after you. They shouldn't be a problem for a skilled individual such as yourself.

See you soon.
mission_onfoot_inbox_playerhunter_bounty:

$#PilotName2; was a bounty hunter contracted to take you out. Guess the $#PrimaryMissionType; job you pulled ticked off the wrong people.

mission_onfoot_inbox_playerhunter_police:

System security learned of your involvement with the $#PrimaryMissionType; contract. Officer $#PilotName2; was assigned to stop you. Wasn’t their day, huh?

Try and keep a low profile on your way to $#DestinationStationName;.

Good luck,
$#MinorFaction;
mission_onfoot_inbox_wrinkle_alert_001:
Commander,

Looks like I've got a leak. An informant has reported that they've just received an alert to all personnel with your description on it. I guess the target is preparing for your arrival.

I still need the job finished so I'm willing to increase the payout significantly. Try not to get killed, okay?
mission_onfoot_inbox_wrinkle_alert_002:
Commander,

The target’s communications network must be good - they know you're coming.

I'm not cancelling the contract, you understand? I will make it worth your while though. Do whatever you need to do and I’ll bump up the payout when this is over.
mission_onfoot_inbox_wrinkle_alert_003:
Commander,

It seems like someone overheard our exchange. There's a urgent broadcast headed to $#DestinationSettlementName; right now and your name is the headline.

I know how this works; unforeseen consequences and all that. Don't worry, you'll be adequately compensated for the extra hassle.

You take out the target while I try and find out who's been listening in.

mission_onfoot_inbox_wrinkle_mb_poi: Urgent update: $#PilotName1; has been tracked to a different location. Updating the target location data now.
mission_onfoot_inbox_wrinkle_poi_001:
Commander, I have urgent news.

One of my scouts spotted $#PilotName1; seemingly fleeing from the settlement. The attempt has been halted, but I couldn’t say how much time you have to complete the job.

I've sent the location to you now. Let's put an end to this.
mission_onfoot_inbox_wrinkle_poi_002:
Commander,

The target made a break for it. Fortunately, I pulled a few strings to ensure they didn't get far. I'm sending you the new location now.

Make sure they don't get away.
mission_onfoot_inbox_wrinkle_poi_003:
Commander,

$#PilotName1; was just reassigned to another location. I anticipated this might happen and had a smuggler in the area to trail them and make a mess of the transport’s engines.

Unfortunately that’s all the involvement the smuggler is willing to provide so I'll still need you to track down the target before they're rescued. The location is attached. I look forward to this being over.

mission_onfoot_massacre_001_missioncompl: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacre_001_narrative:
You have no idea how much I hate scavengers. The worst scum in the universe, preying on the weak and causing nothing but misery. I’d wipe them all out if I could. For now, though, I’ll settle for putting down any that you find before they hit more of my company’s settlements.

We’ve been having power supply problems which, of course, means evacuations and empty facilities. And somehow these rats always manage to sniff out which ones to hit just when they’re most vulnerable. We can’t afford to keep losing resources, so please, hunt down any scavengers lurking at the location I have on file.
mission_onfoot_massacre_002_missioncompl: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacre_002_narrative:
There’s been a wave of data thefts recently that have my people very concerned. The thefts might look like random acts to an outsider, but I can tell you right now that they’re connected. In every instance, the stolen data contains sensitive information about the group I work with. So you can understand why I need you to put an end to this hacking spree.

We know which gang the thieves are affiliated with, but there’s no way of knowing which specific individuals were involved. If they think there's safety in numbers, though, they don’t know my associates very well. I want you to wipe out as many of the dirtbags as you can find. Eventually, the thieves will get the message and find some other group to annoy.
mission_onfoot_massacre_003_missioncompl: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacre_003_narrative:
Satellites aren’t cheap. There are design costs, production expenses, and once launched you need to maintain them. I oversee my company’s whole satellite network, and one of our primary models was recently damaged by a scavenger crew trying their luck. Not for the first time, either. I want to make sure it doesn't happen again.

We've traced the crew's affiliation. Kill as many of them as you can find and they’ll soon learn to keep their grubby paws off of company assets.
mission_onfoot_massacre_004_missioncompl: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacre_004_narrative:
I'm going to lay this out straight: I want you to kill some people. Specifically, the pain-in-our-collective-asses group of thieves who've been targeting our settlements these past few months. If those idiots hadn't got it into their heads to raid us exclusively we probably would have shrugged off the losses, but enough's enough.

Local law enforcement will eventually wipe them out, of course, but not for a while. I'd rather spend a little and see immediate results. We need to make our settlements secure again for the workers.

So, you want to make some credits with that weapon of yours?
mission_onfoot_massacre_005_missioncompl: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacre_005_narrative:
A group of criminals have been hijacking shipments and killing couriers along a planet-to-port trade route. Ruthless, but not entirely unheard of. A recent victim was a childhood friend of my boss, though, and she’s about as pissed off as I’ve ever seen her.

My boss has demanded we find whoever's responsible for the murder. The bandit giving orders is quite a big deal in the local underworld, so going after them directly is more than we can deal with. The grubs doing the dirty work, though? They should be easy pickings.

Hit a bunch of them and I'll see if that can calm my boss down. Don’t be shy about putting them down either - not one of them could claim innocence.
mission_onfoot_massacre_006_missioncompl: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacre_006_narrative:
A pirate gang in the system has grown bold in recent months. They're attacking settlements now - my company’s settlements. The higher-ups are naturally worried that these quick raids have been so successful. I've formed a plan to put a stop to them. It's a simple plan, but I'm certain it'll be effective.

I need this done quickly; promotional reviews are due and I want the credit for putting a stop to the raids. There's a bigger office with an external viewport that I've had my eye on for a while. Take out a bunch of these criminals quickly for me and I'll make it worth your while. Oh, and you'll be making the system safer for many honest workers, of course. If that's an extra incentive for you.
mission_onfoot_massacre_007_missioncompl: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacre_007_narrative:
I never knew that abductions were happening in this system until one of my friends went missing a few months back after a courier job. The authorities found him a couple of weeks back. Judgement was he'd been held captive for labour and was killed attempting to escape.

Nobody was ever charged, though. I've been investigating myself and now I see just how many missing person reports are filed each month. And the authorities do nothing! They say there’s not enough evidence. Well, if they won’t act, then it’s down to good-hearted people like us, Commander.

I have the location where my friend was last seen, and the group there have been questioned multiple times about the disappearances. I'm convinced they're involved and they need to pay for what they're doing.
mission_onfoot_massacre_008_missioncompl: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacre_008_narrative:
One of my team’s most respected members disappeared a few years ago. We’d given him up for dead, but he resurfaced last month. We hardly recognised him. He’d been taken by a gang of criminals who enslaved him for the heck of it. They treated him real bad and almost broke his spirit. But somehow he escaped, and now he wants revenge.

The bastards who had him are still at the same location. Guess they think they're untouchable. I've been asked to hire some people to make a dent in their organisation. You fit the bill, Commander. There's a good payday in it for you.

Sometimes it isn't clear if a target deserves death, but trust me: with this crew there's no doubt.
mission_onfoot_massacre_009_missioncompl: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacre_009_narrative:
Perhaps you’re familiar with the pirate problem in this sector: raids, cargo theft, smuggling and so forth? Well, the pirate gangs have branched out into kidnapping. Their most recent victims were some potential investors who were visiting this system at my company’s request. At this point, you're probably wondering why I'm telling you rather than the police. The simple truth is that our investors were explicit in their preference for the police remaining unaware of their arrival. Sometimes a business has to look beyond the conventional to secure funding.#10;
All I need you to do is permanently deal with the kidnappers. We'll recover our investors afterwards. With luck, they'll be feeling more generous towards us once you’ve wiped out their abductors.
mission_onfoot_massacre_010_missioncompl: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacre_010_narrative:
My squad has identified a target which I believe is of strategic importance to our enemies and which - thanks to our ongoing war efforts on other fronts - has become precariously exposed. Command has authorised the release of additional funds so that we can hire mercenaries to exploit this weakness before they can compensate with additional bodies of their own. All the other details are attached.#10;
This job's going to get bloody. Make sure you're prepared.
mission_onfoot_massacre_011_missioncompl: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacre_011_narrative:
It’s quite clear how the war is going in this system. But allow me to speak plainly: some of the fronts we're fighting on could go either way. That's why we need brave Commanders like yourself who're willing to take up arms and contribute to the effort. With people like you on our side, we could be tipping the balance in one of these areas.#10;
So, what do you say? Do you want to join the right side of history?
mission_onfoot_massacre_012_missioncompl: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacre_012_narrative:
Not a day goes by that our enemies don't stoop to ever more desperate tactics. They don't care who they kill - as far as they're concerned, we're all legitimate targets. We can't allow that to continue, and that's why we need everyone with combat training to do their bit.#10;
As a free agent, I know you don't have a stake in this game, and that's why command has released extra funds so that we can hire mercenaries like yourself. Do the right thing and I'll make it worth your while.
mission_onfoot_massacre_013_missioncompl: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacre_013_narrative:
This war needs to end, and it needs to end soon. Too many good people have died already. That's why I’m asking commanders like yourself to join the fight. We desperately need to bring peace to our system. That won't happen until we've driven every single enemy fighter out from under their rocks and stepped on them like the insects they are.#10;
I can offer you compensation, of course, but more than that we can offer you purpose. Are you in?

mission_onfoot_massacre_missioncomplete: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacre_narrative:
My team has been planning a delicate operation for months to mine, refine and transport highly volatile materials. The whole thing is dangerous work, but it’s worth a lot of money to us and we’ve considered every variable and potential problem. What we didn't predict was just how disruptive a group of hard-headed criminals can be. They've already destroyed a number of our ships and thousands of tons of cargo. We can’t allow them to keep on interfering.

I have information on where to find one of their settlements. I don’t expect you to wipe out the whole gang, but if you eliminate enough of them the rest should scatter. My team can then get back to work without any more problems.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_001_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_001_narra:
I’m looking for somebody who isn’t afraid of a little dirty work and knows not to ask questions.

There’s a corporation out there that needs a lesson in personal accountability. They’ve been spreading their operations to areas they should know to stay far away from. You could argue that they’re putting their workers in unnecessary danger.

Hunt down this corp’s personnel wherever you find them. I want their bosses to truly understand what bad decisions can mean. The hunt for profits doesn’t allow for innocent bystanders.

If you want the credits, take the contract and follow the objectives. As I said: no questions.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_002_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_002_narra:
My company’s boss has spent all week talking to security advisors and come to a rather bold conclusion. We’re going to strike at one of our biggest rivals by eliminating their workers. I’m told this rival has stolen some highly sensitive data from us, so we are responding with a show of force.

Exactly how killing these people will help us is too far above my authority level to appreciate. I’ve only been tasked with hiring somebody ruthless enough to carry out the job. I have faith such violence is the only option we have, and I’m sure my boss will sleep soundly when it is done.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_003_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_003_narra:
This was supposed to be a good year for sales. I promised my bosses the weapons division would be moving more units than ever before. But we’ve had one of our weakest quarters ever, and I’m hanging onto my career by a thread. When did people start feeling so safe that they don't need to expand their personal defence options? I think it’s time to change that, and there’s one corporation in particular that needs a change of heart.

It's typically one of my best customers, but orders have dropped to an all-time low. Put down their security personnel and the execs will quickly remember how my weapons can save lives.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_004_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_004_narra:
My company has been playing it safe for far too long, but finally we're going on the offensive. I’ve been pushing for a more aggressive strategy, so I’m very happy to bring you a fantastic offer. A contract is a contract, but by the Gods, I am having fun with this one!

The board have issued several directives in a specific order, and you will be responsible for the first of them. A strategic strike by an independent mercenary. You have carte blanche to take down any of the target group's members, providing you can handle the heat. Go on, treat yourself!
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_005_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_005_narra:
The corporation I work for has been trying to muscle its way into a certain system for months now. But you know how it is- there’s plenty of competition. The manager tasked with cracking this problem has sent me out with an ingenious idea: scare the crap out of at least one of the companies, and see if that opens a little space for us.

I want the target personnel to feel it just isn’t safe anymore. Wiping out the security personnel should do the trick. But I’ll leave the method up to you. Just make sure there are enough bodies left behind to send the rest running for the nearest shuttle.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_006_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_006_narra:
My clients like to keep tabs on certain crews, making sure they keep in line. Business is about give and take. Well, after a recent fact-finding operation we discovered encoded messages that discuss a territorial expansion. That didn’t go down well with certain people, so I've been instructed to find someone who can persuade one overly ambitious team to change their mind.

Officially, my clients will denounce any attack on this group as barbaric. But anybody worth a damn understands how things are done, so don’t hold back. These notions of expansion must be thoroughly put to rest.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_007_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_007_narra:
I'm out to get the bastards who attacked my company, and I don’t care how much it costs or how many people like you I have to hire. Everyone knows what my team is capable of, but somehow these assholes thought they'd test us. They organised a raid on one of our settlements that left multiple dead. But payback's gonna be twice that.

My bosses will take care of any PR problems if the journos connect the attacks, and you look smart enough to avoid getting the authorities involved. So all that remains is to leave a trail of bodies at the location I give you. Don't worry about the pay, either; you'll be suitably compensated.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_008_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_008_narra:
I have a job of the utmost importance for a Commander who knows how to keep their mouth shut after getting their hands dirty. My superiors have given me few details other than the desired outcome: the multiple, tragic deaths of a certain organisation's employees. It's probably best not to ask any questions anyway.

Sometimes we do what is asked of us to the best of our ability while setting our morals aside. At the end of the day you will get paid, my contract will be complete and everyone can move on. What do you say?
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_009_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_009_narra: I'll keep this short because I don't know a great deal myself. What I have is the target, which is supplied in the attached details, and the name of the client offering a rather generous remuneration for that target's end. If I were you, I wouldn't scrutinize this mission too closely. You either won't like what you see or you'll put the pair of us in someone else's crosshairs. Just take the job and collect the fee, okay?

mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_missionco: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_massacreillegal_narrative:
My crew’s been observing a rival corporation for a while, making sure they’re too busy with their internal politics to pay any real attention to us. Now we’re hearing some news about a merger with one of their competitors, which would be a problem. If this goes through, they’ll be newly focused and heavily resourced. I want to make sure that the merger never goes ahead.

I’ve always found fear is the best method to control a situation like this. If we demonstrate that a merger would put both companies in harm's way, perhaps the weaker board members will reconsider. So hit those bastards with extreme prejudice. I expect a decent body count at the end of it.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_001_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_001_narrative:
The authorities around here are too busy protecting corporate interests to care about people like me. My team might be small, but that doesn’t mean we don't get targeted too.

There’s a group of scavengers who’ve been chipping away at our assets for months. I'm done sitting around waiting for local security to act – as if they ever would. So instead I’m looking for some freelance law enforcement.

The scavengers have avoided hitting any of the big corp settlements because they’re scared of the heat that goes with it.  But I know where they’re camped. Now I need them gone.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_002_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_002_narrative:
Sometimes you just have to take the law into your own hands if you want to get anything done. My clients are sick and tired of being targeted by a gang of criminals, who treat perfectly reputable settlements as their personal vending machines. They’ve stolen from us three times in the last month and we’re just not going to take it anymore.

There’s no chance of getting our things back, but at least we can stop them from ruining us completely. And if your statement is loud enough maybe everyone else will know to leave us alone, too.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_003_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_003_narrative:
My client has had a number of chemicals go missing from settlements it operates. Individually, the chemicals are pretty innocuous compounds, but when listed together they read like an ingredient list for narcotic production. If my hunch is correct, that means the thieves will be back for more soon enough.

Thing is, my client has some long-standing security issues. I'm trying to improve things, but it's moving slowly; if more chemicals go missing in the meantime, I'm likely to be replaced. The risk of ambitious guarantees made when negotiating my salary, you see.

Of course, nothing else will go missing if there's nobody left to steal it. I've moved some numbers around in my budget and paid for information leading to the thieves’ current location. There are a few credits left as a reward, should you choose to wipe out our light-fingered friends.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_004_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_004_narrative:
A criminal syndicate has been using my company’s settlements to make high-grade weapons. Can you imagine the damage this could do to our reputation? We didn’t even realise what was going on until the authorities alerted us. They’d been investigating some suspicious shipments and discovered a whole clandestine operation. We've thankfully proven our innocence, but there is now an expectation to handle the problem and clean up our facilities.

I’d like you to deal with the settlement where the bulk of this criminal activity has taken place. These cockroaches have to be exterminated as quickly as possible if we have any hope of containing the scandal before it leaks to the journos.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_005_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_005_narrative: One of my company's primary shipping routes has been raided by pirates for months now. The mongrels seemed to vanish into thin air every time they hit one of our couriers, so spent a lot of credits scouting the nearby systems. Now their little nest has been identified. They've seriously disrupted our operation, but once we get rid of them we can get back to normal.This has to be a real show of force, so the pirates have no choice but to move on. I want you to tear up their base, Commander. Up to it?
mission_onfoot_onslaught_006_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_006_narrative:
You and I both know how dangerous space is. Anyone hauling cargo can expect to get hit by pirates at some point or another; it's practically inevitable. But when pirates obliterate a passenger transport, seemingly just for the hell of it? Nobody signed up for that. Certainly not my friends, who were on board at the time.

The authorities have identified the group that did it, but bringing them to justice is taking longer than I can accept. A few more weeks and the bastards might have moved on altogether. I'm not going to let that happen. I want to see my friend's killers put down.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_007_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_007_narrative:
You wouldn’t believe how much trouble one pirate can cause. Or at least the evidence suggests it's one pirate terrorising traders throughout the system. A bunch of us decided to pool our resources to track them down, but they're an elusive prick - always spoken of and never seen. Some of us, me included, aren’t convinced this nemesis exists. They're more like a bogeyman: a legend to scare us all, and keep us in our place. Either way, we can't let things carry on as they are.

We’ve found the settlement the pirate crew operates from and, whether their leader is real or not, we can at least wipe out the rats pledged to them. A bunch of flesh and blood criminals are a lot easier to kill than a ghost.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_008_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_008_narrative:
A couple of suspected slavers have been operating locally in recent months, but a pirate group has been keeping us busy so we didn't treat the investigation as a priority. That was a stupid mistake, and one of our officers almost paid for it with her life. They attempted to abduct her during a recon mission and she barely got away. Now the slavers have our full attention.

I’ve been given enough funds to hunt them down, but since we have no way of knowing who they are, we’ve decided to hit the settlement the slavers use as their staging ground. The people there know exactly who they're working for, so they're complicit. Don’t leave anyone alive.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_009_missioncomp: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_009_narrative:
The only good slaver is a dead one. I’ve always believed that, but this conviction was driven home when a close friend was abducted a couple of years ago. The authorities weren’t getting anywhere, so I decided to try and track him down myself. I just couldn’t bear the thought of him like that. Well, I finally found out what happened to him a few weeks back. They killed him not long after his disappearance. I like to think it's because he wouldn't give in.

It’s little consolation, but I managed to find out where the slavers who took him are based. I want them annihilated. They won’t take anyone ever again, and there will be a measure of vengeance for my friend.
