mission_onfoot_onslaught_narrative:
It pays to have friends in the right places. Politicians, police, the military…These people are very useful to have on your side but every so often you have to give a little back. This is why we take good care of such important liaisons.

Recently, one of my more useful system authority contacts was recovering sensitive tech from a wrecked satellite when a scavenger crew dropped in and started firing immediately. Not a particularly inventive lot, it seems.

My contact made it out but they are understandably unhappy that the assignment I issued them resulted in an extended med bay visit. Flowers and chocolate aren't going to cut it, so I need to prove my interest in their well being. Some expensive data has revealed where the scavs came from. I just need someone to pay them a visit they won’t forget.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_offline_001_mis: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_offline_001_nar:
You ever have one of those tasks you delay so many times that you forget about it completely until you wake in a cold sweat, with the realisation you’ve made a colossal mistake?

Yeah, that's me right now. I was meant to arrange a security detail for one of the facilities we took offline temporarily. It sounds important in hindsight, I know. Now I hear that one of our satellites has picked up scavengers nearby and that spells trouble for my continued employment.

I need you to make sure the site is free of scavengers. If it isn't, get rid of them. Once the contract is fulfilled I'll have the evidence that I hired someone. I’ll just ‘forget’ to date the report.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_offline_002_mis: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_offline_002_nar:
I have a security operation which has landed on my desk. With business booming at the moment, I need to sub-contract it to someone who can handle a gun.

Here's the deal: a small-time organisation chose to shut down one of their facilities due to cash flow issues. After some frankly suspicious accounting, this company is planning to restart operations at the site, but some local raiders have started sniffing around. The place won't be worth a damn if they decide to occupy the place so we need someone to chase the raiders away.

A few deaths should do the trick. Think you can manage it?
mission_onfoot_onslaught_offline_003_mis: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_offline_003_nar:
I'm going to keep this short because we’re both busy people. One of my company's settlements was taken offline due to some logistical issues, and a band of scavs who've been irritating us for some time has established a camp there. It was like they were just waiting for an opportunity.

Now I would enjoy nothing more than blasting the vermin away but I lack the bravery to do so. Therefore I secured a reasonable budget to hire a professional. Would you clear out those scavs for me?
mission_onfoot_onslaught_offline_004_mis: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_offline_004_nar:
I've been trying to climb the corporate ladder at my company and I’ve found the perfect way. See, the company is looking to expand its operation and I’ve identified just the site to acquire. It'd been abandoned for a while so I purchased the rights for a price that seemed too good to be true.

My instinct was right. The seller didn’t tell me about the scavenger nest that plagues the site. So now I’ve spent company money on a settlement we can’t access without getting shot at. Doesn’t look good on the quarterly report.

If I don’t clear the scavengers out then I'll be clearing my desk instead. I can't use any company assets to secure it because I don't want my boss learning about my mistake. So, can I count on your gun along with your discretion?
mission_onfoot_onslaught_offline_005_mis: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_offline_005_nar:
I work for a company whose higher-ups could be best described as idiots. Idiots with plenty of money, but idiots all the same. They're engaged in an aggressive spending spree to purchase a bunch of settlements while neglecting investment in the security personnel needed to protect them. That’s now proving to be a problem as several of the sites we've bought have been targeted by scavengers.

It’s going to take us a while to establish security teams, so in the meantime we need some contractors to secure those locations. Does that sound like something you can do?

mission_onfoot_onslaught_offline_narrati:
My team had to withdraw from a settlement recently because of…well, politics, I guess. The plan is to head back soon, but we've had reports that scavs are scouting the area for stuff to steal. Letting them pick the place clean is the last thing we need.

Those politics I mentioned haven’t quite gone away yet and I can’t spare the personnel to check the site is secure. If you could take a look I'd really appreciate it. Oh, and if you find any scavs there, well... we could all use a little target practice now and again.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_offline_travelp:
Travel to $#DestinationSettlementName:style:name=keyword; in the $#DestinationSystemName:style:name=keyword; system.
Eliminate the scavengers occupying the settlement.
Once the settlement is aware of your intentions, you cannot retreat else the contract will be rescinded.
mission_onfoot_onslaught_travelpanel_des:
Travel to $#DestinationSettlementName:style:name=keyword; in the $#DestinationSystemName:style:name=keyword; system.
Eliminate the criminal faction members occupying the settlement.
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_001_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_001_narr:
When someone steals your property, you can go get it back. But when they steal your ideas, your secrets…that's a little harder to put back in a bottle. Unless you eliminate everyone who knows about them, of course.

I want everybody currently working on the blueprints stolen from my company dead. I don’t care whether they were involved in the heist or not.

It’s taken some time and some information tracking down the thieves, but I know where that work is being done now. It’s just a matter of wiping out the whole settlement. Because nobody steals from me and gets away with it.
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_002_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_002_narr:
I used to be nothing but a data pusher, dreaming of being involved in excitement and high drama. Well, now I’m right in the thick of it - and it’s everything I ever dreamed of! My superiors have devised an elaborate scheme against a competing company that involves layers of subterfuge and strategic planning. Of course, I don’t know most of the details, but they’ve put me in charge of a crucial part of the plan: creating a diversion!

It has to be something really big if we want the distraction to work – something that will have their whole security forces in a panic. Trust me, this is going to be fun.
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_003_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_003_narr:
I'm going to level with you, I don't know how this usually works, but I need to hire someone to do a job for the company I work for. And not a nice job. They want a settlement cleaned out.

I wish I could tell you more - I'm practically as need-to-know as you are. This isn't what I do for the company usually, but I got a message from a department so far above me it hurts my neck just to look at them. Thing is, from the content of the message, I'm pretty sure it'd hurt my neck a whole lot more if I didn't do as they asked.

I have a horrible feeling that someone's about to become a scapegoat. Not you, of course! Someone else. Could you do it for the right price?
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_004_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_004_narr:
I've been working with some military contractors who want to take over several sites near their operations. But there's been a lot of push-back from the current owners of those sites. Those owners are extremely vocal, as it happens.  My clients think the settlements are failing to see the big picture. These acquisitions will help security for everyone in the system.

Should one of the sites fall victim to an attack as a result of poor security, the others would doubtlessly see the wisdom in selling up. I can't just cross my fingers and hope a band of criminals arrive when we need them. The pricks tend to overcharge, anyway. Maybe I can rely upon you instead?
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_005_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_005_narr:
The group I represent is always on the lookout for new opportunities. Weak companies, settlements in financial trouble, understaffed facilities… We search, isolate and move in. Sometimes a nudge in the right direction is needed, as in the case of the organisation we've been after recently.

They are struggling to meet the wage budgets needed to keep their settlements up and running, and the workers they can afford don't stick around long. Imagine how much more vulnerable they’d be if that workforce came under a truly savage attack. That’s when my group would come in with a truly gracious offer.
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_006_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_006_narr:
You have no idea how hard it is to find decent workers. It doesn’t help that my crew has a bit of a reputation, which we in no way deserve. It forces us to get creative with our HR policies. Especially now that we have a critical and rather time-sensitive project in the works. There’s no time to try and convince people with the right skills to hop on board. We have to try the brute force approach to recruitment.

I’ve identified a settlement with the kind of people we need, but we can’t exactly just kidnap them. Not with all those guards milling around the place, anyway. If you could put the security team down, we can come along and start headhunting the workers. By that I mean offer them jobs, not…never mind. Interested?
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_007_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_007_narr:
Whenever someone under my command dies, I feel a sense of responsibility. And when they die because they were killed without good reason, my response is to bring vengeance on the people responsible. Usually, I have time to plan a rescue mission for those captured on a mission, but this time we never had the chance. The enemy guards treated them worse than an animal. They didn’t survive the first night.

My force’s advisors are already planning a full-scale retaliation, but that could take months. I need a quick, effective tool to cause those bastards as much pain as possible. I know just the place to do it. And I think you have what it takes.
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_008_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_008_narr:
My bosses are making a big push at the moment, expanding operations into new territories. These efforts are costly, though. We’d rather not lose more people to firefights than we have to. That’s why I’m approaching mercenaries like you to lend a hand.

Just between us: I actually volunteered to personally hire somebody for this job. No need for details – let’s just say I’ve been waiting a long time for payback.

Not so long ago I’d be there with you, lighting those pricks up. Sadly I have plenty of other things to organise these days. Just remember we want the path to success as clear as possible, so don’t hold back.
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_009_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_009_narr:
Want to know what my favourite word is? Advancement. I started out as a lowly security guard and ended up commanding my own unit for a time. Currently, I'm getting into much bigger things. I’ve already been involved in some high-level political and tactical meetings and a little idea of mine seemed to have a few people take note. It should go down well if I see this through and that's partly where I'm hoping you come in.

I’ve planned out attacks on multiple settlements that will weaken our competitors significantly and put us in a much more advantageous position. I've already got mercenaries leading missions at the others and I want you to take on a strike at one of the remaining facilities. When you succeed, it'll look great for both of us and I'm sure you'll able to leverage that success to your advantage in the future as well.

mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_missionc: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_narrativ:
The company I represent has built a reputation as market leaders in the local system. Lesser businesses have tried to secure a foothold with our customer base but they've never really threatened to succeed. Either their product is inferior or costs more to produce.

A recent start-up has caught the eye, however. The product they're advertising is quite good. Affordable, reliable and aesthetically pleasing. It could claim a sizeable chunk of our quarterly profits if left unchecked. My company has a responsibility to its shareholders to prevent that from happening.

The outright slaughter of the company’s workers should do the trick. Somewhat bold, you could say, but effective. Are you confident you can handle this task for me?
mission_onfoot_onslaughtillegal_travelpa:

Eliminate the occupants of the settlement.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_001_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_001_narra:
I recently hired someone very much like you to obtain confidential documents from another company. The target has been doing much better than us, and my bosses wanted to find out how. Thing is, we haven’t discovered much in the data except for one coded entry referencing a highly classified process. We have to find out exactly what it is.

If, as I suspect, they’re doing something illegal then a sample should be enough to report them to the regulatory agencies. Maybe you can help me get rid of this business rival for good.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_002_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_002_narra:
In all my years, I’ve seen pretty much everything there is to see in my line of work. So when something surprises me it tends to stick in the mind.

A company I’ve never heard of releasing a product that completely out-performs the established brand I represent was one such surprise. Our board of directors is less than pleased, so it’s up to me – more accurately, up to you - to find out just how they accomplished this feat.

There has to be some new chemical or manufacturing technique involved that we're yet to discover. Given these upstarts hit the market without warning, that’s enough to raise suspicions. I'm sure with your help we can figure everything out.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_003_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_003_narra:
A recent industrial accident has hit my team pretty hard. We lost a few friends, while others have a long road to recovery. I promised them that I wouldn’t rest until I found out what happened and why. And now I finally have a lead.

I’ve run some background checks on all the chemical shipments we received in the weeks before the incident. One of them came from a company with a reputation for skipping quality control procedures to cut costs. If I ask to examine the manufacturing process myself, the owners could cover up any wrongdoing.

If you obtain a raw sample of the target settlement’s product, I can run some tests and confirm my suspicions. It would mean a lot to me, Commander.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_004_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_004_narra:
I work with a pharmaceutical organisation currently investigating a curious matter. We’ve seen a huge spike in reports of serious side-effects to common medications. At first, I couldn’t work out why, but then it hit me: our newly contracted supplier must be cutting their drugs with junk.

I should have known the cheap prices this supplier offered was too good to be true. But I can cancel the contract if I have proof of negligence. Bring me a sample from one of their facilities and I’ll have my lab run some tests. With your help, we’ll be able to put things right before somebody gets killed.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_005_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_005_narra:
My crew’s always run a respectable operation. I take a lot of pride in making sure we use cost-effective and reliable methods wherever possible.  So you can imagine what a sucker-punch it was to see another company – just a small-time outfit until now - producing a higher yield with a lower quarterly investment. How is this possible?

This isn’t just about ego. Our business is starting to suffer since these upstarts are drawing all the contracts! I have to know what they’re doing over there that makes their output so high. Collect a sample for me and I’ll pay you for the help.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_006_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_006_narra:
Refining rare materials is a delicate, expensive business. You can’t afford to lose too much of the raw resource without biting into the profit margin. There's one material in particular that we've repeatedly had issues with. I've recently learned that another crew has solved the same problem, producing high yields consistently. I must know how they do it!

My team are skilled, so it has to be the refinement process itself. So how about you help me find out what it is? Grab a sample from their facility and bring it here. You’ll earn a few credits for it.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_007_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_007_narra:
Between corporate spies, double-agents, whistleblowers and idiots who just can’t keep their mouths shut, it’s hard to keep a secret in my line of work. Anything worth knowing eventually comes out. So it’s no surprise that somebody blabbed about a versatile new compound that could be worth a great deal of money.

The problem is I have no idea where the compound is being tested. If I had to make an educated guess, there’s one settlement that has been unusually quiet on the usual industry channels since the secret leaked. Grab me a sample of their latest production batch and I can take a closer look.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_008_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_008_narra:
When I lost my job at a chemical refinery, all I could think about was revenge. At first, I considered just blowing the place up. Then I calmed down and started planning an elaborate sabotage operation. But satisfaction doesn’t pay the bills, as my mother used to say. So I came up with a third idea.

I know for a fact that the refinery owners ignore multiple safety procedures to save on expenses. My word alone isn’t enough to blackmail them, though, so I need solid proof. Bring me a chemical sample and I’ll be able to force a generous severance bonus. It’s only fair, after all.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_009_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_009_narra:
You know the best way to strike a blow your enemies will remember? Beat them in court. Even the biggest corporations feel the pain of losing a case. The damage to a reputation can be greater than any fine. I’m telling you, there’s nothing sweeter than a judgement going your way.

Now I’m close to sticking it to the company that put me out of business. I’ve known for a long time the sleazeballs were covering up something. I’ve just never been able to prove it until now. The private investigator I hired has found a solid lead: the company is using an outlawed refinement process in their facilities. Once I have a sample, my lawyers are finally going to nail them. I’ll pay you well to collect it for me.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_covert_00: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.

My team are skilled, so it has to be the refinement process itself. So how about you help me find out what it is? Grab a sample from their facility and bring it here. You’ll earn a few credits for it.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_ncd_007_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_ncd_007_n: Nonviolent Heist: Take a sample from $#DestinationSettlementName;

Between corporate spies, double-agents, whistleblowers and idiots who just can’t keep their mouths shut, it’s hard to keep a secret in my line of work. Anything worth knowing eventually comes out. So it’s no surprise that somebody blabbed about a versatile new compound that could be worth a great deal of money.

The problem is I have no idea where the compound is being tested. If I had to make an educated guess, there’s one settlement which has been unusually quiet on the usual industry channels since the secret leaked. Grab me a sample of their latest production batch and I can take a closer look.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_ncd_008_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_ncd_008_n: Nonviolent Heist: Take a sample from $#DestinationSettlementName;

When I lost my job at a chemical refinery, all I could think about was revenge. At first, I considered just blowing the place up. Then I calmed down and started planning an elaborate sabotage operation. But satisfaction doesn’t pay the bills, as my mother used to say. So I came up with a third idea.

I know for a fact that the refinery owners ignore multiple safety procedures to save on expenses. My word alone isn’t enough to blackmail them, though, so I need solid proof. Bring me a chemical sample and I’ll be able to force a generous severance bonus. It’s only fair, after all.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_ncd_009_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_productionheist_ncd_009_n: Nonviolent Heist: Take a sample from $#DestinationSettlementName;

You know the best way to strike a blow your enemies will remember? Beat them in court. Even the biggest corporations feel the pain of losing a case. The damage to a reputation can be greater than any fine. I’m telling you, there’s nothing sweeter than a judgement going your way.

Now I’m close to sticking it to the company that put me out of business. I’ve known for a long time the sleazeballs were covering up something. I’ve just never been able to prove it until now. The private investigator I hired has found a solid lead: the company is using an outlawed refinement process in their facilities. Once I have a sample, my lawyers are finally going to nail them. I’ll pay you well to collect it for me.

I don’t know how the bastards manage, but they always seem to have the right amount of produce for each new order. It’s time to get to the bottom of this.

I need you to retrieve a sample of the process they’re using so our research team can analyse it. If it’s something we can reproduce it’ll help. If not then at least we’ll know it’s time to get dirty. Either way, you’ll have gotten us answers.

mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_001_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_001_narrati:
A person can have all the guns, ships and soldiers they want, but the real power comes from information. The absence of information, in turn, can be particularly inhibiting.

One of my client’s databases was taken offline recently. Usually backups are arranged for the most important files, but in this case the entire settlement went down before a remote copy could be arranged.

I suspect the act of sabotage responsible may have been related to this irretrievable data. An opportunist with the means to profit from the situation, perhaps. Maybe a rival company looking to gain an advantage. Regardless, the crux of the matter is that the settlement must be brought back online as soon as possible.
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_002_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_002_narrati:
Wars can make great investments, providing you back the winning side. But every investment come with a little risk, right?

As it happens, there's an ongoing conflict that appears to be reaching the conclusion my clients intended. A considerable financial reward is all but secured but for one minor hiccup. A recent skirmish spilt over into a nearby settlement, and the workers were forced to evacuate.

For every hour the settlement is offline my client is losing credits. If it stays down much longer, it will start eating into the profits this conflict is estimated to bring in. While I appreciate the irony, some of my peers are claiming I should have seen it coming. So let’s shut them up and put things right again, hm?
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_003_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_003_narrati:
Isn’t life just great? In the same week, my company has finally dealt with a merc who’d repeatedly plundered our supply lines and the black market fence who’d been taking her loot. There’s still work to do in the aftermath, though. First up is bringing an important settlement the merc sabotaged back online.

A lot of assembly parts used in our territory passed through this one settlement, so we need to get it functional as soon as possible. Get down there, boot it up and I’ll give you a suitable monetary reward.
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_004_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_004_narrati:
My organisation has been going through a rough patch, wedged right between aggressive pirates and a hostile corp with mercs on contract. We were forced to cease operations at a few of our settlements as our security forces were too thinly spread.

Unfortunately, our food stores aren’t lasting quite as long as we’d hoped. We need one of those settlements to restart production as soon as possible. Implementing rations for our personnel at this stage would utterly shatter morale.

I wish I could spare the personnel to get it back online but we're fighting fires everywhere. I need you to do it for us.
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_005_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_005_narrati:
My team isn’t like most of the ones you’re probably used to dealing with. We’re not playing some high-risk game or attempting to crush the competition. No, we’re just trying to survive.

Our facilities produce pretty mundane stuff, so we have to rely on grants to make up a certain percentage of our income. But due to some political manoeuvring involving people we’ve never met, most of those grants got cancelled last year and we had to shut down several settlements.

After a lot of lobbying, we’ve managed to secure a loan but that won’t do us much good unless we can the settlements working again to produce tradable goods. There’s one, in particular, we simply must have back online. I hope you can help us out.
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_006_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_006_narrati:
I never thought our company would struggle as much as it has recently, and our financial resources have been stretched to their limits. Not to mention the strain our workforce has been under due to increased quotas. Accidents, shattered morale, and even a few strikes recently. In the end, we had to take one of our most important settlements offline before the whole team walked out for good.

We’ve just about turned the corner now, thanks to a few new contracts and some renegotiated contracts. But I’ve been ordered to bring that settlement online as quickly as possible. The security detail that’s supposed to install the new power regulator is weeks behind schedule, and we simply can’t wait any longer. Please, help us out?
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_007_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_007_narrati:
My company shut down one of our settlements recently. It was a situation completely out of our hands, but we persevered because that’s just the kind of mentality we possess. Of course, a lot of production time was lost, and the stress and hardship experienced by our workforce was considerable.

So we were greatly relieved when the settlement insurers finally paid out the substantial policy we’d taken out with them. Can you believe there were suspicions that we’d engineered the whole situation as some kind of scam? An outrageous thing to suggest. As if we’d ever stoop to such deviancy.

Anyway, now that we have been properly compensated we should put that settlement back into service. Turns out the problem was just a missing regulator all along. Odd how the insurance inspectors didn't notice. An independent contractor should be able to install a replacement easily and off the record, don’t you think?
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_008_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_008_narrati:
There has been a recent wave of raids on our settlements by a group of anarchists. They’ve even managed to take a few of them out of commission. I told everyone in the company that our security systems were out of date and our guards lacked training, but nobody listened to me. I’d let the idiots deal with the mess by themselves, but a friend of mine has a lot of money tied up in one of those settlements. She needs it back online as soon as possible.

I’m doing this due to my generous spirit, by the way. My friend is in a position to help me financially with a few personal matters but that is entirely coincidental. I don’t want you leaving with the wrong impression. Now, are you willing to earn some credits with me?
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_009_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_009_narrati:
The thing about corporate spies is that they always seem to know when you’re most vulnerable. Our security forces have been overworked, trying to quell a series of bandit attacks, when someone steals the power regulator from one of our reactors. I have a suspicion of who it is, but the whole personnel roster has been detained for interrogation.

Until we’ve identified the mole, I’m using outsider contracts to run tasks. I’d like you to get the settlement back online for me. Shall we discuss payment?

mission_onfoot_rebootrestore_narrative:
Sometimes investments don’t pan out. That’s just the nature of the beast. But when they’re failing because some asshole can’t resist pulling their weapon on a rival, that’s when my people get irritated. There’s one settlement in particular that we’ve put a lot of money into, but a conflict nobody cares about managed to knock it offline when the fighting spilled into the power centre.

We need you to get it up and running while there’s still a chance we can keep that investment profitable. The sooner people are back to work in the facility, the better our portfolio looks. And it’ll do wonders for my stress levels.

mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_001_missio: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_001_narrat:
One of our settlements is about to be attacked. I’m almost certain of it. One of my superiors got a tip about an uptick in activity at a nearby military outpost and, given the logistics, we look to be the targets. We’re only a small operation, so we don’t yet have the resources to adequately defend ourselves. And we can’t afford to draw attention by putting out a hit on the outpost’s leadership. I've tried that in the past, it gets real messy, real quick.

Which leaves persuasion that there are more important matters than raiding settlements. For that I need to give these would-be attackers some problems and shutting their whole facility down is a pretty good start.

They're not going to expect a lone operative at such a well-guarded location. I'd send one of our team but we need someone who can't be traced back to us, at least not quickly. What do you say?
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_002_missio: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_002_narrat:
I’d like you to help me solve a mystery. There’s a new company out there running a quiet, unassuming agricultural settlement. On the face of it, it’s nothing anyone should be worried about, but something about the numbers doesn't add up. I started digging a little deeper and, from what I’ve been able to establish, they’re doing more than grow vegetables if you get my meaning.

I could hire some people to work undercover at the facility, or get a software hack in their network and dig through encrypted files for some answers, but both of those options take quite some time. Why not turn just turn the lights out and force an outright evacuation first? Then I can dig through the place personally.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_003_missio: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_003_narrat:
You’ve got to respect the kind of people who will do anything to get an edge. For example, there’s a company that’s been kicking our ass the last few months. We couldn’t figure out how they were outperforming us by such a margin. It took a few credits and a touch of unethical behaviour, but we finally discovered that this company has disabled multiple safety protocols and have been pushing their machines way beyond safe operating conditions.

We passed this information on to the authorities, of course, but these snakes seem to have friends in high places and have been tipped off. They’re refitting everything before an inspection can be held! I could definitely use a victory, so take their facility’s reactor offline. We’ll see how they put those security features back in place without any power.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_004_missio: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_004_narrat:
A few years ago, a research facility I ran with my business partner suffered some financial trouble. It was like we were cursed, the way kept going wrong. When this company showed up and offered to buy us out, we had no choice but to sell. I moved on, found new things and kept afloat but my partner never really got over it. Well, it turns out all the subsequent obsessing was worth it. He found out exactly what had caused our bad luck.

A competitor knew we had a good thing going, rather than step up their performance, they undermined us at every turn us stepping in as guardian angels with a buyout. Well, I've got a few things planned for these meatheads. To start with, let’s see how one of their settlements does without a functioning reactor.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_005_missio: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_005_narrat:
The ancient expression ‘revenge is a dish best served cold’ never really made sense to me until recently. A group of my company’s former employees resigned together and took a significant amount of valuable research with them. Days later, they all somehow found jobs at the same corp. Remarkable, isn’t it?

I’ve been monitoring the progress of that company’s continued development of our data. They've recently started a series of highly expensive experiments and I'd like to see them cut short. It would level the playing field again if nothing else. Interested?
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_006_missio: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_006_narrat:
An old business partner of mine is such a shit person. After abandoning the company we founded years ago, taking our most valuable assets and saddling me with a ton of debt, they sought to steal every contract I bid for. Thankfully they went quiet for a while, but I’ve just discovered they took a role with a corp branch famed for lacking any tolerance for failure. It’s the perfect opportunity to stick it to them for old time’s sake.

The extraction operation they’re in charge of has some tight deadlines coming up, and there’s no better way to guarantee it fails than shutting down the settlement reactor. I like to think they’ll know it was my fault. You’ll remain nameless, of course.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_007_missio: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_007_narrat:
My employers have a whole department devoted to coming up with market strategies. The competitor we’re concentrating on right now has a range of businesses, so we were expecting our military advisors to recommend a raid on some of their factories. But instead, the geeks came up with something unexpected: knocking out one of their tourist settlements.

It’s ingenious in its own unique way. The company won’t be expecting it and they’ll have no way of tying it to us if an independent merc is responsible. Plus, it won’t just hurt them financially - it will also tank the morale of the workers in other settlements who use the place as a free vacation. Do you want to see the details?
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_008_missio: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_008_narrat:
There’s a nice enough tourist spot that's experienced a loss of revenue, mainly thanks to the work my crew has put in. But we haven’t been able to prevent visitors from flocking to the place altogether. That’s a problem since my bosses have made clear the failure of that operation is vital to a wider planning strategy. I think it’s time we tried something more definitive.

What could spoil a perfectly good vacation spot more than the whole damn place losing power? Blackouts, panicked evacuations, demands for refunds… That performance isn't exactly to secure the place a prime slot on the galactic index. More importantly, it’s going to play hell with their future scheduling. Maybe then I can wrap this task up and move on to other things.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_009_missio: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_009_narrat:
When I go on a nice relaxing break, it’s time to kick back and drink just as much as I damn well please. Maybe I’m a little loud and call people a few names as a result. If I behave like that at work then sure, ask me to calm down. But if I've paid you good money to put up with me? Then you’re gonna shut your mouth and take it for as long as I see fit. 

What I don't expect is to be marched to the nearest landing pad and thrown on my ass at the door of a shuttle. I looked like a complete idiot in front of my friends! I'm not letting that go. If I can't have the holiday I paid for with my hard-earned credits, then I don't see why anyone else should enjoy one. I’ll give you the vacation budget I never got to spend to take the place offline. It's just what the losers deserve.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_010_missio: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_010_narrat:
Thank you for stopping by. There’s a lot to do in this system but only so many people skilled enough to go around.

A group that my company does business with has been supplying one of the factions currently at war in the system. It’s important to dissuade them from doing so, but in a way that doesn't antagonise them. Sending one of our people could arouse suspicion which is why a Commander would be perfect for the job. You’re familiar with the operation of a power centre, I hope?

The target settlement is one which I’m fairly certain is involved in the supply contributions. Without power, the workers will have some difficulty maintaining their output.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_011_missio: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_011_narrat:
According to my squad’s intel, some local companies which we thought were neutral parties in the ongoing system conflict have taken it upon themselves to supplying our enemies. And that won't do at all. As such we're looking for someone who can slip into a settlement to carry out a little sabotage for us. Something tells me you're the perfect fit.

Get inside the target facility, pull its power regulator, and get out before they find you. Sounds straightforward, doesn’t it? Don't mess it up and you’ll get paid.

mission_onfoot_sabotage_power_narrative:
I'm certain I don't need to tell you how difficult it can be to earn a living in the galaxy. So many of us are scraping by, doing what we can to get enough credits to cover expenses. The bureaucracy in this system just grinds down those of us in the transportation sector. The crooks in the customs offices constantly hold our cargo up for unnecessary checks. And even when hauling something innocuous, you can bet someone will try and extort a percentage out of you.

I've got some items that I simply cannot afford to have held up by the never-ending inspections. It would be very advantageous if a certain military settlement were to lose power soon. You know, to distract system authorities for a few hours, and let us legitimate traders pass unimpeded for once.

mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_001_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_001_n:
My team has been doing everything possible to win a contract that would finally establish our credentials. Maybe even get us noticed by the higher-ups. But another bidder is trying to make us look bad and they’re using every dirty trick in the book.

These cheaters spied on us and even tried to shut down some of our factories. I’m not going to let them walk all over us, so It’s time to hit back! I want you to insert a biochemical agent into one of their production lines to prove that their facilities are unreliable. It’s not how I usually do things, but they’ve honestly left us no choice.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_002_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_002_n:
My organisation is a big believer in the value of competition. It’s healthy for the market, keeps us all alert and breeds a hunger for success. We must not let anyone disturb the current equilibrium by, for example, announcing a rival high-quality product to be sold at a markedly lower price. It just isn’t fair.

Which is why we’d like to see production at a specific facility disrupted. You know, just so its owners don’t forget the unwritten rules of honest competition. If that doesn’t work, well, maybe we’ll need to use other methods.

Think you can help us out? All we want is a fair and even selection for our consumers without the confusion of different price points. That’s not so much to ask, is it?
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_003_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_003_n:
Want some advice? Never start your own business. You wouldn’t believe how cut-throat people can be. You think you can make a living by offering a good product, maybe do well enough to expand your enterprise a little. Before you know it, you have rivals smearing your name and trying to disrupt your supply lines.

There’s one company doing something that I simply will not stand for: stealing my idea with the intent to flood the market with an inferior version of my product. I can’t compete with their resources, but maybe I can make sure my customers stay loyal to the original brand. I need you to sabotage my rival’s facility and make sure their merchandise doesn’t even pass safety checks. Think you can do that?
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_004_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_004_n:
Aren’t you sick of violence? It seems like death, destruction and mayhem lurks in every area of the bubble. But it doesn’t have to be this way. I’ve been working with a group that’s trying to spread peace, to get people talking to each other. We’re making progress but we’ve found a source of poison right under our noses: a factory producing weapon components for a violent extremist group.

This settlement represents everything we’re against by fuelling violence to make a profit. Our efforts to help them see sense haven't helped. We won’t fight them. That’s not our way. But if you could grind that process to a halt then the violence could be stopped, at least for a while.

Just try not to hurt any of the workers at the site. Okay?
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_005_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_005_n:
I challenge you to name a bigger driver of progress than war. New and improved weapons are being created all the time to suit the challenges of modern conflict. When both your cause and your life depends on the firepower at your disposal,  you must demand the most advanced technology available.

I have quite a few shares in a company at the vanguard of biochemical deployment. Just recently this investment has started to look like it will pay off in a big way...then came the announcement that another company is working on counter-measures to an early prototype of the biochemical weapon. If this rival project proves effective then it will make my investment worthless. I'll pay you to cripple the countermeasure development, at least until I’ve unloaded all my stocks.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_006_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_006_n:
I’ve been working closely with a small chemical production firm. They’re just starting out, but I helped them land a large contract that could establish them in the market. The whole thing was supposed to be top secret, but somehow another company - a real behemoth - has discovered the deal and is racing to make its own version of the product. If that version hits retail first, my team's contract is dead in the water.

I’m pretty sure this other company has stolen our most vital data, giving it a head start. There’s just no way my guys can compete financially, either. Unless someone can ruin this company's operation.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_007_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_007_n:
The community I live in has always had problems, but lately it’s been getting worse. No mystery what’s behind it all: Drugs. Gangs constantly competing with one another, trying to manufacture, sell and distribute as much as they can. It's high-quality stuff, too, which means the bigger gangs are making a big profit. More credits will lead to expansion, recruitment, increased violence… We have to do something before it’s too late.

Confronting the criminals directly is too risky. We could turn our home into a warzone. But I’ve found out where the gangs are buying some key manufacturing ingredients. Cut off the source and, if we’re lucky, the operation will be forced to shrink.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_008_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_008_n:
A corp took over food production and distribution for a population district a while back by offering fair quality, cheap food. Over time the competition moved on to other markets, after which the corp’s true goal became very clear.

These ghouls are now charging higher and higher prices for reduced quality food. They’re either saving money on cultivation or quality inspections because almost all of it tastes like garbage. You need to help me put a stop to it by ruining one of their production facilities. Maybe if the food actually IS garbage the authorities will start taking a closer look.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_009_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_009_n:
The galaxy is full of opportunities, friend; I sure have one for you today. This is your chance to change people’s lives for the better and give a plucky business a real boost. All it takes is a tiny bit of sabotage. Hardly any, really!

My associates and I are in the fascinating field of pharmaceuticals and we’re on the verge of creating a better tomorrow. The process we need to complete our work can only be done in a handful of facilities, but we just can’t seem to get access to any. It's all ‘Can you provide references’ or ‘What are your statistical findings’. Total yawn, am I right?

Here’s the good news: if the facility we’re after starts failing, the corporation that owns it will surely look for new management. And we’ll be there, ready to work our magic! Surely you can’t resist offering my visionary team a helping hand up the ladder?
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_010_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_010_n:
My company’s been at its financial peak for a few years now. There’s a good reason for that: we’re efficient, smart and we crush anyone who stands in our way. Like this pathetic new ‘rival’ that’s crawled out of some slum thinking they can take us on. It’s time for a swift lesson how competition works in this system.

I could just let them trip over themselves, watch them fumble around the market like the losers they are. But it’s so much more fun to give them a hard push, wouldn’t you agree? Once they’ve fallen apart, I’ll take a look at the pieces and see if there’s any worth keeping. All you need to do is introduce a little bad luck to their facility. For a fee, of course.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_011_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_011_n:
There’s nothing sweeter than finding a brand new, completely untapped field of minerals to exploit. I’ve helped plenty of companies locate just the right place to dig. In fact, one of my recent discoveries was among the best. A real motherlode. Unfortunately the consortium I arranged a finder’s fee with wasn't able to claim it in time. A competitor caught wind of the prospect and moved quickly.

Before I make my throat sore yelling at my staff for letting word slip, I need a hand. There’s a legal challenge in the works and I have lobbyists petitioning on my client’s behalf, but what I need is to slow these thieves down. Think you could handle that for me, Commander?
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_012_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_012_n:
If you think criminal gangs are bad, you should try entering corporate politics. Every week there’s a new case of back-stabbing, veiled threats or blackmail. Right now, my clients are dead set on a less-than-friendly takeover of another company, and they need some help greasing the wheels of business.

The target corp is holding firm for the moment, fighting off the usual bribes and executive title promises, clinging on to the hope that it can survive in the big leagues. I'd like to ensure the current owners are fully aware of how this is going to play out. Go and cause some problems at one of the corp’s facilities. When its profit margins take a hit, we’ll step in with a new offer.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_013_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_013_n:
It’s not easy getting ahead in any business. My client has been working relentlessly to get a new project off the ground, but their biggest rival has pretty much cornered the market already. They need a secret weapon, and I’m thinking that could be you.

Nobody has to get hurt. I just want to slow down the market leader’s operation long enough to give other companies a chance to step up. My clients are prepared to push every contact and distributor they know. You throw a wrench in the target facility’s production and I’ll take care of the rest.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_014_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_014_n:
A farming settlement is trying to interfere with my client's business. And just because there’s a food shortage in the region, it's assumed they'll be allowed to proceed. This is a line of thinking in drastic need of correction.

Look, we don't want the local population to go hungry but there are investors to think about. These farmers think they have the moral high ground but they're just looking for an advantage like everybody else. They'll feed the hungry, replenish food stores and look like heroes.

Fortunately, I believe in the free market. If the food shortage continues then traders will bring the necessary deliveries to the commodity market for a premium, which my client can then sell to the public for an even greater profit. Let’s make sure all these farmers end up with are is a harvest of ruined crops.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_015_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_015_n:
Ever been fired from a job you loved? That’s what happened to me a few years ago, right when I was on the verge of a project breakthrough. I landed on my feet, securing a respectable position with another lab shortly after. But the injustice still gets to me. The only reason my previous boss canned me was because he was jealous of my talent. Well, it’s payback time.

That buffoon is currently running an agricultural research unit for an up-and-coming corp. Thinks he’s going to make a name with them and coast on the glory for the rest of his career. So how about we mess up his plans a little?
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_016_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_016_n:
My organisation has experienced considerable success in recruiting and placing intelligence agents recently. One of the individuals we inserted at a food production facility has caught wind of a new germination accelerant currently in the trial phase. If successful, it could be rather detrimental to a high-paying client currently enjoying the dominant share of that particular market.

As such, my boss has given me a not-so-subtle nudge to make sure that the trial goes poorly. I don’t want to shut them down completely – it’s just competition, after all. We just want some disruption to the trial while a more suitable plan is formulated.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_017_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_017_n:
A client of mine has been competing with another company for years now, fighting over contracts, racing to the next technological fad and so on. It’s been quite fun to watch, being honest. Anyway, this rival company is close to finalising a way of processing materials that is much more efficient than the current method. My client is not exactly thrilled by this development.

There's a downside to this experimental approach, however. It takes a very long time to reach full effectiveness, and if something goes wrong the whole process has to be shut down, potentially wasting a significant number of resources. I’d like to demonstrate that particular flaw to any potential investors and I believe you can help me do that.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_018_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_018_n:
There are a lot of ways to stay on top in my industry. Violence, piracy and threats all have their place. Personally, I find a more subtle approach is far cleaner.

I engineered a rumour among the workforce of a rival’s settlement, suggesting their wages were being cut to accommodate huge bonuses for the executive team. It has the workers on the brink of a strike, but other developments mean I need to hurry things up a little. A little interference with their production line, a few more whispers here and there about who to blame…I’ll have the whole place so paranoid they’ll be quitting just to stay sane. Sounds fun, doesn’t it?
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_019_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_019_n:
I'll keep this simple because time is of the essence. The organisation I work for is currently engaged in talks with a long-term competitor, in the hope of bringing a very bitter rivalry to an end. But one of our informants has evidence of shipping orders which would indicate that at least some part of the rival hierarchy plans on a military intervention, which would destroy any hopes of an agreement.

I think that a breakthrough in discussions is imminent, but we need time. It is vital that we stall this nascent military operation but nobody must know we're behind it. Which is why I need your help, Commander.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_020_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_020_n:
Nothing makes me prouder than mentoring people on a path to success. Credits don’t matter to me; my real legacy will be a whole new generation of entrepreneurs leading humanity through the next century. So I couldn’t be happier that one of my employees recently decided to step down and pursue their own operation. Like any good teacher, I want to offer them a final lesson.

They’ve very shrewdly taken over an extraction settlement, which is a great first step. But they tend to underestimate the challenges inherent in such a project. I’d like you to test their resolve by sabotaging their refinement process. I’m confident they have the capital to recover at this early stage and it will focus the strategy going forward.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_021_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_021_n:
I’ve recently discovered a fantastic business opportunity which needs a little push to fully realise itself.

You see, a company experiencing significant financial struggles has found itself on the cusp of closure, meaning a savvy investor can step in and rescue the operation for a fraction of the true cost. Unfortunately, the company in question has gotten the idea of a last-ditch effort to get things back on track. If by some miracle they succeeded, the cost of investment would skyrocket. And we don’t want that, do we?

All you have to do is pay a visit to the company’s primary settlement and ensure its output remains as terrible as it’s been for the past few months. I’m sure this will convince them that new ownership is the real solution.
mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_022_m: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.

mission_onfoot_sabotage_production_narra:
Like any powerful organisation, our faction has enemies – it comes with the territory. But one of our rivals has decided to kick things up a notch, and they’ve shown they’re willing to play dirty. Very dirty. They’ve been targeting our homes, even our families. I don’t know about you, but that’s where I draw the line.

We’ve identified a facility that is of central importance to the enemy’s operational network. If we could take it out, even temporarily, it would give us some much-needed breathing room. A chance to recover, regroup, and maybe regain the upper hand.

Your job will be to travel to the facility, infiltrate it, and take it out of commission. I don’t care how you do it, as long as you take it offline.

I hope you can help us, Commander. I really do.
