mission_onfoot_salvage_001_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_001_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_001_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_001_narrative:
Listen, I need your help something fierce. Everyone’s freaking out because one of my gang's ships went down carrying a super important schematic. And, of course, I’m the one who’ll get the blame if it’s never recovered. It’s not like it’s my fault the courier crashed, but still, it’ll be me who pays the consequences.

I’ve tracked down the crash site, so all you have to do is get down to the planet, find that damn schematic and bring it back. Then maybe I’ll get to keep my legs for a while. Right until the next disaster.
mission_onfoot_salvage_002_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_002_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_002_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_002_narrative:
When arranging a large corporate move between systems, you kind of expect a few items to get damaged in transit. But losing a whole damn shipment to pirates? I've never had that happen before.

The credit value is covered through insurance, but I'm missing a few things which are important to me. You know, sentimental stuff. If you could get them back, it'd mean a lot to me. I have a location to start searching. And feel free to take anything else you find - it's all been paid off. Just don't mention it to the insurance company.
mission_onfoot_salvage_003_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_003_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_003_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_003_narrative:
I am arranging for evidence and prisoners to be shuttled all over this damn system while overworked and underpaid, so the last thing I need is one of my couriers going missing with a drive full of evidence. The transmission from the tracking beacon puts them on a planetary surface, although whether it was a controlled landing I can't say. All I know for sure is the ship ain't moving or answering comms.

Whatever happened, I need that evidence back ASAP or criminals are going to walk free.
mission_onfoot_salvage_004_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_004_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_004_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_004_narrative:
This is horrible, but I work for a small vacation company and one of our complimentary hire ships has tragically crashed. It only had a couple of guests on board so it hasn't reached the local newscasts, thank the gods. We have no idea what caused the accident, though. Other than the location transponder, the ship just stopped sending information.

If you could recover the ship's surveillance equipment then maybe we can figure out what happened. Certainly, our legal team is anxious to get as much information as possible.
mission_onfoot_salvage_005_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_005_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_005_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_005_narrative:
I'm sorry to say that one of our company's xenobiological research missions has ended in disaster. Through what we can only assume was pilot error, a ship carrying several of our scientists has crashed. Early indications show there were no survivors.

We know that ship was carrying the results of their research in a genetic data bank. With any luck it's still intact. If it can be recovered then, as tragic as this loss is, at least the mission won't have been completely in vain.
mission_onfoot_salvage_006_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_006_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_006_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_006_narrative:
I'm going to go ahead and presume you've run into pirates a bunch of times. Well I hadn't until recently! My colleagues and I were scared to death! Fortunately, we had a few guards with us who knew what they were doing, and I managed to escape.

I was carrying a geological sample when these terrifying people dropped in, so I stashed it and ran. Hey, they might be pirates but that doesn't mean they can't appreciate a rare geological find. I'm wasn't risking them catching up to me and doing horrible, violent things to me just because I had a vial of dirt!

It's not very interesting to look at, I'll admit. So despite my concern, it's very likely the sample is still where I left it. I'm not especially keen on going back out myself just yet. Would you go for me?
mission_onfoot_salvage_007_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_007_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_007_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_007_narrative:
There was a recent assassination attempt on a well-known researcher. What seems to have slipped past the news reports that this researcher, at the time of the attempt on their life, was on a planetside expedition. It would appear they left a few things behind, too. I suppose gunfire heading your way has a habit of shifting one’s priorities around.

Now, I don’t know anything about the assassination itself – I wouldn’t dream of getting involved in such matters – but I do have certain professional curiosity in the researcher’s things. See if you can retrieve their documentation in particular.
mission_onfoot_salvage_008_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_008_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_008_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_008_narrative:
It's pretty simple - I just need you to grab some data from a crashed SRV. I would have grabbed it myself after the accident, but we were rescued by my company's security force and the data relates to... Well, it isn't something I should have had on me. I couldn't risk getting caught, and if I go back to the site myself it's going to look suspicious.

Look, just go grab it. If my bosses ever find out about this, I am vapour.
mission_onfoot_salvage_009_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_009_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_009_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_009_narrative:
You know how they say one man's trash is another man's treasure? I've got a lead on a downed beacon. It's been written off by the company so I imagine most of it's been destroyed, but it's one of the newer models and they've got some very nice tech in them. And I just so happen to know someone who'd pay a premium for recovered parts, assuming any survived.

Regretfully, I can't go to the crash site myself as I’ve got other business to attend. But maybe you could take a look on my behalf, in exchange for a few credits?
mission_onfoot_salvage_010_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_010_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_010_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_010_narrative:
I don't need to tell you how important secure transmissions are, right? Encryption is often the only thing keeping my company’s plans hidden from the prying eyes of rivals. That's why it's incredibly annoying that a solar flare has knocked out one of our orbital communication beacons. The damned thing even slammed into the planet’s surface before we could send out a mechanic. Now anyone could recover the encryption software we built into it.

I need the circuitry back in company possession as soon as possible. And I want an outside agent like yourself to do it. Keeping the details of this one off the records avoids questions about what we're putting in our satellites to begin with.
mission_onfoot_salvage_011_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_011_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_011_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_011_narrative:
I'm not sure if this will be your kind of mission, but I've been contacted by a component collector who's interested in an old communication beacon that recently crashed. According to the collector, the beacon is some rare variant which is no longer manufactured. I don't know if that's true, of course. They all look the same to me.

Anyway, my client has been trying to obtain some circuitry from this variant for ages and now that this one's been declared a write-off they'd like someone to search for an intact board at the crash site. Call it junk if you want, but a respectable reward has been offered for a successful recovery.
mission_onfoot_salvage_012_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_012_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_012_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_012_narrative:
Satellites come crashing down all at a surprising rate. Stellar comms networks utilise a significant number of them, so it’s no surprise when one ends up in the bottom of a crater. It’s a good source of work for my salvage company. A few days ago, a pretty powerful corp asked me to retrieve one such satellite and they were very eager to make it my highest priority. My best guess is there’s something important buried in the databanks.

Every member of my crew is occupied with other jobs, so I could use a hand on this one. I have a reputation to maintain, after all. Think you can bring this 'sensitive' piece of technology back in one piece?
mission_onfoot_salvage_013_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_013_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_013_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_013_narrative:
I’ve had enough of scavengers. First, they pounce on crashed ships and offline settlements, stripping them clean. Now they’re nudging satellites out of orbit so they can scrounge the wreckage for parts! Some scavengers like to keep a low profile, but not this gang. They couldn’t care less who knows what they’re doing.

One day I’m going to hire someone to wipe these dustheads out, but right now I just need the components for one of our satellites recovered. It was recently knocked out of orbit so I need you to get to it before they do.
mission_onfoot_salvage_014_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_014_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_014_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_014_narrative:
I work for a company which has invested a lot of money into its communications network, which includes a good number of satellites. One of these satellites recently crashed, which is more common than you'd think. But it doesn't usually happen with new equipment. When several of the same models go down in quick succession, it makes me very suspicious.

That suspicion was confirmed when we went to salvage the previous crash sites. A specific component was missing each time. I'm not sure who is responsible. Could be one of our rivals. Could be scavengers. Could have been the tech I sent to investigate, for all I know. But whoever it wasn’t interested in other, more expensive salvage. Just this one component.

Something's up. If you can recover the requested item from our latest wreck, I have a feeling it will answer a lot of questions.
mission_onfoot_salvage_015_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_015_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_015_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_015_narrative:
My crew just lost one of our ships and I'm damned certain I know who shot it down. But payback is a secondary concern right now. You see, the ship was returning from a research facility in another system. We've heard rumours that a hostile faction has developed a new synthetic pathogen and intend to use it against rival settlements, including ours. The lost ship was smuggling a sample to us.

Most likely the pilot thought they were good and safe when they made it back to this system. Turns out they weren't so lucky. If that sample is still intact we need it recovered from the wreckage. Are you in?
mission_onfoot_salvage_016_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_016_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_016_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_016_narrative:
Have you ever been attacked by raiders? They're vicious. I was one of several driving SRVs when they ambushed us, guns blazing. I only escaped by the skin of my teeth. Some of the others weren't so lucky.

In the scramble to get out of there, I didn’t have time to recover important company schematics which were in one of the other vehicles. It feels stupid to ask a stranger to get them after everything that happened, but I can't go back there. I’m not a soldier. Would you go for me if I pay you?
mission_onfoot_salvage_017_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_017_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_017_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_017_narrative:
One of my client’s new, experimental beacons stopped transmitting recently. It was assumed to be a small technical problem, but a faint signal was detected at a suspected crash site. The beacon was only deployed within the past few months, so sabotage is a suspected cause.

Regardless of the cause, a key piece of circuitry must be recovered. It’s a highly valuable proprietary technology, stored in a state-of-the-art protective housing. It survived the crash, trust me. You don’t need to know what the circuit does, as I’m sure a Commander fully appreciates. Just bring it to me and you’ll get paid.
mission_onfoot_salvage_018_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_018_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_018_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_018_narrative:
My client owned a satellite performing an extensive planetary scan in the system. They tried downloading the archives from it, but there was a problem. The satellite was logging the scan data just fine - it just wasn't sending that data on to my client’s network. A remote repair attempt was made but must have failed pretty spectacularly because the bloody thing crashed shortly afterwards.

I can't spare any people for a site recovery at the moment, so if you can pull the data from the wreckage it would add a spoonful of sugar to a very sour situation. You’ll be paid for the work, of course.
mission_onfoot_salvage_019_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_019_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_019_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_019_narrative:
I need you to recover some intelligence which is critical to my faction's ongoing conflict. The data was travelling with a courier from a few systems over but their ship never arrived. Fortunately, the pilot had the presence of mind to trigger an encrypted beacon and we just caught their signal a few days ago.

I can't say for sure that the data we need will be near the beacon, but it's worth finding out. If any of our teams head out there it could alert the enemy to the signal's presence. It's not exactly in a tactically vital area of the planet. But I'm willing to bet a good payday that you're up to the task I'm offering.
mission_onfoot_salvage_020_missioncomple: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_020_name: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_020_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_020_narrative:
My organisation has heard worrying reports that our rivals are developing a new hazardous chemical, possibly for a bio-weapon. One of our agents managed to interdict a transport ship suspected of carrying a batch. The agent confirmed acquiring a sample from it but communications ceased shortly after. Their encrypted beacon came online hours ago, giving us a location. To be honest, it doesn't look like good news.

I don't know if our agent was attacked, suffered a mechanical problem or whatever else. Maybe the sample leaked. I need someone with your skills to go down and investigate. We must find out what our enemies are cooking up, and I'm willing to offer credits to bring that sample to us quickly.
mission_onfoot_salvage_bs_001_missioncom: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_bs_001_name: Find the $#CommodityName; in an empty settlement
mission_onfoot_salvage_bs_001_name_title: Recovery: Find the $#CommodityName; in an empty settlement
mission_onfoot_salvage_bs_001_narrative:
I swear on every deity this universe has to offer that it’s impossible to carry out a settlement evacuation without someone forgetting something important. This time, it was some berk in the research department that neglected to secure a dangerous chemical. The stuff could cause real damage in the wrong hands. I’m sure they remembered to pack their Insight suites, of course.

I don’t want a terrorist attack or tragic accident on my team’s reputation just because some nerd cared more about their games than public safety. I need you to secure those materials as soon as possible, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_bs_002_missioncom: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_bs_002_name: Find the $#CommodityName; in an empty settlement
mission_onfoot_salvage_bs_002_name_title: Recovery: Find the $#CommodityName; in an empty settlement
mission_onfoot_salvage_bs_002_narrative:
A friend of mine had to leave the last settlement he worked at in a hurry and left something behind. It’s just an entertainment suite, but…well, he’s a person of niche interests, you see. His old co-workers made fun of him when they found out what kind of games he collected. I understand why he doesn’t want to go back and pick them up.

The staff would recognise me from some company events I went to, but no one will know you. I bet you could stroll in there and pick the games up without anyone noticing. Just remember to be discrete and bring them right to me. My friend will be so happy to get them back!
mission_onfoot_salvage_bs_003_missioncom: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvage_bs_003_name: Find the $#CommodityName; in an empty settlement
mission_onfoot_salvage_bs_003_name_title: Recovery: Find the $#CommodityName; in an empty settlement
mission_onfoot_salvage_bs_003_narrative:
The corporation I represent was forced to evacuate one of its settlements not long ago. A pretty routine procedure carried out many times before. The problem is when the personnel returned they find personal items missing or vandalized. This wasn’t a simple theft, Commander. Somebody was sending a message.

I’m now tasked with finding out who is responsible. Some of the surveillance systems had been disabled, but not all of them. Bring me back whatever data you can find and I’ll analyse it. With luck, I’ll be able to identify the perpetrator before long.

mission_onfoot_salvage_bs_name_title: Recovery: Find the $#CommodityName; in an empty settlement
mission_onfoot_salvage_bs_narrative:
I’ve lost months of research because of some stupid evacuation order. Fine, yes, the settlement had received warning of a major attack, but my lab was fully secure. I could have carried on. Instead, I was hurried out and had to leave all my experiments behind. They’ll be ruined by now!

It’s not just a question of recovering important data. It’s also about making sure it doesn’t fall into the wrong hands. Sure, I doubt anyone else is smart enough to know how valuable my work is, but I can’t risk a rival company obtaining that information. Will you recover it for me?

mission_onfoot_salvage_name_title: Retrieval: Grab the $#CommodityName; from a crash site
mission_onfoot_salvage_narrative:
Listen, I need your help something fierce. Everyone’s freaking out because one of my gang's ships went down carrying a super important schematic. And, of course, I’m the one who’ll get the blame if it’s never recovered. It’s not like it’s my fault the courier crashed, but still, it’ll be me who pays the consequences.

I’ve tracked down the crash site, so all you have to do is get down to the planet, find that damn schematic and bring it back. Then maybe I’ll get to keep my legs for a while. Right until the next disaster.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_001_missio: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_001_narrat:
This contract should be pretty routine, if not technically legal. One of the communication beacons my department monitors went offline recently and has wound up in pieces on a planet. I'm sure it was simply some accident but company policy is to do everything by the rules and check for anything untoward.

However, it isn't company policy to commit crimes for the sake of an accident report, and this beacon is the property of another faction. This is why I need an independent contractor to extract the memory chip for us. I don't imagine it'll be too taxing a task for a Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_002_missio: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_002_narrat:
I'm have a contact who's currently undercover at a production facility. They contact me at the same time every week and the data they feed us about the operators is highly valuable. But this week they got cut off part-way through a report when a beacon just so happened to have its transmitter fried at the wrong moment.

I don't like coincidences and I have a horrible feeling our contact's been made. But if there's any chance that beacon managed to pick up the data they were transmitting before it fell out of the sky, then I need it.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_003_missio: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_003_narrat:
I hope I'm wrong about this, but I may have accidentally fried one of my company's communication beacons. I was completing remote maintenance on it when all the systems flatlined. The damn thing thrust out of orbit and crashed. I know it sounds stupid but I've had a lot going on recently, okay?

My company is already arranging to send someone to investigate the crash site. I'd like you to recover the memory first so I can find out what went wrong before my bosses do. Just in case. Oh, and since this isn't an official company contract it's considered stealing. But you're okay with that if the credits are good, right?
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_004_missio: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_004_narrat:
I represent certain parties who had recent cause to eliminate a problematic figure in rival space. They believed the operation went without a hitch, having first taken care of the nearby communication beacons. But developments in the past few days have raised doubts. There's a chance that one of the beacons was merely damaged and was able to transmit a distress call from the target's ship.

If that's the case, then my client needs to know what was transmitted without showing undue interest themselves. They know where the beacon crashed, they just need you to recover the logs from it before someone else does.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_005_missio: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_005_narrat:
If you ask me, there's nothing lower in this galaxy than traitors to our glorious cause. And as it happens, I think I have identified one such traitor.

I've managed to get hold of their communication logs - doesn't matter how - and if I had something I could cross-reference them against, I am sure I could expose them as the two-faced rat that they are. All I need are the logs from the right beacon.

Problem is, I paid someone to do the job but the idiot boosted his vessel at the wrong moment and knocked the damn beacon out of orbit. Then cried off that it was too dangerous to recover. But I think it won't be too dangerous for you, eh?
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_006_missio: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_006_narrat:
Given how much space humanity has to work in, it is particularly irritating when people insist on sticking their nose in the activities of neighbours. That happened to us recently when a military satellite took an interest in one of our settlements. A place which we'd prefer remained unobserved.

Luckily, said satellite recently had a truly tragic accident and crashed. But between you and me, I’d like to find out why it was looking at us in the first place. Bring me the scan records; you can keep anything else you find.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_007_missio: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_007_narrat:
It's difficult to get an edge these days, so sometimes one is forced to do things which aren't exactly legal. For example, you might need to piggyback a satellite network offering greater coverage than your own. The trick is having a contingency plan for when the owners find out. That way you can erase any sign of your involvement at the touch of a button.

Which is all well and good until a micro-asteroid hits the satellite and knocks it offline before you can flip the magic switch. If that satellite's memory chip is intact, then not only does it contain data that we want, it also contains telemetry that can get us killed. I need it before the owners come looking for their downed property.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_008_missio: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_008_narrat:
My boss has reason to believe a recent shipment of satellites is a key part of a planned military operation against our operation. Luckily we have people installed at the manufacturer who managed to fit certain modifications which spoof the satellite's output to hide our activities. Of course, one of the satellites almost immediately malfunctioned and crashed. I guess the modifications were not thoroughly tested.

If our enemies get to that wreckage and find anything amiss - or if one of our agents are detected nearby - they'll know something's up. We can't risk our people on the inside being exposed. Hell, even if we pull them out, that could put a target on their back as well.

What we require is an outside agent to recover that altered part. What do you say?
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_009_missio: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_009_narrat:
I represent a well-respected company which specialises in the production of satellites and other communication technology. It recently came to my attention that a small number of our products had substandard components used in their manufacture which may have led to early mechanical failure.

This, of course, is not something our clients need to find out. Not least because some of our clients aren't the sort of people we should be selling to in the first place, in some people's minds. As you can see, it is better for all involved if this situation remains need-to-know.

So, I would like to head this all off by having you recover a specific component from the wreckage before anyone else arrives. You'll be paid upon delivery, okay?
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_010_missio: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_010_narrat:
People are attracted to definite sides, without shades of grey. They like good and evil. Right and wrong. But the reality is rarely so accommodating, which is why things commonly go awry. Recently some target information was incorrectly decrypted and a mistaken target was wiped out.

But I don't think it serves any purpose for such things to be dragged into the light. If a few dozen of the wrong people died, then prosecuting those who did it - accidentally, remember - won't make the tragic victims any less dead.

So, when a simple comms satellite captures something it shouldn't have... Well, I think everyone would be best served if the information on it was recovered by the right people. We took the satellite out of commission. Now I just need somebody to obtain the data. Are you willing to protect the brave souls who were merely following orders?
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_011_missio: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_011_narrat:
I used to be in charge of monitoring my employer’s satellites across several star systems. It was important to dispatch a repair team the moment something started acting funny. Sometimes, though, perfectly functional satellites get replaced just because they're old. You're meant to shut them off and scupper them, but some of us simply take them off the network and leave them running. People pay to run their comms through unregistered channels.

Now, with most systems at risk of some faction or another initiating conflict at a moment’s notice, it’s interesting what old, perfectly functional satellites nobody remembers will pick up. Some very valuable data will trip over those hidden channels. And one of the longer serving models finally crashed just recently. To the right people, the memory chip on that thing is worth a lot of credits. How about you go collect it before someone else does?
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_001_mis: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_001_nam: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
Scavenge: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_001_nar:
I represent a powerful research group that’s had an important specimen stolen from their labs. An extraordinarily old and rare fossil that, no matter what anyone says, is legally owned. I’ve assured my associates I will find a way to get their original property back.

I’ve been monitoring the settlement this fossil was taken to and arranged a sudden evacuation under health and safety pretences, leaving the fossil unprotected. All you have to do is bring it to me so that I can return it to its rightful owners.

Your assistance will ensure there is no need for the authorities to be involved in the original theft. It would be such a waste of their time.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_002_mis: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_002_nam: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
Scavenge: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_002_nar:
You have no idea of the kind of pressures a researcher like me faces. My bosses don’t expect results, they expect miracles. And those miracles have to happen yesterday. As though theorising a method of speeding up our manufacturing process was as simple as mixing a cocktail. There’s no way I was going to be able to meet such outrageous deadlines by myself but, luckily for me, another company has already done the practical work.

A lab with far more resources than ours has developed a vital catalyst for the exact chemical reaction I need. Taking this component should be easy enough. The lab workers are involved in a funding dispute and have temporarily shut down the facility as a result. This is the perfect time to act.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_003_mis: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_003_nam: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
Scavenge: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_003_nar:
The danger inherent in biological weapons is constant, Commander. Theoretically, any rogue group with enough credits and the right contacts could obtain a weapon capable of devastating populated worlds. The group I work with is committed to ending all biological warfare. And we’ve just received word of a new experimental pathogen under development.

We prefer to do our work in the political spectrum, which is why I’m looking for somebody with no official ties to obtain a sample. We’ve gone to considerable lengths to ensure the settlement working on the pathogen is offline. Are you willing to play a part in this mission of peace?
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_004_mis: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_004_nam: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
Scavenge: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_004_nar:
You wouldn’t believe the amount of cut-throat competition that occurs in the mining industry. That’s why people like me get hired. My job is to sniff out opportunities and seize the best ones for my client. This time I have a real whopper on my hands. If my information is correct, there’s a settlement sitting on a lode worth billions.

The idiots who currently run the extraction facility blew their budget before securing a regular income. They’ve been forced to shut down for a while, meaning you can sneak in and obtain a sample. With it, I can convince my clients to invest in the mining operation before anyone else gets involved.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_005_mis: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_005_nam: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
Scavenge: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_005_nar:
My team is always on the lookout for the next big opportunity. Weapons, archaeological artefacts, chemicals: if it’s worth something, we’ll deal in it. We send out scouts to find inactive settlements and you’d be amazed what they come back with. People leave all sorts of things behind in an evacuation.

A few days back, one of our scout teams was interrupted by scavengers. I’m happy they got out alive, but there’s a ship schematic mentioned in their report I would very much like to take a look at. I hope I can count on you to bring it to me.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_006_mis: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_006_nam: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
Scavenge: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_006_nar:
For weeks now I’ve been investigating a criminal operating in plain sight. They masquerade as a legitimate trader, but I’m sure it’s a front for a smuggling operation. I’m a private investigator, and the authorities who should deal with this won’t listen to me. Keep asking for solid evidence. In the meantime, this so-called trader is hurting several businesses in the area, including my client’s.

I may never get a better chance than right now to act. A settlement they regularly work from just gone offline. It was an emergency evacuation, so I’m banking on the trader leaving something useful behind. With the right data, I’ll have the proof I need to put them in a cell.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_007_mis: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_007_nam: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
Scavenge: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_007_nar:
New vehicle designs are hard to come by these days. The megacorps have a monopoly on the most popular designs, so we low-level manufacturers are looking for the tiniest advantage we find. I’ve promised my bosses I’d make the most of any available opportunity, and there’s one reliable way to find them. Steal from the competition.

Right now, there’s one prototype design I’d like to look over. Snatch the schematic and bring it here. I’ll pay to know whether it has any interesting modifications we should borrow.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_008_mis: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_008_nam: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
Scavenge: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_008_nar:
You can’t trust anyone these days. Someone I called a colleague and a friend turned out to be a corporate spy, leaking our secrets to the competition. The worst part is that there’s no way of knowing how much damage they’ve done unless we can determine exactly what they managed to access.

Fortunately for me, an associate of mine claims to have witnessed a meeting between this two-faced creep and his real employers. Not only that but the meeting location recently suspended operation for a few days. That's a lot of luck and I don't want to squander it. Get to that facility and retrieve the data listed in the contract. At least then we’ll know where we stand.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_009_mis: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_009_nam: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
Scavenge: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_009_nar:
If you’ve ever worn a high-quality suit, chances are the company I work for had a hand in manufacturing some of the parts. There’s a lot of competition to provide high-grade components to the megacorps, and everyone’s trying to one-up each other to secure new contracts. That’s why we have to work hard to maintain our position, even if it means borrowing an idea or two.

There’s talk of another company working on a smart new prototype that could make the difference between landing a big contract and being lost in the shuffle. Corps are attracted to new ideas like bugs to a striplight, y’see. The good news is that the settlement where the schematic is being developed recently went offline for some system convention, so the data's just sitting there waiting to be copied.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_mb_miss: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_mb_name: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
Scavenge: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_mission: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_name: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_name_ti: Scavenge: Get the $#CommodityName; from an evacuated site
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_bs_narrati:
It’s always worth keeping an eye on the competition because you never know when they’ll do something stupid. Like leaving some incredibly valuable research behind when they’re forced to evacuate a settlement. Such mistakes allow an unscrupulous rival like the one I represent to swoop in and collect.

Crop gene splicing doesn’t sound very glamourous, but there’s a lot of money in the agriculture industry. And if you can bring me that research before anybody else can grab it, my client will make sure you are adequately reimbursed.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_deliverpan:

Return to your mission provider at $#StartStationName:style:name=keyword; in the $#StartStationSystemName:style:name=keyword; system.

mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_mb_mission: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_missioncom: It’s been a pleasure working with you, Commander.
mission_onfoot_salvageillegal_narrative:
It's always good to keep your ear to the ground, right? That's what I do. I built my own decryption rig so I can monitor broadcasts in this system because you never know what you'll hear. Mostly it's just fuzz, but sometimes it catches something. I hooked into an interesting channel recently; something that sounded very sensitive. It was sensitive enough that the beacon I'd tapped into got taken out soon after.

But those beacons are built tough. I bet the remainder of the message is still in its onboard memory. So if I can get that information to its intended recipient, maybe they'll make it worth my while? I just need you to pick it up for me.
mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_001_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_001_narra:
You ever hear that phrase about one person’s trash being another person’s treasure? Or maybe it was something about passion and poison…Anyway, the idea is that not everyone views opportunity the same way.
One of the settlements I do business with - legitimate business, of course - has been complaining that a contraband operation has sprung up near them. They're worried, but it's music to my ears! See, I've been cooking stuff for personal use in my lab for a while and I've gotten real good at it. But if I could turn my hobby into a business? I'd be rich!
I've managed to get in contact with the smugglers and one of them is waiting for a sample of my wares. Take this over to them and who knows? This could be the start of something beautiful.
mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_002_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_002_narra:
Things are tough around here at the moment. No matter what state the economy is in, someone finds a way to screw over cargo pilots. Runs aren't always as profitable as they should be. Especially when you're getting interdicted by raiders every so often
That's why some of us have to look outside the law to survive. For me that means smuggling. Nothing too illegal, mind. I’m not interested in hurting people. Just stuff which sits in the grey areas of society.
Anyway, it was all going fine until a rival smuggler tipped off security at this starport. That's how my ship got impounded. Fortunately, I managed to get the package I'm meant to be delivering off of my ship before they could find it. I just need someone to carry it over the finish line for me.
You fancy helping a fellow pilot out of a bad situation, Commander?
mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_003_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_003_narra:
I need someone discreet to get a package to my best customer. I'd normally hand jobs like this off to my regular courier, but her ship was wrecked by raiders last month and she hasn't scraped together the credits for a new one yet. Lucky you, huh?
Anyway, I want to keep this customer sweet because they represent a good percentage of my business. I'm kind of amazed they buy as much as they do, being honest. As far as I know they're just some worker at a settlement. Must be selling it on to the locals, I guess. They certainly can't be using it all themselves. If they were, most of their organs would be melting by now.
Whatever they're doing with it, I don't much care. Credits are credits. You wanna earn a few by carrying this package over to them?
mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_004_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_004_narra:
I have a problem. I run a relatively small chemical supply business and, unlike the corps, I'm operating on thin margins. So you can imagine my annoyance when I heard about another company who wants to expand into my territory. If I lose just a handful of contracts, that's the end for me.
Fortunately I think I have a way out of this. I've got a cousin who works at their nearest facility who owes me, well, everything. It took some convincing but they've agreed to adulterate a few of the new competitor’s production lines using a contaminant I've synthesized.
It won't destroy anything, but it's enough to get some negative attention and make them look like a bad switch for my current clients. Please, get the chemical to my cousin before they change their mind.
mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_005_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_005_narra:
I wish I was like you. Someone who was their own boss, able to chart their own course in the galaxy. Me? I'm stuck in a dead-end job with useless co-workers and an egomaniac for a boss. I'd quit, but I can't afford to. Not yet, at least.
You see, the one good thing about this job is that it provides access to a vast array of industrial chemicals and the necessary equipment to mix them. And because I'm surrounded by fools who haven’t conducted a stock check in months, I pretty much have carte blanche to do as I please.
Which is what I've done. I have a buyer waiting for a sample of my latest concoction. Deliver it to them, and this could be the start of something beautiful.
Oh, and try not to get scanned. Unrecognised chemical compounds tend to piss off the guards.
mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_006_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_006_narra:
You ever have something fall into your hands which you're pretty sure was meant for somebody else?
An encrypted memory chip arrived at my apartment recently. No labels, no name, nothing. Can’t say I was expecting it either, but lucky for me I’m not a stranger when it comes to decryption. That’s usually how you find the good stuff.

The data on the chip? Crazy. Real explosive stuff. The sort of thing which brings down faction officials.

When the original courier realises their mistake, I'm probably dead. But before that can happen I intend to become dead rich. I've found a buyer for the data. I just need someone to deliver it, while I make arrangements to travel as far and fast in the opposite direction as possible. Can you help me out?
mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_007_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_007_narra:
This whole starport is conspiring against me! I'm a good person. I pay my faction fees. I don't bother anyone who doesn't bother me first. I even donate to charity!
But the way security around here treats me is disgusting. The constant checks, public searches, vehicle scans for no good reason, even overnight stays in a cell while my records are dragged though. I'm being persecuted, and for what? Honestly, I have no idea!
I’m trying to run a business while all this is going on. Talk about impossible. I was going to make an urgent delivery today but they just impounded my ship again. Something needs to be done about this outrageous harassment.
Friend, if you could get the package to my customer for me, I would be truly indebted to you. Oh, but be careful not to get scanned. It's full of narcotics.
mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_008_missi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! Long may your service to us continue.
mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_008_narra:
Do you like consuming media on your Insight? Of course you do. It's impossible to experience everything, though. There are so many content providers and all of them want a periodic credit fee from you. Just for the privilege of retaining access to their stuff.
Get this, though: a local broadcaster accidentally opened a data port hooked to a storage network and I managed to grab a ridiculous amount of media before they closed it! So now, if anyone wants a particular show or interactive suite, I can provide a copy to keep forever on a personal data bank. I just need to arrange physical deliveries. It’s safer than using the comms networks.
Yeah, technically it's illegal. I'm betting the authorities are too busy with the people smuggling drugs and weapons to worry about everyday Insight content, right? Then again, these execs sure do get tetchy about their intellectual property…
Will you run this delivery for me? I’ll pay you a cut of the credits.

mission_onfoot_smuggle_contact_narrative:
I've got a pal over at another settlement who's asked me if I could get him some 'specialist entertainment'. You know the kind. So I looked into it for him and I've found a guy here who can get me almost anything I want. All the latest Insights, stims, narcotics, even food that was banned for being dangerous to human health. In fact, if you're after anything yourself I could probably hook you up?
…Actually, scratch that. Forget I said anything. This conversation never took place. That suit of yours isn’t recording, is it? Hah, I bet you fell for my joke!
Just get the package over to my friend, would you?

Use caution - spire sites are considered highly dangerous.

mission_onfoothelp_salvagebodysite: You have accepted a contract to retrieve an item from an offline settlement. Make your way to the settlement and locate the item. mission_outsideofstartzone_welcome_descr:
$#minorFaction:style:name=keyword; wishes to offer new Commanders in the area an opportunity to work with us.
Please locate our contact at $#DestinationStationName:style:name=keyword; in $#DestinationStationSystemName:style:name=keyword;.
A $#Reward:currency:style:name=keyword; payment will be provided alongside local mission board contracts.
Helpful guides and articles are available in the Codex, found in your ship's Internal interface panel.
mission_outsideofstartzone_welcome_faile:
$#minorFaction:style:name=keyword; are no longer offering their initial financial incentive for travelling to $#DestinationStationSystemName:style:name=keyword;.
You can find additional job opportunities at most starports and outposts throughout the galaxy.
mission_outsideofstartzone_welcome_gotod:
Welcome Commander,

Glad to see that you've arrived in our system. To fulfil the terms of our offer and collect your credit reward, select $#DestinationStationName:style:name=keyword; as your target and travel here to dock.
If you haven't already, you can find this starport in the Navigation tab, available from on the left-side navigation panel.

We'll look forward to your arrival.


$#MissionGiverFactionContactTitle; $#MissionGiverFactionContact;

Hello Commander,

It appears you've launched and are heading out on your first journey as a licensed Commander. Hopefully you're considering coming to $#DestinationStationSystemName:style:name=keyword; to take advantage of our offer.

In the meantime, should you wish to practice any specific areas of piloting a ship, check out the training simulations found in the Internal interface panel.

Regards,
$#MissionGiverFactionContactTitle; $#MissionGiverFactionContact;
mission_outsideofstartzone_welcome_intro:
Greetings, Commander.

We would like to invite you to participate in a unique opportunity to earn some credits and build your reputation in this system.
A mission has been added to your Transactions screen in the External interface panel. Please read through the details and consider our offer carefully.
Perhaps we'll work together soon.

Fly safe,
$#MissionGiverFactionContactTitle; $#MissionGiverFactionContact;

Fly safe, Commander $#CommanderName;.
Well done, Commander. Please confirm your reward at this screen to continue.

Good to see you, Commander.

The total of $#Reward:currency:style:name=keyword; has been successfully added to your balance. You may now view the mission board to take advantage of further opportunities available to you. This is a great way to earn credits and increase your reputation in the system.

Remember that the Pilot's Handbook, tutorials of varying difficulty, and additional challenges can all be accessed through the home tab on the right side panel of your cockpit.

Good luck out there, Commander $#CommanderName;.

Regards,
$#MissionGiverFactionContactTitle; $#MissionGiverFactionContact;

We are contacting you to confirm that the credit incentive offered by $#minorFaction:style:name=keyword; has now expired. Hopefully the reason you declined to accept this opportunity is down to the busy schedule of a newly licensed Commander!

Fly safe, Commander $#CommanderName;.
mission_outsideofstartzone_welcome_remin:

mission_reason_blopsassassination_electi: If you can discreetly silence this rabble-rousing politician, it will help us in the coming elections.
mission_reason_blopsassassination_famine: Our famine situation is being made worse by the greed of this entrepreneur, so we're authorising a hit to serve the greater good.
mission_reason_blopsassassination_indust: The industrial world can be ultra-competitive, and while murder of influential rivals isn't exactly rare, it's usually executed with discretion.
mission_reason_blopsassassination_outbre: This individual is one of those directly responsible for the recent outbreak and must be punished. A covert hit is authorised.
mission_reason_blopsassassination_theocr: Even the most enlightened theocracy has enemies – enemies that must be discreetly removed from this plane of existence.
mission_reason_blopscourier_boom_spawn: The economic boom requires sensitive economic data to be transported, so we trust you are both discreet and efficient.
mission_reason_blopscourier_bust_spawn: If you can help us to move confidential financial data, it will alleviate our poor economic situation.
mission_reason_blopscourier_civilunrest: If this confidential data about who's funding resistance movements is delivered quickly, we can hasten the end of this civil unrest.
mission_reason_blopscourier_civilwar: We can end this civil war if you can deliver this classified data about certain leaders' true allegiance.
mission_reason_blopscourier_corporation_: Information is vital for any corporation, and moving it covertly is doubly important.
mission_reason_blopscourier_elections: Our position in the elections will be improved if you can deliver this information about our opponents to where it is needed.
mission_reason_blopscourier_expansion: Our expansion efforts rely upon this secret data arriving safely, so we need a trustworthy courier.
mission_reason_blopscourier_famine: Restricted information on food management methods will help relieve this famine, and we require a trusted courier to deliver it.
mission_reason_blopscourier_govermental: The information we require you to transport is highly sensitive and vital to our government's stability.
mission_reason_blopscourier_lockdown: By transporting this sensitive information, you can help us to end this lockdown.
mission_reason_blopscourier_outbreak: There's more to this outbreak than meets the eye. It is crucial that this data about 'patient zero' reaches its destination.
mission_reason_blopscourier_war_spawn: The war effort relies on the transportation of secret tactical information, so this courier mission is a priority.
mission_reason_blopsdisable_civilunrest: If you can help us in quietly shutting down the surface bases that are asking too many questions, it will help reduce civil unrest.
mission_reason_blopsdisable_civilwar: To help end this civil war as quickly as possible, we've sanctioned black ops activities to disable the other side's planetary facilities.
mission_reason_blopsdisable_construction: Competition in the construction industry has become intense. So damaging our rivals' planetary structures will be good for our business.
mission_reason_blopsdisable_expansion: Our expansion efforts can be helped if you can covertly shut down certain planetary bases that are destabilising our plans.
mission_reason_blopsdisable_lockdown: You can improve our security situation here by disabling these rebellious surface installations. Just make sure you're not discovered.
mission_reason_blopsdisable_patronage_sp: Secretly disabling these planetary facilities will support our patronage.
mission_reason_blopsdisable_war: Disabling the enemy's surface installations will help our war effort. But if you're caught, we'll deny ever knowing you, so be careful.
mission_reason_blopshack_civilunrest: Take on this mission to hack the agitators' network and you'll be playing an important role in bringing the unrest to a swift end.
mission_reason_blopshack_civilwar: This hacking mission will further our cause by gaining insight into our adversary's plans.
mission_reason_blopshack_educational: We need to source some hard-to-find data to supply important research, which requires a cyber attack under the radar.
mission_reason_blopshack_elections: This covert hacking operation will provide us with information we can use for blackmail purposes in the coming elections.
mission_reason_blopshack_expansion: As long as we're not caught, this hacking operation will give us the research we need to expand into another system.
mission_reason_blopshack_lockdown: Completing this covert hack against selected targets will help to improve the security situation.
mission_reason_blopshack_prisoncolony_sp: On occasion, a prison colony needs to bypass ordinary information protocols to keep things running smoothly.
mission_reason_blopshack_war: This covert hacking operation will help our intelligence services in the war.
mission_reason_blopsmassacre_bust: Perform a covert offensive against this financially reckless group, and you will help us to reverse this economic downturn.
mission_reason_blopsmassacre_civilunrest: If you help us to quietly eliminate this band of  troublemakers, it might allow us to quell this civil unrest.
mission_reason_blopsmassacre_elections: We can nudge things in our favour in the coming election if you undertake a covert strike against our political opponents.
mission_reason_blopsmassacre_famine: It's unfortunate, but we need to take lethal action against this group of food-smuggling criminals to help end the famine.
mission_reason_blopsmassacre_multigov_sp: With complementary interests, a multi-government initiative sometimes needs to terminate a common enemy.
mission_reason_blopsmassacre_outbreak: Permanently shutting down this group, who are blocking medical research that might save thousands of lives, will help us with the recent outbreak.
mission_reason_blopsmassacre_penal: Covert operations are an essential part of life around here. It's regrettable, but your skills will help to keep our colony stable.
mission_reason_blopspiracy_boom_spawn: The economic uptick has provided opportunities for piracy operations, which will benefit both us and you.
mission_reason_blopspiracy_bust: If you can hijack enough cargo, the proceeds will help us to survive the economic mess we are in.
mission_reason_blopspiracy_civilwar: An act of piracy against our enemy's ships could turn the tide of the civil war, provided of course that it can't be linked to us.
mission_reason_blopspiracy_dictatorship_: It might seem like a dictatorship can take whatever it wants, but it's best to be circumspect. So undertake this piracy action discreetly.
mission_reason_blopspiracy_elections: This false flag pirate operation could swing things in our favour in the coming polls, as long as we're not connected.
mission_reason_blopspiracy_famine: Piracy contracts such as this, which bring in money and supplies, are our only way of staying alive during this time of famine.
mission_reason_blopspiracy_financial: Covert acquisitions aren't unusual in the world of finance, but this time it's taking place in space rather than a boardroom.
mission_reason_blopspiracy_outbreak: If we're going to survive this outbreak, we need to secure vital supplies. If that means piracy, so be it.
mission_reason_blopspiracy_war: Take on this piracy action against our enemy and it will give our military some breathing space.
mission_reason_blopssmuggle_boom_spawn: You can help to strengthen our economy by smuggling these items before their tax value becomes known.
mission_reason_blopssmuggle_bust: Help us to recover from economic disaster by transporting these valuable goods to their buyers. We cannot be connected with their movement.
mission_reason_blopssmuggle_confederacy_: Sometimes a confederacy requires the covert movement of goods between us and our allies.
mission_reason_blopssmuggle_extraction: Keeping the peace around here sometimes relies on looking the other way, and smuggling is a part of that.
mission_reason_blopssmuggle_famine: You can help us to tackle the ongoing famine by transporting some vital supplies to where they're needed most.
mission_reason_blopssmuggle_lockdown: If you can smuggle these items to their rightful owners in double-quick time, they'll fund our efforts to end the lockdown.
mission_reason_blopssmuggle_outbreak: It's not smuggling so much as survival. The income that these items will provide can boost our efforts to resist the outbreak.
mission_reason_none: A job has come up that I think you can help us with.
mission_reprewardonly: Instead of physical rewards, completing this mission will increase your standing with this faction.

mission_startzone_enter1_inboxreminder_c:
Hello CMDR!

Taking some time to explore the galaxy, huh? Just want to remind that you still have to complete your registration as a pilot. You need to be at the $#StartStationName:style:name=keyword; in $#StartStationSystemName:style:name=keyword; system to complete the process.

I will speak to you again once it is done. Farewell.
mission_startzone_enter1_inboxtheo_conte:
Welcome to your new ship, Commander. Your Pilots' Federation license has been issued and you are now a fully independent pilot, free to traverse the galaxy however you wish. An introductory mission has been assigned to you. You can review your active missions in the Transactions tab of the External interface panel.

To complete this mission, access Starport Services from the menu presented in the centre of your dashboard. Then select the Mission Board from the general services list on the left of the presented screen.

You'll be able to complete your mission here, with one of the Pilots' Federation representatives. To review what I have discussed, select your Comms panel and scroll through the recorded text.
mission_startzone_enter1_missioncomplete:
Well done, Commander. You've successfully completed the introductory mission. I've added 1,000 credits to your balance as a reward.

The mission board is one of the most common ways of obtaining work. Available missions can be accepted immediately, while missions which have certain unmet requirements – such as a certain amount of cargo space or reputation – will be unavailable.
mission_startzone_enter2_failed_contents:
The $#Reward:currency:style:name=keyword; reward is no longer available.
However, you can find many more opportunities offered by the $#minorFaction:style:name=keyword; and other factions throughout the galaxy.
mission_startzone_enter2_inboxtheoinspac:
Hello Commander,

There's one thing I haven't mentioned yet. You've been granted a Pilots' Federation District Permit. The collection of systems you currently find yourself in is part of the Pilots' Federation District. These systems are administered specifically to allow new Commanders to get to grips with life as an independent pilot in relative safety.

The associate permit grants you access to the district until both of the following criteria is fulfilled:
- You achieve a Pilots' Federation rank
- You successfully dock at any station located outside of the district.

I advise exploring the systems within the district as an introduction to your journey. You are free to depart whenever you wish, of course. Perhaps we'll see you at Mawson Dock soon.
mission_startzone_enter2_missioncancelle:
Greetings, Commander.

This is to confirm that you have declined the initial credit reward from $#minorFaction:style:name=keyword;, and the offer has been withdrawn at your request. We would like to offer our congratulations to you as a newly licensed Commander and wish you the best of luck.

 Should you wish to learn more about a variety of useful topics, please refer to the Pilot's Handbook which is accessible via the Home tab on the Internal interface panel.

Fly safe, Commander $#CommanderName;.
mission_startzone_enter2_missioncomplete:
Thank you for coming, Commander.

I've been waiting for this data. It's the latest move in a game of three-dimensional chess I've been playing with the station controller of Coelho Station. He doesn't know I'm just seventeen moves from victory!

I've added 10,000 credits to your balance, as instructed by Theo Arcosta. Seems you've impressed him enough for the Pilots' Federation to invest in the beginning of your career. I wish you nothing but good luck out there, rookie!
mission_startzone_enter2_missionexpiredi:
Greetings, Commander.

We regret to inform you that the time limit to collect your initial credit reward from $#minorFaction:style:name=keyword; has now expired. Hopefully this is due to the busy schedule of a newly licensed Commander! 

Should you wish to learn more about a variety of useful topics, please refer to the Pilot's Handbook which is accessible through the Home tab on the Internal interface panel.

Fly safe, Commander $#CommanderName;.
mission_startzone_enter2_reminderinbox:
Greetings, Commander.
We would like to inform you that the initial credit reward offered by $#minorFaction:style:name=keyword; remains available for the next 24 hours, after which we will assume it is not required. We hope to see you at $#DestinationStationName:style:name=keyword; in $#DestinationStationSystemName:style:name=keyword; soon.

Fly safe,
$#minorFaction:style:name=keyword;.
mission_startzone_enter2_spawn: Time to take on your first solo journey.
mission_startzone_enter2_theofirstinbox:
Good. A few credits have been added to your balance. Call it a welcome package.

If you'd like to earn a few more, another mission has been assigned to you. Again, you'll find the contract in your Transactions screen.

This time you'll need to travel back to Mawson Dock in the Dromi system. You can select the destination on the Navigation panel. Alternatively, you can access the galaxy map directly from the "Open Galaxy Map" button in the mission transaction.

I'll contact you upon arrival at Mawson Dock if you decide to complete this mission. If you choose to take a different path then I wish you luck, Commander.
mission_startzone_enter2_theomissioncomp:
Well done, Commander. You've proven that you can travel between systems and interact with the mission board.

From this point on you'll need to select your own missions. There are a variety of contracts available throughout the galaxy which require a competent pilot.

Once again, there are training missions available for you to practice a variety of controls and challenges.
The Pilots' Handbook, found in the Internal interface panel, also provides a wealth of advice on most professions.

I'll look forward to watching your progress, Commander. Make us proud. 

This is Theo Arcosta, signing off.

Congratulations on completing your assessment. On behalf of the $#minorFaction:style:name=keyword; we'd like to offer you $#Reward:currency:style:name=keyword; towards your new career. mission_startzone_exit_gotodestinationsy:
Greetings, Commander.

It appears you are embarking on your journey beyond the Pilots' Federation District. Before you leave, there are a few things we should make you aware of:
- Docking outside of the starting area will automatically revoke your access to the Pilots' Federation District.
- The Pilot's Handbook and Training Simulations are always available on the Home tab on the Internal interface panel.

We hope that you've enjoyed your time with us and we look forward to seeing your progress.
mission_startzone_exit_missioncomplete: Time to show the galaxy what you're capable of, Commander. We'll be keeping an eye on your progress going forward. Make us proud.
mission_startzone_exit_missioncompletein:
Congratulations, Commander.

We would like to take the opportunity to wish you the best of luck in your coming adventures. Remember that all cockpits have access to the Pilot's Handbook and Pilots' Federation Training Simulations. These can be used to refresh your knowledge of previous lessons, learn more about a new skill or source general information about the galaxy. You can find these on the Home tab on the Internal interface panel.

Safe travels, Commander $#CommanderName;.
mission_startzone_exit_spawn: We think you're ready to begin your true journey, Commander. The galaxy awaits.

You're now in $#DestinationStationSystemNameSystem:style:name=keyword;. A system-wide conflict between two rival factions is currently simulated here. This is an opportune time to experience system conflict as part of a training exercise, within the relative safety of Pilots' Federation Space.

mission_stealgoods: We'd like you to steal $#CommodityQuantity:style:name=keyword; $#CommodityName:style:name=keyword; carried by $#pilotname1:style:name=keyword;.
mission_supplylineassassins_completed_00: That looks like all of them for now. Thank you, Commander. Get those deliveries here as soon as you can.
We think that's the last of them. Time to bring the goods home, Commander.
The enemy will think twice before trying that again. Time to bring that cargo to us, Commander.
That should be the last enemy down, Commander. Hope you're got enough juice to get those supplies here in time.
Doesn't look like anyone else fancies they luck against you, Commander. Bring the supplies to us and we'll call it a job well done.
mission_supplylineassassins_progress_001: Excellent job. Keep an eye out though, there are more of them.
mission_supplylineassassins_progress_002: Good work, Commander. Be careful - there are more of them heading for your position.
mission_supplylineassassins_progress_003: Great flying. Stay focused: more enemies are inbound.
mission_supplylineassassins_progress_004: Excellent work. Don't drop off just yet. More enemies have your position.
mission_supplylineassassins_progress_005: Nice stickwork. There's more enemies heading your way, so keep it up.
mission_supplylineassassins_start_001:
I've just gotten word that someone's taking advantage of the Thargoid situation by sending hitmen out to stop anyone getting supplies to us. Selfish, but smart.

If you're good, you can probably dodge them - but should you happen to take any of them out I'll find some extra credits for you. Lives depend on having this supply line secured.
mission_supplylineassassins_start_002:
Heads up: One of our rivals thinks the Thargoid threat in our system is a good opportunity to weaken us further. They’re sending goons to intercept deliveries we’ve contracted. 

You can maybe outrun them, but if you happen to eliminate them instead I’ll bump up your compensation. We need those supplies, Commander.
mission_supplylineassassins_start_003: We’ve caught wind of a rival sending pilots to intercept our shipment. Seems a Thargoid invasion is just leverage to these snakes. If you avoid them and complete the delivery I’ll appreciate it, but if you can teach these assassins a permanent lesson I’ll increase your payment.
mission_supplylineassassins_start_004:
Update for you, Commander: there’s likely an assassin on your tail. Someone’s decided to undermine our resistance against the Thargoids in the hopes they’ll eliminate a rival faction for them. 

These dirtbags have no morals, so if you can blow them away I’ll make sure you get a little extra in your payment. Otherwise just outrun them if you can. We need that cargo!
mission_supplylineassassins_start_005:
Keep an eye on your scanners – we think one of our rivals is looking to prevent our shipments from reaching us. Thargoids invasion or not, some people just want to see the local competition burn.   

If someone tries to stop you, we’ll pay extra if you destroy them. It’s important to send a message, after all. But the priority is getting that cargo to us, Commander.
mission_systemsecurity_interdiction_01: This is system security. Power down immediately.
mission_systemsecurity_interdiction_02: I'm engaging the target now. Stand by.
mission_systemsecurity_interdiction_03: You've been identified and sentenced for your recent crimes.
mission_systemsecurity_interdiction_04: Your criminal act has not gone unnoticed, Commander.
mission_systemsecurity_interdiction_05: Submit, Commander! Don't make this harder than it needs to be.
mission_systemsecurity_postinterdiction_: I guess you thought you could break the law without anyone noticing.
You brought this on yourself. I hope the credits were worth risking your life for.
You'll never commit a crime in my system again.
Illegal contracts in my jurisdiction are not tolerated.
There's no second chances for crooks like you.

mission_tg_escapepodevac_spawn: We managed to recover some escape pods before the Thargoids could grab them. The occupants need your help getting out of the system, Commander.
mission_tg_escapepodrescue_spawn: We have numerous injured civilians in escape pods waiting for ride to a nearby infirmary. I hope you can get them past the Thargoid fleet.
mission_tg_onfoot_reboot_spawn: The sooner we get local settlements back online the better. Our infrastructure needs to be re-established if we’re going to hold the system.
mission_tg_passengerevac_spawn: There are queues of refugees waiting for evacuation to a safe location. Can you help get these people to safety before more Thargoids arrive?
mission_tg_passengerrescue_spawn: This starport’s inhabitants need to be transported to safety, Commander. It’s important to get them out of here as quickly as possible. The Thargoids aren’t letting up.

It appears you have uncovered all the data, Commander.

As a demonstration of my gratitude, I've added a completion bonus to your reward.

The logs you have uncovered will be invaluable to my ongoing research. The galaxy owes you a great debt, Commander. Safe journey home.

mission_thedead_002_failtitle: Decrypting the Guardian Logs: Codex Scan Failed
mission_thedead_002_fulldescription:
Assist Ram Tah in decoding data at Guardian Structures.

Use artefacts and relics to interact with active obelisks, all of which are found at the structure sites.

You must use an SRV to investigate the structures.
mission_thedead_002_fulldescription_inbo:
Commander,

I have an opportunity you'd be foolish to turn down.

New Guardian sites have been discovered. The codices at these locations could reveal a great deal more about the Guardians' society. 

I have developed a way to decrypt the data from these Guardian sites and will relay the relevant information back to you as soon as I have it.

Although I cannot specify the various combinations of objects and data types required, my decryption software should help decipher the ancient data. The key is using the ancient objects with active obelisks to unlock the data.

I've taken the liberty of uploading my decryption key to your ship's systems. Unfortunately, the ancient technology adapts to the cipher after a few weeks, so our task is time critical.

Please explore as many ancient sites as you can find. If you find all the data entries, there will be a bonus in it for you. 

Good luck,
Ram Tah
mission_thedead_002_invaliddata:
I'm afraid there's been an error, Commander. According to a subroutine in the software I uploaded to your ship, this is not a valid combination. I suggest trying different ancient item combinations at this active codex to unlock the data within.

Some appear to require two objects in your hold to decode, while others only require a single object to unlock.
mission_thedead_002_message_001:
Message from Ram Tah:

I'm sorry to interrupt you, Commander, but I installed a subroutine in my code to alert me if anyone finds a working ancient artefact. It appears that the item you just collected will help unlock one of the Guardian codices. You should try to use it so that we can begin to decrypt the relevant log. Find a codex and scan it to see if the data can be decoded.

I await your inevitable success.

Ram Tah
mission_thedead_002_message_002:
Message from Ram Tah:

That's a stellar effort, Commander! You've uncovered some very valuable data. My code will decrypt the data into a readable format for you. I'll relay the relevant information to your database right away. This information could be integral to the ongoing technological development of the human race.
Please continue trying different combinations. Looking at the data, there may be more sites out there with different data to collect.

Until next time.

Ram Tah
mission_thedead_002_message_003:
Message from Ram Tah:

Greetings, Commander! It appears that's all the data there is at this site. I'm sure there are more out there just waiting to be uncovered. We must find more sites. There is so much more to learn about the Guardians.

Good luck.

Ram Tah
mission_thedead_002_message_004:
Message from Ram Tah:

Well done, Commander! You have my eternal thanks. We could not have decrypted these latest codices without your dedication to this critical mission.

If I learn of more Guardian sites in the future, I won't hesitate to contact you.

Ram Tah
mission_thedead_002_missioncomplete:
That's everything I require, Commander. I could not have decrypted these Guardian logs without your diligent service.

You have my eternal thanks.
mission_thedead_bulletincompletemission:
Looks like you've found all the data, Commander, so it's time to head home.

As a reward for your dedication, I've added a completion bonus to your payment.

The galaxy owes you a huge debt. We could not have uncovered the secrets of the Guardians without your hard work.
