mission_thedead_message_002:
Message from Ram Tah:

Congratulations, Commander! You've uncovered some very valuable data. My code should have been able to translate the data into a readable format for you. I'll add this data to our research database. You have brought us one step closer to understanding the purpose of these ruins and the beings that created them.
Please continue trying different combinations. Looking at the data, it seems there may be more sites out there with different data to collect.

I'll be in touch.

Ram Tah
mission_thedead_message_003:
Message from Ram Tah:

Greetings, Commander! It looks like we may have exhausted this site. There must be more out there, as we have only begun to translate all the data recovered from the codices. We must find more sites so that we can learn even more about the ruins.

I'll be in touch.

Ram Tah
mission_thedead_message_004:
Message from Ram Tah:

Thank you, Commander! The galaxy owes you a huge debt. We could not have uncovered the secrets of the Guardians without your hard work and dedication.

It has been a pleasure working with you.

 Let me know if you ever need some engineering assistance.
mission_thedead_missioncomplete:
That's just what we need, Commander $#CommanderName;. Thank you. We could not have uncovered the secrets of the Guardians without your hard work and dedication.

It has been a pleasure working with you.

Let me know if you ever need some engineering assistance.

mission_treasure_type_barnacle_reward_01:
These mysterious objects are recently discovered alien entities nicknamed 'large barnacles' by interstellar explorers. These appear to be common in certain parts of space, although no one is certain why.

Many have researched the barnacles and the materials known as 'meta-alloys' associated with them.

The barnacles and other objects have taken on an almost religious or otherworldly context for some extreme groups, with reports of people worshipping them or seeing them as a message of some higher race of beings. Others see them as the first sign of a possible alien invasion.

For now, they remain a mystery.
mission_treasure_type_crashedship_01:
We know of a crashed vessel with a valuable cargo, although the real money can be earned by scanning the data core there.
You'll need to be quick as the wreck is scheduled for clean-up in the next couple of weeks.
mission_treasure_type_crashedship_02: We have the location of a crashed ship carrying some interesting data. Our source tells us a clean-up crew is on the way, so you only have a few days to collect the data.
mission_treasure_type_crashedship_03:
We've heard about a crash site with a reported treasure trove of cargo canisters. But the real prize is the ship's data core.
Our contact mentioned that a recovery crew is scheduled to be sent out in a couple of weeks. So you have until then to scan the core and pick up the data.
mission_treasure_type_crashedship_04:
We can provide coordinates for a crashed ship with a profitable stash of cargo.
To earn some real money, you should scan any data cores you find there.
mission_treasure_type_crashedship_05:
We know of a crashed ship with an abundance of cargo to be collected.
Make sure to scan the ship's data core, as that'll be the big earner for you.
A clean-up crew is due to arrive in a couple of weeks, so you'd better head over soon.
mission_treasure_type_crashedship_06:
We've intercepted a distress signal. If you can get there before the search-and-rescue team, maybe you can turn a profit from any data or cargo on board.
The team is scheduled to arrive in two weeks' time.
mission_treasure_type_crashedship_reward:
Commander's Log:

Mayday! We're going down, all systems failing. Crew have abandoned ship.
No time to jettison cargo or transmit data to Control. Mayday! I repeat, Mayday!

Transport 15 to Command. We've encountered an anomaly. It's fried our systems and we're going down.
All cargo and data is secure and transponder is in place for the search-and-rescue team. Crew escape pods launched.
What the hell was that! We've been hit from behind...systems disabled...oh gods, it's killed us! I can't pull up...brace, brace, brace...
Mayday! Calling security forces, pirate attack in progress. Mayday!
We've got to report this...they ripped us out of...nothing works...what do they want from us...that noise...help us...

Emergency, systems malfunction! Escape pods inoperative. 
 I warned you that this crate needed to be decommissioned. Our blood is on your hands. Damn you!
This is an emergency distress call! My systems are failing and I've been caught in the gravitational pull of... Where the hell am I?
Mayday. I repeat, Mayday. Warning, hazardous cargo on board! Emergency landing protocols are in place. Mayday. I repeat, Mayday.
This is transport Erianne 12. We're going down. All hands lost. Attack came out of nowhere. We had no time to react.
Emergency broadcast. This is transport 6592. We've been attacked by pirates and we're going down. All hands have evacuated.

Oh my gods... It can't be! These things are a myth...
That noise! What's that...

It's been 26 days since we crashed here. No comms, no rescue. We got the Mayday out, but no response. 
How can they leave us to die out here? You'd think they would at least want their cargo back. 
I guess the bottom line is, we're acceptable losses.

I can't believe we survived the crash just to waste away out here. At least the SRV is operational. 
We've set the transponder so someone should find the wreck, but we can't wait. We're going to try something. 
With a little luck, we'll find a settlement or relay station. We have nothing left but hope.

Commander's Log:

It's been 14 days since the crash. Supplies are running low and with limited medical equipment, we're in pretty bad shape. 
Jenkins is still unconscious…I think it might be best for everyone if he didn't wake up. 
I don't know what I'm saying. Help will come. It must!

Commander's Log: 

This place would be beautiful if it wasn't for the fact that the ship is totalled and I have no way to get off world. 
If I raid the cargo, I should have enough supplies to last a few weeks until the company sends a rescue ship. I'll probably lose my job over this, but it's better than losing my life.

Commander's Log:

The hunger is starting to get to me…I've started seeing things. I know the deep-space explorers like to tell stories, but these light shows are something else.
They almost seem alive.

Crew Log:

I've salvaged what I can from the wreck. It's doesn't look like much survived the crash intact. 
I think I can get the SRV working again, and then I'm going to look for help. If I can boost the SRV's comms then I might be able to get a signal to a passing ship.

Crew Log:

I buried the Captain and the others today. 
I'm no good at this sort of thing, but I said a few words over them. I dunno, maybe it helped. 
My ribs are still busted up pretty bad, it's hard to breathe sometimes. I'm just going to shut my eyes for a while…so tired...

Crew Log:

I know they say space travel is a lonely business, but nothing prepares you for being totally alone like this. No comms, no ships. 
What I wouldn't give to hear another person's voice right now.

Crew Log:

Honey, I'm so sorry. It looks like I'm going to have to break my promise to be back for Gracie's birthday. I don't know if anyone will find this, but I needed to say it. 
I'm sorry. I love you.
mission_treasure_type_derelict_01: We've detected some kind of old ship, not sure of the date it went down. Without a scan, we don't even have a hull ident. That's where you come in.
mission_treasure_type_derelict_02: This crashed ship is old. The wreck was spotted by a bunch of tourists. One said it was a haunted ghost ship. Nothing to worry about, I'm sure. We'd go and scan it ourselves, but we're…ah…busy right now.
mission_treasure_type_derelict_03: No idea what a ship was doing out there. It's been abandoned for years, by the look of the superficial scan we have right now. We need a more detailed overview. We'll pay for the data.
mission_treasure_type_derelict_04: This ship went missing years ago, struck an asteroid or something by the look of it. It's only just been found by automated probes. But they couldn't tell us what we need to know, so we want you to perform a proper scan.
mission_treasure_type_derelict_05: A lot of ships seem to go down in that region. This one was lost a few years back. We need the data for our records, if you can scan it for us. And…watch your six out there, Commander.
mission_treasure_type_derelict_reward_01:
Comms Record:

I don't know what you expect to find out here.
This wreck's been here forever and I've never heard of any secret treasure being hidden inside.
Someone's messing with you.
mission_treasure_type_derelict_reward_02:
***Internal sensor array activated***

Security systems coming online.

Hey look, something's happening! I told you this thing still had power. Maybe we could fix it up and have a second ship. Let me just see if I can override the security measures.

***Security breach detected. Removing threat.***

Wait a sec, what's that? Oh hell, shut it off! Shut it off!
mission_treasure_type_derelict_reward_03:
Comms Record:

I thought you said this ship was a derelict?

Someone's been here, and recently. Look, there are boot prints in the dust and this console has been pulled apart.

Let's get out of here.
mission_treasure_type_derelict_reward_04:
Comms Record:

I don't care what those bureaucrats say, this is my home. I've lived here for 35 years and no clean-up crew is going to take it away from me.
mission_treasure_type_derelict_reward_05:
Commander's Log: March 13th 3301.

It's my birthday. I had forgotten all about that with the crash and everything that's happened since.

Somehow it seems important to remember. Just because it proves I'm still a human being.
mission_treasure_type_derelict_reward_06:
Commander's Log: August 10th 3300

I was right, no one's coming. No one even knows we're out here.

Collins, Worthington, Gouldstone…all gone.

If those smugglers hadn't turned up when they did, I would have been out of food all together.
mission_treasure_type_derelict_reward_07:
Commander's Log: July 20th 3301

I guess I'm stuck here for the foreseeable future.
I've deleted the logs from the past two weeks. I couldn't stand the negativity I was spewing out.

I've got to own this or it will kill me.
Time I got on with life.
First order of business, what to call my new home. I think...Planet Dave. Yeah, I like the sound of that.
mission_treasure_type_derelict_reward_08:
Commander's Log: November 9th 3300

I saw the explosions in orbit – some factions fighting over this lump of useless rock as if it had some kind of significance in the grand scheme of things.

I'll head out tomorrow and see if anything useful crashed nearby. Not sure how much longer I can hold out using the ship as a shelter.
mission_treasure_type_derelict_reward_09:
Commander's Logs: May 26th 3302

What I wouldn't give for an engineer right now.
A planet's worth of resources and no way to get off this rock.
At least this derelict offers some shelter.
mission_treasure_type_derelict_reward_10:
Commander's Log: December 16th 3301

 We're done for. They're coming.
mission_treasure_type_explorercrash_01: Looks like that explorer ship didn't get very far and we want to know why. If you scan the site for us, we'll see you're rewarded.
mission_treasure_type_explorercrash_02: My sister went exploring and never came back. I'm trying to figure out what happened to her. If you can you scan this site and bring the data back, I'll pay.
mission_treasure_type_explorercrash_03: Something is odd about this one. Who goes exploring in a ship with that kind of setup? Scan the wreckage and bring the data back, and we'll reward your effort.
mission_treasure_type_explorercrash_04: That explorer ship hit the surface pretty hard, but it still looks a bit too neat and tidy. We're checking into a false insurance claim. Recce this crash site for us, and we'll compensate you for your time.
mission_treasure_type_explorercrash_05: We'd appreciate it if you could scan the wreckage of this exploration expedition and bring the data back. What we're looking for is classified.
mission_treasure_type_explorercrash_rewa:
Commander's Log:

Emergency! This is exploration team NANJ-XIIMC. Systems shutting down. Planetary impact imminent.
Mayday! This is exploration vessel JPR-II. We have hit an anomaly, it's caused our FSD to overload. All instrumentation failed. We have no idea where we are. Mayday. I repeat, Mayday.

Commander's Log:

I'm storing this data in the secured drive. It's too important to lose.
We've had reports of attacks against explorer vessels recently. 
It's just paranoia, but I'd rather be safe than sorry.

Crew Log:

I can't wait to get this information back to the lab. Universal Cartographics can have the basic data, but we've found so much more than just new stars and planets.

Wait... What...what's that noise…

Under attack from unknown hostile force. All attempts to communicate have failed.
We're going down. Help us!

Crew Log:

The Captain seems jittery coming back to inhabited systems. He says he just likes the peace and quiet of deep space. But I know he's worried about us having a target on our backs with all this data on board.
Why pirates would attack exploration vessels is beyond me. I mean, it's not like they can collect the data if they shoot us down.
This is exploration team NANJ-XIIMC. Systems shutting down. Planetary impact imminent. All six crew ejected. Transponders in place, so hopefully someone will pick us up.

Crew Log:

I knew when I signed up for this expedition that there was a risk we wouldn't make it back.
But now that it's happened, I can't stop thinking about the crash.
I thought I was lucky to survive, but Tanaka was the lucky one. At least she didn't have to watch as we all keel over one by one down here.

Crew log:

I keep thinking of my mother's last words before I left.
"Be careful. It's dangerous and no one knows what's out there."
How right she was.

Oh well, nothing to do now but sit back, enjoy the view and hope for a rescue before my air runs out.
And it is a really nice view.

Crew log:

We've seen so much out here. Some of it beautiful, some terrifying.
I know this is the end, but I wouldn't have changed it for the world.
If anyone finds this, please use the data we've collected for a good cause. I'd hate to think we gave our lives for nothing.

Crew log:

I can't believe I survived that crash. I must have a guardian angel looking over me or something.
Now I just need to work out a way off this rock and back to civilisation.
If I can get the comms and GalNet back online, maybe I can call for help. 

Right, stop talking to yourself and let's get to it.

Crew log:

I don't know what happened, I must have blacked out.
The last thing I remember was jumping out of...what was the name of the system?
I remember a calm voice. Or maybe it was a song. Maybe I'm just going crazy.
The rescue beacon is working, so hopefully a ship will pick me up in a few days.

Crew log:

I can still hear Mike telling me not to go. That it would end our marriage. That I'd be throwing my life away.
I made my choice and I can live with that. I can.
But I'd give anything to see a friendly face right now.

Crew log:

Six months with no contact with another human being and then boom! 
The first populated system we jump into, we get attacked by some scumbag with an itchy trigger finger.
The ship's a total write-off, but if we're lucky, the exploration data is still cached in its data core. At least no one was killed this time.

Crew log:

I can see the insurance report now: 'No payout due to unsanctioned ship modifications.' How do they expect us to explore distant systems without modifying the ships?
At least the data is intact. Once we get to a starport, I should be able to sell it and get a new ship.

Commander's Log:

I don't know how I got away. One minute I'm scanning the planet and the next, this thing comes out of nowhere.
I barely managed to jump before it had time to get a bead on me. But I'm safe now.

\Wait...what? That can't be... How can it be in front of me in a frame shift jump?
Oh gods, no!

Commander's Log:

Come on baby, this can't be happening. We've been through too much, seen too much. Don't fall apart on me now, we're almost there.
Once we get home, how about we get you a nice service and maybe upgrade a few systems? Come on sweetheart, what do you say?

***Systems failing. Abandon ship. Abandon ship.***

Commander's Log:

Well, I guess I have to look on the bright side. I survived a crash that would have killed most people. I still have a working SRV and enough supplies to last a few weeks.

The ship's not going anywhere and the data is secure, so I may as well explore my new home.

Commander's Log:

I think this expedition is cursed. It's only day five and we've had every kind of problem you can imagine.
If I didn't know better, I'd say someone is trying to sabotage the expedition. Which makes me think.

What's out there that they don't want us to find?

Commander's Log: 

Sagittarius A*, here we come! I can't wait to see what's out there. This is so exciting. This is the best thing that's ever happened to me.
mission_treasure_type_hvtsettlement_01: Our operatives have found some high-value data at a settlement belonging to our competitor. We would appreciate your help scanning it so we can keep ahead of them.
mission_treasure_type_hvtsettlement_02: We have identified the location of some very lucrative data. If you can recover it before anyone else, there will be a handsome reward in it for you.
mission_treasure_type_hvtsettlement_03:
One of our associates has intercepted part of a data packet. We want the rest of it.
If you can get there before anyone can secure the datapoint, maybe you can turn a profit from any information recovered.
mission_treasure_type_hvtsettlement_04: A security systems failure has left a lot of very lucrative data lying around. We need you to recover it for us. You can keep whatever else you find at the site.
mission_treasure_type_hvtsettlement_05: This needs to be on the down-low, Commander. We've got a lead on some high-value data. If you can recover it, maybe we can put it to good use.
mission_treasure_type_hvtsettlement_rewa: Corporate Data Log: Files attached as per your requirements. You were right, he was visiting illegal clubs almost three times a week. Someone in his position should really have known better. Check out the holo-data – I promise you it's juicy stuff!

Corporate Data Log: The chairman of the board has been eliminated. Your way is now clear to take up her position. Don't worry, you won't have any trouble getting support from other board members. I've applied some gentle persuasion so you'll have the majority vote. Deposit the payment as per my instructions, and remember - it would be foolish of you to try and double-cross me.

Corporate Data Log: We've had a breakthrough. The nano-tech they were using was corrupted and now we have the proof. Three thousand people died as a result of those experiments, and all the evidence to back up the claim is attached. Be careful - the corporation will kill to keep this under wraps. Get it out there as quickly as you can, and make sure you do it anonymously or we're both dead.

Corporate Data Log: They're coming for me, I don't have long. All hard copies of the money-laundering files are in a briefcase marked 'Tiffany's'. I've left it at the main hotel reception of the Worldcraft Theme Park on New California. I've instructed the concierge to give it to a Miss Golightly. You know what to do with it. And good luck.

Corporate Data Log: I've left him sleeping like a baby. The sedative should wear off in about an hour and he won't have a clue what just happened. I'm posting the holovid to you now, you can watch it if you like but I wouldn't if I were you. Anyway - happy blackmailing!

Corporate Data Log: It's true - all of it was true. They haven't been manufacturing agricultural parts at all. They're making people! Clones! And then selling them to the military. I'm sending you all the details on an encrypted channel but be careful with this, it goes all the way to the top. Once you've gone down the rabbit hole, there's no coming back.

Corporate Data Log: I've got the evidence and yes, there was a massive cover-up. Those miners didn't die due to an equipment malfunction. They were searching for Tantalum but got a lot more than they bargained for - some kind of ancient tech with built-in auto-defences. The corporation has since circumvented the defences and moved the tech to another location. I'm sending details now. Do what you can...and stay safe.

Corporate Data Log: The office party was a blast, and yes - the security-cam footage is worth a fortune. So what do you want to see first? Who's having an affair, who's the Onionhead fiend, or who decided to break into the chief executive's office and decrypt his private files?

Corporate Data Log: I managed to tap into her private correspondence and it looks like you were right. She's been selling corporate secrets to a rival organisation. Sirius Corp will have a field day with this...or you could just take this straight to her and see what it's worth.

Corporate Data Log: This could bring Rockforth down. That liner wasn't hit by a stray asteroid, it had a faulty supercapacitor. Blew the whole ship to smithereens. This is the cover-up of the century and all the evidence is right here. All I have to do is get it to the right people. Heading out now - wish me luck!

Corporate Data Log: Seriously, I've got the scoop of the century. Remember in 3252 when Duke Mastopolos was killed in an accident? You know the one - a hover-ballerina fell on him. Anyway, that's not important. What matters is it was no accident. It was his wife, Gabriella Mastopolos, who caused the whole thing. This is massive. A scandal like this could bring the whole company down. Hang on...there's someone at the door...

Corporate Data Log: We've finally got them. Yes, the Achilles Corporation. I know we haven't been able to make anything stick before, but this time I have hard evidence of wrongdoing. All I have to do is get this file to the authorities. Let's just hope they haven't intercepted my comms link. Who knows what they'd do to stop this getting out.

Corporate Data Log: I don't have time to tell you the details...they're nearly here. All you need to know is that it wasn't the separatists who blew up that manufacturing plant - it was the corporation itself. All three CEOs made a killing on insurance claims. Look, everything you need to know is in the data-scan I just sent. I just hope I've got enough time to get out of here before they find me...

Corporate Data Log:That's them - the Greenventure Group. I know they have a reputation for being environmentally friendly but they ain't. Three of the systems they terraformed last year had rare flora and fauna that they just wiped out to make way for colonisation. I have all the evidence I need. This is the big one - this is gonna make me rich...

Corporate Data Log: I know I shouldn't have looked but I did. Argent Incorporated were paying me a lot of money for my discretion but I just couldn't stop myself opening up that crate. Anyway, it wasn't high-end art I was transporting - unless high-end art is made by aliens nowadays! Whatever it is, it's not human and it sure don't look legal. Not sure what I'm gonna do with it yet, but I'm definitely not delivering it for the measly pittance they were originally paying me...

Corporate Data Log: I've no idea who they have making all those public appearances but it is NOT the CEO. And I know this for a fact because I saw his body in the morgue! They must have done some extensive surgery on a stand-in, or got a lookalike or a clone or something. I'm telling you, the guy is as dead as disco!

Corporate Data Log: The vice president of the corporation with two anti-grav dancers and a synthetic unicorn? I just don't believe it. Let me take a look at the holo-vid... Jumping jehoshaphat, my eyes!

Corporate Data Log: Rodriguez has become a liability. I don't care if his uncle is the CEO, he needs to be eliminated. I know it seems harsh but that's life in the big city, I'm afraid. And no - I don't want it to look like an accident. We need to send a message.

Corporate Data Log: It's all the evidence we need that we're not alone in the galaxy. The corporation has been hiding it all this time. For years their deep-space exploration vessels have been picking up anomalous comms and heat signatures that definitely aren't human. I'm going to blow the lid off this whole thing. If my Mk II can make it to the next station, the whole galaxy will know the truth. Just a second...what's that in the distance? Looks like a ship. But I've never seen anything like it bef...

Corporate Data Log: Yes, that exclusive arms deal might not be quite as exclusive as the board would like. Looks like the VP has been playing both sides, delivering munitions to the Feds and the Imps. This is not going to go down well at the next AGM...

Corporate Data Log: I showed him the proof and he just laughed at me. Laughed! He said it didn't matter how much dirt I had on him, he was still the top dog, and there wasn't a damn thing I could do to topple him from the throne. Now I'm just sitting here waiting. I know he's gonna make me pay for what I've done, for even attempting to threaten his position. It's coming soon, I can feel it...

Corporate Data Log: I've got the files aboard the ship. If I try to broadcast what I've got, they'll find me for sure. They have people everywhere - damn corporate agents. My only hope is to keep moving, hopping from system to system, and hope they can't track me. But I'm getting tired. If I could just get some rest, maybe I could think straight, find a way out of this. All I need is to close my eyes, just for a little...

Corporate Data Log: I'm heading to the meeting now. I've already told the CEO that I knew what she was up to. Embezzlement's a dirty word, so we avoided it in our conversation. Anyway, she almost seemed pleased that I'd found out her secret. Said it was good work and she admired my talent for snooping. I'm meeting her for lunch, we're going to talk about my future. I thought it was a bit weird to meet at her mansion, but what could possibly go wrong?

Corporate Data Log: They said their new product was safe as houses, but I've spent the past year reverse-engineering it. And what did I find? Onionhead! That's what I found! Concentrated Onionhead in an energy drink! No wonder it's so popular. Anyway, I'm presenting my evidence to the authorities. They'll make sure this gets out to the public. Boy, am I going to be famous!
mission_treasure_type_mercenarywreckage_: Hidden in this mercenary wreckage, you should find some scannable data that's worth a lot of credits.
We know of an abandoned mercenary wreckage containing valuable data that can be scanned.
A mercenary ship was shot down a few months back but we've found the crash site. There's credits to be made if you can scan it for us.
Some mercenaries ran a Federal blockade and came off the worse for wear. We'd like you to scan the site. We'll pay well.
Looks like the mercenaries had to dump and run in a hurry. The debris is still out there, so scan it for us and we'll pay you well.

Mayday! This is privateer vessel KB-61020. I'm going down.
The lead was a trap, they were waiting for me. Too many to fight off. 
I don't suppose I'll make it out of this.

The bounty data is secure in the ship's data core. It should survive the crash. If found, pass it on to my family as compensation.

Comms Record:

Sorry boss, but I don't see where the profit is in this job.
Sure I feel bad for those people, but if there's no reward, why are we doing this?
I mean, mercenaries are meant to get paid.

Comms Record:

Control, this is BH XV-386. Have sustained heavy damage and unable to return to base. Job has been completed and the information is secure in the ship's data core.
Going to attempt a landing on planetoid near my current location. 386 out.

Comms Record:

I told you this was a stupid idea and now you've killed us all.
I was an honest trader before I hooked up with you.
If I survive this, I'm going to kill you!

Comms Record:

Forget it! That hunk of junk isn't going anywhere.

We've still got the Cobra, so lets just load up what we can and get out of here before those bounty hunters come back and finish the job!

Comms Record:

So this is the cop who thought he could sabotage my ship?
 Well it looks like you only did half the job, Mr Policeman.

Take this trash for a walk outside.
Mayday! To any passing ships. This is independent merchant vessel JPS-4962. We've crash-landed on a planet and all nav systems are down. Position unknown. Is there anyone out there? Mayday!

Comms Record:

To hostile pilots. Please hold your fire, we are not a mercenary vessel! We are a merchant ship carrying aid.

You're making a mistake, I don't care what your intel says. 
I repeat, we are a merchant vessel on a humanitarian mission carrying aid. Please hold your fire!

Comms Record:

Great, now what do we do? The ship's totalled and someone disabled the transponder so no one can track our position.
We're doomed! We're going to die down here.
What are we going to do!

Commander's Log:

I guess this is the downside to being off the beaten path. I know that in my line of work it's sometimes necessary, but when something like this happens, it really sucks.

Commander's Log:

Okay, so let's see. I've got three days of food and water, an emergency shelter and several tons of useless scrap metal.
I can probably stretch the food and water to six days if I really try.
I just have to hope someone heard my distress signal and picks me up within a week.

Here's to hope.

Commander's Log:

I think I'm finally losing it…or maybe it's just all the explosions and laser fire from the crash burnt into my eyes…but I could swear those lights were real.

I don't think they're hostile, but there does seem to be some kind of intelligence to their movements.

Comms Record:

This is the twentieth wreckage we've searched. Are you going to say what we're looking for or not?
I keep telling you, there is nothing out here worth finding.
It's not like these ships have a data core worth a fortune hidden inside.

Comms Record:

I'm going to kill him, that lying scumbag.
I paid a fortune for this encryption key and the damn thing doesn't work.

I'm going to kill him!

Commander's Log:

I don't know how I survived. I can't remember the actual crash, just my systems failing and the planet getting closer in the cockpit window. Then nothing until I woke up here.

Looking at the wreck, I should be dead, but somehow I'm here without a scratch.
mission_treasure_type_militarycache_01: Some kind of military equipment store has turned up on our radar. Might just be junk, but it's worth taking a look. We'd like you to run a scan. We'll pay for your time and trouble.
mission_treasure_type_militarycache_02: There was some kind of firefight recently. All sorts of stuff is lying about as a result. Might be hazardous, so if you can run a scan and let us know what you find, you'll be compensated.
mission_treasure_type_militarycache_03: Top brass have been playing it down, but we think some kind of military equipment has been stashed out there. Run a recce for us and we'll pay handsomely. We never had this conversation, of course.
mission_treasure_type_militarycache_04: Whatever's in that cache is military grade. Not sure if they're hoping it'll be buried and forgotten, or something else is going on. I need a scan before we can mount an expedition.
mission_treasure_type_militarycache_05: That cache definitely contains something. Might be military-grade weapons, might be Granny Hudson's recipe for trumble soup. Either way, we need a scan of this site.
mission_treasure_type_militarycache_rewa:
Quartermaster's Log:

All items accounted for and stored according to executive order 988. Skimmers and security measures in place. 
Moving on to next location.

Sit Rep:

The site's a mess. Wreckage all over the place.
All useful parts from the ships have been salvaged.
 Schedule site for cleanup.

Comms Record:

Our intel is saying the site has been compromised. Time to move the item to a new location.

As far as anyone else knows, this is just a shipwreck.
Clean the site according to executive order 4762.

Command out.

Sit Rep:

Site MES-81 cleared. The wreckage will cover the cache so that no one finds it. Signal the quartermaster, site is ready for shipment.

Comms Record:

Why have the brass got us caching this stuff out here? Are they expecting something to happen?
They'd tell us, right? I mean, if we were going to war. They'd tell us.

Comms Record:

We'll be glad we had these caches when it all hits the fan.
It might seem pointless now, but when you're in a firefight, knowing there is a place nearby to reload and repair is a big weight off.

Sit Rep:

Site SJK-324 fully operational.

Patrol waypoints are in place.
Everything is set for the offensive.

Comms Record:

We've hit the mother lode. This is military-grade stuff.
Load up as much as you can. This will make us a load of hard credits.

Lets be quick though, I don't want the military finding us here stealing their equipment.

Sit Rep:

Hansel to Command.

The breadcrumbs have been laid, ready for the wicked witch.

 Moving to rendezvous with Gretel in sector 16.

Sit Rep:

Units 2, 3 and 6 are green.
Unit 7 is compromised, suspected pirate activity.
Units 8 and 9 are green.
Unit 10 is a total loss due to seismic disturbance at that location.

Operational status is amber.
mission_treasure_type_minersite_01: We're curious about what this mining operation is trying to dig up. We'd like you to scan the site and bring the data back. We'll make it worth your while.
mission_treasure_type_minersite_02: Those miners were after some kind of mineral deposit, but something has gone wrong. Scan the site and bring the data back, and we'll reimburse you.
mission_treasure_type_minersite_03: What those miners are doing might be illegal. We need you to scan the site for us and bring back the data. We'll compensate you, of course.
mission_treasure_type_minersite_04: We're very interested to know if those miners have found something valuable. Scan the site then hightail it back here with the data, and we'll cut you in.
mission_treasure_type_minersite_05: They've got some kind of rig drilling down there. Looks like it might be fancy new tech. We need a scan of the site. Credits are waiting if you can get the data back pronto.
mission_treasure_type_minersite_reward_0:
Duty Report:

Unit 58 repaired, all auto-miners fully operational.
Looks like the survey data was spot on, I'm seeing a good yield from this site. Recommend moving another 20 units down here from site IMK-43.

Duty Report:

That's five units in as many weeks. We need to get some replacement drilling equipment down here or this operation will be a bust. 
We can't afford to have another job go bad on us, we'll lose our franchise rights.

Duty Report:

Maintenance programme carried out – all units working at optimum levels. 
Request permission to check out a nearby meteor strike. Could be a prospective source of rare deposits.

Duty Report:

Looks like Unit 8 chewed through 100 metres last night, which is not part of the logs. 
Either we've got a malfunction or someone is using our equipment illegally.

Duty Report:

It seems the raiders haven't taken the hint. Skimmer tracking shows there was another attempted raid last night. 
Doesn't seem to be too much damage, but Unit 45 will need an overhaul and ammo reload.

Comms Record:

Mitchell, looks like we hit the jackpot here. Two days of digging and we're already over the estimates the survey showed. 
Just make sure no one at the office notices our little side-project, and we'll be set for life in a matter of weeks.

Automated Report:

Unit 6 at 75%, Unit 7 at 90%, Unit 8 at 93%. Signal for commodities extraction sent. 
All units standing by.

Automated Message:
\Warning! Unauthorised access. Mining units compromised.
Alerting local security forces.

Comms Record:

Davies, this is going to work. The subroutine is in place on all mining units in sector 12. 
As these things chew up minerals, we scan them and get a voucher for the market value. It's untraceable.
mission_treasure_type_minersite_reward_1:
Comms Record:

Okay, okay, I'm on it. I'm just reworking the generator now. Unit 39 is fried and will need to be replaced.
I'll be back at base in a few hours.

Comms Record: 

I don't know why I should be out here doing all the work, when it's those jerks at Command that caused the problem. 
Tell them to stop cutting corners if they want this project to run smoothly.

Comms Record: 

This whole system is a horrific hack job.
Whoever worked out the locations of these things really didn't think about us poor wretches having to drive out to fix them every three days.

Comms Record: 

Patricks, if this is another one of your pranks, I'm going to kill you. I double-checked all units and found zip. 
I don't care what your console is telling you, there is nothing wrong with the mining platforms here.

Embedded Message Detected: 

This is a message for the pilot currently raiding our mining platforms. 
Smile, scumbag! Your SRV carrier signal has been logged and you've just been posted as a target on every bounty hunter message board in the region.

Embedded Message Detected: 

Run and hide, thief. We are not the kind of operation you can steal from. 
I don't care who you are. When we find you, you're dead.

Automated Message:

 Subroutine 653 initiated. 
SRV carrier signal recorded. Local security networks notified of illegal activity. 
Have a nice day.

Incoming Comms: 

Nelson, is that you? 
It's been two days since your transponder stopped transmitting. What's going on out there?

Embedded Message Detected: 

Hey buddy, spend that data voucher you've just picked up quickly. 
This theft has not gone un-noticed and you can bet we'll be coming for you.

Automated Message: 

Commodity voucher collection recorded. Voucher reference: AMK-498. 
Updating company database. 
Have a nice day.
mission_treasure_type_minersite_reward_2:
Automated Message: 

Commodity voucher accessed. Commodity pickup initiated. Program ends. 
Have a nice day.
mission_treasure_type_piratestash_01:
We've received reports of a pirate stash, but the real prize is a data core to be scanned there.
Our informant says the pirates are due to move on in a couple of weeks, so time is limited on this.
mission_treasure_type_piratestash_02:
There's a hidden pirate stash that we can direct you to. The treasure is good, but the data core you can scan will make the trip worthwhile.
Our guy on the inside says the pirates are getting ready to move on, so there is a limited window of opportunity here.
mission_treasure_type_piratestash_03:
A pirate stash will usually have some cargo to plunder, but this one will earn you credits for scanning the data core hidden with it.
Word is that the pirates are due to move soon, so if you want to get the data, you'd better hurry.
mission_treasure_type_piratestash_04:
If you can find this pirate stash, you could score big by scanning a data core they stole recently.
Our source says the pirates will be moving their stash in a couple of weeks, so you only have until then.
mission_treasure_type_piratestash_05:
We know of a pirate stash with an abundance of cargo to be collected. The scannable data core is the real prize though.
 Don't waste time, as our sources tell us that the pirates are getting ready to move out.
mission_treasure_type_piratestash_reward:
Comms Record: 

I hope you don't expect me to draw an X on a map for you! The only person getting the transponder code is me.

Comms Record: 

I've hidden the coordinates in the local news network servers. As long as the carrier signal isn't compromised in some way, it's undetectable and untraceable, so we're in the clear.

Comms Record: 
\I'm not handing you a treasure map. Once I get paid, I'll tell you where we hid the goods.

Comms Record: 

I swear if you draw an X on the ground, I'll shoot you myself. Lets just stash this and head to the safe house.
Okay, that's the valuables stashed. Now let's contact the buyer and get paid.

***Secure channel established***

 This is Lieutenant Stott. I'm in. The gang believed my backstory. Once I have their confidence, I should be able to find out who's funding these clowns.

Comms Record: 

I'll execute any one of you that crosses me. Now get this cargo stashed.

Comms Record: 

Ditch the data core, it's the cargo we're after. We can't fence data, it's worthless.

Comms Record: 

You shouldn't have signed up to this if you didn't want to get your hands dirty. If we hadn't vented that ship, its crew would have called the police and we'd be history.

Comms Record: 

If I hadn't shot him, we'd be knee-deep in police by now. Do you want us to get caught?

Comms Record: 

Dump the data, we can't split that three ways... Oh yeah, of course I mean four ways.

Comms Record: 

No one is going to look for this stuff here. We'll come back for it in a couple of weeks once the dust settles, and then it's the good life for us.

Comms Record: 

Time we got paid. Stash the goods and I'll contact the buyer.
 And this time make sure it's hidden. I don't want to come back to find some do-gooder handed it in to the cops.

Comms Record: 

Looks like the buyer's been compromised, permanently. I guess this cargo is hotter than we thought. Time to lie low for a few weeks. I'll be in touch when this blows over.

Comms Record: 

I don't care what it says on those crates. This is a big pay day for us. Keep your mouths shut and we're in the clear.

Comms Record: 

Stash the cargo and make sure any transponders are disabled. We didn't steal these things just for someone to track them down. 
We'll come back in a few days to collect them once the heat is off.

Comms Record: 

No one is going to look here. We'll come back and pick this up once the police have finished sweeping this system.

Comms Record: 

Right, now this time, someone remember where we left the goods. I don't want to have to search the whole planet.

Comms Record: 

I'm going to contact the buyer. If I come back and find a single item out of place, I'll kill every last one of you.

Comms Record: 

The next person I find stealing from me will take a walk out of the airlock. 
Now get the valuables hidden. And someone dispose of that body.
mission_treasure_type_rebelsupply_01: We've located what we think is a stash of supplies for that local rebellion. We need a scan to make sure. We'll pay for the data.
mission_treasure_type_rebelsupply_02: It looks like some kind of supply operation was operating hereabouts. We're not sure what's there, that's why we need a scan of the site. Come back with the data and we'll see you're rewarded.
mission_treasure_type_rebelsupply_03: We're tidying up after the war. Scan this site and let us know what's there. Help yourself to anything interesting, we just want the data.
mission_treasure_type_rebelsupply_04: This site contains rebel supplies, we think. If we can cut off their support, we can bring the conflict to a close. All we want is a recce of the site, if you can do that for us.
mission_treasure_type_rebelsupply_05: They're trying to destabilise the system. We're trying to close down their supply chain. Grab a scan of this site for us to confirm it's a viable target. We need this data.
mission_treasure_type_rebelsupply_reward:
Comms Record:

Don't ask where we got them from, but there's enough firepower here to turn our rebellion into a full-scale civil war.

Remember, this is all for the cause. I don't want to see anyone trying to make a profit out of these weapons.

Comms Record:

Yes, we can supply your fighters with weapons, ships and whatever you need to stage your little war.

We just need a list of drop locations and payments through our secure channel.
Also, if you get caught with this stuff, we never had this conversation. I don't exist.
 Do we have an understanding?

Comms Record:

I can't let anyone get hold of this information, it's too important to the rebellion.
Why won't it delete the data?

Okay, plan B. I'll bury it so deep that no one will be able to decrypt it.

Commander's Log:

Looks like security has increased in the system.
It seems the word is out about our planned offensive. They're trying to cut off our supply lines.

Well, we won't go quietly.

Comms Record:

It's now or never! We're not going to get another shot at this.
If the security forces get wind of what we're doing out here, we're all dead.

Pick up the goods at sites three and four, and meet me at the rendezvous.

Comms Record:

Do you know what we went through to get you these weapons?
It wasn't an easy task, I'll tell you. And now you want to back out because some politician has listened to your cause and come up with a diplomatic solution.

That's not how we do business.
Someone kill this idiot, and make sure they find the body!

Now, let's start a war.

Comms Record:

I think that's the last shipment. We should be good to go.
When is the operation going ahead? I just worry about someone finding this stuff and reporting it to the authorities.

Comms Record:

And you're sure that they don't suspect anything?
Good, then the operation is a go.

If it all goes well, we'll meet back at the rendezvous point.
Good luck.

Comms Record:

Oh gods, how many of them are there?
I thought you said they would be taken by surprise! This is a massacre!
Tell all remaining ships to retreat.

We're hit, going down! All of you get to the escape pods! I'll try to keep it level while you eject.

Secure channel established

We've found the rebel stronghold.
I suggest a surprise frontal assault.
Let's crush this pitiful rebellion before they have a chance to do any damage.
mission_treasure_type_salvagestore_01: We have a proposition for you. We need this salvage site scanned. We want the data, but you can keep whatever else you find.
mission_treasure_type_salvagestore_02: There's a salvage site not too far from here. We need a scan for our records, but if you want to help yourself to anything lying around, there'll be no questions asked from us.
mission_treasure_type_salvagestore_03: Some kind of abandoned salvage store has been detected. We'll need you to assess it for our inventory, but if a couple of items go missing, it won't be a problem. Just be discreet about it.
mission_treasure_type_salvagestore_04: Various items were stolen from here a couple of months back. It's all gone through the insurance, but we need a scan of the salvage for our records. The stash itself? Well, I'm sure we can just look the other way.
mission_treasure_type_salvagestore_05: This salvage is a nice little stash of cargo by all accounts. I wouldn't mind knowing what is out there. If you can you run a scan and let me know, there's credits to be made.
mission_treasure_type_smugglercache_01: We know of a smuggler's cache with some valuable items, but make sure to scan the data there for the big credits.
mission_treasure_type_smugglercache_02: We've located a smuggler's cache. It should have some valuable goods, but the data you can scan there is the real prize.
mission_treasure_type_smugglercache_03: A smuggler's cache will usually have some valuable cargo to plunder, but this one will earn you credits for the scanned data.
mission_treasure_type_smugglercache_04: If you can locate this smuggler's cache, you should earn a good sum with the scanned data.
mission_treasure_type_smugglercache_05: Try to find this smuggler's cache, and make sure to scan the data for a big earner.
mission_treasure_type_smugglercache_rewa:
Comms Record:

Okay, let's leave the goods here while we scout out security at the delivery point. No one will look in this wreckage.

Comms Record:

Local security forces are clearing this site out. It looks like we've lost our hiding place. 
Time to pack up and leave before they find out what we've been up to.

Comms Record:

Trust me, any smuggler worth his rep will have a cache. Shipping this stuff here is easier than buying it at a market each time our clients want goods brought in.
Now let's stash this lot and get the next load.

Comms Record:

I told you, I don't trust banks or station security. No one is going to look for credit data on a wrecked ship in the middle of nowhere.
That's why it's the safest place in the galaxy.

Comms Record:

Okay, that's all the goods stashed away. Make sure the data core is secure. 
If that fell into the wrong hands, our clients would be exposed. I don't need to tell you, these are not the kind of people we want to upset.

Comms Record:

Looks like it's time to find a new cache site. My contact inside the security forces says they plan to do a clean-up of this site soon.

Pack up what we can carry, we'll come back for the rest once the new site is secured.

Secure channel established:

This is Sergeant Halil, security code AXX-93TU. 

Our intel was correct. The smuggling operation is being launched from here and about a dozen other sites in the surrounding systems.
Send backup. We'll grab the perps and then come back to gather the evidence later.

Comms Records:

Yes, okay, I'm a cop. But listen to me, damn it! If you do this, you won't just be wanted for smuggling and petty theft, it'll be murder.
Do you want to go down for that?

Hold on, please...please wait, I have a family...

Comms Record:

As you can see, our operation is fully secure. We can handle any goods you want smuggled in or out of any location.
Pickups and drops can be arranged at any one of our planetside locations for a very reasonable fee.

We do of course keep certain records about our clients, for insurance purposes. I'm sure you understand.

Comms Record:

We need to clear out of here! My sources tell me that security forces are going to raid this site any day.
Grab what you can and make sure not to leave any evidence.
mission_tw_collect_alert_missioncomplete: You've really helped us out, Commander. Thank you!
mission_tw_collect_alert_spawn: We need to maintain our stocks if we're going to push back the Thargoids. If you bring us a few things it'll help a lot of people.
mission_tw_collect_recovery_missioncompl: Thank you. If you're sticking around for a while there are plenty more contracts available.
mission_tw_collect_recovery_spawn: We need to get this place back up and running following Thargoid assault. Your assistance would be appreciated.
mission_tw_collect_underattack_missionco: This is a big help, Commander. Thank you!
mission_tw_collect_underattack_spawn: We have so many wounded to take care of. Our people desperately need these supplies.
mission_tw_collectwing_alert_missioncomp: Thanks to everyone who contributed. We needed this cargo.
mission_tw_collectwing_alert_name: Emergency Bulk Supply Contract: $#CommodityQuantity; units of $#CommodityName;
mission_tw_collectwing_alert_spawn: We have to ensure our forces have enough supplies to prevent the Thargoids from establishing themselves in this system.
mission_tw_collectwing_repairing_mission: There's plenty more work where that came from. We need to get this port operation as soon as possible.
mission_tw_collectwing_repairing_name: Station Repair Bulk Supply Contract: $#CommodityQuantity; units of $#CommodityName;
mission_tw_collectwing_repairing_spawn: We've got a lot of repairs to carry out, Commander. Can you help us source the materials to get the work done?
mission_tw_collectwing_underattack_missi: We'll put these supplies to good use. Sending payment now.
mission_tw_collectwing_underattack_name: Emergency Bulk Supply Contract: $#CommodityQuantity; Units of $#CommodityName;
mission_tw_collectwing_underattack_spawn: There's a lot of injured people at this port, Commander. We need supplies to take care of them.
mission_tw_delivery_missioncomplete: Can't thank you enough for coming through on the job. Let's hope it makes a difference.
mission_tw_delivery_spawn: We can't turn away from what's happening out there. Can you deliver these supplies to a faction engaging the Thargoids?
mission_tw_massacre_basilisk_plural_miss: Thank you for your efforts, Commander. Those Interceptor variants can be a handful.
mission_tw_massacre_basilisk_plural_spaw: We've got to put these Basilisks down. Get out there and raise some hell.
mission_tw_massacre_basilisk_singular_mi: I hope it didn't put up too much of a fight. Thank you, Commander.
mission_tw_massacre_basilisk_singular_sp: These Basilisks have been causing trouble for us, Commander. Feel like taking one down?
mission_tw_massacre_cyclops_plural_missi: Pretty impressive stick work, Commander. Thank you for your contribution.
mission_tw_massacre_cyclops_plural_spawn: These Interceptors are no joke. Load up on guns and bring them down!
mission_tw_massacre_cyclops_singular_mis: Thank you for your efforts, Commander. You're doing your part.
mission_tw_massacre_cyclops_singular_nam: Hunt and destroy a Cyclops Interceptor
mission_tw_massacre_cyclops_singular_spa: It's them or us. Fit some decent weapons and see if you can take on a Cyclops Interceptor.
mission_tw_massacre_hydra_plural_mission: Incredible work, Commander. That's the kind of flying which could win us this war.
mission_tw_massacre_hydra_plural_spawn: Hydras are the strongest Thargoid Interceptors we've seen. I hope you're up to the challenge.
mission_tw_massacre_hydra_singular_missi: That's a kill to be proud of, Commander. Great job.
mission_tw_massacre_hydra_singular_spawn: Multiple Hydras are terrifying. I hope you're well equipped and have some backup out there.
mission_tw_massacre_medusa_plural_missio: Must have been quite the show! Well done, Commander.
mission_tw_massacre_medusa_plural_spawn: The Medusa variants are really tough. Maybe bring some friends for this hunt?
mission_tw_massacre_medusa_singular_miss: Well done. You must be a solid pilot to handle that menace.
mission_tw_massacre_medusa_singular_spaw: Medusas are not for the faint of heart. I hope you've got what it takes.
mission_tw_massacre_scout_plural_mission: Speedy blighters, aren't they? Thank you for your efforts, Commander.
mission_tw_massacre_scout_plural_spawn: Thargoid Scouts are swarming this system. How about you swipe a few away for us?
mission_tw_massacre_scout_singular_missi: Thank you for your efforts, Commander. One more down.
mission_tw_massacre_scout_singular_name: Hunt and exterminate a Thargoid Scout
mission_tw_massacre_scout_singular_spawn: New to Thargoid hunting? Outfit some decent weapons and try taking one of the smaller ones.

mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_nr_spawn: We need to recover some telemetry from one of our settlements, can you help?
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_001_mi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! With the power back on, we should be able to download the latest telemetry to support our fight against the Thargoids.
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_001_na:
Good to see you, Commander. I sure hope you're here to help.

There is some telemetry stored locally at a settlement which could be important to the anti-xeno defence effort. Settlement personnel didn't have time to transfer the data before Thargoids knocked out the power. I need somebody to travel to that settlement, get the power back on and extract the data while it's still recent and useful. There's a chance of encountering Thargoids in the area, too. Blow them up, avoid them, doesn't matter to me - the data is the aim here.

You'll get a good reward for helping us with this job. And who knows: maybe it'll prove to be as important as we think and help turn the tide of the conflict in that system.
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_002_mi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! With the power back on, we should be able to download the latest telemetry to support our fight against the Thargoids.
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_002_na:
The Thargoid war has always supplied certain opportunities, Commander. Smart factions have discovered ways to make a profit from the conflict. And no, not by trading military supplies. That particular game is absolutely overloaded. The really interesting work lies in stellar faction politics.

You see, one day the war is going to end. When it does - assuming humanity wins and we're all still here - all of the factions currently focused on anti-xeno defence efforts will need to evaluate what's been happening around them. Those who haven't been paying attention will learn that their rivals are waiting to strike. There's an old saying: When the cat's away, the mouse will collect all of the cat's financers, security contracts and skilled personnel. Or something to that effect.

Go to a settlement, switch the power on and recover the requested data.  The faction providing your reward will be appreciative. Try not to get yourself killed.
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_003_mi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! With the power back on, we should be able to download the latest telemetry to support our fight against the Thargoids.
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_003_na:
My client is offering payment for an independent contractor to recover a competitor's data. It seems there are a lot of credits to be made from a new business partnership in the system, and negotiations have left only two candidates. Corporate espionage is as much a part of business as advertising or recruitment, so I expect what I'm saying is nothing you haven't heard before. 

The quirk in this case, at least, is that the data my client has asked for is currently stored on the network of a settlement which has been evacuated due to Thargoid attack. There's an added bonus that getting settlements back online will allow remote access to its telemetry records, helping the local war efforts. Who doesn't want to feel good about themselves while making a few credits?

You'll need to navigate the risk of Thargoids interception, bring the settlement online and secure the data package. But the reward will be worth your time.
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_004_mi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! With the power back on, we should be able to download the latest telemetry to support our fight against the Thargoids.
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_004_na:
Hello, Commander. Looking for work? Of course you are. 

I have a contract from a faction which was recently forced to abandon one of its settlements due to Thargoid assault. The power went down before all sensitive data could be transferred from the local network, so they're hiring a freelancer to get the reactor up and running. I'd like you to recover one particular file of importance, as well - before somebody else does. 

Consider it part of the war effort. After all, keeping factions happy will help them to invest more attention to anti-xeno operations. You'll be paid for you time, of course. and success will allow for further contracts in the future. A glorious mechanism of mutual benefit. Unless we lose the war, in which case everything will come to grinding halt. But let's remain optimistic, shall we?
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_005_mi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! With the power back on, we should be able to download the latest telemetry to support our fight against the Thargoids.
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_005_na:
One of the management team for a surface settlement was working on a highly important project, the results of which are eagerly awaited by several different corporations. As a Thargoid fleet swept in, forcing the settlement's evacuation, the individual sent to recover the data locally never made it to the shuttles. Regrettable, but the fact is that data remains unrecovered. 

There's a general request from the anti-xeno military forces to get settlements back up and running, as the comms infrastructure is important. You're the ideal candidate to support the local war effort while recovering this missing data package, Commander. I expect you're no stranger to working in dangerous locations, and reliability is synonymous with the Pilots' Federation. When networks go down, and remote access terminals are dead, it takes heroes like you to keep the exchange of vital data flowing. 

Payment? Yes, obviously there will be payment. I've simply assumed you had a greater motivation that wealth during these tough times.
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_006_mi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! With the power back on, we should be able to download the latest telemetry to support our fight against the Thargoids.
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_006_na:
Have you heard the news? There's an overall directive to get Thargoid-controlled systems up and running. They say it helps the war effort. People have different ideas about why, but that's a question for the military. All you and I need to worry about is that Thargoids really dislike humans showing up in those areas. 

Which makes the contract I have on offer a hard sell. A friend of mine has left something vital to their continued employment at a surface settlement. When they told me I nearly fell out my chair. It's like forgetting to bring your head to the food stalls. But I owe this person a favour, so I promised to find someone that can recover the forgotten package before their boss finds out.

Think you can handle this while getting the power back online? Sure you can. Find the item when the lights are on, bring it safely back and I'll give you a nice reward.
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_007_mi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! With the power back on, we should be able to download the latest telemetry to support our fight against the Thargoids.
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_007_na:
Millions of innocent people have had their lives irrevocably changed by the Thargoid invasion. Loved ones lost. Homes destroyed. The trauma of attack by monstrous creatures. Myself, and many others like me, are doing what we can to help combat personal who risk so much to keep us safe.  

Many valuable objects were left behind in the rush to evacuate military settlements. Some are irreplaceable personal items. Others are vital to a work project. Often settlements will have research samples that have taken years to produce. Think of the cumulative time spent, the memories if we don't act! 

You probably already know that getting settlements back online helps us push back against Thargoid control. I have a contract for you that will reward you for doing so, and help one individual to move forward with the next step of their journey. It may be dangerous, but I will pay handsomely. Are you interested?
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_008_mi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! With the power back on, we should be able to download the latest telemetry to support our fight against the Thargoids.
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_008_na:
A faction I'm friendly with has learned of a tech project which was nearing completion at a rival corp's settlement. The settlement has fallen behind Thargoid invasion lines, meaning there's an opportunity to take a closer look at what that corp was working on. There must be a sample or a record somewhere which can be recovered, and there's a big reward for doing so. 

Sounds easy, don't it? Well, there's a reason I'm not doing it myself: Thargoids are still hopping around the system, and they're on the hunt for our ships. It's going to take someone with a stiffer spine than I have to get tangled up with alien murder machines.  

But getting power back on at that settlement will help the system defence efforts. So this is about the bigger picture just as much as it is you and I making some scratch. Switch the reactor on, find the items and get back to me for your payment.
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_009_mi: Great work, Commander $#CommanderName;! With the power back on, we should be able to download the latest telemetry to support our fight against the Thargoids.
mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_009_na:
There's a lot of money to be made from restoring power to settlements which the Thargoids have taken control of. At least, there is if you have a side-hustle going. 

Does that sound callous? Don't worry. The refugees have some pretty serious humanitarian efforts looking out for them. Charities are falling over themselves to help out. And getting settlements back online will provide support to our brave AX forces.  

I don't see many of these selfless angels getting their hands dirty behind enemy lines, though. They're not scrabbling through abandoned buildings with Thargoids firing at them. Funny, that. Which is where freelancers like you and I come in. People in a position to pay extra need certain items extracted from those settlements after the reactor's been switched on. If you follow the contract details, I'll give you a sizeable cut of the reward.

mission_tw_onfoot_reboot_occupied_mb_spa: You'll need to enter Thargoid-controlled territory for this mission. It's important, Commander.
mission_tw_passengerevacuation_alert_aba: Okay, I guess. Thanks for getting us out of danger. Drop us off at the next port and we'll find another ride.
Ah, really? Well, at least we're safe. We ARE safe, right? Drop us off at the next suitable location and we'll find another way to move on.
If you've got other matters to attend we understand, but we do need to continue our journey. Please drop us off somewhere safe and we'll find another transport.
Dropping the contract? Well, at least we're out of the Thargoid invasion. Stop by the next port on your journey and we'll find another ship, I suppose.
We appreciate you transporting us away from the Thargoids, but abandoning the contract has left us in a bit of a situation. Let us off at the next port and we'll work it out from there.
mission_tw_passengerevacuation_alert_eje: Thanks but no thanks. We're leaving!
We'll take our chances in the black. Thanks for the escape pods!
Our treatment has been unacceptable! We're out of here.
Just because you saved us doesn't mean we have to take this kind of treatment. We're trying our luck with your escape pods.
We've had enough of this outrageous treatment. Time to get out of here!
mission_tw_passengerevacuation_alert_imp: Hey, how much longer is the journey? There's an annoying child crying its eyes out back here and I need a break.
Is the journey going to take much longer? I've got friends waiting for me at the destination and they'll be worried sick.
If I'd known the journey would be this long, I'd have taken my chances with the Thargoids. Do you get paid by the hour? Hurry up!
I'm SO bored! Can we pick up the pace a little? It feels like I've been in this cabin forever.
If we don't reach our destination soon I'm going to bang my head against an airlock for entertainment. Please hurry up.
mission_tw_passengerevacuation_alert_mis: Thank you so much. Hopefully we can go back home soon. Take care!
mission_tw_passengerevacuation_alert_spa: We've got civilians we need to get out of this system. Can you spare some room on your ship?
mission_tw_passengerevacuation_alert_unh: We've all disembarked. Good luck with whatever else you have on your mind.
That was a rough trip. Thanks for the ride, but maybe next time spare a thought for the people in your hold?
Well we're clear of the Thargoid threat, at least. But your customer service skills could use a little work. Good luck.
We've finally made it. Appreciate the help, but we're glad to be off your ship. Maybe you're happy to see the back of us, too.
Everybody has disembarked, Commander. I do have some complaints about your piloting style, but since you helped us to safety it'd be selfish to share them. Let's just leave things at goodbye.
mission_tw_passengerevacuation_burning_a: Apologies if we've been a burden to you, Commander. But thank you for keeping us safe. Please let us disembark at a nearby port.
Well, at least we're not at the mercy of Thargoids anymore. Set us down at a port and you can do whatever you like next.
I hope you have a better contract lined up with a big payment. That's the only thing I can think of that would excuse abandoning us. Let us out at a port.
I hope the people fighting Thargoids in our home system have more determination than you do. We'll get out at the next port and you can get on with your life.
If you're not going to complete the contract, at least let us out at the nearest port. We still have a journey to make before we can start putting our lives back together.
mission_tw_passengerevacuation_burning_e: Whichever flight school you went to made a mistake letting you pass! We're getting out of here.
Did you forget we're sitting in your hold? We can't stand any more of this behaviour - we're leaving.
We're taking your escape pods and getting out of this ship. Thanks for the save. No thanks for the flying.
We appreciate you offering to help, but this is far too stressful a ride. Time to leave.
It's been a hard ride and we're out of patience. We'll try out luck with the escape pods. So long, Commander.
mission_tw_passengerevacuation_burning_i: This is taking too long, Commander. We want to get to the rescue ship as quickly as possible. Can you pick up the pace?
Did you stop for lunch or something? This journey is taking far too long. Hurry up!
We really appreciate all you're doing for us, but we've got some people panicking back here who could really use setting down soon. How much longer?
Are we there yet? Are we there yet? Are we there yet? Are we there yet? Are we there yet?
All this technology to travel light years in seconds, and you're still taking forever to get us to the rescue ship. Could you try to hurry things up, Commander?
mission_tw_passengerevacuation_burning_m: You saved our lives, Commander. We'll never forget what you did for us today.
mission_tw_passengerevacuation_burning_s: Lives are in danger and time is running out. Transport our people to a rescue ship if you can.
mission_tw_passengerevacuation_burning_u: We've all disembarked. Good luck with whatever else you have on your mind.
That was a rough trip. Thanks for the ride, but maybe next time spare a thought for the people in your hold?
Well we're clear of the Thargoid threat, at least. But your customer service skills could use a little work. Good luck.
We've finally made it. Appreciate the help, but we're glad to be off your ship. Maybe you're happy to see the back of us, too.
Everybody has disembarked, Commander. I do have some complaints about your piloting style, but since you helped us to safety it'd be selfish to share them. Let's just leave things at goodbye.
mission_tw_passengerevacuation_underatta: I don't know what you're doing. Whatever, just drop us off where you can and we'll try and find our own way.
Changed your mind on being our hero, huh? Fine, your call. Let us off at the next available port.
We just heard you've cancelled the contract. Well, we'll have to arrange another transport. Let us out at the next port, please.
Not interested in getting us to the rescue ship? At least drop us off at the next port so we can find our own way there.
I suppose we'll have to pay another pilot to carry us to the rescue ship. We don't have much left after the evacuation... Please let us off at the nearest port.
That's enough - we're getting out of here. Thanks for the awful ride!
We'll take our chances in the escape pods, thanks. Try and be more considerate of your passengers next time.
After the stress of evacuating our homes, you treat us like this? We're taking escape pods and leaving.
So much for helping out - we're safe but we're scared! Time to get out of here...
This just isn't good enough. We're not sticking around for another disaster. So long.
We really appreciate all you're doing for us but we've got some people panicking back here and they need to get off this ship soon. How much longer?
It's been a rough few days for everyone back here and we're exhausted. Is it going to be much longer until we reach the rescue ship?
After the terrible treatment I've faced over evacuating my home, I'm now stuck in this ship with a bunch of sad sacks. Get me to the rescue ship, you goofball!
In the rush to evacuate I only brought one Insight program and I'm bored of it. You didn't provide much in the way of entertainment. Let's hurry it up, yeah?

I'm really grateful that you're taking time out of your day to take us to the rescue ship. Honestly. You're a great person. But could you fly a little faster because I'm so over this whole journey? Thanks.
Thank you so much. Without you, I have no idea what would have happened to us.
We need all the help we can get before the Thargoids finish this place off. Can you transport our civilians to a rescue ship?
We've all disembarked. Good luck with whatever else you have on your mind.
That was a rough trip. Thanks for the ride, but maybe next time spare a thought for the people in your hold?
Well we're clear of the Thargoid threat, at least. But your customer service skills could use a little work. Good luck.
We've finally made it. Appreciate the help, but we're glad to be off your ship. Maybe you're happy to see the back of us, too.
Everybody has disembarked, Commander. I do have some complaints about your piloting style, but since you helped us to safety it'd be selfish to share them. Let's just leave things at goodbye.
mission_tw_refugeebulk_abandoned_inbox_0: What do you mean you're abandoning our contract? I can't believe someone would... Fine, set us down at a nearby port.
mission_tw_refugeebulk_arrivedwithpassen: We're here! There's a lot of chatter in the cabin, Commander. We're excited to be disembarking soon.
Not long to go now, Commander. I wonder how long it'll take to process everybody when we land? Hopefully the queues aren't too long.
This is the last system on our travels, correct? Time to break out the champagne! Oh, wait... I had to leave it behind.
We're looking forward to finding out where we'll be living for now. Maybe it'll be a system with multiple stars. That would be nice.
You're a class pilot to get us all to our destination without any losses. It's appreciated back here, Commander. To the dock!
Thanks for getting us to this system, Commander. I only wish all of us were here to see it. But we know you've done your best.
There's no Thargoids here, at least. No aliens to snatch us up. I'll say a prayer for the people we lost on the way.
We all hoped that we'd make it to this system together, but knew the dangers when we stepped on board. I'm glad some of us have made it here despite the risks. Get us to our port, Commander.
We're nearly home. Or, where home will be for a while. Not everyone made it, but those who did are grateful. We're ready to dock now.
There's comfort in knowing we're far away from the Thargoids. Hopefully we'll never see another one for as long as we live. Damn them all.
mission_tw_refugeebulk_damagerecieved_in: Something hit the hull! We're not in any danger, are we? You have to keep us safe, Commander!
mission_tw_refugeebulk_disgruntledpassen: You got us here, but we're pretty shaken up. Thanks for getting us to safety, but don't expect a tip. I hope you'll be more careful with your passengers one day.
We've decided to take our chances with the escape pods. Thank you for evacuating us, but your treatment of refugees leaves a lot to be desired.
We don't think that staying on this ship is the best decision, Commander. Please take us to the nearest port so we can disembark.
mission_tw_refugeebulk_failureinboxmessa: You tried your best, Commander... Maybe next time.
mission_tw_refugeebulk_lostdemandedgoods: You're no longer carrying the goods I requested, Commander. (these won't be used, but I can repurpose them in the scientist mission).
mission_tw_refugeebulk_nearlydisgruntled: This trip is taking far too long. Hurry up and deliver us to the agreed port, Commander!
Please be more considerate, Commander. We need to arrive at our destination intact!
mission_tw_refugeebulk_newdestinationinb: Apologies for the change of plan, but our relocation plans have changed. Take me to $#AltDestinationStationName; in the $#AltDestinationSystemName; system.

mission_tw_refugeebulk_ntfluffmessage_pm: I just wanted to say that I hope you don't blame yourself for losing passengers. Thargoid space is dangerous. We all knew the risks when boarding the ship. Just focus on getting the rest of us safely to our destination.
mission_tw_refugeebulk_passengerejectinb: We're not accepting this kind of treatment, Commander. We'll take our chances with the escape pods.
