npccrew_fighterpilot_background_01: I served honourably in the Federal Navy for several years.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_02: My father served in the Federal Navy as a fighter pilot, and I followed in his footsteps.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_03: As my mother flew as a fighter pilot in the Federal Navy, I felt compelled to join.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_04: I joined the Federal Navy at an early age, at the same time as my brother in fact!
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_05: My sister flew Condors for the Federal Navy, and as soon as I was old enough, I did the same.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_06: I lived the dream as a fighter jock in the Federal Navy, flying the F-63 in Farragut squadron.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_07: Considering that my family are all pilots, it was inevitable that I joined too. However a member of a crew on a capital ship wasn't for me, so I became a fighter pilot.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_08: The navy recruiter caught me at the right time in my life, and I signed up as a pilot in one of the Battlecruiser fighter squadrons.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_09: I loved the Federal Navy, and indeed served for many distinguished years.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_10: For many years the Federal Navy was my life.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_100: My parents were both pilots. They wanted me to do something safer, but that was never going to happen.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_11: I served with distinction in the Imperial Navy, and saw quite a bit of action during my service.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_12: Like my father, I joined the Imperial Navy at an early age. Unlike him I became a fighter pilot.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_13: My mother was an ace in an Imperial fighter squadron. It seemed only natural to do the same.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_14: I always knew that I would follow the family tradition and serve in the Imperial Navy.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_15: The glamour of flying close protection in an Imperial Fighter captured my imagination as a child, so I signed up as soon as I could.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_16: I've seen many operations in my time as an Imperial Navy fighter pilot.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_17: While I started out as an engineer on a Majestic class, I soon discovered a thrill for flying and transferred to a fighter squadron.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_18: It was an honour to serve in the Imperial Navy.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_19: My sister piloted transports for the Imperial Navy and told me stories of the exotic places she visited. So of course I signed up.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_20: I earned my freedom as an Imperial slave, but didn't know what to do with my life until I met that damned recruiter.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_21: I developed my skills as a fighter pilot in the proving grounds of CQC.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_22: The constant battles in the CQC arenas helped me hone my piloting over many seasons.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_23: I'm a veteran of the CQC arenas with more victories than I can count.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_24: I'm from a long line of pilots, and I'm just keeping up the family tradition.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_25: I used to be an engineer, back in the day, then I started flying a Mk III.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_26: Ten years as an Imperial bounty hunter honed my piloting skills to be razor sharp.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_27: I was born on Sol, but always had this burning ambition to get out there and see some of the galaxy.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_28: I honed my craft piloting a Beluga out towards Reorte. I can't tell you how boring it was.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_29: I was a mechanic for Lakon Spaceways until I got bitten by the flying bug.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_30: I used to be based out of Indaol, flying exploration missions for adventurous scientists.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_31: I was a pilot for Astrogator Tours, best adventure holidays in the galaxy. Those were the days.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_32: You might not believe it but I was wealthy once. Flew my own Dolphin class yacht.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_33: I cut my teeth flying prototype ships for Sirius Corp. I've been in some scrapes, that's for sure.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_34: I used to fly package tours for Worldcraft - best package tours in the bubble.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_35: I flew a Federal Corvette for Wreaken Construction & Mining. You'd be surprised how much action I've seen.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_36: I used to transport Imperial prisoners to and from the Tantalum mines. Well, mainly just to them.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_37: I was a test pilot for Achilles Aerospace for years. I had some fun times on that job.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_38: Got more years in the pilot seat than I can remember. Used to fly a Lakon Type 7 transporter.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_39: Worked in a Faulcon deLacy shipyard back in the day. But don't hold that against me. I'm a flyer now.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_40: I flew luxury liners for Saud Kruger back before I went freelance. Best years of my life.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_41: You won't believe the jobs I've had all over the galaxy. My favourite must have been flying the tour ship for those old rockers Jjagged Banner.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_42: I used to fly courier ships for Argent Incorporated. You wouldn't believe some of the things I've transported - but of course I can't tell you about them.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_43: Spent my early days flying an Imperial Cutter. That was one beautiful ship.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_44: I used to fly a transport for the Federal Intelligence Agency. Maybe I shouldn't have told you that.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_45: I started out as part of the Imperial Diplomatic Corps, flying Senators from one all night shindig to the next. Those guys know how to party.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_46: Learned my craft piloting a Federal Dropship. Had more than my share of close calls, I can tell you.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_47: I flew a supply ship transporting slaves. I'm not proud of it, but I needed the money.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_48: You won't meet a better flyer. I used to be quite the pirate hunter in my day.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_49: Flew an Orca Class Yacht from one side of the galaxy to the other. You just can't beat the open spaceways.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_50: I used to fly a medical transport back in the day. You could say I was instrumental in curing the Volungu Blight, but don't thank me all at once. No seriously.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_51: I used to fly with the Citizens of Tradition. We showed those insurgents in Falisci a thing or two.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_52: I flew a medical supply ship, once upon a time. Did my bit to stop the Cerberus Plague.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_53: I've flown more exploration missions than you can count. Seen some pretty strange things out there too.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_54: My mother used to be in Interpol, flying all over the galaxy on one mission or another. Naturally I wanted a piece of that action.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_55: My father was in an Imperial Guard unit assigned to a high-ranking Senator. Following him across the galaxy gave me a taste for space travel.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_56: My mother was in the Federal Security Services, always travelling the space lanes after some criminal or other. I always wanted to see the stars like her.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_57: I spent years flying a heavy freighter. Lakon Type-9. I called her Mabel.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_58: I was a bounty hunter, back in my heyday. Two hundred and sixty one bounties - all clean kills.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_59: I was on the crew of an O'Brian Class Battlecruiser not so long ago.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_60: I used to be a test pilot. Even did some time flying the experimental Manticore for the Alliance.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_61: I was part of the Imperial Navy. I know, the best of the best.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_62: I've done my time and I can fly like you wouldn't believe. Never did make it into the Pilots' Federation though.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_63: Cut my teeth flying a Fer-de-Lance. That was one beautiful ship.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_64: I used to transport androids for a living. I'm not ashamed to say, those things used to creep me out.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_65: I used to transport Lavian Brandy back in the day. And when I say 'transport' I actually mean smuggle!
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_66: Used to fly a Space Dredger. Not the most glamorous work but it was honest.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_67: When I was younger my grandmother used to tell me tales of aliens among the stars. I always wanted to go out and find one for myself.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_68: I was crew on an Imperial Interdictor. Ah, those were the days
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_69: I was born in a little backwater system you'll never have heard of. Never thought I'd get to see the galaxy.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_70: My home system is in the back of beyond. It's a wonder I've managed to see so much of the galaxy.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_71: My parents were both scientists but I never wanted to go into the family business. It was always the pilot's life for me.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_72: Always wanted to fly the spaceways when I was a kid. Nothing like heading off into the black.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_73: Did my time flying a Panther Clipper LX. That was one exciting job.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_74: Worked my way up from scrubbing floors to doing dishes to being a pilot. I'm living the dream.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_75: Had a misspent youth and did my time in the penal colony. But I've become a damned good pilot since then.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_76: I used to watch a lot of holo-vids about pilots when I was a kid. There was only one thing I was ever going to do.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_77: When I was a kid I'd stare up at the stars and wonder what was going on up there. I was only ever going to become a pilot.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_78: I learned how to fly in an F63 Condor. Now I can fly pretty much anything.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_79: I come from a long line of spacefarers. You could say I'm carrying on a family tradition.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_80: Did a stint on an Imperial Liner. It was how I got my start.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_81: Done every kind of spacefaring job you could think of in my time. You might say I'm a jack of all trades.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_82: I come from a long line of miners. Got so I could fly that mining craft with my eyes shut.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_83: I'm from Leesti originally. Couldn't wait to get off that rock and get myself out into the black.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_84: I come from Zaonce. Ever been? Trust me, you'd prefer life in the Void too!
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_85: I was born on Ulrich in the Orerve system. If you'd ever been you'd know what a miracle it is that I've made it this far.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_86: I was crew aboard a Federal Corvette, back in my younger days.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_87: I come from Anayol, my parents were from mining stock. But that was never good enough for me - I wanted to see the stars.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_88: You probably can't tell from the accent, but I'm from Achenar. Couldn't wait to get out of that place and see the galaxy.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_89: I'm from a little planet called Valhalla. Hot as hell! Couldn't wait to make it up into the cold of space when I was a kid.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_90: I grew up in Biggs Colony. I thought it was a dangerous place until a made it up into the unforgiving expanse of space.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_91: I used to fly whiskey out of New Caledonia. Those were some good times, I can tell you!
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_92: I always wanted to see the world. I mean worlds!
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_93: There was never going to be any other choice for me - I had to end up in the cockpit one way or another.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_94: I tried a few careers in my younger days, but once I was sitting in that cockpit for the first time I knew I'd found my calling.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_95: Great granny was a pilot. Granny was a pilot. Mammy was a pilot. Yep, I know - predictable really.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_96: Always wanted to head off into the stars, even before I could first walk.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_97: I remember the first time I was in a cockpit sat on my father's knee. We crashed that first time, but nobody died!
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_98: I just wanted to see some of the galaxy when I was a kid. Never realised that yearning would take me anywhere.
npccrew_fighterpilot_background_99: I won an old Cobra Mk I in a card game. Learned to fly it in a week. The rest is history.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_01: After the death of my father on a transporter during the Cerberus Plague outbreak, I just bummed the space lanes looking for purpose. I now have that purpose by protecting others.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_02: I just wasn't seeing enough action, so I decided to set up shop for myself.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_03: Things changed for me after my wife left me, so I decided to spread my wings further afield.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_04: After a time I realised that there had to be more in the galaxy, so now I sign on to a crew and see where it takes me.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_05: I had to move elsewhere when I divorced my partner, but couldn't settle, so now I hire on to crews and bounce around the trade routes.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_06: I switched my life up through simple boredom - I needed more of a thrill.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_07: After I recovered from a crash I knew I had to do something different, but all I knew was how to fly.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_08: It might seem strange, but operating as a mercenary pilot actually gives me more flying time. It was no choice at all for me really.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_09: There's a certain freedom with my life now. I join a crew and we visit exciting places, and sometimes I get to shoot people.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_10: It took a family tragedy to make me understand that I was wasting my life, but what else could I do? I strove to fight for myself, or at least for a decent crew.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_100: I was involved in a pretty horrific accident. When I came out the other side I knew I needed a fresh start.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_11: Betrayal provided the catalyst I needed to set up my own operation, and I haven't looked back since.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_12: I inherited a ship, a classic Cobra Mk III, and tried trading for a while. But even that old beauty wallowed like a pig compared to the fighters I was used to.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_13: Sometimes things don't go to plan, and that forces a change in your life. It's still too difficult to talk about.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_14: I have many fond memories of my early career, but it wasn't until I got going on my own that I really started to get the most from life.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_15: It's in my blood. The action, I mean. And to get the most of it I travel looking for crews to hire with.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_16: They wouldn't let me fly any more, so I had to go into business for myself. It was the right choice.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_17: I had a bad smash. The accident board cleared me of any fault, but they still kicked me out. Well, since then I showed them who can still fly.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_18: There were complications, ones that I can't go into for confidentiality reasons, but I had to leave. Setting up on my own seemed like the best way forward.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_19: You hear about 'The Missing', but it wasn't until my family vanished that I realised the truth of it. Now I know all too well the pain, and my search for them continues.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_20: It's the journey that I love, and I wanted a greater adventure. The old vocation held me back too much, so I had to change things up.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_21: There comes a time when every one has to stand on their own, so I did just that. It was difficult to adjust at first, but worth the effort.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_22: I needed to spread my wings a little, try something new.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_23: I decided freelance was the way to go. And lucky for you I did.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_24: I wanted to get out there, see a little more of the galaxy, so I decided to hire on as crew and see where it took me.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_25: I got my heart broken, decided to get away from it all. A new start was what I needed.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_26: I wanted to earn some real money, and I thought hiring myself out to the highest bidder was the way to do it.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_27: Everything changed when my son was kidnapped by a pirate gang. I need to find him, and hiring myself to crews seems the easiest way to search the galaxy.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_28: Recently my partner ran off with a deep space explorer. I just needed a change after that.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_29: I was in an accident. It changed me, made me want to get out there and see the galaxy, earning my way on my own terms.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_30: I heard about the Thargoids. Aliens on the edge of the galaxy they say. I decided hiring on as a crewman would be the best chance I have of seeing them.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_31: I got into serious debt after I gambled everything away. Needed to recoup some funds so thought this was the best way to do it.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_32: I'd seen enough of the same old thing. It was time for me to make some changes.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_33: There was an incident with a consignment of Onionhead and local law enforcement. Hiring on as crew was the best way for me to leave all that behind.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_34: I hired on as crew because I like the variety. No two days are ever the same.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_35: My homeworld turned into a war zone and I had to get out of there. Most sensible thing to do was join a crew.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_36: I was one of the few survivors of the Cerberus Plague. After a thing like that you start needing a change. Joining a crew seemed just the thing.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_37: I got bored with the old life. Fancied doing something new.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_38: There comes a time when you realise you have to change, or you'll end up doing the same thing forever. I made a change.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_39: When my partner died I thought my whole world had ended. I gave up my old life and had to start something new. And here I am.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_40: One word - divorce. That's what made me leave everything behind, pack up and sell my skills to anyone who wanted them.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_41: My partner decided it was best if we have some time apart. So I took them at their word and made off to the stars.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_42: After I got locked up - don't worry, I was framed - I couldn't face going back to my old life. So I decided to become part of someone's crew.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_43: My brother died working on a mining rig. It made me realise life is short and you should chase your dreams. My dream was to see the galaxy, so what better way than this.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_44: I was hurt pretty bad in a crash. When I was recovering I made myself a promise I'd get out there and see as many systems as I could.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_45: I've always wanted to find that special someone, and it was never going to happen where I was. Hopefully by becoming part of someone's crew I'll eventually get my wish.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_46: I came down with a disease not so long ago, nearly killed me. After that I wanted a new lease of life - see some of the galaxy.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_47: I got fired from my old job. Not my fault, obviously, I was unfairly dismissed.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_48: I was pensioned out of my previous career. But I'm not one to sit back and just waste away forever - I decided to sign up as a crewman.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_49: Things were going great until my other half decided to get pregnant. The only way I can support the family is to do this.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_50: My baby boy came along and I want the best for him. Doing this is the best way to make that happen.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_51: I've always been a hard worker, but somehow my finances are always in the red. This was one way of earning extra credits.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_52: My best friend was killed in a ship crash not too long ago. That kind of thing makes you review your life. I reviewed mine and here I am.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_53: Times have been tough, and when they came to repossess my home I knew I needed a fresh start.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_54: My daughter left to become a naval cadet. After that there was nothing keeping me tied down, so I decided to do something new, see some of the galaxy.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_55: Had a slight falling out with my old boss, so needed to find a new career.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_56: It's like I suddenly had some kind of epiphany, as though something were calling to me across the stars. So I packed up and decided to join a crew.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_57: Had a little trouble with the law out in Ross 128. Last thing I wanted was a one way trip to the Warren, so I decided it was time for a change of career.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_58: Did a little bit of Onionhead, back in the day. Made me see the galaxy in a whole new light. You could say it changed me for the better.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_59: Dodgy financial advice and some foolish investments sent me bankrupt. I needed a new start and here I am.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_60: It was time I learned a new trade, got me some experience out in the galaxy.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_61: It was time I put myself out there. I'd been doing the same thing for too long and wanted to get out and see the galaxy. What better way than as part of someone's crew.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_62: I just woke up and it was like I'd reached an apotheosis. Like I was connecting with symbolic universal realities. I knew then I needed to leave my old path behind and put myself out in the galaxy.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_63: I had a yearning building up inside until I could quell it no longer. I wanted fame and fortune, and I was going to get it. So I signed up as crew. Bring on the adventure.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_64: I won't lie - I had a mid-life crisis. Consider this like me getting a tattoo or buying a brand new ship.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_65: Everything I knew was wiped out by civil war. I needed to leave all that behind me and start again.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_66: All my life I felt I'd been living for someone else. I needed to strike out on my own and see new horizons.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_67: For a long time I didn't know who I was. The only way I felt I could find myself was to get out and see the galaxy.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_68: My partner died from the Cerberus Plague. I needed to change my life completely or the loss would have just consumed me.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_69: I was doing well until the divorce. Then I ended up with nothing. Time to start afresh.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_70: When I separated from my partner I decided I needed a big change in my life. What better change than to sign on as crew.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_71: Prison eats some people up, makes them bitter and twisted. Not me - I decided to start again, make something of myself.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_72: Had a best friend. We did everything together until he was killed in a pirate raid. I vowed to find the culprits and hired on as crew to find them.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_73: Had a serious crash and got busted up pretty bad. My ship was totalled and I had no insurance. Only way I can save for another is to do this.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_74: I got married not too long back. Didn't realise my partner had such expensive tastes. That's why I need this extra work.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_75: I got ill not very long back, nearly died too. That kind of thing makes you think about life... about yourself. I wanted a new start, to see some of the galaxy, and here I am.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_76: I always got on with my old employer... right up until she fired me. So it was time for a change.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_77: Retirement always seemed a great idea, up until I did it. Boredom made me realise I needed to get back out there and sign on as crew.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_78: Doing the same thing day in and day out was driving me nuts. It was time to get out and do something different.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_79: It was the birth of my daughter that made me realise I had to strike out and make something of myself.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_80: I've never been very good with cash. That became most evident when I lost everything on a bad investment. I decided I needed to change.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_81: A friend of mine was killed when his Cobra hit an asteroid. That was it for me, I needed to get away and start something fresh.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_82: There was me, mortgaged up to the hilt, swimming in debt. I just woke up one morning and thought, screw this, I'm gonna join a crew. And that was it.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_83: My son went and joined the Imperial Guard. Not heard from him in a year. If I'd waited around I would have wasted away, so I decided to go find myself by signing on as crew.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_84: I've never had much luck with employers, so thought freelance might be the way to go.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_85: I've always been a deeply devout person, but one day I woke up and realised I needed to go off into the heavens - to see the stars and connect with them for real.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_86: I made a big mistake and ended up in prison for it. Now I'm out I'm determined to turn things around for myself.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_87: I was a little too partial to Lavian brandy, way back when. Lost everything because of it. Now I'm sober I'm looking to start afresh.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_88: I had a lot of money saved up at one time but one bad investment and I ended up with nothing. It was time for me to start something new.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_89: I'd never really taught myself about the galaxy, and I wanted to change that. I decided signing on as crew was the best way to experience it all.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_90: I needed a change - to get out there and really see the galaxy. What better way than going freelance and picking my own jobs.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_91: I was watching a newsfeed one day, where a guy just packed up all his things and went off to start a new career in the stars. It suddenly dawned on me: I could do that!
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_92: I liked my old career, but it never gave me quite the thrill of travel and new experiences I needed. I decided it was time for a change.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_93: I got into my forties and suddenly wondered what I was doing with my life. It was then I decided to go off and see the galaxy as part of a crew.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_94: When war came to my home system it was flee or die. I had to make a new start.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_95: As much as I loved my previous vocation I still didn't feel in control of my destiny. I had to make a change and here I am.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_96: My previous job was good but it did nothing for my self esteem. I needed something new to give me a boost, and what better than this.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_97: When my partner passed away everything crumbled around me. I had to start again somehow. So I packed up everything and joined a crew.
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_98: I went through quite a sticky divorce, and after that I needed to change my life. Mainly because I was left with nothing!
npccrew_fighterpilot_change_99: When I split up with my partner it made me question everything. I needed something more from life, and heading out to the stars as part of a crew was the best way to get it.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_01: The standout moment of my career so far has to be the Battle of Lugh. I bagged nine kills in that campaign.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_02: I recall an attack by a pirate gang on a transport I was defending. I was taking hits from all directions, but kept them away from my host ship long enough for them to escape.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_03: There's almost too many successful victories to remember. Well, there was this one time, in an asteroid cluster I ambushed a pirate. He didn't see me coming.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_04: It's the hardest fights you remember the most. Especially in something as fragile as a short-range fighter. You have to keep moving - that's the trick.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_05: I'm never comfortable describing specific moments, unless you're there it's difficult to get it across, but I'm still here, and that counts for something.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_06: Escort patrols. I love them, although I've always enjoyed formation flying. You have to keep your eyes peeled though.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_07: Things are much faster these days. If you're not careful then you can be out before you know it. Luckily I keep my wits about me.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_08: I took out five pirates once. Just me in a short-range fighter, and them in their Cobras. It was almost a shame to see such classic ships in pieces.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_09: The best part of flying a fighter is the agility. You can run rings around almost anyone, and it's all the more satisfying when you take out a multi-million credit monster.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_10: I've fought in many battles, and they're intense periods of scary chaos. But the one on one duels, they really test a pilot's skill.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_100: My best day was during the Sorbago Rebellion. Took down a dozen enemy fighters without a scratch on me. No word of a lie!
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_11: There was a fleet action that I took part in on the border between the Federation and the Empire. Running convoy escorts was a much safer proposition.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_12: Close protection duty for mining convoys certainly improves the skills. Painite makes for an attractive target, yet the company never seemed to hire enough protection, which made the fights touch and go sometimes.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_13: Some people consider escort runs to be the safe and simple option. Well I can tell you that they don't know what they're talking about. Fighting an Imperial Clipper in a fighter while your Type-9 runs, is no fun at all.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_14: Never give up. That's my advice. And if you're hauling cargo then make sure to have a suitable escort.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_15: I like protecting the passenger ships the most. Those Belugas sure are something.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_16: Mining operations have generated the most work for me. Those ring systems provide too much cover, but the best finds always seem to be where pirates are waiting. It makes for some intense combat, and if you're lucky - some decent bonuses.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_17: I provided support on an exploration supply run once. The dread emptiness of the real black. You hear rumours of ships disappearing, but it turned out to be quietest run I've ever flown.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_18: Outnumbered and outgunned I fought them off. A hero? No, just a damned fine pilot.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_19: I've seen action all over the galaxy - even out in the so-called Merope Bubble. I saw some weird stuff out there.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_20: Civil wars are the worst. It's one of the reasons I prefer escort jobs now. The bitterness is just too much for me.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_21: I was part of a task force that liberated rebels in the Jera System. You could say standing up for the oppressed is kind of my thing.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_22: I made my name at Kappa Fornacis, helping stop the spread of illegal drugs. I earned my stripes that day.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_23: Pirates were doing a roaring trade in slaves around the Durius System until I took them out. Single handed too.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_24: You must have heard of the Sorbago Rebellion? I took down thirteen Cobras during that campaign.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_25: I don't want to blow my own trumpet, but I was a finalist in the Buckyball Race. That's what kind of flyer you're dealing with.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_26: When piracy was rife in Istanu, I was the first to answer the call for help. Took almost a dozen pirate bounties. Those miners bought me drinks for weeks.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_27: I managed to distinguish myself during the civil war in Balaikda. Took down more Vipers than I can remember.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_28: Last year I was a runner up in the St. Valentine's Day Regatta. Not quite the fastest pilot in the galaxy, but pretty close.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_29: I fought in the campaign against the Purple Gang of Falisci. Got so they'd see my ship and fly off into the black as quick as they could.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_30: Couple of years ago I took on the Polahukuna Raiders. They came to fear my name.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_31: I'm a veteran of the conflict against the Banki Gold Gang. We showed those upstarts a thing or two.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_32: I'm a veteran of the war on Lugh. Took on the Crimson State Group and lived to tell the tale.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_33: Remember the civil war on 78 Ursae Majoris? I helped end that one.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_34: I just missed out on the record for the Buckyball Run A*. Just over 10 hours it took me, that's damn good going!
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_35: I was part of the task force that helped defend Volungu against its attackers. We gave those Faveols a damn good thrashing
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_36: For a time I was part of a task force defending Zaonce from pirate raiders. We showed those gangs a thing or two.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_37: When Silver United Solutions put out the call for pilots to repel criminals from the Old Worlds I was first in line. The Zaonce Jet Gang didn't know what hit it.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_38: I fought at Quivira, but I'd rather not say what side I was on. All you need to know is I took down twenty enemy fighters.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_39: I earned a deadly reputation in the Ceti Sector not long back. The farmers around there had attracted a lot of unsavoury types, but that's what happens when you grow Onionhead.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_40: I was part of the vanguard force during Operation Charybdis. Took down more Kumo Crew pirates than I care to remember.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_41: Operation Davy Jones was where I made my name. I was proud to blow those Kumo Crew scum out of the void.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_42: I single-handedly defended a medical convoy during the Cerberus Plague, and I was proud to do it.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_43: I was a fighter pilot during Operation Augeas in BD-22 3573. We sent those criminals packing, and no mistake.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_44: Lost a lot of friends during the Pegasi Pirate War. I also showered myself in glory, so it wasn't all bad.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_45: I made the finals of the XYZ Fight Club not too long ago. That is one tough competition - only the best dog-fighters in the galaxy need apply.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_46: I've completed the Hutton Run in record time. Got the mug to prove it too.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_47: Distinguished myself during the Pegasi Pirate War. Just ask anyone who was there - they'll know my reputation.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_48: I fought as a gun-for-hire during the war against Emperor's Dawn. Saw some real action in the Maausk system, but I don't like to talk about it.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_49: I was part of a task force that delivered vital medicine to Ocrinox's Orbiter. We saved a lot of lives.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_50: I helped defend refugees during the Pegasi Pirate War. We saved a lot of lives in the Amitrite system and I'm proud of what we achieved.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_51: I flew as a test pilot for the new Imperial Eagle. I was instrumental in producing the next generation of fighters.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_52: I helped clear the Carnoeck system of pirates in the wake of the Bacon Protest celebrations. We routed those ruffians and kept the spaceways clear for decent folk.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_53: I was instrumental in clearing the pirates from the Robigo system. Sirius Corp paid a pretty penny for that job, I can tell you!
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_54: I took part in the Cobra Crunch in the Athena system. I earned my reputation that day.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_55: When the Explorer's Association asked for help getting rid of pirates in the Kaushpoos system I was first to hear the call. We showed that scum what for!
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_56: I fought against the Cayutorme Syndicate on the side of the Empire. I don't hold any allegiance to them, but a payday is a payday.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_57: My name got around during the Galactic 'Top Gun' Championship. I didn't win, but I was pretty close.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_58: Built a deadly reputation in the Xelabara system taking down pirates. I earned plenty of credits with that job.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_59: I've flown my share of combat missions but I'm proudest of my achievements in search-and-rescue. Anyone can shoot a ship down - takes a special pilot to rescue one.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_60: I was a ranked finalist for the Mischief Mile not too long back. You'll struggle to find a faster pilot.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_61: I was one of the first pilots ever to complete the Achenar Challenge. You've got to be crazy, or the best pilot around, to do it. Guess which I am!
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_62: I came close to winning the Turbo Hour Endurance Race. There was some stiff competition but I held my own.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_63: I was part of an initiative to bring supplies to thousands of former slaves in LFT 37. That was my crowning glory.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_64: When the Emperor's Dawn shadow cells were discovered on Ch'i Lin, I was in the vanguard sent to wipe them out.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_65: I was part of the task force sent in to clear out the Blue Hand Gang from Orulas. I was proud of the way we dealt with those void rats.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_66: When marauders started targeting traders in LHS 3447, I was there to answer the call for help. We showed those raiders what for.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_67: I was one of the first pilots to complete the expedition to Beagle Point. There weren't many of us who finished that one.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_68: When the Morrina Pro-Alliance Party offered kill orders on all wanted ships in their system it was an offer I couldn't refuse. I handed in more bounty vouchers than I can remember in that one.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_69: When the Buckyball Racing Club organised the Kessel Run I was the first to sign up. Crossed the finish with the first batch of pilots too.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_70: I was part of an initiative to deliver aid to Morrina. I'm proud of the medicines and supplies we delivered. We saved a lot of lives.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_71: When the Diamond Frogs requested aid from the puritanical raiders hampering their trade routes I was there to help. Cut down my fair share of those fanatics.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_72: When the kill order was given on all wanted ships in the Ngolibardu system I was there in the thick of it. I took some scalps during that conflict.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_73: The authorities in Mehet put out a kill order for all wanted ships. I delivered more bounty vouchers than I can remember during that one.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_74: I fought in the Battle of Lugh. Sometimes I wake in the night remembering the battles I fought.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_75: Have you ever been caught in the midst of a pirate attack? I have... It's glorious!
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_76: I've forgotten almost as many engagements as I can remember. Once took two pirate vessels out with the same heatseeker. One day I'll tell you how I did it.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_77: Never underestimate how deadly a short-range fighter can be. It could be the end of you.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_78: The fact that after so many encounters I'm still alive should be testament enough to my skills.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_79: You'd be surprised the scrapes you get in flying escort. Safety isn't always in numbers.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_80: It all happens so fast. When you're in the thick of it you barely have the time to think. Luckily I'm a quick thinker.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_81: I've had my fair share of close encounters with pirates. They've always come to regret it though... if they've survived that is.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_82: I've always loved the manoeuvrability of short-range fighters - you can make mincemeat out of the lumbering space whales you're usually up against.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_83: A one on one dogfight is always the most intense, and the most rewarding.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_84: Fleet actions are intense, but there's nothing like a one-on-one dogfight to get the blood pumping.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_85: I've run a lot of close protection in my day. Mining convoys tend to be the most lucrative, I've never known a mining company not want to throw credits at good escort pilots.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_86: I've done more escort runs than you've had hot dinners. You might think I've seen it all, but there'll always be something that surprises you in this business.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_87: Tenacity will always win out. I've been down and almost out, interdicted, down to my last drop of fuel. Just grit your teeth and keep pressing the trigger.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_88: Bravery ain't taking on a strong enemy. It's risking your life to save some other sap. That's where the reward comes in.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_89: There's always someone ready to take down a mining convoy. Luckily there's always someone like me ready to defend it.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_90: I once did convoy protection on a long-range exploration mission. Saw more than my share of the void during that one.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_91: I've earned my stripes in the big black more than once. You only start to show your mettle when you're outnumbered and outgunned and come through the other side.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_92: I've done my share of jobs from one side of the galaxy to the other, and I still haven't seen it all.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_93: I was part of a support group sent in to relieve freedom fighters during a civil war. That was a tough one. I don't often talk about it.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_94: Every time a system opens itself up to pirates there's work for people like me. Gotta love a good payday!
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_95: I once liberated a convoy of slaves. Took more than my share of pirate kills that day.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_96: I helped take care of the Blue Hand Gang in Orulas. No one took more pirate kills than me.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_97: I helped the trading convoys in LHS 3447. We took down those raiders like we were scything through wheat.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_98: I tend to go for pirate bounties. Don't know what it is but I just hate those robbers and murderers.
npccrew_fighterpilot_highlight_99: It seemed like a good idea when I signed up to fight in Lugh. That was a tough battle. I was lucky to get out with my life.
occupiedcryopod_info: Escape pods are typically made from composite materials designed to withstand extremes of pressure and temperature, and can protect a single occupant in the event of ship destruction.
occupiedcryopod_info_short: Escape pods can protect a single occupant in the event of ship destruction.
ochoengchillies_info:
Due to the relaxation of various genetic modification laws, Ochoeng prides itself on having produced the galaxy's hottest chilli pepper. There have been numerous calls to reclassify the substances as toxic, however the produce remains legal in most systems.

This rare good is legal in all markets.

olivine_info:
Produced by: Surface Mining only
Consumed by: Industrial, Refinery and Tourism

Chemical formula (Mg,Fe)2SiO4. Olivine is a common yellow-green mineral found across the galaxy and mostly used to produce high yields of aluminium. In gemstone form, known as peridot, it is sold in tourism destination as a charm to ward off irrational fears and nightmares, however those claims are disputed.
olivine_info_short: Produced by: Surface Mining only Consumed by: Industrial, Refinery and Tourism Olivine is a common yellow-green mineral found across the galaxy and mostly used to produce high yields of aluminium.

onionhead_info:
The Onionhead flower is native to HIP 55118, and its seeds contain the well-known psychedelic narcotic. Illegal in most jurisdictions.

This rare good is legal in all Imperial markets, and Independent and Allied Democracy, Dictatorship and Confederacy markets. It is prohibited in all other markets.

Please note that if a market’s controlling faction changes, some formerly legal rare goods may become illegal. Should this occur the rare good will be unavailable for sale or purchase at that market for the duration of the prohibiting faction’s tenure.

op_rackhamspeak_log_001_body:
Rackham's Peak is situated in the HIP 58832 system, one of the highest practical locations above the galactic plane. Its construction was funded by Rackham Capital Investments, in conjunction with Universal Cartographics and other scientific research companies.

Mr Rackham officiated at the outpost's opening ceremony, which was followed by an extravagant press party for media representatives and attending celebrities. He gave this statement:

 "The top of the galaxy is now open for business! Rackham's Peak is a free port where everyone is welcome, a place where explorers and entrepreneurs can enjoy drinks while overlooking the entire Milky Way. Aim high, Commanders!"

ophiuchiexinoartefacts_info:
These strange sculptures are believed by some to have been created by an extinct sentient race. Others have theorised that the sculptures are natural formations caused by local weather patterns. Most economists agree that there are massive profits to be made from the gullibility of wealthy collectors.

This rare good is legal in all markets.

orca_armour_mirrored_info: Hull reinforcement using a specially formulated structure, offering superior protection against thermal damage caused by energy weapons. It is vulnerable to projectile weapons and other kinetic attacks.
orca_armour_reactive_info: Hull reinforcement using a dynamically reactive, impact-resistant material offering superior protection against projectile weapons and other kinetic attacks. It is vulnerable to thermal damage caused by energy weapons.

orca_info:
The Orca is a high-end passenger ship manufactured by Saud Kruger, the market leader in civilian-transport vessels. Like Saud Kruger's other ships, the Orca can accommodate a luxury-tier passenger cabin, allowing it to transport passengers in comfort and style. The Orca has not been designed for combat or exploration, however, and its internal compartments cannot accommodate military modules.

The Orca has been designed for large-size landing pads.

outfitting2_description_afmrepaircapacit: The amount of raw material required for repairs that the module can store.

outfitting2_description_armourpenetratio: This rating determines how successful a weapon is going to be at dealing its full raw damage to a target. If this rating is higher than a ship's Armour Rating then it will deal its full raw damage. If not then damage will be reduced proportionally.
outfitting2_description_boottime: The amount of time the module requires to reboot after being powered down.
outfitting2_description_breachdamage: The amount of damage a weapon will deal to modules within a ship if it successfully breaches the hull.
outfitting2_description_brokenregenrate: The rate a shield will regenerate whilst broken and reforming.
outfitting2_description_burstrateoffire: How many shots per second the weapon can achieve within a single burst.
outfitting2_description_burstsize: How many shots are in each burst of weapon fire.
outfitting2_description_cabincapacity: The number of passengers that the cabin can accommodate.
outfitting2_description_cabinclass: The type of accommodation provided by this cabin.
outfitting2_description_cargocapacity: The number of cargo canisters this rack can accommodate.
outfitting2_description_causticresistanc: The module's ability to resist caustic damage to the ship.
outfitting2_description_chaffjamduration: The time the chaff can effectively jam tracking for.
outfitting2_description_class: The overall rating of the module's performance taking all attributes into account for use in rough comparisons.
outfitting2_description_damage: The amount of raw damage per shot.
outfitting2_description_damagefalloffran: The weapon will do full damage out to this range, then damage starts to fall off.

outpostblackknightflee01: Am I too quick for you? Your attacks seem to keep missing.
outpostblackknightflee02: I am too quick for such weak and slow attacks. I had hoped for a more worthy opponent
outpostblackknightflee03: I had hoped for a more worthy adversary, it's a pity you cannot shoot straight, Commander.
outpostblackknightneardeath01: Ha ha, tis only a flesh wound. I shall have you yet.
outpostblackknightneardeath02: OK, we'll call it a draw then.
outpostblackknightneardeath03: I'll give you one last chance to surrender.
outpostblackknightneardeath04: I don't want to have to hurt you.
outpostblackknightneardeath05: Fear not, the Black Knight is never truly defeated. I shall return.
outpostblackknightonarrival01: Good Commander, I'm afraid I cannot let you pass. I have sworn a solemn vow, that no one will pass unless they defeat me in single combat.
outpostblackknightonarrival02: Halt, who goes there? None shall pass, unless they can defeat me in single combat, so I have vowed.
outpostblackknightonarrival03: Who dares challenge the Black Knight? I am invincible.
outpostblackknightonarrival04: You shall not pass, attempt to and thou shall die. I cannot be defeated.
outpostblackknightshieldsdown01: I laugh at thee. A knight needs no shields, we have the stronger armour of knightly honour.
outpostblackknightshieldsdown02: You may think that you have me on the ropes but I chose to cast off my shield. I shall have at thee.
outpostblackknightshieldsdown03: I cast off my shields and will conquer you as a true knight.
outpostblackknightsnapshot02: Prepare yourself for a smiting for I shall smote you good.
outpostblackknightsnapshot03: I jest you not, you shall be defeated.
outpostblackknightunderfire01: Ha! You call that shooting, stop running and I'll show you shooting.
outpostblackknightunderfire02: Thou cannot hope to defeat me. I serve a greater power.
outpostblackknightunderfire03: Face me, Commander, or art thou a coward?
outpostblackknightunderfire04: Turn and face me, Commander, only a coward attacks from behind.
outpostblackknightunderfire05: You will rue the day you encountered the Black Knight... Start rueing!
outpostblackknightunderfire06: Thou should fall on thy sword. Thou cannot hope to win this battle.
outpostblackknightunderfire07: I have you right where I want you. I shall be victorious.
outpostblackknightunderfire08: You fight well for a commoner, Commander, but I have been trained in the arts of true combat. You cannot defeat me.
outpostblackknightunderfire09: Thou must have been at the Onionhead if thou thinks I can be defeated.
outpostblackknightunderfire10: Vile Wretch! I shall teach you the meaning of knightly justice.
outpostpirateraidpiratesonarrival01: We of the Scarlet Banner give you one chance to surrender this station to our control before we take it by force.
outpostpirateraidpiratesonarrival02: This station now belongs to the Scarlet Banner, any opposition will be met with deadly force.
outpostpirateraidpiratesonarrival03: This station now belongs to the Scarlet Banner, bow down before us.
outpostpirateraidpiratesonarrival04: This station is now under the control of the Scarlet Banner. Defiance will be met with death.
outpostpirateraidpiratesonarrival05: All ships attack! I want our people on board now, we're taking that station for the Scarlet Banner.
outpostpirateraidpoliceonarrival01: We've got hostile contacts! Lots of contacts! Defend the station.
outpostpirateraidpoliceonarrival02: Who do these jokers think they are coming here causing a fracas? Let them have it.
outpostpirateraidpoliceonarrival03: Oh hell no! We are not letting this pirate scum take the station. Engage all targets, fire at will.
outpostpoliceraidpiratesonarrival01: You security puppets shouldn't be here, this is our territory. Kill them all!
outpostpoliceraidpiratesonarrival02: Looks like the man has finally caught up with us. But we don't listen to the man out here. Let them have it.
outpostpoliceraidpiratesonarrival03: You want to take this station? Come and get it if you think you're tough enough.
outpostpoliceraidpiratesonarrival04: What is the meaning of this attack, this is a legitimate place of business....ha ha ha ha, can't say this garbage and keep a straight face. Kill them all!
outpostpoliceraidpiratesonarrival05: You've got no jurisdiction out here, Mr Policeman. Better run on home before you get hurt.
outpostpoliceraidpoliceonarrival01: Lead to all security force vessels, it's time we took out the trash. Secure the station and eliminate all wanted targets.
outpostpoliceraidpoliceonarrival02: We've put up with this trash for long enough. Under executive order 615 we are taking control of this station.
outpostpoliceraidpoliceonarrival03: This is an open broadcast to pirate station. We are here under executive order 615 to liberate this station and return it to lawful operations.
outpostpoliceraidpoliceonarrival04: This hive of scum and villainy has been a blight on this sector for too long. Prepare for justice.
outpostpoliceraidpoliceonarrival05: You scumbags have prayed on this sector for long enough. Time you were gone, and I mean really gone. Eliminate all wanted targets!
outpostprotestantipiracyprotestleader01: The only good pirate is a dead pirate!
outpostprotestantipiracyprotestleader02: These lowlifes threaten us, take our goods and worse. How many traders have died just because they wouldn't give up their hard earned cargo? It's time this stopped.
outpostprotestantipiracyprotestleader03: Why should pirates make a profit by taking what is ours? I say hunt them all down and let them eat vacuum.
outpostprotestantipiracyprotestleader04: Our leaders seem to think that pirates are an unavoidable evil in the galaxy. I say line them all up against the wall and shoot them, then we can do the same with the pirates.
outpostprotestantipiracyprotestleader05: The security forces don't seem to be able to stop the pirates from attacking, the so called bounty hunters and hotshot privateers are no better. I say we get the military in here and destroy the pirates at the source. Who's with me?
outpostprotestantipiracyprotestleader06: These pirates are making our lives a living hell. The government should be forced to do something about this.
outpostprotestantipiracyprotestleader07: Our leaders need to grow a pair and deal with this pirate problem now!
outpostprotestantipiracyprotestleader08: I guess the powers that be don't care if pirates take our goods and destroy our ships. It's not their money that is being stolen, it's not their lives at risk. Why should they care?
outpostprotestantipiracyprotestleader09: We know that the galaxy is a dangerous place. We know there are risks in being out here. But our governments need to protect honest pilots from the pirates infesting this sector.
outpostprotestantipiracyprotestleader10: For too long we have put up with the destructive parasite that is piracy infecting our civilisation. Well no more! Let us rise up and rid ourselves of these cockroaches.
outpostprotestantislaveryprotestleader01: Free the slaves! Free the slaves! Free the slaves!
outpostprotestantislaveryprotestleader02: No more slaves. Everyone's soul is created equal and created free. Let them be slaves no more!
outpostprotestantislaveryprotestleader03: Break the chains of oppression, let our people go. End slavery in the Empire today.
outpostprotestantislaveryprotestleader04: Stop slavery now! The power is in your hands to put an end to this barbaric industry. For too many centuries the Empire has grown fat on the blood of slaves. We say no more!
outpostprotestantislaveryprotestleader05: Brothers and sisters, how can you live your lives knowing that a large proportion of our community are held in slavery against their will? We must act to stop this inhuman practice that has corrupted our way of life.
outpostprotestantislaveryprotestleader06: Politicians take notice, your people are speaking out. Stop slavery now, we no longer want to be judged for the actions of our leaders and their reliance on this evil industry.
outpostprotestantislaveryprotestleader07: We will fight until all Imperial citizens are free. Cast off the chains of the slave industry that are strangling our great civilization.
outpostprotestantislaveryprotestleader08: The Empire is cursed to crumble as long as it supports so called legal slavery. Make our Empire the beacon it once was and abandon this barbaric practice.
outpostprotestantislaveryprotestleader09: If we rid ourselves of slavery, we can rid ourselves of the people traffickers, the lawless that would kidnap people from their homes and sell them to the highest bidder. Free the Empire from their grip. Stop slavery!
outpostprotestantislaveryprotestleader10: They say indentured servants owe their masters their lives, but I say it's the so called masters that owe their lives to their indentured slaves. Pay this debt, set them free. Stop slavery!
outpostprotestantiwarprotestleader01: Strike out brothers and sisters and put an end to this destructive conflict that is ripping our galaxy apart. Together we can bring peace to the galaxy.
outpostprotestantiwarprotestleader02: We no longer want to continue fighting the war of the rich and powerful. It is our blood that is being spilled. If they want to make war, let them fight it.
outpostprotestantiwarprotestleader03: Why are we as a species still so hell bent on killing each other? We need to put an end to war and live in peace with one another.
outpostprotestantiwarprotestleader04: We need to stand together and demand a peace plan between all major factions. No More War.
outpostprotestantiwarprotestleader05: Don't be fooled by the rhetoric our leaders pour forth. Change has to come, we need to stop fighting each other.
outpostprotestantiwarprotestleader06: A wise man once said "What is war good for?" The answer..."Absolutely nothing!"
outpostprotestantiwarprotestleader07: War divides us! We are all human beings, we should be working together for the betterment of mankind.
outpostprotestantiwarprotestleader08: There are no winners in this endless conflict. The puppet masters controlling the military don't care about the damage they do to normal citizens.
outpostprotestantiwarprotestleader09: Bring our troops home. There is enough space in the galaxy for every soul. We need to stop the endless conflict.
outpostprotestantiwarprotestleader10: Our leaders are worried about the costs of their constant wars and hike up taxes saying its for our protection. The only thing we need protection from is our war mongering leaders and their genocidal tendencies.
outpostprotestbust01protestleader01: Are we going to sit by and let the fat cats get fatter while we are crushed by the austerity measures they put in place?
outpostprotestbust01protestleader02: Why should we have to put up with these living conditions when the powers that be are to blame for what is happening here? I say they should be the ones to pay, not us.
outpostprotestbust01protestleader03: Why should we have to play the game these powers have created? They think we are just pieces for them to move and sacrifice for their own gain. Well no more! We are the real power, they would be nothing without us.
outpostprotestbust01protestleader04: Rise up brothers and sisters! We are the real power in the galaxy, not our so called leaders. Bring these would be powers to their knees and then they will have to listen to our demands.
outpostprotestbust01protestleader05: Our leaders need to understand that they cannot push us around anymore. We demand fair pay and working conditions and a return of the worker benefits that were stolen from us.
outpostprotestbust01protestleader06: We're mad as hell and we're not going to take it anymore!
outpostprotestbust01protestleader07: Is it our fault that the government has failed. No! Is it our fault that businesses are failing? No! Our leaders need to take responsibility for driving this system into the ground.
outpostprotestbust01protestleader08: I say no more! No more shall we stand by and watch our hard work line the coffers of the rich. No more shall we be downtrodden and abused. No more shall be lose our livelihoods on the whim of politicians and corporate bosses. No more!
outpostprotestbust01protestleader09: We are the people, our voices need to be heard. Politicians and corporate bosses you better listen to us.
outpostprotestbust01protestleader10: Occupy the station my friends. We fight for living wages and benefits for workers. Fair pay for a fair day's work makes the economy grow.
outpostprotestbust01protestleader11: Is it our fault that honest hard working folk can't put food on the table because the big shots take everything from us? No!
outpostprotestbust01protestleader12: I say no more! Stand up and be counted. No more shall we stand by and watch our livelihoods fall into the vacuum of space.
outpostprotestcivilrightsprotestleader01: What gives you the right to tell me how to live my life? Where I can or cannot go, what job I can have, where I can live? I am a human being and I have the right to follow my own path.
outpostprotestcivilrightsprotestleader02: Whatever happened to innocent until proven guilty? Automated crime detection systems have made a mockery of the word justice.
outpostprotestcivilrightsprotestleader03: Constant scans and interdictions are against our rights to free travel between systems! It's a big brother system gone mad.
outpostprotestcivilrightsprotestleader04: We are living in a police state my friends. Security forces are killing with impunity, who makes sure the law makers are obeying the law?
outpostprotestcivilrightsprotestleader05: Who are these powerful organisations that seem to be above the law? They sweep in here and change everything regardless of the impact it has on the people. Well I for one will not bow to these new powers. I have rights!
outpostprotestcivilrightsprotestleader06: What gives the police the right to say what cargo I can have in my ship? I have the right to transport whatever I want. It's my ship!
outpostprotestcivilrightsprotestleader07: Who are these powers to thrust their brand of "Freedom" upon us? "Bow down before us and accept freedom," they cry. Freedom is our right not something that they can give.
outpostprotestcivilrightsprotestleader08: Why should we obey the laws of our so called leaders when they flaunt the law and crush the rights of the honest men and women that live in this system?
outpostprotestcivilrightsprotestleader09: How can security forces blockading systems and locking down stations be legal? Do we not have the right to free movement? Do we not have the right to trade and earn a living? Do we not have the right to live our lives the way we see fit?
outpostprotestcivilrightsprotestleader10: Rise up and be heard, fight for your rights before our so called leaders take them away in the name of freedom.
outpostprotestfamineprotestleader01: More Food! Less War! More Food! Less War! More Food! Less War!
outpostprotestfamineprotestleader02: The crisis is growing out of control while our food supplies decrease more rapidly than ever. Yet our leaders do nothing.
outpostprotestfamineprotestleader03: People are starving and our so-called leaders sit on their hands and make empty gestures of support while they gorge themselves like kings.
outpostprotestfamineprotestleader04: Our leaders should be spending more money on feeding their people rather than supporting war and genocide!
outpostprotestfamineprotestleader05: What good is expanding into new frontiers when we cannot feed ourselves? We can't be in a state of constant growth, it's unsustainable.
outpostprotestfamineprotestleader06: What use are rare goods and gold when it's food and water we need? Why are our markets full of so-called traders peddling wares we don't need when we are starving?
outpostprotestfamineprotestleader07: We can't eat metals, machinery or exotic items. We need food! Why are we still paying traders for these useless items?
outpostprotestfamineprotestleader08: We don't see our leaders running short of food. We don't see their children starving. And why is that? Because the corrupt powers that be are keeping all the food for themselves while they leave us to die.
outpostprotestfamineprotestleader09: Millions of credits have been given in aid to help the victims of this famine. Where is this money you ask? Lining the pockets of our so-called leaders instead of being spent on feeding the people.
outpostprotestfamineprotestleader10: We've all seen the ships full of food and aid arriving, but where have they all gone. Not to the people that need them. We should act now and make our leaders confess to misappropriating this aid.
outpostprotestjoblossesprotestleader01: Jobs for people, not for machines! Jobs for people, not for machines! Jobs for people, not for machines!
outpostprotestjoblossesprotestleader02: Apparently we're no longer cost effective. So they think they can just replace us with robot workers. What happened to a person's right to work?
outpostprotestjoblossesprotestleader03: I say we smash these mechanical monstrosities and take our jobs back.
outpostprotestjoblossesprotestleader04: Why is it always the little guy that gets laid off? Why are we let go when our bosses claim even more profits and grow fat on our hard work?
outpostprotestjoblossesprotestleader05: I'm sick of working for masters that fail to take responsibility for their mistakes, forcing their workers to break themselves to achieve unrealistic goals.
outpostprotestjoblossesprotestleader06: Why should be break ourselves to line the pockets of the rich? Why should we be the first to suffer when things take a downward turn?
outpostprotestjoblossesprotestleader07: Lets see them operate the stations without us. Strike! Strike! Strike!
outpostprotestjoblossesprotestleader08: Why does progress and efficiency always mean that people lose their livelihoods?
outpostprotestjoblossesprotestleader09: Why are our bosses patting themselves on the backs and getting millions of credits in bonuses, while we lose our jobs due to cost cutting? I ask you is that fair?
outpostprotestjoblossesprotestleader10: Strike for greater worker rights! Workers of the galaxy unite!
outpostprotestoutbreakmedsprotestleader0: This outbreak is growing out of control and our leaders seem powerless to stop it. Now we find out that they have been withholding meds. This is unacceptable.
Why don't our leaders give us the meds we need? Why don't they do what needs to be done to cure the sick? Because they don't care, that's why!

There are people dying and the politicians and health agencies still can't provided enough meds. Leaving us to deal with black market scumbags who hike up the prices of vital medicines. We must stand up and make our leaders take responsibility for this mess.

We don't see our leaders running short on meds. We don't see their children falling ill. We don't see their bodies lining the corridors of hospitals. And why is that? Because the corrupt powers that be are keeping all the meds for themselves while they leave us to die.

Why should we be made to suffer, when our so called leaders sit in their ivory towers where they can ignore what is going on. Listen to your people, we need meds urgently or there may not be anyone around to vote for you next election.
We've all seen the ships full of meds arriving, but where have they all gone. Not to the people that need them. We should act now and make our leaders confess to misappropriating this aid.
Our leaders have let us down, we must act for ourselves to get the meds we desperately need.
Millions of credits have been given in aid to help the victims of this outbreak. Where is this money you ask? Lining the pockets of our so-called leaders instead of being spent on crucial medicines.
Why should we lay down and die when our leaders line their pockets with money send to aid the sick?
outpostprotestoutbreakmedsprotestleader1: Where are the medicines promised by the government to help with this crisis? I'll tell you where: the rich are stockpiling them while the common men, women and children get sicker and sicker. That's the real sickness here.
outspanoutoffuelpilot_approached_01: Hello love. I see you on my sensors. Can you help a lady in distress? I just need a little fuel, anything you can spare. I was out looking for a lost Canonn Expedition. If you refuel me I'll tell you where to find them.
outspanoutoffuelpilot_approached_02: Finally someone has heard my message! Thanks lovely. I had started to give up hope. Please help me, I need fuel. I was out looking for a lost Canonn Expedition. If you refuel me I'll tell you where to find them.
outspanoutoffuelpilot_approached_03: To the commander of approaching vessel, please help a lady in need, can you spare some fuel? I was out looking for a lost Canonn Expedition. If you refuel me I'll tell you where to find them.
outspanoutoffuelpilot_approached_04: Please help me, Commander, I've been adrift for days, I'm running low of tea and biscuits. I just need a little fuel to help me get home. I was out looking for a lost Canonn Expedition. If you refuel me I'll tell you where to find them.
outspanoutoffuelpilot_approached_05: I had given up hope that someone would get my signal. I was out looking for a lost Canonn Expedition. Please help. If you refuel me I'll tell you where to find them.
outspanoutoffuelpilot_raided_01: You no good, back stabbing space trash! Just kick a pilot when She's down why don't you. That's it you're going on the list.
outspanoutoffuelpilot_raided_02: I didn't think anyone would be out this far, But I guess scumbags like you are everywhere just looking to take advantage of a situation like this.
outspanoutoffuelpilot_raided_03: You miserable space filth! It's not enough that I'm stranded, now I have to deal with this too?
outspanoutoffuelpilot_raided_04: Well thank you very much! I bet your mother is really proud of you.
outspanoutoffuelpilot_raided_05: Thank you, Commander, for finally proving to me that humanity are the worst species in the galaxy.
outspanoutoffuelpilot_refueled_01: Thank you, Commander. A lot of pilots might not have been so generous. I'm here to find a missing expedition. They are on planet A 4 c in the Col 173 Sector LJ-F C12-0 system. Lat: 23.5 Long:154.87. Can you go find them please?
outspanoutoffuelpilot_refueled_02: Thank you, Commander, you really helped me out there. I'm here to find a missing expedition. They are on planet A 4 c in the Col 173 Sector LJ-F C12-0 system. Lat: 23.5 Long:154.87. Can you go find them please?
outspanoutoffuelpilot_refueled_03: Thank you, Commander, I thought I was a goner for a minute there. You've really saved my bacon. I'm here to find a missing expedition. They are on planet A 4 c in the Col 173 Sector LJ-F C12-0 system. Lat: 23.5 Long:154.87. Can you go find them please?
outspanoutoffuelpilot_refueled_04: Thank you, Commander, you're a real life saver. Happy to see there are some decent human beings out here. I'm here to find a missing expedition. They are on planet A 4 c in the Col 173 Sector LJ-F C12-0 system. Lat: 23.5 Long:154.87. Can you go find them please?
outspanoutoffuelpilot_refueled_05: Thank you, Commander. Glad to see that there are still some decent folks out here in the big black. I'm here to find a missing expedition. They are on planet A 4 c in the Col 173 Sector LJ-F C12-0 system. Lat: 23.5 Long:154.87. Can you go find them please?
outspanoutoffuelpilot_refueled_06: Thank you, Commander, without your help I would have been dead in the water. I'm here to find a missing expedition. They are on planet A 4 c in the Col 173 Sector LJ-F C12-0 system. Lat: 23.5 Long:154.87. Can you go find them please?
outspanoutoffuelpilot_refueled_07: Thanks, Commander. A few more hours and I would have been history. I'm here to find a missing expedition. They are on planet A 4 c in the Col 173 Sector LJ-F C12-0 system. Lat: 23.5 Long:154.87. Can you go find them please?
outspanoutoffuelpilot_refueled_08: Thanks, Commander. It's really lucky you were passing through, I was starting to fear the worst. I'm here to find a missing expedition. They are on planet A 4 c in the Col 173 Sector LJ-F C12-0 system. Lat: 23.5 Long:154.87. Can you go find them please?
outspanoutoffuelpilot_refueled_09: I owe you one, Commander. This fuel should get me back to the Gnosis. I was here to find a missing expedition. They are on planet A 4 c in the Col 173 Sector LJ-F C12-0 system. Lat: 23.5 Long:154.87. Can you go find them please?
outspanoutoffuelpilot_refueled_10: Thank you doesn't seem enough for what you have done, Commander, but it's all I have to give, oh and next time you're near Varati pop in to the Gnosis for a cup of tea. I was here to find a missing expedition on planet A 4 c in the Col 173 Sector LJ-F C12-0 system. Lat: 23.5 Long:154.87. Can you go find them please?
outspanoutoffuelpilot_stationed_01: Hello? Is there anyone out there to help a Canonn member in need? I need fuel. Mayday! Mayday!
outspanoutoffuelpilot_stationed_02: To any commanders in the system, I'm stranded and out of fuel. Please respond.
outspanoutoffuelpilot_stationed_03: Mayday! Can anyone read me? Mayday! This is Lady Outspan of Canonn. I'm out of fuel. Please respond. Mayday!
outspanoutoffuelpilot_stationed_04: I really hope someone can hear this...I forgot my fuel scoop and headed out. A rookie mistake I know, but it can happen to us all from time to time. Currently adrift and in need of assistance. Is there anyone out there reading me?
outspanoutoffuelpilot_stationed_05: Please help... This is Lady Outspan of Canonn. I need fuel.
outspanoutoffuelpilot_stationed_06: Calling any ships in the system... Mayday! This is Lady Outspan of Canonn. I was on a rescue mission for Canonn. Need fuel, adrift and systems failing. Mayday!
outspanoutoffuelpilot_stationed_07: Please help... I need fuel... I'm on my way to investigate a missing Canonn expedition. Please help.
outspanoutoffuelpilot_stationed_08: Mayday! Mayday! This is Lady Outspan of Canonn. Out of fuel and drifting outside an automated relay station. Please help. Mayday!
outspanoutoffuelpilot_stationed_09: Mayday! This is Lady Outspan... The other Canonn members are never going to let me live this down... erm... I'm out of fuel... Please help... Mayday!
outspanoutoffuelpilot_stationed_10: Mayday! In need of immediate assistance. Down to zero fuel. This is so embarrassing. Can anyone help?
outspanoutoffuelpilot_underfire_01: If my ship wasn't crippled I'd turn you to space dust and not for any scientific reason.
outspanoutoffuelpilot_underfire_02: Oh you're brave, shooting at a stranded ship. Is this how you get your kicks?
outspanoutoffuelpilot_underfire_03: Just kick me while I'm down why don't you. I bet your parents are so proud of you.
outspanoutoffuelpilot_underfire_04: Rigth that's it! No biscuits for you?
outspanoutoffuelpilot_underfire_05: Mayday! Out of fuel and under attack. Mayday!

panther_info:
The Panther Clipper LX is one of the largest ships likely to be owned by a private individual. It is also the largest ship that will fit in the internal docking bays of space stations. Piloting one requires real skill. Its cargo carrying capacity is massive, although like most transport ships it is lightly armed and poorly armoured.

This ship requires a large sized landing pad to dock.
panthermkii_armour_grade1_info: Hull reinforcement that provides standard protection against all types of attack.
panthermkii_armour_grade2_info: Hull reinforcement using an advanced structure and higher quality compounds, offering improved protection against all types of attack.
panthermkii_armour_grade3_info: Hull reinforcement using an advanced structure and military-grade compounds, offering superior protection against all types of attack.
panthermkii_armour_mirrored_info: Hull reinforcement using a specially formulated structure, offering superior protection against thermal damage caused by energy weapons. It is vulnerable to projectile weapons and other kinetic attacks.
panthermkii_armour_reactive_info: Hull reinforcement using a dynamically reactive, impact-resistant material offering superior protection against projectile weapons and other kinetic attacks. It is vulnerable to thermal damage caused by energy weapons.
panthermkii_cockpit_info: Transparent protective canopy on a ship's cockpit that shields pilots from the many dangers of space travel.

panthermkii_info:
Zorgon Peterson's first large ship evolves the iconic Panther Clipper design for the modern era. It offers the highest cargo capacity of any non-capital class craft, along with numerous hardpoints across its massive hull to deter pirates. Adaptable stabilisers and specialised drive housing lets the Panther Clipper Mk II make full use of overcharged Frame Shift Drives. Skilled hands will be needed to ease this vessel's bulk through a starport access corridor, however.

The Panther Clipper Mk II has been designed for large-size landing pads.
