pavoniseargrubs_info:
Native to the harsh desert climate, these unpleasant creatures will burrow into any soft surface, including flesh, to avoid the hot sun. Their resemblance of a walking human ear lead to their name. Some slavers use these grubs as a restraining device for their captives, attaching a dormant extra ear to the forehead of their slave that can be remotely triggered.

This rare good is legal in all Feudal markets; Independent, Imperial and Allied Dictatorship markets; Independent and Allied Corporate and Patronage markets; and Imperial and Allied Prison markets.

Please note that if a market’s controlling faction changes, some formerly legal rare goods may become illegal. Should this occur the rare good will be unavailable for sale or purchase at that market for the duration of the prohibiting faction’s tenure.

perpetual_toil_01_body:
Perpetual Toil log #237. Captain Olivia Mara, September 4th 3254.

Another day, another credit. I’m calculating our tonnage and things are looking rosy. The mining crews have outdone themselves this quarter – we're making excellent progress in our asteroid. I've never seen so many gemstones in a single rock. Ten percent on this haul is gonna make everyone real happy.

The new hydroponics dome is finished, so the crew will be able to supplement rations with fresh fruit and vegetables in a few weeks. The logistics chief, Andros, is organising a celebration in the mess hall tonight. I don’t mind saying on record that I’m tired of reheated protein packs. Maybe for our next trip the company will give us sealed meals that look vaguely like the picture on the label? A girl can dream.

One matter to note: Mining Team B stumbled upon a cavern deep in the rock. There’s evidence of liquid dripping down the walls. I've asked for structural surveys before anyone ventures further in there. Our initial scans didn't catch any interior spaces, so I want to be certain that further mining won’t destabilise the surrounding area.

Anyway, that's all for now. I'm heading down to the mess hall. I hope Andros allocated this party some wine.
perpetual_toil_02_body:
Perpetual Toil log #238. Captain Olivia Mara, September 6th.

Mining Crew B, uh... They found something in the cavern.

While the structural surveys were taking place, the shift leader reported a substance seeping from the rock face. ‘Like blood’, she said. At first they thought it was a sealed water reservoir or something, but it wasn’t. I saw the camera feed. It was too thick.

I've now read the eyewitness reports three times and I still don’t know what to make of them. One miner describes an ooze, like unrefined oil. Another swears it was a swarm of insects, crawling and writhing over each other. A third simply logged a single word: ‘Demons’.

Maybe the mind plays tricks down in the dark. But everyone who saw it at least agreed on one thing. It – whatever ‘it’ is - appears to be alive. We’ve collected a sample of the life form. It’s down in the lab now. Science Chief Pendleton is making sure it’s not dangerous. We ran health checks on everyone in Crew B and found nothing concerning. Looks like we got lucky.

I've told no one at the company yet. My gut tells me they’ll shut down this operation and kick everyone off the ship if we report a biological discovery. Meaning we won’t get our cut of the gems we’ve already pulled up. Well, screw that. I’m not letting my crew get shafted by red tape.

I wonder what the bonus would be if we analysed the life form ourselves...?
perpetual_toil_03_body:
Perpetual Toil log #239. Captain Olivia Mara, September 9th.

Okay. I need to get this down while it's still fresh, even though part of me would rather never have to think about it again.

Two days ago, I made the call to send Mining Crew B back into that cavern. Pendleton didn’t find anything dangerous in the sample they collected, and we’ve got a mission schedule to follow. I keep telling myself it was the right thing to do.

This morning Crew B’s shift leader sent a garbled message. Said the life form in the cavern was "moving wrong." Then... nothing. Comms went dead mid-sentence. I sent a security detail after them. Standard procedure: six people, fully equipped for search and rescue.

Three came back.

I've spoken to each and almost wish I hadn't. All three agree Crew B were already dead when they arrived, and that's the only consistent detail they’ll give. Nobody agrees on HOW the miners died! One insists the walls were "breathing." Another keeps watching the corner of the med bay. They can’t stop shaking. I... I don't know what to make of it all.

I've sealed the main access door between us and the asteroid interior. Pulled all other mining crews out. Whatever's in there stays in there, away from my ship.

The company expects an update by the end of the week. My crew will want reassurances that I can't give to them about our safety. And I keep coming back to the same thought, over and over: I sent Crew B back in.

I did that.
perpetual_toil_04_body:
Perpetual Toil log #240. Captain Olivia Mara. September...

Date is... I can't recall.

The life form sample we took. Stored in the lab, behind reinforced glass. That Pendleton swore was contained. It started to hum. A low buzzing at the edge of your hearing, like an itch under your skull that wouldn’t stop. We ran it through every audio filter we had to try and shut it out, but nothing worked. Just a constant hum that crawled under the skin.

People who heard it said it felt like being watched. I just told them to focus and get on with their jobs. Then the life form in the asteroid came passed through the sealed door. Through solid bulkhead. It's on my ship! And it’s slaughtering my crew! The.... The reports coming up from the lower decks aren't reports anymore. They're just screams.

We sent out a distress call. For whatever that's worth I've given the order to get to the shuttles and abandon the Toil. Fewer than a hundred are going to reach them from secured areas.

The rest... the decks where that thing is, I've sealed them. Over half my crew is trapped there.

Save who I can, right? Isn’t that what a captain's supposed to do? Assess the situation. Make hard calls. Think of people as numbers. Follow protocol.

I could hear those still alive crying for help through comms as the shuttles fired up. Begging me to let them into the landing bays. But they already knew the truth.

ph01_tutorial_tutorial_additional_allian: The Alliance is always on the lookout for pilots to take on contracts for its many factions. Its representatives cover the entire political spectrum.
This arguably makes the Alliance the more representative of the three superpowers. The Assembly has largely stayed clear of galactic disputes, too.
The Alliance's devotion to egalitarianism leaves it with no centralised structure, and the Alliance Defence Force has no academy nor ranks.
Many find the Alliance's ethos appealing, however. Independent pilots often accept contracts posted within their space.
ph01_tutorial_tutorial_additional_contro: That function has been temporarily locked.
Your ship is following a preset course. Control will be returned to you soon.
ph01_tutorial_tutorial_additional_empire: If you choose to work with the Empire, I would fully understand. They appreciate what humanity has achieved, after all.
Humanity is the peak of evolution. Look at how far we have come as a civilization, at the marvels that generations of work and sacrifice have yielded.
And those at the top of this society, blessed with privilege and wisdom, demand a certain level of respect.
The Empire recognises this. If the Imperials weren't so socially repressive I may have sought to join them myself.
ph01_tutorial_tutorial_additional_explor: Well, while you're sitting there, perhaps contemplating the vastness of the universe through your canopy, allow me to share a story.
A Commander I once knew decided to embark upon a deep-space exploration trip. He wanted to visit systems that humanity had never before graced.
He outfitted an Asp for the journey, I believe. And then off he went. A calling to explore is not uncommon among Commanders. Perhaps you'll hear it too.
A few months later the man returned. Within days he was taking contracts again, as though he'd never left. No long, boring anecdotes about his trip. No recordings to share. Nothing.
Eventually I asked him about his journey. At first he didn't respond...but then he looked me in the eye and whispered: "We still know nothing."
ph01_tutorial_tutorial_additional_federa: You may decide to offer your services to the Federation. Many do, after all. It is the birthplace of democracy and liberty. One citizen, one vote.
We as individuals have come to expect our voices to be heard, and voting for our government representatives is as good a method as any of ensuring that.
Of course, the influence of corporations on Federal legislation is substantial. Votes are always for sale, and governors can be lobbied.
Fortunately, for independent pilots, this dynamic often results in contracts. The Federation will reward those who serve its interests.
ph01_tutorial_tutorial_additional_refine: Once I had to stop at an old refinery in the Synuefe sector, to collect a stranded diplomat. A mechanical fault had forced her to land.
The locals were covered in grime from their work and exhibited all the charm and intellect of an exhaust manifold.
That said, you should explore every manner of starport, outpost and surface port along your journey...you'll establish where you wish to spend your time soon enough.
ph01_tutorial_tutorial_additional_stealt: A little advice: If the enemy does not know where you are, they'll never disturb your work.
Most pilots nowadays believe that expensive thrusters and a bigger array of weaponry will win battles for them.
Well, one cannot hit what one cannot see. And out in the black, I am a ghost.

Before you start shooting, however, try analysing the megaship with the data link scanner.

Your target will not react until it registers shield damage. Engage when ready.
Of course, the Pilots' Federation is not in the habit of endangering applicants. This ship's damage output has been drastically reduced, presenting minimal risk.

The schematic next to the sensor display shows your target's shield and hull status.
Your laser is a thermal weapon, which is excellent at stripping away a target's shields.
That was the last target. Even if you're planning on a peaceful career, understanding the basics of combat is vital for a pilot's long-term survival.
For advanced combat information you should refer to the Pilot's Handbook, which we'll cover in more detail soon.
Try not to stray too far from the combat area, pilot.
For a successful evaluation, you must demonstrate an ability to defend yourself.
Your firepower greatly outclasses that of your target. Running means you miss out on an opportunity to learn.

Next, you need to activate your weapons by cycling to a different fire group.
You'll notice that your weapons are now listed on your HUD. Fire groups allow you to manage your hardpoints efficiently.
Let's begin the combat evaluation. Destroy several of the canisters.
Your ship has two weapons installed. Make sure you use both your primary and secondary triggers.
Thrusters are particularly useful for navigating around large structures. Why not give them a try?

pirate_onunsatisfactorycargodropped09: You have to make it worth my while.

piratedpassengers03: We have women and children on board, please leave us be!
piratedpassengers04: We have nothing of value on board, this is just a passenger ship.

piratedpassengers06: We can't afford to surrender anything, we'll be putting the health and safety of our passengers at risk!

piratehitman_hunterhostilesc_relevant05: This contract is gonna be easy. Look! They're right there!
piratelord_arrival03: I am wanted, but never taken.
piratelord_arrival04: No system is beyond my grasp.
piratelord_arrival05: My legacy will echo among the stars.
piratelord_arrival06: I am here. Soon you will not be.
piratelord_arrival07: This region is part of my domain.
piratelord_arrival08: All who pass through must pay me fealty.

piratelord_niggledbynewship03: Bravery and stupidity are often the same thing.
piratelord_onauthoritydetection03: There will be no law here.
piratelord_onauthoritydetection04: Out here, I am the law.
piratelord_ondeclarepiracyattack01: You are nothing but dust to me.
piratelord_ondeclarepiracyattack02: You face a glorious death at my hands.
piratelord_ondeclarepiracyattack03: To succumb to my power is nothing to be ashamed of.

piratelord_ondeclarepiracyattack06: You are about to meet your end.

piratelord_ondeclarepiracyattack09: This will not end well for you.

piratelord_onpiratedcargotheft05: Are you so foolish as to steal from me?

piratelord_onsatisfactorycargodropped05: You have just purchased your life.

My needs are great, this cargo does not satisfy them.
piratelord_patrolcoms01: Many have challenged me, now they are nothing but debris.
piratelord_patrolcoms02: None dare claim my bounty. None would be able.
piratelord_patrolcoms04: Wherever I am is my jurisdiction.
piratelord_patrolcoms05: I am a law unto myself.
piratelord_patrolcoms07: No one can challenge me here.
piratelord_patrolcoms08: Do you have something for me?
piratelord_patrolcoms09: It surprises me that people don't learn to keep away.
piratelord_patrolcoms10: Those who don't pay me tribute are destroyed.
pirateraid_agricultural_01: This will make for a fine Onionhead farm!
pirateraid_agricultural_02: The perfect facility to grow the goods!
pirateraid_agricultural_03: Such little security? Time to reap what you sow!
pirateraid_agricultural_04: I can't wait for our first harvest.
pirateraid_agricultural_05: Soon, we'll grow our own Opinion! Pssst... the 'pi' is silent. Ha ha!
pirateraid_agricultural_06: With a facility like this we can breed the perfect strain!
pirateraid_agricultural_07: Soon we'll practically be growing credits!
pirateraid_agricultural_08: Buyers from Anarchy systems parsecs away will be coming here for our product!
pirateraid_agricultural_09: First we exterminate these pests, and then we can farm!
pirateraid_agricultural_10: With this place we can finally stop growing product in my mother's basement! Oops, that shouldn't have been on open comms...
pirateraid_industrial_01: With all of this machinery, we can really enhance our arsenal.
pirateraid_industrial_02: The perfect facility to start developing some real fire-power!
pirateraid_industrial_03: We can even sell dud-modules for high credits. It's not like they'll survive a trip back for a refund...
pirateraid_industrial_04: First we take over this place and then we just force some chumps to build whatever we want!
pirateraid_industrial_05: The boss will reward us heavily for getting him his own production line.
pirateraid_industrial_06: Equipment like this will really further the boss' plans!
pirateraid_industrial_07: Domestic appliances? Evacuation shelters? Why build this junk when you can build guns?
pirateraid_industrial_08: Everyone will be coming here from Anarchy systems parsecs away for the gear we'll build!
pirateraid_industrial_09: Once we start building some real weapons we can blow the lid off this sector!
pirateraid_industrial_10: As soon is this place is ours, our financial situation will see a real BOOM! Ha ha!
pirateraid_police_01: Let's take the man down a notch!
pirateraid_police_02: That shield you wear won't protect you from this!
pirateraid_police_03: Let's play "Pin the Pulse Laser on the Police!".
pirateraid_police_04: This is for all those years I spent locked up!
pirateraid_police_05: Blow a hole in their ship and leave it looking like a doughnut, they'll love it!
pirateraid_police_06: After this, we won't be looking over our shoulders any more...
pirateraid_police_07: Soon we'll be able to work without any of your interference.
pirateraid_police_08: You won't be scanning anyone when you're dead.
pirateraid_police_09: This is for all our buddies you've taken from us!
pirateraid_police_10: This is for always thwarting our business!
pirateraid_scientific_02: Take out the security but leave the lab geeks, we need them.
pirateraid_scientific_03: People will pay a high price for the research we'll take from this place.
pirateraid_scientific_04: With this place we can have scientists build weaponry of the future.
pirateraid_scientific_05: Engineers? Pfft, who needs 'em? We'll have our own personal science team to enhance our modules.
pirateraid_scientific_07: Now we'll control the tech rather than scavenging and stealing scraps!
pirateraid_scientific_08: This facility is now under new management...
pirateraid_scientific_09: My parents always said I should pay more attention to science.
pirateraid_scientific_10: We can stop the futile medical research now, and move you scientists onto developing something that'll make some real money...

platinum_info:
Produced by: Mining only
Consumed by: All except Agri, Refinery, Extraction and Military

Platinum, Pt, atomic number 78. Melting point 2041K. A grey-white precious metal used as a catalyst within many industrial processes, in addition to its value in electronics and luxury goods because of its resistance to corrosion.
platinum_info_short: Produced by: Mining Consumed by: All except Agri, Refinery, Extraction and Military Atomic number 78. Melting point 2041K.
platinumaloy_info:
An ultra-strong metal alloy used in the manufacture of robotics, heavy machinery and weaponry.
Due to the dangerous nature of mining and processing the alloy and fusing it with Platinum, most systems refused to produce it and the technique was almost lost.
Now the factions of the Nahuatl system are the only people with the knowledge to create the metal.

This rare good is legal in all markets.
platinumaloy_info_short: An ultra-strong metal alloy used in the manufacture of robotics, heavy machinery and weaponry. Now the factions of the Nahuatl system are the only people with the knowledge to create the metal.

politicianbadrally01: No one ever helped me get ahead. I started out with an Anaconda and one billion credits and worked my way up.
politicianbadrally02: I'm going to post more security ships all around the system. And cut spending on security, too. It's a win-win. Trust me.
politicianbadrally03: Some of you might think politicians are corrupt. Well if having all the power, all the money and no morals is corrupt, then we're corrupt.
politicianbadrally04: I will never apologise for being richer and more powerful than the little people. Some of us are meant to lead and some of you are meant to follow.
politicianbadrally05: People don't want to know the truth, they just want to get the job done. If I'm elected I'll get the job done.
politicianbadrally06: I will make this system a galactic powerhouse. I will make jobs, I will make war, I will make money.
politicianbadrally07: The truth is overrated. If I wanted to tell the truth I would not have become a politician.
politicianbadrally08: Leading is not about listening, it's about doing. A vote for me is a vote for action.
politicianbadrally09: It's not a question of morality, it's a question of results. I'm here to make the hard choices, can my opponent say that?
politicianbadrally10: Unlike my opponents, I will do whatever it takes to give this system the success it deserves. Whatever it takes!
politiciangoodrally01: I want to help the people, we need jobs, we need equality. We need to shake up politics and get rid of corruption.
politiciangoodrally02: It's money, money, money in government. That needs to change. Whatever happened to ideas, principles and working for the people?
politiciangoodrally03: If we work together and stay on the right path, eventually we will make progress happen.
politiciangoodrally04: The first duty of politicians is to protect the people, not run their lives. We must fight for our rights as citizens.
politiciangoodrally05: If you think that the government is running the show you are a fool. It's the corporations and the money men that hold all the power.
politiciangoodrally06: Elect me and I promise to put an end to corruption and stop this destructive conflict we all face.
politiciangoodrally07: Sooner or later the people will realise that the government does not care about them. All it cares about is keeping and expanding its own power.
politiciangoodrally08: We politicians are not perfect, but the least we can be is honest. Can my opponents commit to that?
politiciangoodrally09: I may not be right all the time, but at least I can say I'm morally right in what I do. I promise to always do the right thing.
politiciangoodrally10: If elected I will give the power back to the people. Government is there to serve the people. People should not have to serve the government.

pow_ppcontr_helpbody:
Fortifying systems makes them more stable meaning they cost less upkeep so there is more capital to be spent on other activates.

In general you should fortify the systems with the highest upkeep cost. Fortification is not automatic you need to reach the trigger level and ensure that the value exceeds any undermining that is happening.

 Not all systems are as easy to fortify as others. Distance from your Power's headquarters' population, and how aligned the governments that make up the exploited systems, are factored into the cost. However, should undermining succeed the upkeep of the system will be increased, reducing the capital available to spend.

Undermining can potentially result in a deficient putting a number of the Power's systems into a state of turmoil.

If the deficit is not rectified in the second week then the systems in turmoil are lost.
pow_ppcontr_overvundrbody:
If you are looking to undermine other Powers rather than fortify your own then contacts in those systems will provide details of the activities required.

You can also find out how to undermine a Power by looking at the control overview of that Power.

The nature of the undermining depends on the Power that is being undermined and your Power's relationship with them.

Successfully undermining the Power will increase the amount of capital available for upkeep. This reduces their capabilities and potentially gives them a deficit, plunging some of their systems into turmoil.

pow_ppexpa_helpbody:
The final step to create a control system is expansion. The difficulty of expansion is determined by distance from your Power's headquarters, the system's population and the government types in the surrounding systems.

Expansion is not guaranteed, should you fail to reach the trigger value, or the opposition outmatch your total, the system will be lost. If your expansion zone overlaps another system that is successfully expanded both expansions will fail. You will need to undermine any of these candidates to ensure success.

Once successfully expanded you will be able to exploit the systems in the area.

Should your exploitation zone overlap that of another Power the systems in the overlap are conflicted and will not provide any capital, reducing the profit of both control systems.

Expanding in to areas where upkeep outweighs the return is a risky strategy as it could put you in to a deficit.

The final step to create a control system is expansion. How hard it is to expand is determined by distance from your Power's Headquarters, the system's population and the government types in the system.

Expansion is not guaranteed, should you fail to reach the trigger value, or the opposition out matches you, then the system will be lost. If your exploitation zone overlaps another system that is successfully expanded then both expansions will fail. You will need to oppose any of these candidates to ensure success.

Once successfully expanded the Power can exploit the systems in the volume. Should your exploitation zone overlap that of another Power the systems in the overlap are conflicted and will not provide any capital and so reduce the profit of both control systems.

Expanding into areas where upkeep outweighs the return is a risky strategy as it could put you into a deficit.

pow_ppprep_helpbodyb:
Preparing a system is the first step in bringing it under control of a Power.

The best systems are the ones that provide the most capital for the least upkeep. The further away the system is from the Power's headquarters and the larger the population then the harder it is going to be to acquire. It will also require more capital to control.

In order to manage our efforts, systems must reach the preparation trigger before we start to action them.

Once the trigger level is reached it is ranked against others, if its preparation value is in the top ten it will appear on the Power's preparation screen.

Only the top ten systems are eligible for expansion.

Once a system is in the top ten you can choose to nominate it, helping to push it further up the ranks. 

Powers only have a limited amount of capital to spend so not every system can be successfully prepared.

Once triggered, and you have the capital, only two things can stop you. First, other Powers can try and prepare the same system. If their preparation value exceeds yours the system will have been lost along with the capital invested in the expansion.

Secondly, if your system is near a system that is being expanded into and the expansion is successful then preparation will fail.

power_help_cycles_1: Powerplay operates in “cycles”. Each cycle lasts a week, at the end of which all actions for the cycle are resolved.
power_help_cycles_2: During each cycle, Powers manage Command Capital (CC for short). This resource is collected from systems under their sway, and used to purchase expansion attempts into uncontrolled systems, as well as keep hold of systems they already control.
power_help_cycles_3: CC is the lifeblood of a Power; if it starts a cycle with a CC deficit, systems under its control will begin to fall into turmoil, ultimately shaking off control if they remain in turmoil when the cycle ends.
power_help_cycles_4: At the end of each cycle, the Powers are ranked in order of galactic standing based on their territory and actions that occurred that cycle. Powers with high standing enjoy enhanced benefits, whilst Powers with the lowest standing are in danger of collapsing altogether, vanishing in ruin.
power_help_expansion_1: At the start of a cycle, any expansion attempts purchased in the previous cycle become active.
power_help_expansion_2: Supporters complete expansion tasks to secure successful expansion into the system, potentially facing direct opposition from ships pledged to opposing Powers. Supporters can oppose expansion attempts of any Power.
power_help_expansion_2b: Use the Powerplay Expansion view on the Galaxy Map to see where they are expanding or look at the Powers expansion tab to see a list of locations and how to oppose them.
power_help_expansion_3: Different Powers use different ethoses when attempting to expand into a system. Depending on the prevailing government types in charge of nearby systems the threshold for success may increase of decrease. Distance also increases the challenge.
power_help_expansion_4: At the end of the cycle, if enough expansion tasks have been completed to satisfy the success threshold and overcome opposition, the system will become a control system for the Power.
power_help_expansion_4b: All unsuccessful expansions at the end of the cycle are lost.
power_help_expansion_5: Control systems are vital; each one exploits all nearby systems, collecting CC income from them at the end of each cycle. Exploited systems are also protected against preparation or expansion from opposing Powers.
power_help_expansion_6: If a system is close enough to be exploited by control systems of opposing Powers, it is considered contested and provides no income.
power_help_expansion_7: Control systems require an amount of CC upkeep to maintain their status. This is automatically deducted at the end of each cycle. The further away a control system is from a Power's homeworld and the greater the number of control systems they have, the higher its upkeep.
power_help_fortification_1: Each cycle, supporters can complete fortify tasks for a control system in order to reduce the amount of CC upkeep it will require for the following cycle.
power_help_fortification_2: Like expansion attempts, different Powers have different ethoses when it comes to fortification, which may make success easier or more difficult depending on the prevailing government types of nearby systems. Distance also affects this difficulty.
power_help_fortification_3: Fortification is extremely useful; the CC it saves can both help a Power purchase higher cost expansion attempts and prevent the Power from running a CC deficit that would otherwise cause control systems to fall into turmoil, threatening the Power's progress.
power_help_fortification_4: Supporters of any opposing Power can complete undermining tasks to destabilise a control system. If the system's fortification trigger has not been met at the end of the cycle but the undermine has, then the system's income will be added to its upkeep.
power_help_fortification_5: At the end of a cycle, if the fortification trigger is met and undermining has not hit its trigger, there will be no upkeep to pay, next cycle.
power_help_fortification_6: If triggers for both fortify and undermine are met, then there will be no change to the upkeep.
power_help_fortification_7: All unsuccessful fortification and undermining at the end of the cycle is lost.
power_help_fortification_7b: Use the Powerplay Control view on the Galaxy Map to see which systems are being fortified or undermined or look at the Powers control tabs.
power_help_overview_1: Powers represent charismatic, influential individuals and organisations, intent in claiming known space for their own ends.
power_help_overview_2: Once you have ranked up in one of the Pilots' Federation ranks you can pledge to support a Power, helping them expand into new systems, protecting systems already under their control and undermining the efforts of opposing Powers.
power_help_overview_3: You might choose to support a Power based on its superpower affiliation, supporter rewards which increase the more you help the Power, or simply because you agree with its ethos or like its leader.
power_help_overview_4: You can only pledge support to a single Power, but you can withdraw your support at any time, or even defect directly to an opposing Power!
power_help_preperation_1: Before a Power can take control of a system it must be prepared. Only systems that are not controlled, exploited by another Power or in the radius of a system in expansion can be prepared.
power_help_preperation_2: In addition, a Power must have enough CC to purchase an expansion attempt for the system before it can be prepared. Systems that are too expensive are hollow on the powerplay expansion view in the Galaxy Map; the further away a system is from a Power's home world and the higher the population, the more expensive this cost will be. Good systems for expansion are highlighted in green on the powerplay expansion view in the Galaxy Map.
power_help_preperation_3:
Successfully completing preparation tasks for a system will increase its preparation value. At the end of the cycle the Power will purchase expansion attempts, beginning with the most prepared system, until it runs out of CC or successfully purchases all of the top ten most prepared systems. 

More than one Power can prepare a system at the same time. Preparation can occur for multiple Powers in systems that would be within each other's potential 15 light year exploitation radius. In both cases, at the end of the cycle, the Powers that can afford the expansion attempt cost, the one that completed the most preparation will win, whilst all other preparation fails and the command capital invested is lost.
power_help_preperation_3b: All unsuccessful preparation at the end of the cycle is lost.
power_help_preperation_4: Each cycle, you can vote for preparation or consolidation in the overview entry on the preparation tab. You can only vote once you have been pledged and active for more than a month, and you can only vote once each cycle.
power_help_preperation_5: Depending on the ratio of votes, the consolidation entry will move up the top ten preparation list. At the end of the cycle, any systems placed below the consolidation entry will not be elegible for expansion. Any CC blocked by consolidation will be used to increase the undermine success trigger for your systems in the following cycle.
power_help_stats_1: The stats tab shows you useful information about a selected Power, including what kinds of effects they impose on systems they control or exploit.
power_help_successfailure_1: At the end of each powerplay cycle both the Power's standing, CC reserve and each supporters rating within it is computed.
power_help_successfailure_2: If a Power has a CC deficit, not only will it have no CC to carry out preparation, its control systems will be placed into turmoil. The highest upkeep control system is chosen first and its upkeep cost is removed, then the next highest and so on, until the Power no longer has a CC deficit.
power_help_successfailure_3: Any control system already in turmoil at the end of a cycle is lost to the Power and reverts to uncontrolled status.
power_help_successfailure_4:
Your Rating is awarded at the end of each cycle based on how many Merits you have earned from supporting your Power through activities like expansion, preparation, fortification and undermining.

At the end of every cycle you are given a credit bonus in the form of a voucher, the value of which depends on your current rating. Handing in items and vouchers for your Power is also remunerated at a basic level at the point of hand in.
power_help_successfailure_5: As your rating increases, additional Powerplay cargo is made available, as well as increased preparation votes. Each Power has one or more unique benefits. Such benefits might include reduced costs in outfitting or increased rewards for bounties.
power_help_successfailure_6: You can see what the pledge benefits are for a Power by looking at the Pledge tab for the Power in the Powerplay interface.
power_help_successfailure_7: Each Power is ranked relative to all other Powers; territory size, successful preparations and expansions increasing its standing, whilst control systems falling into turmoil or out of control reducing it.
power_help_successfailure_8: Powers at the top end of galactic standing enjoy increased supporter perk benefits.
power_help_successfailure_9: Powers at the bottom end of galactic standing are at risk of collapsing and being removed. Supporters can stave off such an ignominious end by ensuring expansion occurred during the cycle.
power_help_supporter_1: As a supporter pledged to a Power there are special rules to be aware of.
power_help_supporter_2: When in a system controlled or exploited by a Power aligned with a different superpower than your own Power, you can be attacked on sight without penalty and responding will likely be committing a crime.
power_help_supporter_3:
This works both ways: when in a system controlled or exploited by your own Power, you may freely attack vessels pledged to a Power whose superpower alignment is different to your Power. 

If you destroy a ship allied to your Power, or one associated with a Power of the same superpower, you will be reprimanded for Treachery and your Merits and potential Rating reduced.
power_help_supporter_4: Just because two Powers are aligned with the same major faction does not mean that they will not want to oppose each other's ambitions. Normally, such opposition requires tasks that are slightly more covert and less lethal. However, remember that taking such actions will require you to commit crimes.
power_help_supporter_5: As a supporter you may defect to another Power. Doing so allows you to retain some amount of rating with the Power you join. Such actions have consequences; you may be hunted by your previous Power for a time after defection. In destroying these hired attackers you will not be reprimanded for Treachery even if they were associated with the same superpower.
power_help_supporter_6: You can choose to withdraw support for a Power at any time. If you do so, there is a cooling off period before you can pledge to a Power again.

powerplay_hub_help_pagetitle_1: You Are Now A Powerplay Agent
powerplay_hub_help_text_1:
Welcome onboard Commander! You’re now an active agent in Powerplay, with all the benefits and risks the role offers.

At its heart, Powerplay is a strategic game of dominance and control.

Each Power seeks to expand its territory into new systems, whilst maintaining and reinforcing control over its own systems. Agents further their Powers goals by completing Powerplay activities in systems. These activities often involve visiting a Power contact at a port, these operatives can be found in the contacts menu at ports in systems involved in Powerplay. A full list of Powerplay Activities can be found in the Pilot’s Handbook.

As Powers gain control of systems, they become more dominant, this is reflected in their position on the Power Standings. Conversely, losing control of systems will result in a drop in standing.
powerplay_hub_help_text_2:
Systems controlled by a Power can be in one of three states; Exploited, Fortified and Stronghold.

The first level of control Exploited indicates that the Power has a foot hold in the system. Critically this level of control is particularly weak, Exploited systems only remain under a Power’s control at the end of the cycle if they are within range of a friendly Fortified or Stronghold system.

A Power can solidify their control within a system by completing Reinforcement activities. If sufficient reinforcement activities are performed the state will move from Exploited to Fortified. Further Reinforcement will establish the system as a Stronghold.

Strongholds are candidates for harbouring special fleet carrier groups, exclusively accessible by Agents of the controlling Power. These offer access to improved outfitting and shipyard inventories when compared to most ports.

There is a cap to how much a system can be reinforced in a single cycle meaning that only one reinforcement level can be achieved per weekly Powerplay cycle
powerplay_hub_help_text_3:
Systems controlled by a Power – including your own - can be Undermined by rival agents.

Undermining activities work counter to reinforcing activities and can reduce a Power's control by up to one level per weekly cycle. 

Controlled systems are harder to undermine depending on how developed the system is and how far behind the controlling Power’s front line it is situated.

Reinforcing and Undermining activities can cancel each other out creating a tug-of-war between Powers vying for a system. The Power that applies the most effort will move the level of control in their direction.
powerplay_hub_help_text_4:
Exploited systems that are fully Undermined will become Uncontrolled.

Undermining Fortified or Stronghold systems can cause knock-on consequences if they are the only systems supporting Exploited systems with the associated Exploited systems collapsing and becoming Uncontrolled.

Uncontrolled systems are prime targets for Acquisition, providing they reside within the control range of one of your Power’s Fortified or Stronghold systems.

Agents performing appropriate activities in a suitable Uncontrolled system add weight to a race for control. To take control a Power must reach a control score threshold and be ahead in the control race at the end of the cycle. If no Power completes Acquisition in a cycle the race continues in the next cycle.

Multiple Powers actively seeking to expand into an Uncontrolled system will enter into conflict with each other if the Conflict Threshold is reached by at least two Powers.
powerplay_hub_help_text_5:
Weekly Assignments are tasks set by your Power.

These will help you achieve certain goals to further your Power’s control, while offering merits as a reward.

Merits increase your loyalty level, granting access to various perks, module unlocks and cosmetic rewards.

Agents who earn the most merits during a weekly cycle will be displayed on your Power’s Leaderboard and receive even greater rewards for their efforts.

To gain access to the loyalty system and leaderboards, you must complete the initial set of assignments offered after pledging to your Power.

Beyond Weekly Assignments, Agents will receive Merits by performing any Reinforcing, Undermining or Acquisition activities for their Power. Reinforcing activities will generally reward less merits than Undermining and Acquisition.
powerplay_hub_help_text_6:
To review this information in greater detail, you can view the Powerplay article in the Pilot’s Handbook.

This is found in the Codex, available through the internal interface panel while in a ship’s cockpit or the Insight Hub of your suit while disembarked.

powerplay_map_help_text_1: The Powerplay map mode displays information on the territory each Power controls. This map mode will display the current landscape of the galaxy as Powers acquire control of new systems, change control state within systems they influence, or lose systems due to rival undermining efforts.
powerplay_map_help_text_2: The Powerplay map mode panel offers customisation of the data displayed in the galaxy map. The display can filter individual Powers and system control states with a simple click, offering a customisable overview of the core system’s Powerplay composition and a quick comparison of each Power’s territorial footprint.
powerplay_map_help_text_3: The Powerplay information panel displays system information relevant to Powerplay. The control state of the system is shown along with contextual information for that state. Information about activities you can do to either advance your chosen Power’s interests or undermine an opposing Power in the system are shown along with the option to display this system with the Strategic View overlay (see next page).
powerplay_map_help_text_4: The Strategic View shows a system’s relationship with nearby systems based on its Control State. If the system is in the Fortified or Stronghold control state, the control radius of the system will be shown by a blue sphere. Dotted lines will link to all nearby friendly controlled systems, while solid lines to link to all uncontrolled systems in range. If the system is exploited or uncontrolled, the maximum control radius will be displayed along with lines to controlled systems within this area, showing the systems that can/do control it.
powerplay_map_help_text_5: When targeting an unoccupied or contested system, the Powerplay Information panel will display which Powers have a controlled system within range. These Powers are considered eligible to take control of the system. If two or more Powers pass the conflict threshold then the system will enter the contested state. All Powers that reached the threshold will populate in conflict zones, while allowing supporters to use two additional ethos activities in the system. A Power can acquire and thus gain control of the system by passing the minimum control score threshold, though if more than one Power achieves this in a weekly cycle then the Power with the highest score will acquire the system. If no Powers are past the minimum control threshold for a weekly cycle, then the system will not change state.
powerplay_map_help_text_6:
A short glossary of terms for the Powerplay map filters:

Unoccupied – Systems which are not currently controlled by any Power, and are prime candidates for expansion.
Expansion – An uncontrolled system within the range of a Power’s Fortified or Stronghold system where expansion efforts are underway. Acquisition activities are valued here.
Contested – A system where two or more Powers are actively competing for control. Conflict zones can be expected here.
Exploited – A system where your Power has a low level of control. Reinforcement activities are valued here.
Fortified – A system where your Power has a high level of control. Reinforcement activities are valued here.
Stronghold – A system where your Power has a significant level of control. Reinforcement activities are valued here.
powerplay_not_pledged: You are not pledged to a Power yet.
powerplay_pledge_help_text_1:
At the height of humanities history in the 34th century, the political landscape was dominated by three Superpowers: The Federation led by democratically elected Presidents, their long-time waring rivals, the Empire, dynastically maintained by hereditary monarchies, and the Alliance which emerged from a much larger coalition of independent systems united politically by a desire for stability.

Whilst these Superpowers were a dominating force, they were not themselves unified. Each Superpower was itself built from sub-factions known as Powers. Even though these Powers may have been ideologically aligned in some cases their charismatic leaders also had their own agendas. These tensions between Powers, and indeed Superpowers, led to an era of territorial conflict.

This was known as Powerplay.
powerplay_pledge_help_text_2:
Powerplay represents the continuous struggle for dominance and prestige in populated star systems.

Powers seek to establish control over a system, undermine the efforts of rival Powers eager to do the same, and reinforce controlled areas to maintain superiority.

By pledging to a Power, you enter a competitive environment full of challenges, danger and opportunity.

Whether you prefer combat, covert operations, research or trade, weekly assignments allow you to further your Power’s cause and earn rewards or you can choose your own path by performing Power appropriate actions in target systems.
powerplay_pledge_help_text_3:
On the Pledge screen, you can review each of the 12 Powers to find one with an Ethos fitting your playstyle.

A list of earn-able loyalty rewards offered by each Power is also presented here.

Once pledged to a Power you’ll be able to help your power vie for territory, earn merits to gain ranks, and complete weekly assignments – but be careful, since you’ll also be considered hostile by rival Powers!

pp2_assignment_commitcrimes_description:
Perform criminal acts in $#Poweraction; systems to gain bounties against you. While the bounty will make you unpopular in the system, your unlawful actions will undermine the authority of system's controlling Power. 

Refer to the Crime and Punishment article in the Pilot's Handbook for more information on criminal acts and related punishments.
pp2_assignment_commitcrimes_objective: Gain a bounty of $#value; credits in rival Power systems.
pp2_assignment_emppoldata_combat_complet: Congratulations! Your quota of Employee and Political data from $#Poweraction; systems is complete.
pp2_assignment_emppoldata_combat_name: Recover Employee and Political data from $#Poweraction; systems
pp2_assignment_emppoldata_combat_objecti: Obtain $#value; units of Employee and Political data from $#Poweraction; systems and hand it in at a friendly system.
pp2_assignment_emppoldata_preparation_de:
Employee and Political data for this task can be collected from data points in Odyssey settlements located within Acquisition systems. Hand this data in to any system friendly to your Power that has the target Acquisition system within its expansion range.

Either data type will count towards your progress.

Be careful that you are not identified by security forces in the area.

Acquirable systems can be found via the Acquisition map view mode, in the Powerplay tab of the Galaxy Map. For more information on Acquisition, see the Powerplay article in the Pilot's Handbook.

Refer to the Settlements article in the Pilot's Handbook for more information on accessing data ports.
pp2_assignment_emppoldata_undermining_de:
Employee and Political data for this task can be collected from data points in Odyssey settlements located within systems targeted for Undermining by your Power. Hand this data in to any system friendly to your Power.

Either data type will count towards your progress. 

Be careful that you are not identified by security forces in the area.

Refer to the Settlements article in the Pilot's Handbook for more information on accessing data ports.
pp2_assignment_escapepods_complete: Congratulations! Your transport quota of escape pods has been reached.
pp2_assignment_escapepods_description:
Collect Occupied Escape Pods and Damaged Escape Pods in $#Poweraction; systems and return them to the  Search and Rescue contact at any system friendly to your Power.

Refer to the Trade and Smuggling article in the Pilot's Handbook for more information on transporting cargo between markets.
pp2_assignment_escapepods_objective: Collect $#value; escape pods from #Powerstate; systems and return them to a friendly system.
pp2_assignment_escapepods_preparation_de:
Collect escape pods in $#Poweraction; systems and return them to the Search and Rescue contact at any system friendly to your Power that has the target Acquisition system within its expansion range.

Acquirable systems can be found via the Acquisition map view mode, in the Powerplay tab of the Galaxy Map. For more information on Acquisition, see the Powerplay article in the Pilot's Handbook.

Refer to the Salvage and Rescue article in the Pilot's Handbook for more information on transporting escape pods to starport contacts.
pp2_assignment_explorationdata_complete: Congratulations! Your exploration data target has been reached.
pp2_assignment_explorationdata_descripti:
Redeem exploration data at a Universal Cartographic contact in any $#Poweraction; system. Data from any system will count towards the targets. This includes detailed surface scans.

Refer to the Exploration article in the Pilot's Handbook for more information on hacking settlement consoles.
pp2_assignment_explorationdata_objective: Hand in $#value; credits worth of exploration data in any $#Poweraction; system.
pp2_assignment_heists_complete: Congratulations! Your heist quota of $#item; has been reached.
pp2_assignment_heists_description:
Quantities of $#item; can be found at Odyssey settlements. The items will be contained in lockers, typically behind a pass code. You'll need to uncover the pass code using local terminals, assuming you can acquire the correct authority level. Alternatively, you can use an e-breach to hack into a locked container.

Be careful that you are not identified by security forces in the area. E-breaches are grounds for a hostile security response if caught.

Refer to the Settlements article in the Pilot's Handbook for more information on finding & accessing containers.
pp2_assignment_heists_objective: Acquire $#value; $#item; from #Powerstate; systems and return them to a friendly system.
pp2_assignment_holohacks_complete: Congratulations! Your quota of holoscreen hacks has been fulfilled.
pp2_assignment_holohacks_description:
Holographic adverts can be hacked to display promotional images of your Power. This promotes awareness in locations your Power controls, is contesting or has targeted for acquisition. 

Holoscreens outside of ports can be manipulated using a hack limpet. An appropriate limpet controller and supply of limpets will be required to do so.

Using hack limpets will incur a fine, so be careful!
pp2_assignment_holohacks_objective: Hack $#value; holographic adverts at ports in $#Poweraction; systems.
pp2_assignment_holohacks_preparation_des:
Holographic adverts can be hacked to display promotional images of your Power. This promotes awareness in locations your Power controls, is contesting or has targeted for Acquisition. 

Holoscreens outside of ports can be manipulated using a hack limpet. An appropriate limpet controller and supply of limpets will be required to do so.

Using hack limpets will incur a fine, So be careful!

pp2_assignment_organicdata_complete: Congratulations! Your organic data target has been reached.
pp2_assignment_organicdata_description:
Redeem organic data with a Vista Genomics vendor in any $#Poweraction; system. Any data collected with the genetic sampler tool will contribute to the target. 

Genetic samplers are part of the Artemis suit loadout, so be sure to equip this prior to departure. This suit can be purchased from any Pioneer Supplies vendor.

Refer to the Suits and Equipment article in the Pilot's Handbook for more information on using the genetic sampler.
pp2_assignment_organicdata_name: Hand in organic data at $#Poweraction; systems
pp2_assignment_organicdata_objective: Hand in $#value; worth of organic data in any $#Poweraction; system.
pp2_assignment_powerkills_complete: Congratulations! Your quota of enemy Power vessel kills in $#Poweraction; systems is complete.
pp2_assignment_powerkills_description:
Hunt vessels pledged to a rival in $#Poweraction; systems. Scanning a vessel will reveal whether they are pledged to a Power. Destroying rival Power vessels will award merits and contribute to your Power's local progress or undermining efforts.

Refer to the Bounty Hunting article in the Pilot's Handbook for more information on identifying and engaging ships.

pp2_pledgeconfirmation_body:
Pledging to a Power allows you earn merits with them. Completing tasks to support the Power will increase your rank, unlocking various rewards and perks.

Be aware that pledging will allow other ships to identify which Power you have pledged to, and you'll be marked as hostile to opposing Powers.

pp2_pledging_pledgeweighting_desc:
Pledge weighting refers to the level of challenge presented by popular Powers. It is harder to earn higher individual rewards from well-supported Powers due to the increased level of competition in gaining higher ranks. 

The top 4 Powers in the standings will pay out more credits each week. Supporters must consider whether they can reach the upper ranks of these Powers to profit from those payments - or whether to seek higher ranks with less popular Powers instead.

pranavantal_overview_control_ethos: Where most other powers have a significant corporate interest attached to them, Utopia advocates the sharing of knowledge and values for societal reasons over financial ones. The allure of abandoning the chase for credits to join a community of dreamers is attractive.
pranavantal_overview_description: Simguru Pranav Antal, leader of the Utopia movement, is generally considered more commercially minded than his predecessor Rishi Antal. Critics condemn him as a plutocrat with only a superficial interest in Utopia's free technological development ideals. His supporters, by contrast, paint him as combining the wisdom of his father with a shrewd commercial nous. Regardless, both sides agree that Utopia has undergone significant change under Pranav's leadership.
pranavantal_overview_expansion_ethos: While Pranav’s primary focus is future technology, he is not oblivious to the advantages of cultivating a marketable public persona in the here and now. His followers are encouraged to promote Utopia’s ambitions and ideology to reinforce his popularity.
pranavantal_overview_preparation_ethos: Utopian ideals of a free technological movement are promoted heavily to system factions. The promises of increased scientific benefits for local populations are often well received by prospective members.
pranavantal_overview_quotation1: The Sim Archive is an opportunity so vast that most people fail to comprehend it. When they hear ‘the next step of human evolution,’ they assume it’s a marketing slogan. One day, the truth of that description will be apparent.
pranavantal_overview_quotation2: Utopia is part societal movement, part scientific paradise and part leap of faith. The willingness of each member to commit all our creative energy towards a unified technological ambition is a uniquely beautiful thing.
pranavantal_overview_quotation3: I never much cared for Sirius Corporation’s business model. While their products are generally of acceptable quality, the billions of people they have exploited and bullied to create them is repulsive.
pranavantal_overview_quotation4: Transcendence is a vital component of our collective rebirth, free of our base desires and temptations. My father pioneered the idea that our consciousness could be far more potent when unshackled from our physical form. I am honoured to now expand upon those ideas.
pranavantal_overview_quotation5: Some have accused Utopia of being deliberately enigmatic. I disagree. A commune of a hundred billion members is far too big to hide. But I have elected to guard our greatest triumphs until humanity is ready to accept them.
praseodymium_info:
Produced by: Mining only
Consumed by: High Tech and Industrial

Praseodymium, Pr, atomic number 59. Melting point 1208K. This is a soft and malleable metal. It is a rare mineral used for a variety of purposes including: a component in enhanced magnets, an alloy component for metals and laser optics.
praseodymium_info_short: Produced by: Mining Consumed by: High Tech and Industrial Praseodymium, Pr, atomic number 59. Melting point 1208K.
preciousgems_info: These materials have inherent value. They are very useful in maintaining stability in otherwise volatile economies. Alongside the wealth factor, precious gems and metals play a significant role in the generation of extravagant status symbols.
preciousgems_info_short: These materials have inherent value. They are very useful in maintaining stability in otherwise volatile economies.
precipitatedalloys_info:
Component found in ships: frequently used by military and authority vessels.

Precipitated alloys provide extra hardening over standard alloys.
precipitatedalloys_info_short: Component found in ships: frequently used by military and authority vessels.
preflightcheck_backwardkeydesc:
Operates your ship's main propulsion thrusters.

Throttling down causes your ship to slow down or travel directly backwards depending on the amount of throttle set.
preflightcheck_boostdesc:
Activates emergency thruster sequence, colloquially named 'boost'.

For a short time, your main propulsion thrusters will gain a significant speed increase.

Emergency thrust drains ENG capacitor power, and requires a minimum amount of ENG capacitor power to initiate.
preflightcheck_contactdesc:
Locks vessels into your ship's targeting system.

Repeated use cycles through all contacts.
preflightcheck_deployhardpointsdesc:
Deploys and retracts all hardpoints on your ship.

Hardpoints must be deployed before weapons fitted to them can be operated.

Your ship's frame shift drive cannot operate while hardpoints are deployed.
preflightcheck_forwardkeydesc:
Operates your ship's main propulsion thrusters.

Throttling up causes your ship to travel directly forwards, accelerating based on the amount of throttle set.
preflightcheck_fsddesc:
Initiates your ship's frame shift drive.

With no destination system selected, engaging the frame shift drive will initiate supercruise, allowing you to traverse the system at superluminal speed.

Engaging the frame shift drive with a destination system will initiate a hyperspace jump.

Engaging the frame shift drive while a jump or supercruise is already charging will cancel the procedure, and exit supercruise if already active.
preflightcheck_heatsinkdesc:
Launches a heatsink, if fitted.

When activated, heatsink ejectors purge your ship's heat into a heatsink, then eject it from the vessel. Note that the purge takes a short while to complete.
preflightcheck_hostilecontactdesc:
Locks hostile vessels into your ship's targeting system.

Repeated use cycles through all hostile contacts.
preflightcheck_landinggeardesc:
Deploys and retracts your ship's landing gear.

Your ship's landing gear must be deployed to successfully dock.

Deploying landing gear automatically reduces your ship's maximum travel speed.
preflightcheck_lightsdesc: Activates and deactivates your ship's front floodlights.
preflightcheck_mousemotiondesc: Mouse motion controls roll and pitch.
preflightcheck_pitchaxisdesc: Activates your ship's thrusters, causing the nose of the vessel to pitch up or down.
preflightcheck_pitchdownbuttondesc: Activates your ship's thrusters, causing the nose of the vessel to pitch down.
preflightcheck_pitchupbuttondesc: Activates your ship's thrusters, causing the nose of the vessel to pitch up.
preflightcheck_primaryfiredesc:
Activates all weapons and equipment currently assigned to primary fire button.

Weapons and equipment assigned to primary fire will change depending on the active fire group.

Weapons and equipment mounted on hardpoints will need to be deployed before they can be activated.
preflightcheck_rollaxisdesc:
Activates your ship's thrusters, causing your ship to roll clockwise or anticlockwise.

Note that rolling by itself will not change ship direction of travel.
preflightcheck_rollleftbuttondesc:
Activates your ship's thrusters, causing the ship to roll anticlockwise.

Note that rolling by itself will not change ship direction of travel.
preflightcheck_rollrightbuttondesc:
Activates your ship's thrusters, causing the ship to roll clockwise.

Note that rolling by itself will not change ship direction of travel.
preflightcheck_scoopdesc:
Deploys and retracts your ship's cargo scoop, if fitted.

When your cargo scoop is deployed, targeting a cargo canister activates the scoop HUD element.

With the cargo scoop deployed, fly slowly towards a targeted canister, keeping it at the centre of the scoop HUD element to scoop it into your ship's hold.
preflightcheck_secondaryfiredesc:
Activates all weapons and equipment currently assigned to secondary fire button.

Weapons and equipment assigned to secondary fire will change depending on the active fire group.

Weapons and equipment mounted on hardpoints will need to be deployed before they can be activated.
preflightcheck_sensordecreasedesc: Increases the scale of your sensor display, allowing the sensor HUD element to show greater fidelity at the cost of reducing the distance covered.
preflightcheck_sensorincreasedesc: Decreases the scale of your sensor display, allowing the sensor HUD element to cover greater distance, at the cost of fidelity.
preflightcheck_shieldcellbankdesc:
Consumes a shield cell to repair a weakened shield, if fitted.

There is a short delay before the cell energy is transferred to the shield.

A shield cell has no effect once a shield has collapsed - it can only affect a shield that is still active.
preflightcheck_silentrunningdesc:
Activates and deactivates 'silent running' mode.

While silent running, your ship's shields will be turned off and all heat vents will close, effectively hiding your ship's signature, reducing the range at which you will be detected.

Warning: without any capacity to disperse heat, your ship will quickly reach critical temperature and begin to suffer damage.
preflightcheck_subsystemdesc:

A reticule marker will show the location of the subsystem on the targeted vessel to assist in aiming.

Repeated use cycles through all targetable subsystems.
preflightcheck_targetaheaddesc:
Locks vessel or structure most directly in front of your ship's facing, into the ship's targeting system.

Targeting vessels allows your ship to perform a basic scan when facing them, revealing their name, shield and hull strength, and their local criminal status.
preflightcheck_targetnearestthreatdesc:
Locks most threatening contact into the ship's targeting system.

Targeting is prioritised from high to low:

Tracking missile

Engaging hostile

Nearest hostile
preflightcheck_throttleaxisdesc:
Operates your ship's main propulsion thrusters.

Throttling up causes your ship to travel directly forwards, accelerating based on the amount of throttle set.

Throttling down causes your ship to decelerate.
preflightcheck_thrustdowndesc: Activates your ship's thrusters, causing the vessel to lower directly downwards.
preflightcheck_thrustleftdesc: Activates your ship's thrusters, causing the vessel to strafe to the left.
preflightcheck_thrustrightdesc: Activates your ship's thrusters, causing the vessel to strafe to the right.
preflightcheck_thrustupdesc: Activates your ship's thrusters, causing the vessel to rise directly upwards.
preflightcheck_togglereversethrottleinpu:
Sets your main propulsion thrusters to reverse, so that throttling up causes your ship to travel directly backwards rather than forwards.

This control can be toggled.
preflightcheck_uifocusdesc:
Hold to activate UI Focus Mode.

While UI Focus Mode is active, hit $UI_Left;, $UI_Right;, $UI_Up; and $UI_Down; to focus on specific HUD elements.

Hit $UIFocus; again to leave UI Focus Mode.

While focused on a element, use $UI_Left;, $UI_Right;, $UI_Up; and $UI_Down; to navigate and $SelectTarget; to select.
preflightcheck_yawaxisdesc:

prem_finale_001_body:
If you're scanning this, it's because I am dead. Frankly, after all my tribulations, I welcome the oblivion of the void. My closest friends are dead, and I have nothing to live for. Perhaps I will find peace as I return to the stardust that made me. Know that this was my choice.

Some of you knew me as Salomé, others as Kahina Tijani Loren, a Lady of the Empire and former senator of the Prism system. I was branded a murderer and a terrorist, and there is truth in these accusations. I have made poor decisions. I killed, or caused the death, of thousands. To these crimes I freely admit my guilt. I am content to let history judge me.
prem_finale_002_body:
I bring you this message in a time of turmoil. You have little reason to believe me, and less to trust me, but nevertheless I ask you to listen. Because you have been misled.

I was sent on a quest into darkness. I did not know what I was looking for. Many people assisted me, sometimes altruistically and sometimes to further their own agendas. I am grateful to all of them. Some, to my shame, I manipulated to my own ends.

My contact guarded her secrets well - even from herself - to ensure they would be revealed only at the proper time. It seems that time is now.
prem_finale_003_body:
There are patterns of events. A tapestry, if you will.

Treaties were abolished, bringing us closer to the brink of war. Those flashpoints in Mu Koji? Engineered to fan the flames of conflict. Wreaken Construction and Mining was a beneficiary, with its naval shipyards. It was no accident that the share prices of Gutamaya and Core Dynamics rose dramatically.

The Empire turned against me, concocting a ridiculous crime and sentencing me for it. It was just a ruse so they could hold me hostage and access the exploration data I had. Ultimately, it was Imperial forces that saved me. At least some honour remains in the Empire.

The Alliance and the Federation were collaborating behind the scenes. Tsu exposed it, and they ostracised her and left her at the mercy of bounty hunters. The Alliance is no innocent bystander. They know what happened.
prem_finale_004_body:
Scientists were bribed, discoveries were leaked and people were abducted, some never to return.

The Sirius Corporation attempted a hostile takeover of MetaDrive. They murdered the chairman. MetaDrive was developing secret hyperdrive technology and Sirius wanted it. Raan kept it out of their hands and they tried to kill him for it.

Meanwhile, the organisers of the arena catalogued the best pilots in the galaxy. Ask why you would want a list of combat experts…

Explorers are rewarded with cold, hard cash for their discoveries. The Federation tried to buy our service. We showed them what true loyalty was. That exploration data cost many souls.
prem_finale_005_body:
Well, so what? That's what you're thinking.

You need to understand that these events were carefully orchestrated. Nothing happened without a reason.

I don't know the identities of those involved. If I did, I would expose them. I do know they control corporations, the military and some of the galaxy's most powerful individuals. Their reach is wide. You cannot trust anyone in a position of authority. Some are active collaborators, some are mere figureheads. Some don't even know they're being used.

And they are manipulating you. Those of you who trade, who fight in their proxy wars, who sell them exploration data from the depths of the void. They are using you to further their agenda. You, me - all of us have been their tools. They believe themselves the ultimate arbiters of humanity's destiny, above reproach and accountability. They consider themselves the true elites.

Factions and powers, economies and systems, even the arena - they're just tools they use to make us enact their will.
prem_finale_006_body:
They have murdered countless thousands, pitilessly weighing their plans against human lives - the lives of innocents, of friends and family. They claim to act in humanity's interest. They consider us sheep to their shepherds.

They hatched a secret contingency plan - a comprehensive list of earth-like worlds and terraformable planets. We have all contributed to this plan. Only recently did we discover it had been underway for decades. The evidence has been found: a planned subterfuge out in the void.

They can no longer hide from the facts. We have found them.
prem_finale_007_body:
Why all this duplicity?

Because they know everything. They have the history - not the sanitised version from the public records, but the truth. Those reports of strange ships in the void, discounted in the news? Believe them. This is the catalyst. The wheels turn and darkness will fall.

So what can you do?

Challenge the authorities. Force their hand. Refuse to be manipulated. Do not rise to their provocations. Make your own powerplays, organise embargoes and blockade the ports. Break their hold and force them out into the open. Blaze a trail. Visibility is the one thing they cannot abide.

Or do nothing. Be content to be a pawn in their game.
prem_finale_008_body:
For those who killed me, I bear you no ill will. For those who wanted me dead, you have your wish.

For those who loved me and swore allegiance to me, your service and dedication were the brightest light in the darkness of my life. Do not let my death be the end of what you would see done.

My last request is that you always…remember.
prem_zurara_001_body:
Zurara Ship Log Entry

01/10/3270

RECORDING

We managed to overpower the invaders, but not before they took out the main reactor. We're dead in space, with twenty minutes of life support left. Didn't get nothing out of them before they died, but clearly it was all planned. They took a drug which killed them. Doc says it's nicknamed 'Hexedit'. First it kills your memories, then it kills you. Neat and tidy.

So we're dead, just waiting for the end. This will be the last log from the Zurara. Some of the crew have already killed themselves. Others are praying to whatever deity they believe might help them. A few are drinking themselves into oblivion. I don't know what will get us first, the lack of oxygen or the cold. Battery power is about to die.

PAUSE RECORDING
prem_zurara_002_body:
Zurara Ship Log Entry

01/10/3270

RESUME

Me? I'm leaving this log. This far out I doubt anyone will ever hear it, but well, what the hell?

We all signed up for the promise of big payouts, a year of your life in exchange for enough to retire on. I guess I should have looked closer at it, but you would have probably done the same, right? No need to work again. What's clear now is whoever was behind this mission never intended for any of us to come back.

Damn, it's cold in here now.

PAUSE RECORDING
prem_zurara_003_body:
Zurara Ship Log Entry

01/10/3270

RESUME

The folks managing the cargo, jees, they were all psychos. The moment we completed the mission they just 'snapped'. Killed the ship and killed themselves. Some kind of mental conditioning, Doc said. We tried to get word out to the other vessels when we found out. We got a signal out, but I don't know if anyone received it. It will probably freak them out, I don't think they know we're here.

We dropped a series of beacons out here, all targeted around Earth-like or terraformable worlds. We prepped some of the terraform candidates with seeders and biofilters. No one can figure out why it was necessary, but that was the mission. Just as we were turning back... boom, those cargo-handlers went nuts.

PAUSE RECORDING
prem_zurara_004_body:
Zurara Ship Log Entry

01/10/3270

RESUME

So that's it. We don't even know why we've been killed. But someone out there knows, someone out there has blood on their hands, a lot of it. If you figure it out, give them a message from us. You know what I mean.

Funny. We were told there was something bad out here, that it was haunted by ghosts…

I just never figured it would be us doing the haunting…

END RECORDING
prem_zurara_005_body:
Zurara Ship Log - Additional Log Entry - 21/08/3273

FILE ACCESS ADDITIONAL

So this is what they were hiding. I'm leaving the old logs for reference. I might need to come back this way again and re-educate myself. Chances are my memory will get zapped again. If I don't make it I'll have to leave clues for others to follow. So, if you're reading this and you're not me, here's the deal...

PAUSE RECORDING
prem_zurara_006_body:
Zurara Ship Log - Additional Log Entry - 21/08/3273

RESUME

Found this ship. Took me years. This is the evidence. Nothing inside but void-frozen cadavers, perfectly preserved, some with drinks still in their hands. But the log. They sent these poor souls out here because they needed waypoints, all prepped for every eventuality. Three different zones it would seem.

PAUSE RECORDING
prem_zurara_007_body:
Zurara Ship Log - Additional Log Entry - 21/08/3273

RESUME

There's a conspiracy. Guess you figured that out already, but it goes way up, way beyond the Feds, the Imps and the Alliance. Something is coming, don't know what it is, but it's bad and it's all being hidden. All this weird stuff far out in the void? It's some kind of contingency plan. The answer to why and who is back in the core, not out here. That's where I'm going next. Wish me luck.

R.

END RECORDING

Consumed by: Tourism

Chemical formula SiO2. Quartz pyroxenite is an incredibly common mineral found throughout the galaxy near volcanic activity. Quartz itself was once commonly used in the manufacturing of electronics, now relegated to tourist shops selling them as healing crystals and volcanic rock trinkets.
quartzpyroxenite_info_short: Produced by: Surface Mining only Consumed by: Tourism Quartz pyroxenite is an incredibly common mineral found throughout the galaxy near volcanic activity.
