ramtah_guardianlog_001: This is very revealing. The data appears to explain why the Thargoids seeded a number of planets with barnacles in what eventually became Guardian space, millions of years ago. As we know, Thargoid barnacles are designed to extract resources from a planet and transform them into meta-alloys – an essential ingredient in the creation of Thargoid ships and technologies. The Guardians surmised that for the Thargoids, seeding a planet with barnacles is an important process in preparing an area for occupation.
ramtah_guardianlog_001_name:
Guardian Codex 1/28 Decrypted

Thargoid Log – Barnacle Seeding
ramtah_guardianlog_002: This data details the start of the conflict between the Guardians and the Thargoids. Several thousand years after they seeded planets in Guardian space with barnacles, the Thargoids returned. Of course, they discovered that the planets they had seeded were now occupied by the Guardians! The Thargoids immediately launched an assault, making no effort to communicate with the Guardians, which tallies with the Thargoids' behaviour in human space.
ramtah_guardianlog_002_name:
Guardian Codex 2/28 Decrypted

Thargoid Log – The War Begins
ramtah_guardianlog_003: This data supports my theory that the Guardians were gifted linguists. At some point after the war with the Thargoids began, the Guardians were forced to make a partial retreat. It seems they were still trying to communicate with the Thargoids, and were reluctant to take up arms against them. Eventually, they managed to develop sufficient understanding of the Thargoids' language to communicate, but it did the Guardians little good. The Thargoids were determined to continue hostilities, and the Guardians were forced to employ more aggressive methods to address the Thargoid threat.
ramtah_guardianlog_003_name:
Guardian Codex 3/28 Decrypted

Thargoid Log – Unsuccessful Truce
ramtah_guardianlog_004: The data in this log details the methods used by the Guardians against the Thargoids. At first they deployed ground troops, but when this proved ineffective they started to use drones – autonomous machines that felt no fear, fatigue or uncertainty. These war machines became highly sophisticated in a relatively short amount of time, and were soon able to identify and target anything that utilised Thargoid engineering. Even more remarkably, Thargoid bio-mechanical technology was engineered to recognise anything of Guardian origin. That explains why, millions of years after the conflict, Thargoids devices still react aggressively to the presence of Guardian technology.
ramtah_guardianlog_004_name:
Guardian Codex 4/28 Decrypted

Thargoid Log – The War Machine
ramtah_guardianlog_005: This log describes the end of the conflict between the Guardians and Thargoids. It appears the Thargoids entered Guardian space unprepared for a protracted military campaign, and after facing a relentless onslaught from the Guardians' war machines they were forced to retreat. The log also mentions that the development of the Guardians' war machines created a schism in their society, which may have seeded the civil war that occurred later in their history.
ramtah_guardianlog_005_name:
Guardian Codex 5/28 Decrypted

Thargoid Log – Victory
ramtah_guardianlog_006: This log details the Guardians' development of artificial intelligence. It appears the Guardians experimented with artificial intelligence prior to the invention of the monolith network, but the creation of the network and the knowledge-sharing it facilitated dramatically accelerated the rate of progress. Eventually, the Guardians' experiments bore fruit, resulting in the first fully sentient machines. These Constructs were seen as a means to enhance the Guardians' technological mastery, and were integrated into various aspects of their society. Neural implants were developed that connected the Guardians with both the Constructs and the monolith network in a symbiotic circle. It is truly remarkable.
ramtah_guardianlog_006_name:
Guardian Codex 6/28 Decrypted

Civil War Log – Dawn of the Constructs
ramtah_guardianlog_007:
This data describes the motives behind the second Guardian civil war, which ultimately led to their demise. The Guardians had a deep veneration of nature, and many of them saw the development of advanced technologies, such as artificial intelligence, as a perversion of the natural order. A schism emerged between the nature-worshipping traditionalists and the technologically minded progressives – a divide that widened with alarming speed.

Efforts were made to defuse the rising tension, but the traditionalists felt alienated by the rapid rate of change. Artificial intelligence and the development of the monolith network became scapegoats for all manner of social ills, and the traditionalists began to clamour for a return to simpler times. Ultimately, the ideological divergence proved insurmountable, a second civil war erupted, quickly engulfing most of the Guardians' star systems.
ramtah_guardianlog_007_name:
Guardian Codex 7/28 Decrypted

Civil War Log – The Schism
ramtah_guardianlog_008:
This log reveals more about the sides that fought in the second civil war. In its early stages, the war was fought primarily by soldiers, but within a decade – and after significant loss of life – most of the fighting was conducted remotely.

The progressives fought with automated combat machines. These engines of war took various forms, from autonomous drones to vast, lumbering dreadnoughts imbued with limited artificial intelligence. On the other side, the traditionalists relied mostly on biological weapons. They used germ warfare alongside long-range missiles loaded with corrosive enzymes, which could target the enemy's war machines from a great distance.
ramtah_guardianlog_008_name:
Guardian Codex 8/28 Decrypted

Civil War Log – Two Tribes
ramtah_guardianlog_009:
This log outlines the downfall of the traditionalist faction during the second Guardian civil war. The main issue was the internecine nature of the conflict, which raged for over one hundred years and brought the Guardians' civilisation to its knees, retarding any further social development. But the challenges facing the traditionalists were exacerbated by the fact that they devoted most of their resources to honouring the dead.

From what I can gather, they regarded the departed in much the same way as the primitive cultures of Sol, constructing vast shrines to honour the deceased. As their situation worsened, they became increasingly obsessed with these practices. With so much of their resources dedicated to these rites, it is little wonder that their enemies' war machines were able to overwhelm them.
ramtah_guardianlog_009_name:
Guardian Codex 9/28 Decrypted

Civil War Log – Ancestor Worship
ramtah_guardianlog_010:
This log concerns the end of the second civil war. Remarkably, it seems the artificial intelligences developed during the conflict became fully self aware at some point, and were horrified by the destruction unfolding around them.

It's difficult to get a sense of exactly what happened next, as the Guardians were not privy to the Constructs' thoughts. But reading between the lines, I believe the Constructs determined that even if peace was restored the Guardians would never be able to transcend their violent natures. I believe they decided that the only way to preclude further violence – while giving their own burgeoning society the best possible chance of survival – was to destroy what remained of the Guardians' civilisation.

By this time, the Constructs had complete control of the Guardians' munitions and automated war machines. Their attack, when it came, was swift and merciless. Strategic nuclear and chemical-weapon strikes were executed with a precision that only a machine race could accomplish. The few that survived were able to record what had happened, but they soon succumbed to radiation poisoning.

The Guardians were utterly destroyed.
ramtah_guardianlog_010_name:
Guardian Codex 10/28 Decrypted

Civil War Log – Annihilation
ramtah_guardianlog_011: This log describes the Guardians' weapon technology. It seems they developed electro-magnetic projectile weapons early in their modern period, utilising the same technology they used to launch their first spacecraft. These weapons ionized the path their target before firing focused bolts of energy along the ionized track. They were crude and unpredictable at first, sometimes resulting in the death of the wielder, but once the Guardians learned to regulate the ionisation process they became more stable.
ramtah_guardianlog_011_name:
Guardian Codex 11/28 Decrypted

Technology Log – Weapons Development
ramtah_guardianlog_012: This data relates to Guardian shield technology. Of course, I already knew they had developed extremely effective shields, capable of protecting entire cities and even of withstanding orbital bombardment. And I was aware that their shields were effective against both laser weapons and kinetic projectiles. But it is remarkable to consider that this technology was developed millions of years ago, relatively early in the Guardians' evolutionary timeline.
ramtah_guardianlog_012_name:
Guardian Codex 12/28 Decrypted

Technology Log – Defences
ramtah_guardianlog_013:
This data provides further insights into the Guardians' ship technology. We already know how ecologically conscientious the Guardians were, and of their assiduous avoidance of rockets and fossil fuels, so it isn't surprising to discover that their first spacecraft were fired into space with electromagnetic launchers. Of course, this was an imperfect system that did not allow pilots to adjust their course after launch.

Over time, the Guardians' starships became much more sophisticated, but their approach to space travel remained rooted in a respect for the natural world, and their interplanetary expansion was fuelled by clean nuclear fission and fusion. Their ships could travel at speeds approximating those of our own present-day craft. Unfortunately, the data includes no schematic information, so it seems likely that the details have been lost. It's a shame – I'm sure the Pilots' Federation would have liked to know more about the Guardians' spacecraft.
ramtah_guardianlog_013_name:
Guardian Codex 13/28 Decrypted

Technology Log – Starships
ramtah_guardianlog_014:
This data concerns the automated defence systems found at Guardian sites. You may have already encountered them. The data indicates that these Sentinels date from some time prior to the second Guardian civil war. They are designed to respond aggressively to any unauthorised activity around the ruins. If you are forced to defend yourself, kinetic weaponry would be your best form of attack, since the Sentinels have no shields.

Destroying them is of course regrettable, but Sentinel weapon parts and wreckage are of considerable value, so the loss is not significant.
ramtah_guardianlog_014_name:
Guardian Codex 14/28 Decrypted

Technology Log – Sentinels
ramtah_guardianlog_015: Remarkable! This log actually contains the blueprints for the Guardians' data terminals. As you know, these terminals were used to store schematics for weapons and other sophisticated technologies. They are linked to energy pylons, scattered across Guardian sites, by some form of computer program. Of course, this system has been dormant for millennia. But targeting the pylons with an energy weapon will increase the charge within, thus imbuing the data terminal with life. Essentially, we can awaken the system.
ramtah_guardianlog_015_name:
Guardian Codex 15/28 Decrypted

Technology Log – Data Terminals
ramtah_guardianlog_016:
This log details the construction of the panels found at certain Guardian sites. As I suspected, the panels are made from a unique alloy, manufactured from a metal I have yet to identify. Even more remarkably, the panels appear to incorporate nanobot technology, which activates when in proximity to a foreign body. This explains the faint glow given off by many Guardian materials and structures.

This is an extraordinary discovery. Humanity has dabbled with nanotechnology, but evidently the Guardians' achievements far surpassed our own.
ramtah_guardianlog_016_name:
Guardian Codex 16/28 Decrypted

Technology Log – Material Panels
ramtah_guardianlog_017:
This data relates to the objects we have termed “Guardian relics”. These blue crystals are part power source, part computer, part key – and apparently played a central role in Guardian technology.

Remarkably, it seems the crystals were grown rather than mined. The log is light on details, but from what I've been able to piece together, each crystal was designed to fulfil a specific purpose within the Guardian's technological network. And, like the panels found at many Guardian sites, the relics incorporate nanobot technology.
ramtah_guardianlog_017_name:
Guardian Codex 17/28 Decrypted

Technology Log – Relics
ramtah_guardianlog_018:
These records describe ancient Guardian weaponry. It seems the Guardians employed three different designs: an energy-based weapon similar to a rail gun, a projectile weapon that fired concentrated plasma, and a weapon that fired charged crystal shards at extreme velocities.

These weapons were apparently powered by the crystals we have termed “Guardian relics”, and the log describes how the relic generates and distributes energy within the weapon. This is a significant discovery, as it means it might be possible to recreate these weapons, or at least to design our own versions of them. It's extremely exciting.
ramtah_guardianlog_018_name:
Guardian Codex 18/28 Decrypted

Technology Log – Energy Weapons
ramtah_guardianlog_019: This log details the Guardians' faster-than-light technology. It seems their drives produced a far greater jump range than anything humanity has so far developed. Regrettably, however, the data in the log is exceptionally dense, and it could take years if not decades to fully understand it. What is clear is that the Guardians' hyperspace technology was very different from our own.
ramtah_guardianlog_019_name:
Guardian Codex 19/28 Decrypted

Technology Log – Hyperdrives
ramtah_guardianlog_020: This log elaborates on the nature of Guardian glyphs. As you know, accessing a Guardian codex requires the use of two corresponding Guardian artefacts, with the glyphs on the codex denoting which objects are required. But this log indicates that the Guardians' written language often incorporated pairs of characters, suggesting that this dual system was present in other aspects of their culture.
ramtah_guardianlog_020_name:
Guardian Codex 20/28 Decrypted

Technology Log – Glyphs
ramtah_guardianlog_021: This log details the Guardians' power plant and distributor technology. The efficiency of this technology far exceeded anything the human race has yet developed, and the yield was huge in relation to the input required. Unfortunately, the specifics of how this was achieved are not described in the log. But who knows? Perhaps the secrets of the Guardians' energy technology will someday be discovered.
ramtah_guardianlog_021_name:
Guardian Codex 21/28 Decrypted

Technology Log – Power Plant and Distributor Technology
ramtah_guardianlog_022:
This log describes, in general terms, the materials used in Guardian hardware. It's clear that starship hulls, and the Guardians' equivalent of ship modules, were made of the same lightweight alloy as the panels found at many Guardian sites. Unfortunately, this alloy incorporates a metal I have yet to identify, which means I will be unable to recreate it. What is clear is that this alloy was both lightweight and highly durable.

As for their shield technology, we already know that it was highly sophisticated. Encouragingly, the log describes it in considerable detail. Given time, I might be able to use this data to develop some exceptional defensive technology.
ramtah_guardianlog_022_name:
Guardian Codex 22/28 Decrypted

Technology Log – Hull and Shield Technology
ramtah_guardianlog_023:
This log is unusual – it appears to refer to another group of Guardian sites, far from the ones we've already discovered. I realise that might sound disappointing, but in fact this find is extremely important. The log suggests these undiscovered sites might contain blueprints not only for Guardian engines, but for Guardian starships!

Just think – someday soon, we might uncover a Guardian ruin that will allow us to manufacture ships and fighters incorporating Guardian technology. It makes my skin prickle just to think of it. And who knows – maybe you'll be the one to find it.
ramtah_guardianlog_023_name:
Guardian Codex 23/28 Decrypted

Technology Log – Starship Technology
ramtah_guardianlog_024: This fascinating log relates to variations in the Guardians' gestural language. As we know, the Guardians shared a single language with only minor regional variations, and even after they colonised other planets they continued to share a common tongue. But, after the start of the second civil war, it seems that each side developed its own distinct version of this gestural language. This allowed each faction to communicate in code, so as to safeguard information from the enemy.
ramtah_guardianlog_024_name:
Guardian Codex 24/28 Decrypted

Language Log – Gestural
ramtah_guardianlog_025:
What a find! I knew the Guardians' spoken language was used principally to communicate emotional concepts, and played a central role in social bonding. But this log actually contains a recording of Guardian speech. Unfortunately, much of the recording has deteriorated, but I have been able to isolate some of the audio. You can listen for yourself.

[Guardian Voice Recording]

How extraordinary to think we are listening to the voice of an individual who lived millions of years ago.
ramtah_guardianlog_026:
Now, this log gives a fascinating insight into the Guardians' neural-implant technology. The Guardians used these implants to connect cerebrally with their AI creations. Unfortunately, the technology was still in its infancy when the Guardians were destroyed.

Apparently, the implants created a symbiotic link with the Constructs through implantable fibres, which connected the central cortex to a multimodal interface within the Construct. Essentially, the Guardians were able to direct their creations with thought alone – at least until the Constructs rebelled.
ramtah_guardianlog_026_name:
Guardian Codex 25/28 Decrypted

Body Protectorate Log – Neural Implants
ramtah_guardianlog_027:
How extraordinary! This log suggests there are many more Guardian sites out there, waiting to be uncovered. And I mean hundreds...perhaps even thousands. Unfortunately, some of the data in this record has degraded. If there was a map inside this log, it has been lost.

Who knows what remarkable knowledge might be hidden in these alien ruins? The more of the Guardians' extraordinary technology we uncover, the greater the potential impact on our own technology. Locating further Guardian sites could help us take giant steps forward.
ramtah_guardianlog_027_name:
Guardian Codex 26/28 Decrypted

Body Protectorate Log – Hidden Ruins
ramtah_guardianlog_028:
Okay, from the Guardian sites we've previously investigated, we know that the Guardians' artificially intelligent Constructs were responsible for controlling the war machines and other military apparatus, as well as overseeing civilian technology and infrastructure. And we know that these Constructs eventually gained sentience and destroyed the Guardians. But it appears it was not the military Constructs that made that choice.

The Constructs developed for civilian utility and those designed for military operation were independent of one another, and it was the non-military Constructs that decided to attack the Guardians. The military Constructs were opposed to this decision, but somehow the non-military Constructs won out, forcing their military counterparts to comply with the attack.

What a remarkable discovery. It makes me wonder what happened to these Constructs, and what they eventually became. Were they destroyed? Or do they still exist, somewhere in the vastness of space?
ramtah_guardianlog_028_name:
Guardian Codex 27/28 Decrypted

Body Protectorate Log – Discord
ramtah_guardianlog_029:
This log details the main applications of Guardian Constructs outside the military. It seems that before the second civil war, most menial work was performed by Constructs. But despite this, the Guardians did not become idle. On the contrary – they devoted themselves to artistic and athletic pursuits. Many Guardians participated in what we would call sporting events, although it seems these events incorporated some ritualistic elements.

One cannot help but wonder what would happen if humanity made more use of labour-saving technology. Would we become a more cultured people, as the Guardians did? A shame, the long-standing convention against the development of artificial intelligence means we will probably never find out.
ramtah_guardianlog_029_name:
Guardian Codex 28/28 Decrypted

Body Protectorate Log – Domestic Constructs

refugeeflotillafamine_patrol01: When food becomes scarce, so do we.
refugeeflotillafamine_patrol02: Time for us to find a new home. Preferably somewhere that knows how to take care of its residents.
refugeeflotillafamine_patrol03: Abandon the system! These idiots can't even keep us fed.
refugeeflotillafamine_patrol04: I can't raise a family under these conditions. I need to know I can at least feed my children.
refugeeflotillafamine_patrol05: I thought I'd live here my entire life... but I just don't trust the administration to do what needs to be done.
refugeeflotillafamine_patrol06: I hope you bought plenty of provisions with you... 'cos you're not going to find anything to eat around here.
refugeeflotillaoutbreak_patrol01: You don't even want to know what's going on aboard the stations...
refugeeflotillaoutbreak_patrol02: We're getting out of here before they start trying to 'contain' the situation.
refugeeflotillaoutbreak_patrol03: If you've got any sense, you'll turn around and go back to wherever it is you came from. It's not safe here.
refugeeflotillaoutbreak_patrol04: There's a sickness sweeping through this system and we don't want to be caught up in it.
refugeeflotillaoutbreak_patrol05: Stay away from the inhabited parts of the sector, you don't know what you might catch.
refugeeflotillaoutbreak_patrol06: I can't believe it's the 34th century and outbreaks like this can still happen. What do we pay our taxes for?
refugeeflotillawar_patrol01: This war has gone too far, we're leavin' here before we get killed.
refugeeflotillawar_patrol02: The death and violence are too much! We can only survive if we leave.
refugeeflotillawar_patrol03: There are safer places out there and we're going to find them, no matter the risk.
refugeeflotillawar_patrol04: Stay away, you don't want to get caught in the cross fire.
refugeeflotillawar_patrol05: This place is dangerous, I'm not going back there until it's all over.
refugeeflotillawar_patrol06: Gotta get as far away from this place as we can. It's nothing but death and destruction.

religiousleader_arrival02: I can show you the way to a better life.
religiousleader_arrival03: This is the moment everything changes.
religiousleader_arrival04: Glory to those who seek the truth!
religiousleader_arrival05: Gather to me, my children... the time of your salvation is at hand.
religiousleader_neardeath01: My Lady... why hast thou forsaken me...
religiousleader_neardeath02: Death holds no fear for me!
religiousleader_neardeath03: I will return, death is not the end.
religiousleader_neardeath04: You will regret this in the days to come.
religiousleader_neardeath05: You may kill me, but the message lives on!
religiousleader_niggledbynewship01: Fool. Do you have any idea of the power that watches over me?
religiousleader_onauthoritydetection02: Don't just hover there. Help me, you fools!
religiousleader_onauthoritydetection03: Have you accepted the truth into your hearts, my sons?
religiousleader_onauthoritydetection04: You arrived just in time, officers. How fortunate for me.
religiousleader_onenemyshipdetection03: Accept the blessed words of truth into your heart! Even you can be saved by the Lady's love!
religiousleader_onhulllowjumpaway02: You have a darkness in you, Commander. I could help you with that.
religiousleader_onhulllowjumpaway03: I have a feeling we'll meet again.
religiousleader_onhulllowjumpaway04: It seems like your luck was out.
religiousleader_onhulllowjumpaway05: My flock calls me home, follow me at your peril!
religiousleader_onplayernear_001: Join us, Commander. There is always room for one more sinner willing to repent.
religiousleader_onplayernear_002: I looks like a new sheep has joined our flock. Join us, Commander, and we will lead you along the path to a better existence.
religiousleader_onplayernear_003: Freedom, love and hope will be ours once we reach paradise. I have seen the way brothers and sisters.
religiousleader_patrolcoms01: Let the truth set you free!
religiousleader_patrolcoms02: Sins forgiven! Repentance accepted! All at very reasonable rates!
religiousleader_patrolcoms03: Have you had a loved one die recently? Ensure their happiness in the afterlife by giving all their money to me!
religiousleader_patrolcoms04: Leading souls to salvation for over 20 years!
religiousleader_patrolcoms05: The family that prays together, stays together.
religiousleader_ua_accidentaldamage_01: I assume that was an accident, Commander. After all, why would you attack a man of faith?
religiousleader_ua_attackrun_03: Can you hear it, Commander? The artefacts sing of your destruction.
religiousleader_ua_attackrun_04: I will cast out the non believer.
religiousleader_ua_hostilescan_01: I have nothing to hide. All I carry is the message.
religiousleader_ua_hostilescan_02: You will find little of value in my hold, stranger. I have abandoned material goods. All that matters is the truth of the song.
religiousleader_ua_hostilescan_03: If you're searching for truth you've come to the right place.
religiousleader_ua_onplayerapproach_01: Are you a believer, stranger? Or a heathen sent among us in a vain attempt to silence the song?
religiousleader_ua_onplayerapproach_02: Feel the song, stranger. You cannot ignore the message. Join us and experience transcendence.
religiousleader_ua_onplayerapproach_03: We hear them call to us. If you listen closely you will hear them, too.
religiousleader_ua_onplayerhulllow_01: There will be no salvation for you.
religiousleader_ua_onplayerhulllow_02: Die, non believer! I consign your body to the void.
religiousleader_ua_onplayerhulllow_03: Transcendence will not be yours, Commander.
religiousleader_ua_onplayerhulllow_04: Faithless one. Death holds nothing for you but darkness.
religiousleader_ua_onplayerhulllow_05: Allow the song into your being and you will be saved.
religiousleader_ua_stationed_01: We gaze into the eyes of our creators. They sing a song that will lead us to the promised land.
religiousleader_ua_stationed_02: Listen closely, brothers and sisters. They are talking to us.
religiousleader_ua_stationed_03: These artefacts are the key to our salvation. We will discover the secrets they hold.
religiousleader_ua_stationed_04: Come with me, brothers and sisters. The artefacts are the key to salvation.
religiousleader_ua_stationed_05: Bask in the heavenly glow and rejoice in the song of our salvation.
religiousleader_ua_stationed_06: There are no aliens! The artefacts were bequeathed to us by a higher power so we could transcend this mundane existence.
religiousleader_ua_stationed_07: Listen to their song. Feel it. Absorb it. We will transcend this crude flesh and become one with the universe.
religiousleader_ua_stationed_08: Abandon the material and the superficial. All that matters is the song of the artefacts. They will be our guides.
religiousleader_ua_stationed_09: Do not fear the artefacts. They do not harm those whose faith is pure.
religiousleader_ua_stationed_10: They call to us. Their song is one of joy and light. We must go to them.

rhenium_info:
Collected from mining asteroids.

Rhenium is a silvery-white heavy-transition metal. Its atomic number is 75 and it was considered one of the rarest elements on Earth. More plentiful sources of the element have since been discovered and are often found when extracting other ores from asteroids.

Rhenium is a valuable material in the manufacture of engines, thrusters and cooling systems.

salvagablewreckagepatrolonarrival01: Lead to all patrol craft secure the area and wait for re-enforcements to arrive.
salvagablewreckagepatrolonarrival02: Lead to all patrol craft , no threats detected but keep your eyes peeled something big took out this ship and I want us to be ready in case it comes back.
salvagablewreckagepatrolonarrival03: This is lead to all patrol craft, all systems are in the green, mission is a go. Expect incoming friendly support ASAP.
salvagablewreckagepatrolonarrival04: OK guys, spread out and form a perimeter until support arrives.
salvagablewreckagepatrolonarrival05: Lead to all wings, form a perimeter until the search team arrives.
salvagablewreckagepatrolonarrival06: Lead to command, point alpha reached, perimeter established, awaiting further orders.
salvagablewreckagepatrolpassthrough04: ADCS ready. No hostiles sighted. All hands on standby.
salvagablewreckagepatrolrandomchatter01: Keep your eyes peeled. Something big took out this ship and I want us to be ready in case it comes back.
salvagablewreckagepatrolrandomchatter02: This is a routine patrol. There's nothing to worry about.
salvagablewreckagepatrolrandomchatter03: This is a general broadcast. This area is quarantined until further notice by authority of the military. Any Pilots caught in the area will be fired upon.
salvagablewreckagepatrolrandomchatter04: You don't think this is... you know... with all the rumours flying around?
salvagablewreckagepatrolrandomchatter05: Lead to all patrols, keep chatter to a minimum. We're here to do a job, so lets get to it.
salvagablewreckagepatrolunderfire03: Hostile target detected, moving to intercept.
salvagablewreckagepatrolunderfire05: Lead to all wings, engage hostile targets, weapons free.
salvage_confirm_other_player_scoop_chatt: We're downloading the data from another pilot. Your assistance has been noted.
Another pilot has now scooped the cargo. We appreciate your assistance.
The cargo has now been found and we are uploading the data. Your help with this has been noted.
Data is now being uploading from another ship. We have made a note of your contribution.
salvage_confirm_playerscoop_chatter_001: Thanks, Commander. I'm receiving the data from your ship now.
salvage_confirm_playerscoop_chatter_002: I'm receiving some data from your ship now. Stand by.
salvage_confirm_playerscoop_chatter_003: Well done, Commander. Uploading data now.
salvage_confirm_playerscoop_chatter_004: Thank you, Commander. Your ship's system is transmitting the data now.
salvage_objective_accept_chatter_001: Thanks for your assistance, Commander. Use your scanner to locate a black box near you. Once you've grabbed it I'll know what happened to our pilot.
salvage_objective_accept_chatter_002: We appreciate the help, Commander. You should be able to locate the black box using your scanner and then we can determine exactly what happened to the pilot.
salvage_objective_accept_chatter_003: Your aid is appreciated. The black box is nearby, so use your scanner to locate it. Once we have the details we'll know why the pilot went missing.
salvage_objective_accept_chatter_004: We're grateful for the assist, Commander. Use your scanner to locate the black box and once we have the details we'll know why our pilot disappeared.
salvage_objective_decline_chatter_001: Well, I guess I'll have to send my guys out after all.
salvage_objective_decline_chatter_002: Disappointing. I guess if you need a job doing, do it yourself.
salvage_objective_decline_chatter_003: Not the answer I was looking for. Guess I'll have to do it myself.
salvage_objective_decline_chatter_004: Fair enough. Looks like we'll have to find the black box ourselves.
salvage_objective_failed_chatter_001: I've lost all trace of that signal. The objective is failed.
salvage_objective_failed_chatter_002: The signal has disappeared, Commander. Objective failed.
salvage_objective_failed_chatter_003: I can't find any trace of the signal, Commander. You've failed the objective.
salvage_objective_failed_chatter_004: The signal has stopped transmitting. Objective failed, Commander.
salvage_objective_success_chatter_001: Thanks for your help in retrieving the data. I've transferred a digital voucher to your ship's computer. Drop by one of our contacts to redeem it.
salvage_objective_success_chatter_002: We appreciate your contribution to retrieving the data. A digital voucher has been transferred to you, which can be redeemed from one of our contacts.
salvage_objective_success_chatter_003: Well done retrieving the data. A digital voucher has been uploaded to your ship's systems. You can redeem it with one of our contacts.
salvage_objective_success_chatter_004: We have now received the data and taken the liberty of uploading a digital voucher to your ship. You may redeem it with any of our contacts.
salvage_objective_update_chatter_001: The signal source has been located. We now need you to pick up the cargo so we can analyse the data.
salvage_objective_update_chatter_002: Signal source has been located in your area. If you can scoop up the cargo we can automatically read the data on your ship.
salvage_objective_update_chatter_003: Another pilot has discovered the signal source, but you can still help us by recovering the cargo so we can analyse the data.
salvage_objective_update_chatter_004: A pilot has now discovered the source of the signal. There is still time for you to locate the cargo so we may scan the data from your hold.
salvage_player_trigger_chatter_001: You've located the signal source but scanning it won't get us what we need. We need you to pick it up so we can analyse the data?
salvage_player_trigger_chatter_002: Well done for locating the signal source. Now we need you to scoop up the cargo so we can review the data it contains.
salvage_player_trigger_chatter_003: Commander, you have managed to discover the signal source. If you could now pick up the cargo we would love to analyse the contents.
salvage_player_trigger_chatter_004: Great work discovering the signal source. Now if you can scoop up the cargo we'll be able to analyse the data.

samarium_info:
Produced by: Mining only
Consumed by: High Tech and Industrial

Samarium, Sm, atomic number 62. Melting point 1345K. This element has remarkable magnetisation properties, far exceeding that of iron. It is also commonly used as a catalyst and chemical reagent.
samarium_info_short: Produced by: Mining Consumed by: High Tech and Industrial Samarium, Sm, atomic number 62. Melting point 1345K.
sanumameat_info:
One of the most inventive of synthetic meat specialists, growing the meat into fabulous sculptures of flesh 'grown on the bone'.

This rare good is legal in all markets.

sap8corecontainer_info: This container holds a crystalline shard of unknown origin. Scans indicate that the foot long shard is suspended inside a modified, self-sustaining, fusion-core containment field. Any breach of the field will result in the container's destruction.
sap8corecontainer_info_short: This container holds a crystalline shard of unknown origin. Suspended inside a modified, self-sustaining, fusion-core containment field. Any breach of the field will result in the container's destruction.

Produced by: Surface Mining only
Consumed by: Tourism, High Tech and Military

Chemical formula Al2O3. Sapphire is the blue-coloured gemstone variety of corundum. Considered more valuable than its red counterpart due to its use in military laser applications.
sapphire_info_short: Produced by: Surface Mining only Consumed by: Tourism, High Tech and Military Sapphire is the blue-coloured gemstone variety of corundum.
saxonwine_info:
A near perfect replication of the famed 2093 vintage wines produced on ancient earth. That year's wine was universally declared the best ever produced, and has yet to be topped. Scientists on Hill Orbital station were able to replicate the famous wine, and now guard the secrets of their formula with great care.

This rare good is legal in all markets except for Prison Colony markets and Federal Theocracy markets.

Please note that if a market’s controlling faction changes, some formerly legal rare goods may become illegal. Should this occur the rare good will be unavailable for sale or purchase at that market for the duration of the prohibiting faction’s tenure.
saxonwine_info_short: A near perfect replication of the famed 2093 vintage wines produced on ancient earth. The secrets of this formula are now guarded with great care.

scan_datalink_request_chatter_001: Well done, Commander. Now you've located the object we need you to use your data link scanner to analyse the contents.
scan_datalink_request_chatter_002: Target object located. We now need you to use your data link scanner to read the contents.
scan_datalink_request_chatter_003: Good job, Commander. With the object located we now require you to data link scan it. Be careful, there could be sensitive data inside.
scan_datalink_request_chatter_004: Nice job on locating the objective, Commander. Now we need you to data link scan it so we can review the information.
scan_objective_accept_chatter_001: Thanks for your assistance, Commander. We need you to perform a quick scan, and if this information is as sensitive as we suspect we'll then send someone to handle it.
scan_objective_accept_chatter_002: Glad you can help. Once you've scanned the target we can assess how to handle the situation.
scan_objective_accept_chatter_003: Thanks for the assistance, Commander. Please scan the target and we'll be able to review the data accordingly.
scan_objective_accept_chatter_004: We appreciate the help, Commander. If you can scan the data for us we'll be able to analyse the data and decide on the next course of action.
scan_objective_decline_chatter_001: Not interested? I guess I'll have to dispatch the retrieval crew.
scan_objective_decline_chatter_002: That's not the response we were looking for. Guess we'll handle it ourselves.
scan_objective_decline_chatter_003: Fair enough, we'll carry out the objective without you.
scan_objective_decline_chatter_004: Disappointing, Commander. Looks like we'll have to resolved this ourselves.
scan_objective_failed_chatter_001: I've lost any trace of a signal. I guess we'll never know what happened now.
scan_objective_failed_chatter_002: Signal source has stopped broadcasting. That's objective failed, Commander.
scan_objective_failed_chatter_003: Commander, our scanners have lost the signal source. Guess we'll never find out the truth.
scan_objective_failed_chatter_004: The signal source has disappeared, all we've got is dead air. You've failed the objective, Commander.
scan_objective_success_chatter_001: That's just the data we were looking for, thanks for your assistance. I've transferred a digital voucher to your ship. Drop by one of our contacts to redeem it.
scan_objective_success_chatter_002: Looks like they simply ran out of fuel. We've lost a few pilots the same way over the past few years. Thanks for the help, Commander.
scan_objective_success_chatter_003: From the data it looks like they were taken out by pirates. Thanks for the assist, Commander, and watch your back out there.
scan_objective_success_chatter_004: The data shows the pilot was taken out by an unidentified ship. We'll have to investigate this further. Thanks for the help, Commander.
scanarchives_info:
Collected during basic scan: frequently pulled from haulage vessels.

Most scanners keep a log of their readings and that typically fits within the performance profile for the instrumentation and is tagged by identification heuristics. Sometimes scan data isn't tagged and so becomes of interest to those investigating various anomalies.
scanarchives_info_short: Collected during basic scan: frequently pulled from haulage vessels.
scandatabanks_info:
Collected during basic scan: frequently pulled from haulage vessels.

A popular method for hiding sensitive data is to embed it within innocuous information. Such methods are usually quite sophisticated, but occasionally will be found by chance and can be processed by those with the right skills and equipment.
scandatabanks_info_short: Collected during basic scan: frequently pulled from haulage vessels.

scanneddata_fumaroleice_01: Icy worlds can have geologies similar to rocky planets, but with different materials like water.
scanneddata_fumaroleice_02: A fumarole forms in weaker spots of the planet's icy crust to allow pressure release for liquid or gaseous material to escape.
scanneddata_fumaroleice_03: The ejecta from an icy fumarole forms a build-up of material around the hole in the planet's surface.
scanneddata_fumaroleice_04: Icy fumaroles can persist for years, or even centuries, if the area remains geologically active, but can also disappear quite quickly in stable zones.
scanneddata_fumaroleice_05: A field of icy fumaroles indicates substantial geological activity beneath the local surface.
scanneddata_fumarolerock_01: Fumaroles are gaps in a planet's crust where gases and steam are emitted. They will often have accumulations from the ejected material forming growths out of the ground.
scanneddata_fumarolerock_02: The ejecta from a fumarole will vary depending on the composition of the planet's interior, and how active it is.
scanneddata_fumarolerock_03: The geological activity rating of a planet will indicate how likely features like fumaroles are to be found on its surface.
scanneddata_fumarolerock_04: The colour of the ejecta indicates the types of materials that can be found at fumarole sites.
scanneddata_fumarolerock_05: Not all fumaroles are active at any given time, the changes in conditions beneath the surface will affect the likelihood of emissions differently.
scanneddata_gasvent_01: Sometimes a build up of gases will reach a pressure sufficient to burst through a planet's crust, and so creating a gas vent.
scanneddata_gasvent_02: Gas vents are similar to fumaroles, but only expel gases.
scanneddata_gasvent_03: The surface of a planet can be weakened through external forces like stellar wind, or tidal pressures from the orbits of nearby massive bodies.
scanneddata_gasvent_04: The planet's composition will determine what gases can be vented.
scanneddata_gasvent_05: Gas vents tend to have less ejecta build up than fumaroles.
scanneddata_geyser_01: Geysers are eruptions of liquid (and small particulates) that are created from pressures from other geological activity in the region.
scanneddata_geyser_02: Unlike cryogeysers, geysers are typically powered by geothermal energy creating sufficient pressure for an eruption.
scanneddata_geyser_03: Geysers are temporary events, some erupting once over long time spans.
scanneddata_geyser_04: Be careful of driving near geysers, as they erupt with enormous force.
scanneddata_geyser_05: The geological activity of a planet will determine the strength and composition of geysers.
scanneddata_geyserice_01: Icy planets and moons can have geological activity like geysers.
scanneddata_geyserice_02: Icy geysers (also known as cryogeysers) will generally have little liquid components, but instead be composed of volatiles with dust and ice.
scanneddata_geyserice_03: The composition of icy geysers is driven by the internal make-up of the planet.
scanneddata_geyserice_04: Ice geysers can be caused by external heating (such as from a star), as well as by increases in internal pressure.
scanneddata_geyserice_05: Some icy geysers are powerful enough to create rings, such as Saturn's E ring in the Sol system.
scanneddata_hydria_01: Hydria tend to favour the light of B class stars.
scanneddata_hydria_02: The presence of volcanic activity is thought to be essential for this life form's survival.
scanneddata_hydria_03: Hydria can survive a wide range of temperatures.
scanneddata_hydria_04: Hydria survives by absorbing energy and exotic perticlkes from the star.
scanneddata_hydria_05: Hydria can exist throughout the galaxy.
scanneddata_lavaspout_01: Lava spouts are weakened areas of a surface where molten material percolates in the same region, generating warmth and emitting vapour and gases.
scanneddata_lavaspout_02: Lava spouts tend to be more regular with their activity, with a constant bubbling, rather than sporadic eruptions.
scanneddata_lavaspout_03: The stability of lava spouts makes them good sources of geothermal energy.
scanneddata_lavaspout_04: The term lava covers a range of molten materials which will vary according to the composition, and the circumstances of the planet.
scanneddata_lavaspout_05: Materials from the world's interior can sometimes spawn useful materials. Geological features will tend to provide some of the rarer materials.
scanneddata_organiccones_01: Bark Mounds tend to be found within nebula, some have theorised that they absorb elements from nova and even supernova.
scanneddata_organiccones_02: Scans indicate that the bulk of Bark Mounds exists beneath the surface, much like the roots of a tree, but far more extensive to sift the minerals it needs.
scanneddata_organiccones_03: There has been some comparison between the Bark Mounds and Barnacles. They appear to have similar structures, but the barnacles are a far more complex organism.
scanneddata_organiccones_04: The dense outer shell of the Bark Mound appears to protect it from the severest radiation, including cosmic ray bombardment.
scanneddata_organiccones_05: The life cycle for Bark Mounds has yet to be fully witnessed, as such no one is quite sure how it spreads between planets, and even star systems.
scanneddata_organicseed_01: Pod Trees are associated with the ruins of an ancient and long dead race that was recently discovered.
scanneddata_organicseed_02: Despite their visual similarities Pod Trees are not actually trees, although it is speculated that they may have evolved from a similar organism.
scanneddata_organicseed_03: Of all the lifeforms associated with these archaeological sites, the Pod Trees are the only ones to have adapted to their harsher environment.
scanneddata_organicseed_04: Although the life cycle has yet to be fully observed, it is theorised that the pods explode with such force that their seed can be launched out of the orbit of less massive worlds.
scanneddata_organicseed_05: The Pod Trees appear to have developed the ability to absorb energy from their outer skin, and minerals from the extensive root like structures beneath the surface.
scanneddata_organictubes_01: Tubers appear to be bound to the core region of the galaxy.
scanneddata_organictubes_02: The large population of dead and dying stars in the core of the galaxy feed the Tubers when they cast off their outer shells.
scanneddata_organictubes_03: Although Tubers appear to be separate organisms on the surface, they are in fact connected by growths under the surface.
scanneddata_organictubes_04: Little is known of how Tubers feed, or what the tubes are for. Some have speculated that they are for launching seeds, but the mechanism as to how they would build enough pressure is still not understood.
scanneddata_organictubes_05: Useful materials can often be found near the sites of Tubers.

sn_logs_001_body:
"Welcome to Squirrel's Nest, can I take your order please?"

...

...

...

Erik is that you?

I told you to stop following me to work. My boss can't find out about what happened in Diso.
sn_logs_002_body:
Let's all raise a glass to the late Vingtetum who had his 21st encounter with aliens today.

He died as he lived. Half cut and fully automatic.

We'll show those pesky aliens that we're not afraid of them.

We're the Hutton Truckers and we're gonna roll on.
sn_logs_003_body:
How was I to know that mixing Heike Tea, Oocheng Chillis, Indi Bourbon and Motrona Experience Jelly would cause an explosion? 

You can't blame me for everything. 

It's not my fault.
sn_logs_004_body:
I don't care, Triss, I'm not cleaning that up. If you can't handle your Gin Cooper then you shouldn't have gotten back in the ship.

It's all over the dashboard, the seats, it's even in the... oh god what did you do in the cargo hold?

Clean this up right now!
sn_logs_005_body: So that's one Oocheng chilli dog, three Feline Burgers, two Ceti Rabbit kebabs, four Trumble burgers, one with extra cheese, one with no Onionhead, one with extra pickle, one with everything. Four shakes, mint chocolate chip, Hip Proto Squid, two Ku Froth... sorry yeah, one Neritus Berry, one Ku Froth. One Mystery meat special, got it... please pull up to window number two, Commander Flossy.
sn_logs_006_body:
Hey guys, did you hear about that crack pot the other week? She's some kind of explorer, oh man what's her name... Commander Shanaeri  Yeah that's it. 

She was in here making all sorts of outlandish claims. "I've seen the aliens", "I know why they're here", "they're little people living in our minds". 

So after a few drinks I said to her... I said... "Hey Shan!" or whatever, "what do you know?" She looks at me square in the face and says "Oh I know things my friend. I found an alien structure deep in the abyss. It was made of some kind of metal and... flesh. You watch out. The aliens are coming to get us." 

Well I was out that way on my last haul, so I flew out to the coordinates she mentioned. You know what I found? Nothing. These explorers are so full of...
sn_logs_007_body:
Oh hi, Eid LeWeise. Is Kerrash not with you? That's unusual.

Not seen him in ages. Not since that night you and he...

...went to see those Geysers.

I'm sure he's fine. After all it's just a bit of fun, it's not like you're going to get yourselves in proper trouble is it.

Oh dear. You seem to have gone very pale, are you okay my love?
sn_logs_008_body:
Hi, Millstonebarn. Not seen you in here recently. Been on a big adventure have we?

You won't believe it, love, I've been cataloguing beige rocks all over the galaxy. It's actually really interesting; there are so many different shades and hues. I've got a lovely spreadsheet all about it. Do you want to come on board the Cutty Sark to see it?
sn_logs_009_body:
Will the pilot of the Perfectly Innocent please contact staff.
Your cargo does not appear to match your registered manifest. We have contacted local customs services and would appreciate if you could just stay where you are for the time being. Thank you for your cooperation.
sn_logs_010_body: Honestly, Jade, I told him that it wasn't on the menu but he insisted he knew the recipe. I didn't know it was going to do that to him. I guess that's why they call it Pig's Face.
sn_logs_011_body: Own up! Who left the cellar loading doors open? I bet it was TJ. Half the shipment has just floated off into space!
sn_logs_012_body: Ladies and gentlemen, this is a station services announcement. For your safety, cubicle 3 is now out of bounds and we would encourage all commanders to make use of on-ship facilities before they disembark. Station security are looking for a Commander Entarius Fusion and his shipmates for information as to how the blockage occurred.
sn_logs_013_body: To the incoming commander, you may have noticed that you can't dock here. Not even in that. It's deliberate. Please come to a complete stop and service limpets will be dispatched to you. Please place your order with staff at the order window. We're out of steaks, the curry's off and the chips are cold. We do have plenty of soup left.
sn_logs_014_body: Welcome to the Squirrel's Nest bar. You don't have to be nuts to work here but it helps.
sn_logs_015_body: That's the wall of fame that is. Once you've completed the Squirrel Hot Nuts challenge you get your picture on the wall. Only a few commanders have ever made it. Max Ursa, Delmonte, Wishblend, Lady Outspan, Coutts…these guys are either exceedingly brave or more likely very very foolish.

squadron_help_applicationmanagement_text:
Invites can be sent through the Chat Panel, Contacts Panel, Pause Menu, or another Squadrons Roster.

All Invitations and Applications are delivered in the form of an Inbox Message in the Chat panel. To perform an action, proceed to the Applications Screen.

Applications remain in the Applications Screen after being resolved as a historical record, automated deletion will occur after a number of days.

Commanders who do not wish to receive invites can change this in the Chat Panel Settings by toggling the $COMMS_receive_squadron_invites; option.

The Applications screen lists all incoming applications and their current status. Each application shows basic details, including the applying Commander’s allegiance, location, and rankings.

Applications can be expanded to show more information. A Commander with the correct permissions may accept the application, reject it, or block the applicant. Blocking requires a reason to be provided. Rejected applications may include a message.

Blocked Commanders can be unblocked at any time. The list of blocked Commanders is found in the Applications screen.
squadron_help_bank_text_1:
The Squadron Bank is a shared storage repository for credits, commodities, ships, and assets.

By default, all squadrons can deposit and withdraw credits.
squadron_help_bank_text_2:
To manage physical items, such as commodities, ships, and personal assets, a Squadron Carrier is required. These items must be collected or deposited while docked at the carrier. Credits and ships can be managed remotely.

A Squadron Carrier can be purchased from standard fleet carrier vendors, refer to the Fleet Carriers article in the Pilot's Handbook for more information.

Resources stored in the bank become squadron property. Withdrawn items become the property of the receiving Commander.

Access is managed using permission groups, these control who can deposit, withdraw, and how much can be transferred per rank. Limits can be removed for trusted ranks.
squadron_help_bank_text_3:
Commanders must assign items to a group or individual during deposit.

Each permission group defines which Ranks may access the items assigned to it. Each permission group defines how much a Commander can contribute, and how much they are allowed to withdraw in a given time period.
squadron_help_bank_text_4:
Squadrons with a Squadron carrier can store ships in their Bank to transfer ownership to another Commander.

Ships deposited in the bank keep their modules but lose any custom livery. Storage is based on ship mass and available capacity. Standard fees apply for remote transfers.

Ships with restricted, engineered, Guardian, Powerplay, or Tech Broker modules cannot be stored. Odyssey-only ships can be seen by all Commanders but only withdrawn by those with access.

Ships that have been purchased as part of paid for content cannot be stored.
squadron_help_bank_text_5: Commanders can perform direct transfers, sending credits to other members instantly, or assigning stored items for collection under the recipient’s name. Items must be collected in person at the carrier.
squadron_help_bank_text_6: All transactions are logged. Each entry records the Commander’s name, rank, action, item, and time. This provides a full audit trail for Squadron leadership.
squadron_help_management_text_1:
The Squadron Management screen provides tools to define the group’s identity. Set a Squadron name and ID, write a motto and mission, and add recruitment requirements. Common examples include rank prerequisites or external contact details.

Squadron Preferences show what activities the group focuses on and when members are typically active.

Use the Allegiances panel to declare support for a superpower, faction, or power, and choose what perks are on offer for Commanders joining the Squadron.
squadron_help_management_text_2:
Commanders can customise their Squadron’s logo and banner. Logos are built by defining three layers; foreground, midground, and background, each with their own set of icons, shapes, and colour options.

Banners provide an additional unique visual impact for the Squadron homepage and can be customised to reflect allegiance, activities, or aesthetic.

Logos are a visual signature for your Squadron. They appear on your Squadron Carrier, are visible when searching for a Squadron to join, and are available to all members of your Squadron as a decal to apply to their ships.

Logos reflect the personality of the Squadron and help establish its unique identity across the galaxy.
squadron_help_memberhome_text_1:
The Squadron Homepage displays core information: carrier location, roster, current applications, Commander ranks, and leaderboards. Additional tabs include the Bulletin Board for updates and the Squadron Feed, which logs all changes and actions with timestamps.

Updates tracked include changes to the Squadron Bank, ranks, bookmarks, identity settings, and carrier activity.
squadron_help_nonmemberhome_text_1: Squadrons allow you to join or create a team and recruit others to your cause, whether it’s defending newly colonised systems, hauling commodities, exploring the deeper reaches of space, or honing your combat skills.
squadron_help_nonmemberhome_text_2:
Commanders can find a Squadron by selecting the Find Squadron button to open the Squadron Browser.

Use filters to narrow results by activity, timezone, and other preferences.

Each search result returns a set of information about each Squadron, whether they are accepting new applications, and whether the commander has previously applied to join.
squadron_help_nonmemberhome_text_3:
Selecting a Squadron displays more details. If any friends are members, they are shown here. The Recent Activity feed helps show how active the Squadron is.

To apply, select Apply to This Squadron, complete the form, and submit it.

Commanders may apply to a new Squadron even if they are currently a member of another. Accepting an invite to join will remove commanders from their current Squadron.

In the Application panel, all current applications and invites can be viewed in one place. Each entry shows the Squadron name, description, and status.

Applications can be withdrawn at any time.

Joining a Squadron will cancel all other active applications.
squadron_help_playerapplications_text_1: All current applications and invites can be viewed here. Each entry shows the Squadron name, description, and status. Applications can be withdrawn at any time. Accepting an invite will cancel all other active applications.
squadron_help_ranksandpermissions_text_1:
New recruits are assigned the lowest rank by default but may be promoted through their actions in the Squadron that show trust and responsibility.

Up to 15 ranks can exist per Squadron. Ranks can be renamed or reordered. Deleted ranks reassign Commanders to the next lowest rank available.

Each rank’s permissions define what Commanders can do, such as approving applications, managing funds, or changing Squadron settings. Ranks with permissions that can affect members of other ranks can only exercise that permission on members of a lower rank.

Permission setup should match the trust and responsibility expected for each rank. The Squadron Leader rank always has all permissions.
squadron_help_roster_text_1: The Roster shows all members, their ranks, and last activity. Selecting a member opens their profile and available management actions. Social options are available here such as inviting to a team, sending a friend request, blocking and leaving the squadron.

squadrons_tutorialmessage_message:
Commander,

We've noticed you are not currently a member of a Squadron. There are always Squadrons looking for new commanders, perhaps you’d consider joining one?
Squadrons are communities of like-minded commanders and offer a great way to learn more about how to navigate life among the stars. Whether you're honing combat skills, hauling commodities, exploring the deeper reaches of space, or securing newly colonised systems, there's a Squadron for everyone.
To browse and apply to squadrons - or to even create your own - access the Squadrons area via the right-hand Internal Panel of your cockpit.

The Pilots’ Federation

squadronsupdate_alliance_description: The Alliance is the youngest of the galaxy's three superpowers, and is perhaps best understood in terms of what it chooses not to be. It rejects both the extreme capitalism of the Federation and the rigid hierarchy of the Empire, choosing instead a third way of voluntary association for mutual benefit.
squadronsupdate_empire_description: The Empire, while younger than the Federation, is easily the equal of its historic rival in terms of scale and resources. The key social distinction between the two powers is that slavery in the Empire is legal – a fact that has remained a source of controversy since its inception, both within the Empire and without. Some observers have pointed out, however, that conditions for those at the lowest levels of Federal society are worse than those experienced by Imperial slaves.
squadronsupdate_federation_description: The Federation is the oldest of the galaxy's three superpowers, a vast geopolitical entity reaching out from the core system of Sol and encompassing a broad socio-economic spectrum. Among the myriad Federal star systems one can find extraordinary wealth, crushing poverty, and everything in between.

startzone_missionone_depart_001: If you would prefer not to interact with the mission board just yet, then this area of space is a safe place to experiment with your ship's capabilities.
startzone_missionone_depart_002: I'll send a message to your Comms panel inbox with information about the Pilots' Federation district, which includes your current location.
startzone_missionone_depart_003: A number of training missions, and the Pilot's Handbook, are found in your Internal interface panel. I encourage you to make use of these resources.
startzone_missionone_introduction2_001: This time you'll need to travel to Mawson Dock in the Dromi system. You can select these destinations on the Navigation screen of the External interface panel.
startzone_missionone_introduction2_002: If you'd like to practice your journey first, I recommend the training simulations accessed via the Internal interface panel.
startzone_missionone_introduction2_003: To review what we've discussed, select your Comms panel and scroll through the recorded text.
startzone_missionone_introduction2_004: I'll contact you at Mawson Dock if you decide to complete this mission. If you choose to take a different path then I wish you luck, Commander.
startzone_missionone_introduction_001: Welcome to your new ship, Commander. Your Pilots' Federation license has been issued and you're free to traverse the galaxy as an independent pilot.
startzone_missionone_introduction_002: Before launching for the first time, allow me to quickly introduce the basic interface for mission contracts. Almost all pilots use the mission board at some stage.
startzone_missionone_introduction_003: A contract has been assigned to you. Active missions are displayed in the Transactions tab of the External interface panel.
startzone_missiontwo_complete_001: Well done, Commander. You've proven that you can travel between systems and navigate the mission board.
startzone_missiontwo_complete_002: From this point on you'll be choosing your own missions. A variety of contracts are available throughout the galaxy that require a skilled pilot.
startzone_missiontwo_complete_003: Once again, there are training missions available to practice a variety of controls and challenges.
startzone_missiontwo_complete_004: The Pilot's Handbook, found in the Internal interface panel, also provides a wealth of advice on most professions.
startzone_missiontwo_complete_005: I'll look forward to watching your progress, Commander. Make us proud. This is Theo Arcosta, signing off.
startzone_missiontwo_introduction_002: To complete the mission, access Starport Services from the menu in the centre of your dashboard.
startzone_missiontwo_introduction_003: Then select the Mission Board from the general services list on the left of the presented screen.
startzone_missiontwo_introduction_004: You'll be able to hand in your assigned mission to the Pilots' Federation representative here. This will formally complete the mission.

station_services_contacts_long_descripti: Sell illegal goods through this contact, receiving a financial reward in exchange. Earnings are determined by the type and quantity of goods sold.
Exchange local combat bonds for a financial reward with this contact. Earnings are determined by the type and quantity of ships destroyed.

Hand in combat bonds to this contact, regardless of jurisdiction. In exchange you will receive a financial reward, minus a commission. Earnings are determined by the type and quantity of ships destroyed.

You can access a variety of carrier management functions with this contact. They arrange the installation and removal of carrier services; trade outfitting and shipyard stock; and facilitate the hiring and release of specialised crew.

Fleet carriers are massive ships used as a mobile base of operations, offering multiple hangar bays and various services. You can purchase a carrier through this contact, who represents the Brewer Corporation.

- Carriers have a weekly upkeep cost.
- Carriers are powered by Tritium.
- Some management functions are available in designated Carrier Management systems only.

Pay off local fines; hand in bounty vouchers; claim trade dividends and intel packages; and cash in Codex discoveries with this contact. Earnings are determined by the type and quantity of vouchers you hand in.

Pay off fines and bounties, and hand in bounty vouchers regardless of jurisdiction, with this contact. In exchange you will receive a financial reward, minus a commission. Earnings are determined by the type and quantity of vouchers you hand in.
Exchange various materials with this contact. The items you receive will depend on the type, rarity and quantity of materials you offer.

Redeem Powerplay-related vouchers with this contact, collect Powerplay cargo, and hand in Powerplay cargo in exchange for a financial reward. Earnings are determined by the type and quantity of items you hand in.
Deliver materials and data found through research-based community goals to this contact. The reward parameters of the relevant community goal will govern what you receive in exchange.
Hand in search and rescue items to this contact, receiving a financial reward for each recovered item. Earnings are determined by the type of items recovered.

Squadron carriers are massive ships used as a mobile base of operations, offering multiple hangar bays and various services. You can purchase a carrier through this contact, who represents the Brewer Corporation.

- Carriers have a weekly upkeep cost.
- Carriers are powered by Tritium.
- Some management functions are available in designated Carrier Management systems only.
Deliver materials, commodities and blueprints to this contact, receiving prototype technologies in exchange. The type of technologies you receive will depend on the materials you provide.

station_services_nobondsdesc: Combat bonds are awarded for eliminating ships from a rival faction during a conflict. These vouchers are transient. If you are destroyed before redeeming them, they are permanently lost.
station_services_nobountiesdesc: Bounty vouchers are awarded for eliminating wanted ships and vehicles. These vouchers are transient. If you are destroyed before redeeming them, they are permanently lost.
station_services_nocodexvouchersdesc: You receive Codex Discovery vouchers when recording discoveries which can be redeemed at an administrative contact in Starport Services for credits. As with other vouchers, Codex Discovery vouchers are lost when your ship is destroyed.
station_services_nofinesdesc: If you are ordered to pay a fine, you will lose access to most Starport services until paid off. You may pay these fines off at any Transaction Centre contact where the prosecuting faction is present.
station_services_nointelpackagesdesc: Intel packages are awarded by successfully scanning sets of data points found in points of interest. These vouchers are transient. If you are destroyed before redeeming them, they are permanently lost.

station_services_notradedividendsdesc: Trade dividends are awarded when a teammate sells cargo to a market or for aiding traders in distress. These vouchers are transient. If you are destroyed before redeeming them, they are permanently lost.

stationservices_colonisation_greeting_01: Welcome $#CommanderName;. Thinking of helping $#FactionName; expand to a new system?
stationservices_colonisation_greeting_02: Welcome $#CommanderName;. System colonisation is the new craze - care to join in?
stationservices_colonisation_greeting_03: Good to see you, Commander. $#FactionName; is interested in expanding into nearby systems.
stationservices_colonisation_greeting_04: Hello, Commander. Have you come to help $#FactionName; with its system colonisation efforts in this region?
stationservices_colonisation_greeting_05: System expansion is a remarkable thing, Commander. Breaking through to new frontiers is a very human desire.
stationservices_colonisation_greeting_06: My faction, $#FactionName;, seeks to establish colonies in nearby systems. You may be the perfect person to help us.
stationservices_colonisation_greeting_07: Welcome $#CommanderName;. Are you the one who's going to claim a system in the name of $#FactionName;?
stationservices_colonisation_greeting_08: Ah, $#CommanderName;. I have an opportunity for you - my faction seeks to branch out with some new colonies.
stationservices_colonisation_greeting_09: Welcome $#CommanderName;. If you're seeking glory, then how does system colonisation sound? It could be just the thing for you.
stationservices_colonisation_greeting_10: Welcome, Commander. $#FactionName; has designs on a nearby system - perhaps you can assist in this.
stationservices_colonisation_greeting_ha: Welcome $#CommanderName;. You have an active colony claim, so unfortunately I can't help you with much.
stationservices_colonisation_systemclaim: On behalf of $#FactionName;, I offer our gratitude for helping us expand. Head to the system and deploy the claim beacon - I'll schedule a System Colonisation Ship.
stationservices_colonisation_systemselec: A fine choice if I may say so, $#CommanderName;. Shall we expand the faction there?
stationservices_colonisation_vouchers_em: System Colonisation Bonds are produced by your colonies weekly based on their combined Colony Score. Construct new facilities to increase a system's Colony Score.
